readSections: Abstract, contents and §1 Introduction (§1.1 What do we cover), printed pp. 101–105
§2 What is a p-adic L-function (§2.1 classical L-functions, §2.2 motivating questions for Iwasawa theory, §2.3 the Riemann zeta function, §2.4 p-adic L-functions) and the Part I preface, pp. 105–117

§3 Measures and Iwasawa algebras (§3.1 p-adic Banach spaces, §3.2 p-adic measures, §3.3 the Iwasawa algebra, §3.4 Mahler transforms, §3.5 the measure-theoretic toolbox, §3.6 pseudomeasures, §3.7 locally analytic distributions, §3.8 further remarks), pp. 117–136
§4 The Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function (§4.1 the measure µ_a, §4.2 restriction to ℤ_p^×, §4.3 rescaling), pp. 136–139
§5 Interpolation at Dirichlet characters (§5.1 p-power conductor, §5.2 nontrivial tame conductors, §5.3 the Mellin transform), pp. 139–148
§6 The values at s = 1 (§6.1 complex, §6.2 p-adic: Leopoldt's formula, Coleman's polylogarithm formula), §7 The residue of ζ_p at s = 1, §8 The p-adic family of Eisenstein series, pp. 148–161
Part II: §9 Notation, §10 The Coleman map (§10.1–10.5, including the Kummer sequence, Euler systems and Perrin-Riou's programme), pp. 161–174

§11 Iwasawa's theorem on the zeros of the p-adic zeta function and §12 its proof (equivariance of the Coleman map, the fundamental exact sequence, generators of global and local cyclotomic units), pp. 174–189

§13 The Iwasawa Main Conjecture (§13.1 structure theory, §13.2 Galois Λ-modules, §13.3 the Main Conjecture, §13.4 the proof for Vandiver primes, §13.5 Selmer groups and Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjectures), pp. 189–198

Every statement and proof was read line by line; formulas were checked against the arXiv v2 LaTeX and, where the extracted text was garbled, against rendered page images.

summary: Expository notes (Essential Number Theory 2025) on the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic zeta function and the foundations of cyclotomic Iwasawa theory, for p odd. Part I builds p-adic measures, Iwasawa algebras, Mahler/Amice transforms, pseudomeasures and locally analytic distributions (§3), constructs ζ_p as the pseudomeasure ([a]−[1])^{−1}·x^{−1}µ_a from the smoothed Bernoulli measure (§4, Theorem 4.1), proves its interpolation of L(χ,1−k) for all Dirichlet characters of p-power and tame conductor (Theorems 5.1, 5.7, 5.20), Leopoldt's formula for L_p(θ,1) and Coleman's polylogarithm formula (§6), the residue (1−1/p) at s = 1 (§7) and the Eisenstein family (§8). Part II constructs the Coleman map from norm-compatible local units to measures (Theorems 10.2, 10.13, Definition 10.14), shows it sends cyclotomic units to ζ_p (Theorem 10.15, whose printed sign is wrong), proves Iwasawa's theorem U_{∞,1}^+/C_{∞,1}^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorems 11.9, 12.23), states the Main Conjecture ch(𝒳_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorem 13.8, Mazur–Wiles) and proves it for Vandiver primes (Theorem 13.11); appendices treat Iwasawa's µ/λ/ν growth theorem with Ferrero–Washington and survey modular forms. The atlas was built from these notes: of 539 items, 71 are in Mathlib or Tau Ceti at the pinned commits (classical ζ and Dirichlet L-function facts, Gauss sums, Mahler's theorem, the Amice transform, Weierstrass division, cyclotomic fields, continuous cohomology and Kummer theory) and 458 are planned by atlas layers, chiefly PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras, DirichletPadicLFunctions, ColemanPowerSeries, IntegralIwasawaTheory L0–L4, EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture and SelmerIwasawaCohomology. Ten items are missing, all small: facts about duals and bounded measures, a procyclic-generator lemma, Λ(Γ)^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+) with its moment criterion (Lemmas 11.2–11.3), two remarks of §§6 and 8, the statement of Vandiver's conjecture, and Remark 2.3's p-adic BSD statements; each is routed as a source item to an existing layer of those roadmaps, and no new roadmap or Part II is needed. 103 mistakes are recorded, 24 of them in stated results: among these, the sign of Theorem 10.15 (Col(c(a)) = −θ_a·ζ_p), the twist ω^{1−k} missing from Theorem 6.7(ii), Corollary 2.8 at n = 0, Lemma 6.4 for characters of pure p-power conductor, the uniformiser in Theorem 13.1 and the p-parts in Conjecture A.15; the constructions of ζ_p, Iwasawa's theorem and the Vandiver case of the Main Conjecture hold as corrected.

items.name: Announced: Leopoldt's formula for the p-adic L-value at s = 1
items.statement: Standing notation of §§5.3–6 (p odd): ω is the Teichmüller character and ⟨x⟩ = ω(x)⁻¹x on ℤ_p^×; a Dirichlet character θ is written θ = χη with χ of conductor pⁿ (n ≥ 0) and η of conductor D prime to p, and L_p(θ,s) := ∫_{ℤ_p^×} χ(x)⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_η for s ∈ ℤ_p (Definition 5.18; ζ_η := ζ_p when D = 1, issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E35). Let θ be a nontrivial Dirichlet character of conductor N, ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity, G(θ⁻¹) the Gauss sum and log_p the Iwasawa logarithm on ℂ_p^× (log_p(p) = 0; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E44). Then L_p(θ,1) = −(1 − θ(p)p⁻¹)·G(θ⁻¹)⁻¹·Σ_{c∈(ℤ/Nℤ)^×} θ⁻¹(c)·log_p(1 − ε_N^c) (Leopoldt), the p-adic analogue of L(θ,1) = −G(θ⁻¹)⁻¹·Σ_c θ⁻¹(c)·log(1 − ε_N^c). §1.1 announces this as: the values [at s = 1] of the p-adic L-function of a nontrivial Dirichlet character are related to logarithms of cyclotomic units, an instance of the p-adic Beilinson conjectures.
items.locator: §1.1, third bullet of Part I (printed p. 104, PDF 5); proved as Theorem 6.1(ii) in §6 (printed p. 149, PDF 50)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3: 'Prove the complex logarithmic formula and Leopoldt's p-adic formula of Theorem 6.1, with primitive character, chosen Gauss sum and root of unity. Cover pure p-power conductor as well as nontrivial tame conductor.' The packet currently has only the complex side as nodes (DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/complex-lvalue-one-log, complex-lvalue-one-even-log, complex-lvalue-one-odd-bernoulli); ColemanIntegration:L3/recovers-leopoldt-formula ('k = 1 recovers Leopoldt's formula') plans the p-adic formula as the k = 1 case of Coleman's Theorem 6.7. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (no p-adic L-function at all: grep for Kubota, pseudomeasure, padicLFunction in both trees is empty). The exact normalisation of §6 has recorded leads in other chunks (DirichletPadicLFunctions/E15, E16; ColemanIntegration/E9, E15–E23); the chunk covering §6 must check them. The misprint in the §1.1 wording ('character 1') is issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E6.

items.name: Announced: residue of the p-adic zeta function at s = 1
items.statement: p odd. For i ∈ {1,…,p−1} let ζ_{p,i}(s) := ∫_{ℤ_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p (s ∈ ℤ_p, and s ≠ 1 when i = p−1; Definition 5.16 and issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E36). (i) If i ≠ p−1 then ζ_{p,i} is analytic at s = 1. (ii) ζ_{p,p−1} has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1 − p⁻¹. (§1.1: 'The (untwisted) p-adic zeta function has a simple pole at s = 1; in Section 7, we prove an analogous result describing its residue.')
items.locator: §1.1, third bullet of Part I (printed p. 104, PDF 5); proved as Theorem 7.1 in §7 (printed p. 154, PDF 55)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3: 'Prove Theorem 7.1: exactly the trivial weight-space component can have the indicated pole, and in the s-coordinate of RJW its residue is 1−p^−1.' No packet node yet realises Theorem 7.1 (rjw-node-index has no node citing Theorem 7.1). Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Announced: the p-adic family of Eisenstein series
items.statement: p prime, k ≥ 4 even, E_k(z) = ζ(1−k)/2 + Σ_{n≥1} σ_{k−1}(n)qⁿ and its p-stabilisation E_k^{(p)}(z) := E_k(z) − p^{k−1}E_k(pz) = (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k)/2 + Σ_{n≥1} σ^{(p)}_{k−1}(n)qⁿ with σ^{(p)}_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d} d^{k−1}. There is 𝐄 = Σ_{n≥0} A_n qⁿ ∈ Q(ℤ_p^×)[[q]] (Q = total ring of fractions of Λ(ℤ_p^×)) with A_0 = xζ_p/2 ∈ Q(ℤ_p^×) (the twist by x of the pseudomeasure ζ_p/2: x^{−1}A_0 is a pseudomeasure, A_0 itself is not; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E54) and A_n = Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d} δ_d ∈ Λ(ℤ_p^×) for n ≥ 1, such that for every even k ≥ 4, Σ_{n≥0}(∫_{ℤ_p^×} x^{k−1}·A_n)qⁿ = E_k^{(p)}(z).
items.locator: §1.1, fourth bullet of Part I (printed p. 104, PDF 5) and the Part I preface (printed p. 117, PDF 18); proved as Theorem 8.2 in §8 (printed p. 160, PDF 61)
items.note: Packet nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/positive-eisenstein-series ('The positive Eisenstein q-expansion measure'), L4/positive-eisenstein-measure, L4/p-stabilized-eisenstein, L4/p-stabilized-q-expansion, L4/positive-eisenstein-series-modular-comparison cite Theorem 8.2; stage L4: 'Construct the coefficient measures A_n=sum_(d|n,p∤d) delta_d for n>0 and the pseudo-measure A_0=x zeta_p/2. Prove coefficientwise specialization at x^(k−1) gives the p-stabilized form, exactly RJW Theorem 8.2.' The constant term needs Theorem 2.13 (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/58). Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4 and node L4/positive-eisenstein-measure repeat the word 'pseudo-measure' for A_0 (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E54).

items.name: Announced: the norm-compatible tower of cyclotomic units c(a)
items.statement: p odd; (ξ_{pⁿ})_{n≥1} a compatible system of primitive pⁿ-th roots of unity (ξ_{p^{n+1}}^p = ξ_{pⁿ}); K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{pⁿ}), 𝒰_n = 𝒪_{K_n}^×, 𝒰_∞ = lim← 𝒰_n along the norm maps N_{K_n/K_{n−1}}. For an integer a prime to p, c_n(a) := (ξ_{pⁿ}^a − 1)/(ξ_{pⁿ} − 1) ∈ 𝒰_n, and N_{K_n/K_{n−1}}(c_n(a)) = c_{n−1}(a), so c(a) := (c_n(a))_n ∈ 𝒰_∞ (Lemma 10.3). §1.1: 'As one considers the tower ℚ_p(μ_{pⁿ}) … the cyclotomic units fit together into a norm-compatible tower/system.'
items.locator: §1.1, first bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5); constructed in §10.2, Lemma 10.3 (printed p. 165, PDF 66)
items.note: Nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L2/cyclotomic-series-unit ('Cyclotomic unit series', §10.2 between Lemma 10.3 and Proposition 10.4) and EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/smoothed-unit-comparison (cites '§10.2, definition of c_n(a) and Lemma 10.3'). Tau Ceti has cyclotomic-field arithmetic (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic) but no norm-compatible tower of local units (grep for 'normCompatible', 'c_n(a)' found nothing relevant).

items.name: Announced: Coleman's interpolation theorem for norm-compatible units
items.statement: p odd, notation of PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/4, π_n := ξ_{pⁿ} − 1. There is a unique injective homomorphism of multiplicative groups 𝒰_∞ → ℤ_p[[T]]^×, u ↦ f_u, with f_u(π_n) = u_n for all u ∈ 𝒰_∞ and n ≥ 1 (Theorem 10.2); its image is the subgroup (ℤ_p[[T]]^×)^{𝒩 = id} fixed by Coleman's norm operator 𝒩 (Theorem 10.13).
items.locator: §1.1, first bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5: 'The Coleman map is a map that attaches a p-adic measure to any such tower of units'); proved in §10, Theorems 10.2 and 10.13 (printed pp. 164 and 169, PDF 65 and 70)
items.note: Nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L0/norm-compatible-units, L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-map, L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-closed-image cite Theorem 10.2; ColemanPowerSeries:L4 acceptance lists 'Theorems 10.2/10.13/10.15'. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Announced: the Coleman map Col
items.statement: p odd. Col : 𝒰_∞ → Λ(ℤ_p^×) is the composite u ↦ f_u ∈ (ℤ_p[[T]]^×)^{𝒩=id} (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/5), then ∂log with ∂ = (1+T)d/dT, then 1 − φ∘ψ (restriction of measures to ℤ_p^×), then ∂⁻¹ on ℤ_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} (multiplication by x⁻¹), then the inverse Mahler/Amice transform 𝒜⁻¹ (Definition 10.14).
items.locator: §1.1, first bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5); defined in §10.4, Definition 10.14 (printed p. 170, PDF 71)
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2 defines 'Col_0 = A^−1 ◦ ∂^−1 ◦ (1−phi psi) ◦ Delta ◦ Coleman' and records that with this definition Col_0(c(a)) = −([a]−1)ζ_p (sign issue ColemanPowerSeries/E1, belonging to the §10 chunk).

items.name: Announced: ζ_p^an = ζ_p^arith (Coleman map of cyclotomic units)
items.statement: p odd, a a topological generator of ℤ_p^×, θ_a := [a] − [1] ∈ Λ(ℤ_p^×). The arithmetic p-adic zeta function ζ_p^arith is the pseudomeasure obtained from Col(c(a)) (Appendix B.1: 'defining ζ_p^arith via the image under Col of the family of cyclotomic units'), and it equals the analytic one: ζ_p^an = ζ_p^arith. Corrected form with Definition 10.14 as printed: Col(c(a)) = −θ_a·ζ_p, i.e. ζ_p = −Col(c(a))/θ_a ∈ Q(ℤ_p^×) (printed Theorem 10.15: ζ_p = Col(c(a))/θ_a).
items.locator: §1.1, first bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5); proved as Theorem 10.15 (printed p. 170, PDF 71); ζ_p^arith named in Appendix B.1 (printed p. 208, PDF 109)
items.note: Sign checked here from the printed definitions: Proposition 10.4 gives ∂log f_{c(a)} = a − 1 − F_a, Lemma 10.5 gives Res_{ℤ_p^×}(μ_{∂log f_{c(a)}}) = −Res_{ℤ_p^×}(μ_a), so Col(c(a)) = x⁻¹Res(μ_{∂log f_{c(a)}}) = −x⁻¹Res(μ_a) = −θ_a ζ_p by Definition 4.10 (ζ_p := x⁻¹Res μ_a/θ_a). This is the lead ColemanPowerSeries/E1 (§10, not this chunk); stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'The source's Theorem 10.15 has the opposite sign from its preceding definitions'. The §1.1 statement ζ^an = ζ^arith is sign-agnostic because ζ^arith is only described informally there.

items.name: Announced: Iwasawa's theorem (local units modulo cyclotomic units)
items.statement: p odd; Γ^+ = Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^×/{±1}; 𝒰^+_{∞,1} = lim← (principal local units of ℚ_p(μ_{pⁿ})^+) along norms; 𝒞^+_{∞,1} the corresponding module of (closures of) cyclotomic units; I(Γ^+) the augmentation ideal of Λ(Γ^+). The Coleman map induces an isomorphism of Λ(Γ^+)-modules 𝒰^+_{∞,1}/𝒞^+_{∞,1} ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p (I(Γ^+)ζ_p is an ideal of Λ(Γ^+) because ζ_p is a pseudomeasure on Γ^+).
items.locator: §1.1, second bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5: 'Iwasawa's theorem describing the zeros of the p-adic zeta function via modules of cyclotomic units'); stated as Theorem 11.9 (printed p. 177, PDF 78), proved as Theorem 12.23(ii) (printed p. 188, PDF 89)
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4: 'Conclude Theorem 12.23, including U_infty,1^+ / C_infty,1^+ ≃ Z_p[[G^+]] / (I(G^+) zeta_p)'; acceptance lists Theorem 11.9. No node yet cites Theorems 11.9/12.23 in rjw-node-index.

items.name: Announced: the algebraic p-adic zeta function ζ_p^alg
items.statement: p odd; F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, ℳ_∞^+ the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞^+ unramified outside the unique prime above p, 𝒳_∞^+ := Gal(ℳ_∞^+/F_∞^+) with its Λ(Γ^+)-module structure by conjugation. ζ_p^alg := ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+) ⊂ Λ(Γ^+), the characteristic ideal of this finitely generated torsion module.
items.locator: §1.1, third bullet of Part II (printed p. 104, PDF 5: 'an ideal ζ_p^alg in the Iwasawa algebra … arises from the structure of a Galois module'); defined in §13.2–13.3 and Appendix B.1 (printed pp. 191 and 208, PDF 92 and 109); characteristic ideal Definition 13.3 (printed p. 190, PDF 91)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Define X for the p-ramified extension and Y for the everywhere-unramified extension, preserving RJW's notation. Define the completed Galois action by conjugation'. Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal (Definition 13.3). Torsionness of 𝒳_∞^+ is part of Theorem 13.8 (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/10).

items.name: Announced: the Iwasawa Main Conjecture for ζ
items.statement: p odd. 𝒳_∞^+ is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module and ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p, i.e. ζ_p^alg = I(Γ^+)ζ_p^an. (§1.1 says 'the ideal ζ_p^alg is generated by the analytic/arithmetic Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function'; since ζ_p is only a pseudomeasure, the ideal meant is I(Γ^+)ζ_p ⊂ Λ(Γ^+).)
items.locator: §1.1, paragraph after the Part II bullets (printed p. 105, PDF 6); stated as Theorem 13.8 (printed p. 192, PDF 93); formula ζ^alg = I(Γ^+)ζ^an in Appendix B.1 (printed p. 208, PDF 109)
items.note: Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture ('The Iwasawa main conjecture over ℚ for odd p (RJW Theorem 13.8; Rubin Theorem III.2.10)'); stage L3: 'Deduce finite generation and torsion of X^+ and char_(Z_p[[G^+]])(X_infty^+) = I(G^+) zeta_p for every odd prime p. This is the unconditional Theorem 13.8'. The notes themselves prove it only for Vandiver primes (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/11).

items.name: Announced: the Main Conjecture for Vandiver primes
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime with p ∤ h_1^+ := #Cl(ℚ(μ_p)^+) (a Vandiver prime; Definition 13.10). Then 𝒳_∞^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p as Λ(Γ^+)-modules; in particular the Iwasawa Main Conjecture (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/10) holds for p.
items.locator: §1.1, paragraph after the Part II bullets (printed p. 105, PDF 6: 'prove it in the special case where p is a Vandiver prime'); proved as Theorem 13.11 (printed p. 192, PDF 93)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Define Vandiver(p) by p not dividing the class number of Q(mu_p)^+ … Combine L1 with R04.L4 to prove the actual isomorphism X_infty^+ ≃ Z_p[[G^+]] / (I(G^+) zeta_p). Derive Theorem 13.8's ideal equality under Vandiver.' IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4 acceptance also lists 'Theorem 13.11 and its proof'.

items.name: Riemann zeta function
items.statement: For s ∈ ℂ with Re(s) > 1, ζ(s) := Σ_{n≥1} n^{−s}; the series converges absolutely there and defines a holomorphic function on {Re(s) > 1}.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:207 `zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < re s) : riemannZeta s = ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / (n : ℂ) ^ s` (Mathlib's 0^s convention is harmless: the n = 0 term is 0 for Re s > 1). Absolute convergence exactly on Re s > 1: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Dirichlet.lean:252 `LSeriesSummable_one_iff : LSeriesSummable 1 s ↔ 1 < s.re`. Mathlib defines riemannZeta on all of ℂ via Hurwitz zeta (see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/14).

items.name: Euler product for ζ
items.statement: For Re(s) > 1, ζ(s) = Π_p (1 − p^{−s})^{−1}, the product over all primes p (a consequence of unique factorisation).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/DirichletLSeries.lean:91 `riemannZeta_eulerProduct_hasProd (hs : 1 < s.re) : HasProd (fun p : Primes ↦ (1 - (p : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹) (riemannZeta s)`; :98 tprod form. Same statement.

items.name: Meromorphic continuation of ζ (simple pole at 1)
items.statement: ζ extends meromorphically to ℂ: it is holomorphic on ℂ ∖ {1} and has a simple pole at s = 1 (with residue 1, used in §7).
items.locator: §2.1, first bullet (printed p. 106, PDF 7); the residue 1 is recalled at the start of §7 (printed p. 154, PDF 55)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:139 `differentiableAt_riemannZeta {s : ℂ} (hs' : s ≠ 1) : DifferentiableAt ℂ riemannZeta s`; :242 `riemannZeta_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * riemannZeta s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 1)`. Together with PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/12 (agreement with the series on Re s > 1) this is the continuation statement.

items.name: Functional equation of ζ
items.statement: ζ satisfies a functional equation relating ζ(s) and ζ(1−s); explicitly, for s ∉ {1} ∪ {−n : n ∈ ℕ}, ζ(1−s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)cos(πs/2)ζ(s).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:178 `riemannZeta_one_sub {s : ℂ} (hs : ∀ n : ℕ, s ≠ -n) (hs' : s ≠ 1) : riemannZeta (1 - s) = 2 * (2 * π) ^ (-s) * Gamma s * cos (π * s / 2) * riemannZeta s`. The paper gives no explicit form; the explicit form is Mathlib's.

items.name: Dedekind zeta function ζ_F
items.statement: For a number field F, ζ_F(s) := Σ_{0≠I⊆𝒪_F} N(I)^{−s} (sum over nonzero ideals of 𝒪_F), for Re(s) > 1.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49 `def dedekindZeta (s : ℂ) := LSeries (fun n ↦ Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n}) s` — the same series regrouped by norm (LSeries is 0 off its convergence domain, so it is not the continuation).

items.name: Euler product and absolute convergence of ζ_F
items.statement: For a number field F, the series defining ζ_F converges absolutely exactly for Re(s) > 1, and there ζ_F(s) = Π_𝔭 (1 − N(𝔭)^{−s})^{−1}, the product over the nonzero prime ideals 𝔭 of 𝒪_F (printed text says 'prime ideals of K'; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E4).
items.note: Tau Ceti TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/EulerProduct/Analytic.lean:386 `dedekindZeta_eulerProduct_hasProd {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) : HasProd (fun P : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) ↦ (1 - (Ideal.absNorm P.asIdeal : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹) (NumberField.dedekindZeta K s)` (namespace TauCeti); TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Estimates.lean:493 `LSeriesSummable_dedekindZetaCoeff_iff : LSeriesSummable (fun n ↦ (dedekindZetaCoeff K n : ℂ)) s ↔ 1 < s.re`. Same statement.

items.name: Meromorphic continuation and functional equation of ζ_F
items.statement: For a number field F, ζ_F extends meromorphically to ℂ and satisfies a functional equation relating ζ_F(s) and ζ_F(1−s) (for the completed function with its archimedean Γ-factors and |D_F|^{s/2}).
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for completedDedekindZeta / Dedekind continuation / functional equation: nothing (Tau Ceti only has the Euler product and convergence, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/17). Planned: node AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation ('For a character ω of 𝔸^×/k^×, Λ(s, ω) continues to a meromorphic function on ℂ with Λ(s, ω) = ε(s, ω)Λ(1 − s, ω^{−1})'), specialised to trivial ω; AN.4 'Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula'; DirichletPadicLFunctions:KU-zeta 'Completed Dedekind zeta and special values'.

items.name: Dirichlet character and its L-function
items.statement: A Dirichlet character is a homomorphism χ : (ℤ/Nℤ)^× → ℂ^×, extended to χ : ℤ → ℂ by χ(m) := χ(m mod N) if (m,N) = 1 and χ(m) := 0 otherwise. For Re(s) > 1, L(χ,s) := Σ_{n≥1} χ(n)n^{−s} (convergent there); L(χ,s) denotes its continuation elsewhere (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/21).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:40 `abbrev DirichletCharacter (R) (n : ℕ) := MulChar (ZMod n) R` (MulChar vanishes on non-units, which is the zero extension); Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:61 `LFunction (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ) : ℂ`, :75 `LFunction_eq_LSeries (χ) {s} (hs : 1 < re s) : LFunction χ s = LSeries (χ ·) s`. Same object. Note the notes use L(χ,s) for χ given at its conductor in §2.4 (Theorems 2.15–2.16 require primitive χ).

items.name: Euler product for L(χ,s)
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ and Re(s) > 1, L(χ,s) = Π_p (1 − χ(p)p^{−s})^{−1}.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/EulerProduct/DirichletLSeries.lean:114 `DirichletCharacter.LSeries_eulerProduct_hasProd (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (hs : 1 < s.re) : HasProd (fun p : Primes ↦ (1 - χ p * (p : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹) (L ↗χ s)`. Same statement.

items.name: Continuation of Dirichlet L-functions
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ, L(χ,s) extends meromorphically to ℂ; it is entire if χ is nontrivial, and for χ trivial mod N it has only a simple pole at s = 1 (residue Π_{p|N}(1 − p^{−1})).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:92 `differentiableAt_LFunction (χ) (s) (hs : s ≠ 1 ∨ χ ≠ 1)`, :98 `differentiable_LFunction {χ} (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : Differentiable ℂ (LFunction χ)`, :182 `LFunctionTrivChar_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * LFunctionTrivChar N s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 <| ∏ p ∈ N.primeFactors, (1 - (p : ℂ)⁻¹))`. The residue value is Mathlib's refinement; the paper states only continuation and holomorphy for χ ≠ 1.

items.name: Functional equation of Dirichlet L-functions
items.statement: For a primitive Dirichlet character χ of conductor N, the completed L-function Λ(χ,s) (with Γ-factor Γ_ℝ(s) or Γ_ℝ(s+1) according to the parity of χ) satisfies Λ(χ,1−s) = N^{s−1/2}·w(χ)·Λ(χ⁻¹,s) with root number w(χ); this is the 'functional equation relating the values at s and 1−s'.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:284 `IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (s : ℂ) : completedLFunction χ (1 - s) = N ^ (s - 1 / 2) * rootNumber χ * completedLFunction χ⁻¹ s`. The paper's loose wording ('relating the values at s and 1−s') hides that the equation relates χ and χ⁻¹ and needs primitivity; Mathlib's statement is the precise one.

items.name: L-function of an elliptic curve over ℚ
items.statement: For E/ℚ an elliptic curve of conductor N: a_p(E) := p + 1 − #E(𝔽_p) for p ∤ N, the a_n(E) are determined recursively by the a_p(E), and L(E,s) := Σ_{n≥1} a_n(E)n^{−s} = Π_{p∤N}(1 − a_p(E)p^{−s} + p^{1−2s})^{−1}·Π_{p|N} L_p(s), with L_p(s) = 1, (1 − p^{−s})^{−1}, (1 + p^{−s})^{−1} according as E has additive, split multiplicative or nonsplit multiplicative reduction at p.
items.note: Only the coefficient a_p exists: Tau Ceti TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/PointCount.lean:97 `WeierstrassCurve.frobeniusTrace [Finite F] : ℤ` (q + 1 − #E(𝔽_q)). No L-series of an elliptic curve in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep of EllipticCurve/WeierstrassCurve files for LSeries/LFunction/eulerFactor: none). Planned: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0 'Build the interface from the Euler product/Dirichlet series of E to its modular entire continuation'.

items.name: Convergence, continuation and functional equation of L(E,s)
items.statement: For E/ℚ an elliptic curve, the series L(E,s) converges for Re(s) > 3/2, extends to an entire function of s, and satisfies a functional equation relating s and 2−s. (The continuation is known only via the modularity theorem, as §2.2.1 recalls.)
items.locator: §2.1, fourth bullet (printed p. 106, PDF 7); modularity remark in §2.2.1 (printed p. 108, PDF 9)
items.note: EllipticCurveModularity:R29.6: 'Transfer the analytic continuation and functional equation from ModularForms after proving equality of every local factor.' BSD.0: 'modular entire continuation and completed functional equation'. Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: L-function of a modular newform
items.statement: For a newform f = Σ_{n≥1} a_n(f)qⁿ ∈ S_k(Γ_0(N), ω_f) of weight k, level N and character ω_f: L(f,s) := Σ_{n≥1} a_n(f)n^{−s} = Π_{p∤N}(1 − a_p(f)p^{−s} + ω_f(p)p^{k−1−2s})^{−1}·Π_{p|N}(1 − a_p(f)p^{−s})^{−1}.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean:134 `ModularForm.L` (Λ·2/Γ_ℂ) and :157 `hasSum_L` give the Dirichlet series of any modular form of level an arithmetic subgroup; the Euler product for newforms is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep for lSeries_eulerProduct: none). ModularForms Layer 7 plans 'The Euler product for a newform … L(s,f) = ∏_p (1 − aₚ p^{-s} + χ(p) p^{k-1-2s})^{-1}'.

items.name: Convergence, continuation and functional equation of L(f,s)
items.statement: For a newform f of weight k and level N, L(f,s) converges for Re(s) > (k+1)/2, extends to an entire function, and satisfies a functional equation relating s and k−s.
items.note: Partial library: Mathlib LFunction.lean:190 `CuspForm.differentiable_L : Differentiable ℂ (L hk f)`; Tau Ceti TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/LFunction.lean:131 `CuspForm.hasEntireExtension_qExpansion_coeff (hk : 0 < k) … : LSeries.HasEntireExtension (fun n ↦ (qExpansion Γ.strictWidthInfty f).coeff n)` (entire continuation) and :108 abscissa ≤ k/2 + 1 (Hecke bound, weaker than the paper's (k+1)/2, which needs Deligne's bound). The functional equation for newforms (s ↔ k−s) is planned in ModularForms Layer 7 ('Hecke's functional equation … Λ_N(k − s, f) = i^k · Λ_N(s, g)').

items.name: L-function of a p-adic Galois representation
items.statement: Let 𝒢_ℚ = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), L/ℚ_p finite and V a finite-dimensional L-vector space with a continuous linear 𝒢_ℚ-action. L(V,s) := Π_ℓ L_ℓ(V,s) (formal Euler product), with L_ℓ(V,s) := det(Id − Frob_ℓ^{−1}ℓ^{−s} | V^{I_ℓ})^{−1} for ℓ ≠ p (Frob_ℓ arithmetic Frobenius, I_ℓ inertia at ℓ) and, corrected, L_p(V,s) := det(Id − φ·p^{−s} | D_cris(V))^{−1}, D_cris(V) = (B_cris ⊗_{ℚ_p} V|_{𝒢_{ℚ_p}})^{𝒢_{ℚ_p}} with crystalline Frobenius φ (printed: φ^{−1}; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E5).
items.note: No Galois-representation L-function in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1: 'Define completed motivic L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data in admitted cases' (covers the definition through Weil–Deligne data, which at p requires D_pst; partial for the crystalline formula). ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2 'Decomposition groups, inertia and Weil–Deligne representations' supplies Frob_ℓ, I_ℓ. The φ vs φ^{−1} normalisation is issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E5.

items.name: L(ℚ_p(χ), s) is the Dirichlet L-function
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ, viewed through class field theory as a character of 𝒢_ℚ, the 1-dimensional representation V = ℚ_p(χ) (coefficients enlarged to contain the values of χ) has L(V,s) equal to a Dirichlet L-function: L(χ,s), or L(χ⁻¹,s), according to the normalisation of the reciprocity map (arithmetic vs geometric Frobenius), which the text leaves implicit.
items.note: AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: 'Verify real/complex gamma factors, residue constants and ramified Euler factors against reciprocity/Frobenius conventions' (Hecke/Artin interfaces). With L_ℓ(V,s) = det(1 − Frob_ℓ^{−1}ℓ^{−s}) and the arithmetic normalisation χ(Frob_ℓ) = χ(ℓ), one gets Π(1 − χ(ℓ)^{−1}ℓ^{−s})^{−1} = L(χ⁻¹,s); with Deligne's geometric normalisation one gets L(χ,s). The paper's 'one recovers the Dirichlet L-functions' is true for the family, not character-by-character without fixing this. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Analytic class number formula (Theorem 2.2)
items.statement: Let F be a number field with r_1 real embeddings, r_2 pairs of complex embeddings, w roots of unity, discriminant D, regulator R and class number h_F. Then ζ_F has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue res_{s=1}ζ_F(s) = 2^{r_1}(2π)^{r_2}R·h_F/(w√|D|).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77 `tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ (s - 1) * dedekindZeta K s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (dedekindZeta_residue K))` with :56 `dedekindZeta_residue = 2^{nrRealPlaces}(2π)^{nrComplexPlaces}·regulator·classNumber/(torsionOrder·√|discr|)` — the same constant, but only as a one-sided real limit of the Dirichlet series; 'simple pole' needs the meromorphic continuation (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/18). Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: 'For RJW Theorem 2.2, identify the existing Dedekind-zeta Dirichlet series with its meromorphic germ at one. Prove that germ has a simple pole … and identify its residue with Mathlib's existing one-sided limit.' L4 acceptance: 'Theorem 2.2 combines Mathlib's class-number limit with L0's analytic comparison'.

items.name: Mordell–Weil theorem over ℚ
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ, the group E(ℚ) of rational points is a finitely generated abelian group.
items.note: Tau Ceti TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/FinitelyGenerated.lean:129 `theorem fg_point_of_numberField : AddGroup.FG W.Point` for `{F} [Field F] [NumberField F] {W : Affine F} [W.toAffine.IsElliptic]` (namespace WeierstrassCurve.Affine). General case (any number field); ℚ is a special case.

items.name: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture (conjecture)
items.statement: Conjecture. For an elliptic curve E/ℚ, ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = rank_ℤ E(ℚ), and the leading Taylor coefficient of L(E,s) at s = 1 is given by arithmetic invariants of E (the BSD formula).
items.note: Only as a proposition to be stated: PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.6 'Neither higher-rank BSD nor general Bloch–Kato follows from the rank-zero/one routes; the conjectural declarations must be separate'; RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.9 'Give separate public signatures for analytic-rank equality, finite Sha, a fixed-prime leading-term formula, and the full leading-term formula'. Tau Ceti EllipticCurves Layer 7 defines the arithmetic side (BSD quotient) as a stretch goal and keeps 'The conjecture … out'. Needs PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/23–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/24 to be meaningful.

items.name: Heegner points detect analytic rank one
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ (with a suitably chosen imaginary quadratic field satisfying the Heegner hypothesis), the Heegner point in E(ℚ) has infinite order if and only if ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1; hence ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1 ⇒ rank_ℤ E(ℚ) ≥ 1 (Gross–Zagier).
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.3: 'Given analytic rank one over ℚ, use BSD.2 to choose K with the classical/generalized Heegner conditions and L(E^K,1)≠0 … Apply GZ.8 … to obtain a non-torsion Heegner point in E(K)'. The paper's one-line 'iff' suppresses the choice of K and the trace to E(ℚ).

items.name: Rank from Selmer corank when Ш[p^∞] is finite
items.statement: For E/ℚ with Tate–Shafarevich group Ш(E/ℚ) (a torsion group, conjecturally finite): if Ш(E/ℚ)[p^∞] is finite then rank_ℤ E(ℚ) = corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/ℚ) (the ℤ_p-rank of the Pontryagin dual of the p^∞-Selmer group; the text says 'p-Selmer group').
items.note: Tau Ceti has only 2-descent Selmer machinery for Mordell–Weil (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/MordellWeil/SelmerGroup.lean: finite-level μ-map, `pow_rank_le_card_of_range_μ_le`); no Ш and no p^∞-Selmer group. EllipticCurves Layer 7 plans the m-descent sequence 0 → E(K)/mE(K) → Sel_m(E/K) → Ш(E/K)[m] → 0 and Ш; the p^∞-corank statement is the direct-limit consequence (partial coverage).

items.name: BSD in analytic rank ≤ 1 (Gross–Zagier, Kolyvagin, Murty–Murty)
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ with ord_{s=1}L(E,s) ≤ 1 (under the assumptions of the cited works): rank_ℤ E(ℚ) = ord_{s=1}L(E,s) and Ш(E/ℚ) is finite.
items.note: BSD.3 'Analytic rank one implies rank one and finite Sha'; BSD.4 'Analytic rank zero implies rank zero and finite Sha'. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Iwasawa Main Conjecture for elliptic curves (Kato, Skinner–Urban)
items.statement: For E/ℚ and p a prime of good ordinary reduction, under the hypotheses of Skinner–Urban (building on Kato's divisibility), the p-adic Iwasawa main conjecture for E holds: the characteristic ideal of the dual cyclotomic Selmer group equals the ideal generated by the p-adic L-function of E. (Stated in the text only informally: 'the IMC for elliptic curves has been proved much more widely by Skinner–Urban'.)
items.note: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L3 (T3): 'for an elliptic curve E/Q, p>3 a prime of good ordinary reduction, and E[p] irreducible, the ordinary Selmer dual is torsion and the cyclotomic main-conjecture equality holds over Lambda[1/p]'. The paper states no precise hypotheses; the RJW Appendix B chunk states the modular-form version.

items.name: p-adic BSD conjecture (Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum) (conjecture)
items.statement: Conjecture. For E/ℚ and a prime p, the order of vanishing at s = 1 of the p-adic L-function of E equals rank_ℤ E(ℚ) (plus one in the split multiplicative 'trivial zero' case), and its leading coefficient is given by arithmetic data as in BSD with the complex regulator replaced by a p-adic regulator (and an ℒ-invariant factor in the trivial-zero case).
items.note: Searched atlas stage titles/descriptions for 'Mazur–Tate–Teitelbaum', 'MTT', 'p-adic BSD', 'p-adic Birch': no stage plans it. Nearest: GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9 (split ordinary p-adic logarithm formula and exceptional-zero formula as consumers), ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions stages (the p-adic L-function itself). Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti. Routed (source) to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5, with its p-adic height input.

items.name: Trivial zeros in analytic rank 0; p-adic IMC ⇒ p-adic BSD
items.statement: (i) For E/ℚ of analytic rank 0, the p-adic L-function of E vanishes at s = 1 to order 0 or 1; the possible extra ('trivial') zero occurs exactly when E has split multiplicative reduction at p and is governed by local data at p (Greenberg–Stevens); if Ш(E/ℚ) is finite, the p-adic and classical BSD conjectures are then equivalent. (ii) If the p-adic height pairing is nondegenerate, the p-adic IMC for E implies the p-adic BSD conjecture (Schneider).
items.locator: §2.2.3, Remark 2.3, second and third paragraphs (printed p. 110, PDF 11)
items.note: Searched stages for 'trivial zero', 'exceptional zero', 'L-invariant', 'Schneider', 'height pairing': only GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9 ('A multiplicative exceptional-zero formula is a separate construction with its Tate-period/L-invariant term') and AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.5 ('never cancel an exceptional zero') touch it; neither plans these statements. Motivational only; not used later in the notes. Routed (source) to ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5.

items.name: The Iwasawa Main Conjecture for ζ is known for every prime
items.statement: The Iwasawa Main Conjecture for the p-adic Riemann zeta function holds for every prime p: for p odd by Mazur–Wiles [61], for p = 2 by Wiles [83]. (For p odd its precise form is PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/10.)
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3 plans the unconditional odd-p Theorem 13.8 (via Euler systems, not Mazur–Wiles' route); L4 'Abelian fields and p=2 … Greither's abelian/p=2 theorem … include the case p=2 integrally'. The planned routes differ from the cited proofs; the statements agree for p odd, and for p = 2 the formulation must be Greither's (no ± splitting over ℤ_2).

items.name: Gamma function
items.statement: Γ(s) := ∫_0^∞ e^{−t}t^{s−1}dt for Re(s) > 0 (equation (2-1)), extended meromorphically to ℂ.
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:110 `Complex.GammaIntegral (s) := ∫ x in Ioi 0, ↑(-x).exp * ↑x ^ (s - 1)`, :319 `Complex.Gamma_eq_integral {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re) : Gamma s = GammaIntegral s`. Same.

items.name: Γ(s) = (s−1)Γ(s−1)
items.statement: For s ∈ ℂ with s − 1 ∉ {0, −1, −2, …}: Γ(s) = (s−1)Γ(s−1) (used in the proof of Theorem 2.4).
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:312 `Complex.Gamma_add_one (s : ℂ) (h2 : s ≠ 0) : Gamma (s + 1) = s * Gamma s` (holds for every s ≠ 0 with Mathlib's totalised Γ).

items.name: Normalised Mellin transform L(f,s)
items.statement: For f : ℝ_{≥0} → ℝ rapidly decreasing and smooth (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/42), L(f,s) := Γ(s)^{−1}∫_0^∞ f(t)t^{s−1}dt, s ∈ ℂ, Re(s) > 0; 'the Mellin transform of f'.
items.note: Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:91 `mellin (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) : E := ∫ t : ℝ in Ioi 0, (t : ℂ) ^ (s - 1) • f t` is the unnormalised transform; the Γ-normalised continued function is node DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/normalized-mellin-continuation ('The continued normalized Mellin transform'). So: library for M(f,s), planned for L(f,s) on all of ℂ.

items.name: Mellin continuation and values at non-positive integers (Theorem 2.4)
items.statement: Let f : ℝ_{≥0} → ℝ be C^∞ and rapidly decreasing (f and all derivatives f′, f″, … decay exponentially at infinity). Then L(f,s) = Γ(s)^{−1}∫_0^∞ f(t)t^{s−1}dt converges to a holomorphic function on Re(s) > 0, has an analytic continuation to all of ℂ, and L(f,−n) = (−1)^n f^{(n)}(0) for every integer n ≥ 0. (Proof: L(f,s) = −L(f′,s+1) by integration by parts — valid already for Re(s) > 0, the text says Re(s) > 1 — iterated.)
items.note: Nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/normalized-mellin-entire ('Under the common hypotheses, L_f is differentiable over ℂ at every point of ℂ') and L0/normalized-mellin-negative-values ('for every n≥0, L_f(−n)=(−1)^n D_n f(0)'), with hypotheses f smooth within [0,∞) and D_n f = O(exp(−a_n t)); the derivative shift is node L0/normalized-mellin-derivative-shift. Same statement (the node allows complex-valued f: a generalisation). Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (Tau Ceti uses `mellin` only in UpperHalfPlane/ResToImagAxis.lean). The review adds: holomorphy on Re s > 0 is Mathlib mellin_differentiableAt_of_isBigO_rpow_exp (Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:422); the continuation is not.

items.name: Bernoulli numbers
items.statement: The Bernoulli numbers B_n are defined by t/(e^t − 1) = Σ_{n≥0} B_n tⁿ/n! (so B_1 = −1/2).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean:195 `bernoulli (n : ℕ) : ℚ` (convention B_1 = −1/2, :205 `bernoulli_one : bernoulli 1 = -1 / 2`), :266 `bernoulliPowerSeries := mk fun n => algebraMap ℚ A (bernoulli n / n !)`, :269 `bernoulliPowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one : bernoulliPowerSeries A * (exp A - 1) = X` — the formal version of the generating function. The analytic identity on ℝ (smooth kernel) is node DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smooth-bernoulli-derivatives. Beware Mathlib's `bernoulli'` has B′_1 = +1/2.

items.name: Rationality, first values and odd vanishing of Bernoulli numbers (Remark 2.5)
items.statement: B_n ∈ ℚ for all n; B_0 = 1, B_1 = −1/2, B_2 = 1/6, B_3 = 0, B_4 = −1/30; B_k = 0 for every odd k ≥ 3.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean: `bernoulli` is ℚ-valued by definition; :202 bernoulli_zero, :205 bernoulli_one (−1/2), :208 bernoulli_two (6⁻¹), :128 bernoulli'_three (0), :133 bernoulli'_four (−1/30), transferred by :215 `bernoulli_eq_bernoulli'_of_ne_one`; :212 `bernoulli_eq_zero_of_odd {n} (h_odd : Odd n) (hlt : 1 < n) : bernoulli n = 0`.

items.name: Exponential decay of t/(e^t−1) and its derivatives (Lemma 2.6)
items.statement: The function f(t) = t/(e^t − 1) (extended by f(0) = 1) and all of its derivatives decay exponentially as t → ∞; explicitly, with F(t) = Σ_{m≥1} e^{−mt}, f^{(n)}(t) = nF^{(n−1)}(t) + tF^{(n)}(t) ∼ (−1)^n t e^{−t}.
items.note: Nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/bernoulli-ordinary-derivative-decay ('For every m≥0, the mth ordinary real iterated derivative of b(t)=t/(exp(t)−1) is O(exp(−t/2)) as t→+∞') and L0/bernoulli-within-derivative-decay; smoothness at 0 is L0/smooth-bernoulli-smooth. Same content.

items.name: (s−1)ζ(s) = L(f, s−1) (Lemma 2.7)
items.statement: With f(t) = t/(e^t − 1): (s−1)ζ(s) = L(f, s−1) for all s ∈ ℂ (first for Re(s) large via n^{−s} = Γ(s)^{−1}∫_0^∞ e^{−nt}t^{s−1}dt and 1/(e^t−1) = Σ_{n≥1}e^{−nt}, then by continuation; at s = 1 both sides equal 1).
items.note: Nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/bernoulli-mellin-gamma-zeta ('For Re(s)>0, mellin(g,s)=Γ(s+1)ζ(s+1)') and L0/bernoulli-mellin-zeta-comparison ('For every s∈ℂ with s≠0, L(s)=sζ(s+1). At the removable point … L(0)=1'), i.e. the lemma with s ↦ s+1. Same statement.

items.name: Values of ζ at non-positive integers (Corollary 2.8, corrected)
items.statement: For every integer n ≥ 0, ζ(−n) = (−1)^n B_{n+1}/(n+1) (with B_1 = −1/2); equivalently ζ(0) = −1/2 and ζ(−n) = −B_{n+1}/(n+1) for n ≥ 1. In particular ζ(−n) ∈ ℚ for n ≥ 0, and ζ(−n) = 0 for even n ≥ 2. (Printed: ζ(−n) = −B_{n+1}/(n+1) for all n ≥ 0, false at n = 0; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E2.)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/HurwitzZetaValues.lean:251 `riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli (k : ℕ) : riemannZeta (-k) = (-1 : ℂ) ^ k * bernoulli (k + 1) / (k + 1)` (the corrected formula); :240 `riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli'` gives −B′_{k+1}/(k+1), i.e. the printed formula is right only for the B′_1 = +1/2 convention; RiemannZeta.lean:151 `riemannZeta_zero : riemannZeta 0 = -1 / 2`, :173 `riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one (n) : riemannZeta (-2 * (n + 1)) = 0`. Rationality is immediate from `bernoulli : ℕ → ℚ`. Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: 'State the zeta special-value formula with the correct n=0 convention.' The paper derives it from Theorem 2.4 + Lemma 2.7 (planned L0 nodes L0/bernoulli-mellin-values).

items.name: No single p-adic analytic ζ_p on ℤ_p; p−1 branches
items.statement: p odd. There is no single p-adic analytic function on ℤ_p interpolating (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for all k ≥ 1; instead, for each i ∈ {1,…,p−1} the branch ζ_{p,i}(s) := ∫_{ℤ_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p (s ∈ ℤ_p) is p-adic analytic (meromorphic for i = p−1) and ζ_{p,i}(1−k) = (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for all k ≥ 1 with k ≡ i (mod p−1). (Footnote 6 omits the Euler factor (1−p^{k−1}) that Theorem 5.17 carries.)
items.locator: §2.4.2, footnote 6 (printed p. 113, PDF 14) and the paragraph after Remark 2.14 (printed p. 116, PDF 17); Part I preface (printed p. 117, PDF 18); proved in §5.3, Definition 5.16 and Theorem 5.17 (printed p. 147, PDF 48)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3: 'Use Teichmuller decomposition to define the branches and prove Theorems 5.17/5.20.' No node yet (L2 parity nodes tame-character-value-parity etc. cite Theorem 5.17 only for vanishing of odd branches). The 'no single function' claim is explained in §5.3 (x ↦ x^s is not defined on all of ℤ_p^× since exp does not converge on ℤ_p) rather than proved as a theorem; footnote 6 says 'interpolates only the values ζ(1−k)', omitting the Euler factor — a harmless informality, not recorded as an issue.

items.name: Dirichlet characters as continuous characters of Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× (Proposition 2.9(i), corrected)
items.statement: Composition with the projection Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× → (ℤ/Nℤ)^× (product over all primes ℓ, product of the ℓ-adic topologies; Chinese remainder theorem) identifies primitive Dirichlet characters χ (equivalently, Dirichlet characters up to induction to higher modulus) with continuous homomorphisms Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× → ℂ^×; every continuous character factors through some (ℤ/Nℤ)^×, being trivial on U_N = {x ≡ 1 mod N} because {z : |z−1| < 1} contains no nontrivial subgroup of ℂ^×. (Printed: 'an identification between Dirichlet characters χ and continuous characters'; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E7.)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: 'Supply the elementary idele-character identifications in RJW Propositions 2.9/2.11 using the shared idele-class group'; the L0 packet coverage lists this as remaining ('instantiate GlobalNumberFields Layers 9–10 idele/infinity-type conventions') with no node yet. GlobalNumberFields Layer 9: 'Over ℚ, prove the conductor- and parity-compatible dictionary with Dirichlet characters'. Mathlib has conductor/primitive characters (DirichletCharacter.conductor, IsPrimitive, primitiveCharacter) but no profinite dictionary; Tau Ceti TauCeti/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean has only factorsThrough lemmas. Searched both trees for ZHat/ProfiniteInteger/Ẑ: none.

items.name: Continuous characters of ℝ_{>0} (Proposition 2.9(ii))
items.statement: s ↦ (x ↦ x^s) is a bijection ℂ ≅ Hom_cts(ℝ_{>0}, ℂ^×). (Proof: via log, a continuous homomorphism ℝ → ℂ^× lifts through exp : ℂ → ℂ^× — the lifting step is implicit in the text's 'after taking a logarithm' — to a continuous additive g : ℝ → ℂ, and then g(x) = x·g(1).)
items.note: Not stated anywhere. General forms: Tau Ceti TauCeti/Geometry/Lie/Exponential/Classification.lean:278 `existsUnique_eq_mulInvariantOneParameterSubgroup … (φ : ContinuousMonoidHom (Multiplicative ℝ) G) : ∃! v : GroupLieAlgebra I G, φ = mulInvariantOneParameterSubgroup v` for a finite-dimensional Lie group G (applies to G = ℂ^× after identifying its one-parameter subgroups with t ↦ exp(ts)); Mathlib/Topology/Instances/RealVectorSpace.lean:26 `map_real_smul` (continuous additive maps are ℝ-linear, the last step). GlobalNumberFields Layer 10: 'Classify continuous characters of ℝˣ as |x|^s sgn(x)^ε, with s : ℂ'.

items.name: Characters of ℝ_{>0} × Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× (Proposition 2.9, consequence)
items.statement: Every continuous character of ℝ_{>0} × Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× (product topology) is κ_{χ,s}(x,y) = x^s·χ(y) for a unique pair (χ,s) with χ a primitive Dirichlet character and s ∈ ℂ.
items.note: Follows from PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/49 and PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/50 (a character of a product is the product of its restrictions). Planned as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/49–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/50. Uniqueness of χ needs 'primitive' (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E7).

items.name: Ideles of ℚ (Definition 2.10)
items.statement: 𝔸^× = 𝔸_ℚ^× := ℝ^× × Π′_ℓ ℚ_ℓ^× = {(x_ℝ, x_2, x_3, x_5, …) : x_ℓ ∈ ℤ_ℓ^× for all but finitely many ℓ}, a topological group (printed: 'ring'; PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E1) with the restricted product topology (basis U × Π_ℓ U_ℓ, U ⊆ ℝ^× and U_ℓ ⊆ ℚ_ℓ^× open, U_ℓ = ℤ_ℓ^× for almost all ℓ); ℚ^× embeds diagonally.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/AdeleRing.lean:93 `abbrev IdeleGroup := 𝔸[R, K]ˣ` (units of AdeleRing R K = InfiniteAdeleRing K × FiniteAdeleRing R K; use R = ℤ, K = ℚ), :99 `unitEmbedding : Kˣ →* IdeleGroup R K`, :113 principalSubgroup. The topology is Mathlib's units topology (Topology/Algebra/Constructions.lean:101, induced by x ↦ (x, x⁻¹)); that it equals the restricted-product topology of Definition 2.10 is not stated in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (standard, true). GlobalNumberFields Layer 6: 'Define IdeleGroup K as the units of the full adele ring … retaining Mathlib's units topology'. Same object, carrier-level library; the topology comparison is a gap to note.

items.name: Idele class group of ℚ (Remark 2.12)
items.statement: The idele class group of ℚ is ℚ^×\𝔸^× (quotient by the diagonal ℚ^×), with the quotient topology.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/AdeleRing.lean:119 `abbrev IdeleClassGroup := IdeleGroup R K ⧸ IdeleGroup.principalSubgroup R K`. Same object.

items.name: Strong approximation for ℚ^×\𝔸^× (Proposition 2.11)
items.statement: The inclusion ℝ_{>0} × Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× ↪ 𝔸^× induces a topological isomorphism ℝ_{>0} × Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× ≅ ℚ^×\𝔸^×. Hence every continuous character ℚ^×\𝔸^× → ℂ^× is κ_{χ,s} for a (primitive) Dirichlet character χ and s ∈ ℂ.
items.locator: §2.4.2, Proposition 2.11 (printed p. 114, PDF 15); proof cited to Goldfeld–Hundley [34, Proposition I.4.6]
items.note: Searched Mathlib (AdeleRing.lean, FiniteAdeleRing, InfiniteAdeleRing) and Tau Ceti (no idele files at all) for this isomorphism: none. Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 plans 'the elementary idele-character identifications in RJW Propositions 2.9/2.11 using the shared idele-class group'; GlobalNumberFields Layer 6 plans the idele class group, its norm and compactness of the norm-one part, but not this ℚ-specific decomposition (partial).

items.name: All Dirichlet L-functions as one function on idele class characters ((2-3))
items.statement: L : Hom_cts(ℚ^×\𝔸^×, ℂ^×) → ℂ, κ_{χ,s} ↦ L(χ,s) (defined away from the pole of L(1,s) at s = 1); for χ trivial this restricts to ζ viewed on Hom_cts(ℝ_{>0}, ℂ^×), [x ↦ x^s] ↦ ζ(s). In Tate's framework L(χ,s) arises by integrating the idele class character against Haar measure (Tate's global zeta integral with a Schwartz–Bruhat function).
items.locator: §2.4.2, display (2-3) and the paragraph after Remark 2.12 (printed p. 115, PDF 16)
items.note: Node AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/completed-hecke-l-function ('For a character ω of 𝔸^×/k^×, Λ(s, ω) = ∏_v L_v(s, ω_v)') and AL.1/global-zeta-integral; GlobalNumberFields Layer 9 defines HeckeCharacter K := ContinuousMonoidHom (IdeleClassGroup K) ℂˣ. Normalisation caveat (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E9): with the identification of Proposition 2.9, Tate's integral of κ_{χ,s} has unramified factors (1 − χ̄(ℓ)ℓ^{−s})^{−1}, i.e. gives L(χ⁻¹,s), not L(χ,s).

items.name: Tate's thesis: continuation and functional equation via harmonic analysis
items.statement: For every continuous character ω of ℚ^×\𝔸^× (more generally of a number field), the completed L-function Λ(s,ω) = Π_v L_v(s,ω_v) (including the archimedean Γ-factor, 'the Euler factor at the archimedean place') continues meromorphically to ℂ and satisfies Λ(s,ω) = ε(s,ω)Λ(1−s,ω⁻¹); in particular Dirichlet L-functions (and ζ) have analytic continuation and functional equation, proved by Poisson summation on 𝔸/ℚ.
items.locator: §2.4.2, paragraph after (2-3) (printed p. 115, PDF 16); citing Tate [78] and Iwasawa [43]
items.note: Nodes AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/tate-global-functional-equation ('Tate's global functional equation (Main Theorem 4.4.1…)') and AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation ('Λ(s, ω) continues to a meromorphic function on ℂ with Λ(s, ω) = ε(s, ω)Λ(1 − s, ω^{−1})'). For Dirichlet L-functions the conclusion is already in Mathlib by a different route (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/21, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/22); the Tate-thesis proof is not.

items.name: Continuous ℂ_p-valued characters of the idele class group
items.statement: Every continuous character κ : ℚ^×\𝔸^× → ℂ_p^× (= a continuous character of ℝ_{>0} × Π_ℓ ℤ_ℓ^× by PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/54) is trivial on ℝ_{>0} (ℝ_{>0} connected, ℂ_p totally disconnected), and its restriction to Π_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ^× has finite image, i.e. is a Dirichlet character of conductor prime to p. Hence Hom_cts(ℚ^×\𝔸^×, ℂ_p^×) ≅ Hom_cts(ℤ_p^×, ℂ_p^×) × (Π_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ^×)^∧ with (Π_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ^×)^∧ = lim→_{(D,p)=1} ((ℤ/Dℤ)^×)^∧ (the identification used in Remark 2.17).
items.locator: §2.4.3, first paragraph (printed p. 115, PDF 16) and Remark 2.17 (printed pp. 116–117, PDF 17–18)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: 'Supply the elementary idele-character identifications in RJW Propositions 2.9/2.11 using the shared idele-class group, including the archimedean connectedness argument.' No node yet. The text gives the finiteness on Π_{ℓ≠p}ℤ_ℓ^× only as 'using topological arguments'; checked here: by continuity some open U_N = {x ≡ 1 mod N} (p ∤ N) maps into 1 + p²𝒪_{ℂ_p} (resp. 1 + 8𝒪 for p = 2), whose compact subgroups are, via log, torsion-free pro-p groups; each factor of U_N (ℤ_ℓ^× for ℓ ∤ N, 1 + ℓⁿℤ_ℓ for ℓ | N) is finite × pro-ℓ with ℓ ≠ p, hence maps trivially; the subgroup generated by the factors is dense in U_N, so the character is trivial on U_N and has finite image. True.

items.name: Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic zeta function (Theorem 2.13)
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime (standing assumption from §2.2.4: 'We will (for odd p) construct …'). A pseudomeasure on ℤ_p^× is an element λ of the total ring of fractions Q(ℤ_p^×) of Λ(ℤ_p^×) with ([g]−[1])λ ∈ Λ(ℤ_p^×) for all g ∈ ℤ_p^×, integrated against a nontrivial continuous character κ by ∫κ·λ := (κ(g)−1)^{−1}∫κ·([g]−[1])λ for any g with κ(g) ≠ 1 (§3.6). There is a unique pseudomeasure ζ_p = ζ_p^an on ℤ_p^× such that ∫_{ℤ_p^×} x^k·ζ_p (=: ζ_p(x ↦ x^k)) = (1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for every integer k > 0 (the right side lies in ℚ ⊂ ℚ_p by PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/47; at k = 1 both sides are 0 since 1 − p⁰ = 0, although ζ(0) = −1/2).
items.locator: §2.4.3, Theorem 2.13 (printed p. 116, PDF 17); announced in §1.1 (printed p. 104, PDF 5); proved as Theorem 4.1 in §4 (printed p. 136, PDF 37; construction Definition 4.10 and Proposition 4.11, printed pp. 138–139, PDF 39–40)
items.note: Nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure (construction 'ζ_p as mk′(λ_a,θ_a)'), L1/arithmetic-euler-zeta-comparison ('For k>0, the complex image of r_(p,k) equals (1−p^(k−1))riemannZeta(1−k)'), L1/arithmetic-positive-interpolation, L1/arithmetic-interpolation-unique ('If z∈PM satisfies M_k(z)=−(1−p^(k−1))alg(B_k/k) for all k>0, then z=ζ_p'). The packet treats every prime including p = 2 (a generalisation; §4 chooses a topological generator of ℤ_p^×, which exists only for p odd). Stage L1: 'At k=1 the Euler factor is zero; keep this case in the proof rather than claiming zeta(0)=0.' Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (no pseudomeasures; grep for pseudoMeasure/Kubota: none).

items.name: Interpolation of p-power-conductor Dirichlet L-values by ζ_p (Theorem 2.15)
items.statement: p odd. Let χ be a Dirichlet character of conductor pⁿ, n ≥ 0 (primitive mod pⁿ), viewed as the locally constant character of ℤ_p^× factoring through ℤ_p^×/(1+pⁿℤ_p) = (ℤ/pⁿℤ)^×; its values are compared in ℂ and ℂ_p through fixed embeddings of ℚ̄. Then for all k > 0: ∫_{ℤ_p^×} χ(x)x^k·ζ_p = (1 − χ(p)p^{k−1})L(χ,1−k). For n ≥ 1, χ(p) = 0 and this reads ∫χ(x)x^k·ζ_p = L(χ,1−k) (Theorem 5.1); for n = 0 it is Theorem 2.13.
items.locator: §2.4.3, Theorem 2.15 and footnote 8 (printed p. 116, PDF 17); announced in §1.1 (printed p. 104, PDF 5) and the Part I preface (printed p. 117, PDF 18); proved as Theorem 5.1 in §5.1 (printed p. 139, PDF 40)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2: 'Construct the twist by a p-power conductor character and prove the roots-of-unity restriction formula and Gauss-sum computation … This covers RJW Theorems 5.1 and 5.7'. Nodes so far: L2/prime-power-character, L2/twisted-smoothed-measure, L2/twisted-smoothed-gauss-amice (cite Theorem 5.1); the final interpolation node is still listed as remaining in the packet coverage ('derive the pure p-power interpolation formula'). Partial node coverage; stage coverage explicit.

items.name: Tame-conductor measures ζ_η (Theorem 2.16)
items.statement: p odd. Let D > 1 be an integer coprime to p and η a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor D, with values in a finite extension L/ℚ_p via a fixed embedding. There is a unique measure ζ_η on ℤ_p^× (ζ_η ∈ Λ(ℤ_p^×) = 𝒪_L[[ℤ_p^×]], Theorem 5.7) such that for every primitive Dirichlet character χ of conductor pⁿ (n ≥ 0) and every k > 0: ∫_{ℤ_p^×} χ(x)x^k·ζ_η = (1 − (χη)(p)p^{k−1})L(χη, 1−k), where (χη)(p) = 0 if n ≥ 1 and = η(p) if n = 0.
items.locator: §2.4.3, Theorem 2.16 (printed p. 116, PDF 17); announced in §1.1 (printed p. 104, PDF 5); proved as Theorem 5.7 in §5.2 (printed p. 143, PDF 44)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2: 'For primitive eta of conductor D>1 coprime to p, construct the integral measure zeta_eta and prove, for primitive chi of p-power conductor and k≥1, integral chi(x)x^k dzeta_eta = (1−(chi eta)(p)p^(k−1)) L(chi eta,1−k).' Nodes L2/tame-measure, L2/tame-zeta-measure, L2/tame-integral-zeta-measure, L2/twisted-tame-moments, L2/tame-ordinary-moments realise the construction and moments (L2/tame-measure cites Theorem 5.7). Same statement.

items.name: Tame measures assemble to a pseudomeasure on the idele class group (Remark 2.17)
items.statement: Writing ((ℤ/Dℤ)^×)^∧ for the character group, the family (ζ_η) — completed by ζ_p for the trivial tame character, and assigning to an imprimitive η the object of its primitive character — defines a function on Hom_cts(ℤ_p^×, ℂ_p^×) × ((ℤ/Dℤ)^×)^∧ compatible with the maps ((ℤ/Eℤ)^×)^∧ → ((ℤ/Dℤ)^×)^∧ for E | D, hence on Hom_cts(ℤ_p^×, ℂ_p^×) × lim→_{(D,p)=1}((ℤ/Dℤ)^×)^∧ = Hom_cts(ℚ^×\𝔸^×, ℂ_p^×) (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/57): a p-adic pseudomeasure (measure away from the trivial tame component) on the idele class group of ℚ. (Printed: 'they give a measure on the idele class group'; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E8.)
items.note: No packet node cites Remark 2.17. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0 constructs 'the inverse limit of ray class groups with p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus … Define distributions on the actual ray-class quotient'; L3 'For a totally real field F construct the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure … Specialization F=Q agrees with R03' — the general form (partial coverage for ℚ). Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: x^k ≡ x^ℓ mod p^m on ℤ_p^×
items.statement: If k ≡ ℓ (mod p^{m−1}(p−1)) (m ≥ 1), then x^k ≡ x^ℓ (mod p^m) for every x ∈ ℤ_p^×.
items.note: Mathlib/FieldTheory/Finite/Basic.lean:556 `ZMod.pow_totient {n : ℕ} (x : (ZMod n)ˣ) : x ^ φ n = 1` and Mathlib/Data/Nat/Totient.lean:211 `Nat.totient_prime_pow (hp : p.Prime) (hn : 0 < n) : φ (p ^ n) = p ^ (n - 1) * (p - 1)` give it after reducing x mod p^m (a one-line corollary, not stated verbatim).

items.name: Generalised Kummer congruences (Remark 2.18, corrected)
items.statement: Let p be odd, m ≥ 1 and k, ℓ ≥ 1 with k ≡ ℓ (mod p^{m−1}(p−1)). (a) For η a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor D > 1 prime to p (values in 𝒪_L): (1 − η(p)p^{k−1})L(η,1−k) ≡ (1 − η(p)p^{ℓ−1})L(η,1−ℓ) (mod p^m𝒪_L) (from the integral measure ζ_η, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/60). (b) For the Riemann zeta function the congruence (1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) ≡ (1 − p^{ℓ−1})ζ(1−ℓ) (mod p^m) holds in ℤ_(p) when (p−1) ∤ k (Kummer); in general only the smoothed form holds: for any integer a prime to p, (1 − a^k)(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) ≡ (1 − a^ℓ)(1 − p^{ℓ−1})ζ(1−ℓ) (mod p^m). (Printed: the congruence for every η of conductor prime to p, the trivial character included; false for η = 1 when (p−1) | k, see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E3.)
items.note: Nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/weight-period-smoothed-kummer ('If r≥1, k,l≥1 and k≡l modulo p^(r−1)(p−1), then ‖C_a(k)−C_a(l)‖≤p^(−r)', C_a(k)=(1−p^(k−1))(1−a^k)B_k/k), L1/unit-denominator-kummer ('if both 1−a^k and 1−a^l are units in Z, then ‖V(k)−V(l)‖≤p^(−r)', giving (b) with a a primitive root mod p) and L1/generalized-smoothed-kummer; part (a) is L2/tame-character-kummer ('Finite character congruences for tame values'). These nodes allow p = 2 (generalisation). Mathlib has von Staudt–Clausen (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean:663 `vonStaudt_clausen`, :697 `dvd_den_bernoulli`), which is what makes (b) fail when (p−1) | k, but no Kummer congruence (grep 'Kummer congruence': none in Mathlib/Tau Ceti).

items.name: Valuation on an L-vector space
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Let B be an L-vector space. A valuation on B is a function v : B → ℝ ∪ {+∞} such that (i) v(x)=+∞ iff x=0; (ii) v(x+y) ≥ min(v(x),v(y)) for all x,y ∈ B; (iii) v(λx)=v_p(λ)+v(x) for all λ ∈ L, x ∈ B. It induces the norm ‖x‖ = p^{−v(x)} and hence a topology on B.
items.note: Mathlib encodes the same structure multiplicatively through ‖x‖=p^{−v(x)}: NormedAddCommGroup B gives (i) (‖x‖=0 iff x=0); IsUltrametricDist B (Topology/MetricSpace/Ultra/Basic.lean:46), equivalently IsNonarchimedean ‖·‖ by isUltrametricDist_iff_isNonarchimedean_norm (Analysis/Normed/Group/Ultra.lean:68), gives (ii); NormedSpace L B (Analysis/Normed/Module/Basic.lean:40, field ‖a•b‖≤‖a‖‖b‖) upgrades to equality ‖λx‖=|λ|‖x‖ via the instance NormedSpace.toNormSMulClass (same file :50), which is (iii). Same notion, norm rather than additive-valuation language; there is no separate additive 'valuation on a vector space' structure and none is needed.

items.name: L-Banach space
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. An L-Banach space is a complete topological L-vector space B whose topology is induced by a valuation v in the sense of Definition 3.1 (equivalently a complete non-archimedean normed L-vector space).
items.note: Mathlib: [NormedAddCommGroup B] [NormedSpace L B] [IsUltrametricDist B] [CompleteSpace B]. This is exactly the hypothesis bundle used by Mathlib's Mahler theorem for a p-adic Banach space (PadicInt.mahlerEquiv, NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean:357, variables at :247 and :282).

items.name: The Banach space ℓ⁰_∞(I,L) of null families
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For a set I, ℓ⁰_∞(I,L) is the set of families (a_i)_{i∈I} in L tending to 0 along the cofinite filter (for every ε>0, |a_i|_L<ε for all but finitely many i), with valuation v((a_i)_i)=inf_{i∈I} v_p(a_i) (equivalently sup norm); it is an L-Banach space.
items.note: Mathlib: C₀(I,L) = ZeroAtInftyContinuousMap I L (Topology/ContinuousMap/ZeroAtInfty.lean:45) with I discrete, where cocompact = cofinite; sup norm instNormedAddCommGroup (:466) and instCompleteSpace (:444). Mathlib itself uses this model: PadicInt.mahlerEquiv lands in C₀(ℕ,E). Same object (discrete-domain presentation).

items.name: Orthonormal basis of an L-Banach space (corrected)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Let B be an L-Banach space. A family (e_i)_{i∈I} in B is an orthonormal basis if the map ℓ⁰_∞(I,L) → B, (a_i) ↦ Σ_i a_i e_i, is an isometric ISOMORPHISM (a surjective isometry), i.e. every x ∈ B has a unique expansion x=Σ a_i e_i with a_i → 0 and v(x)=inf v_p(a_i). [Printed: 'an isometry'; surjectivity is required, see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E10.]
items.note: Mathlib has no non-archimedean orthonormal-basis notion. Nearest: GeneralSchauderBasis/UnconditionalSchauderBasis (Analysis/Normed/Module/Bases.lean:102) — a biorthogonal expansion without the isometry condition ‖Σa_ie_i‖=sup|a_i|, so only partial. Mathlib's PadicInt.mahlerEquiv is a concrete instance of an orthonormal basis (isometric equivalence C(ℤ_p,E) ≃ C₀(ℕ,E)) but not the general notion. Planned only by stage text: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0 'For Banach spaces whose nonzero norm values lie in the coefficient value group, prove the orthonormal-basis theorem used in RJW Remark 3.4'; packet coverage for L0 lists 'orthonormal bases' as remaining. No packet node.

items.name: Existence of orthonormal bases (Serre/Colmez)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. If B is an L-Banach space with valuation v_B and v_B(B)=v_p(L) (the valuation takes values only in the value set of L), then B admits an orthonormal basis (in the corrected sense of Definition 3.3(2)). Quoted from Colmez [20, Proposition I.1.5].
items.note: Literature result quoted, not proved. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'orthonormal', 'Schauder' in both trees; only the Archimedean/inner-product and general Schauder notions exist). Planned by stage text PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0: 'prove the orthonormal-basis theorem used in RJW Remark 3.4 by lifting a basis of the integral lattice modulo varpi and completing the successive expansions'. No packet node yet (L0 coverage 'remaining' lists orthonormal bases).

items.name: Continuous dual B* = Hom_cts(B,L)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For a topological L-vector space B, B* := Hom_cts(B,L), the space of continuous L-linear functionals on B.
items.note: Mathlib: StrongDual L B := B →L[L] L (Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean:96); WeakDual L B (Topology/Algebra/Module/Spaces/WeakDual.lean:61) is the same set with the weak-* topology. Same object.

items.name: Strong topology on B* (dual valuation)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Let B be an L-Banach space. The strong topology on B* is the topology of the dual valuation v*(μ)=inf_{x∈B, x≠0}(v_p(μ(x))−v(x)) (i.e. the operator norm ‖μ‖=sup_{x≠0}|μ(x)|/‖x‖). Convergence in it is uniform convergence on the unit ball (equivalently on bounded subsets) of B, NOT uniform convergence on all of B. [Printed: inf over all x∈B and 'converges uniformly'; see issues PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E11 and PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E12.]
items.note: Mathlib: the operator norm on B →L[L] L (Analysis/Normed/Operator/Basic.lean, le_opNorm / opNorm_le_bound); for measures Mathlib also names it AbstractMeasure.StrongTopology (NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Topology.lean:48, 'the topology induced by the norm'). The Mathlib doc of StrongDual (ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean:93) describes it as 'uniform convergence on bounded subsets', which is the corrected statement. L0 stage text: 'operator-norm convergence is uniform on the unit ball'.

items.name: Weak topology on B*
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Let B be an L-Banach space. The weak topology on B* is the topology defined by the semivaluations v_x(μ)=v_p(μ(x)), x ∈ B, i.e. the topology of pointwise convergence (weak-* topology): μ_j → μ iff μ_j(x) → μ(x) for every x ∈ B.
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.5, second bullet and footnote 9 (printed p. 119, PDF 20)
items.note: Mathlib: WeakDual L B = WeakBilin (topDualPairing L B) (Topology/Algebra/Module/Spaces/WeakDual.lean:61, 'coarsest topology such that all v ↦ v x are continuous'); for measures AbstractMeasure.WeakTopology := induced by μ ↦ (f ↦ μ f) (NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Topology.lean:40). Same notion.

items.name: Strong dual of a Banach space is Banach
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. If B is an L-Banach space, then B* with the strong topology (operator norm) is complete, hence an L-Banach space.
items.locator: §3.1, Remark 3.6, first sentence (strong part) (printed p. 119, PDF 20)
items.note: Mathlib: instance ContinuousLinearMap.instCompleteSpace (Topology/Algebra/Module/Spaces/ContinuousLinearMap.lean:180; CompleteSpace (E →SL[σ] F) when F complete, E sequential); for normed spaces SeparatingDual.completeSpace_continuousLinearMap_iff (Analysis/Normed/Operator/CompleteCodomain.lean:49) records CompleteSpace (E →L F) ↔ CompleteSpace F. Ultrametricity of the dual norm is not stated in Mathlib but is not claimed by the paper beyond 'L-Banach space'; for p-adic L it follows from the ultrametric codomain.

items.name: Weak topology on B*: completeness claim (corrected) and weak compactness of the unit ball
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Corrected form of the weak half of Remark 3.6: for an L-Banach space B, the closed unit ball {μ ∈ B* : v*(μ) ≥ 0} of B* (for B = 𝒞(G,L) this is M(G,𝒪_L)) is compact, hence complete, for the weak topology, L being locally compact. [Printed: 'The dual B* is complete with both of these topologies'; for infinite-dimensional B the whole of B* is NOT weakly complete — only bounded weakly Cauchy nets converge (Banach–Steinhaus) — see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E13.]
items.locator: §3.1, Remark 3.6, first sentence (weak part) (printed p. 119, PDF 20)
items.note: Weak compactness of dual balls is Mathlib's Banach–Alaoglu WeakDual.isCompact_closedBall (Analysis/Normed/Module/WeakDual.lean:269, needs [ProperSpace 𝕜], true for a finite extension of ℚ_p). Packet: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/integral-measures-weak-compact ('The native space D(Z_p,Z_p), equipped with WeakTopology, is compact') is the special case G=ℤ_p, 𝒪_L=ℤ_p; L0 stage text: 'unrestricted weak completeness of the full continuous dual is not asserted; the integral dual is weakly compact'. The printed unrestricted completeness is false (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E13).

items.name: Reflexivity for the weak topology on B*
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. If B is an L-Banach space and B* carries the weak topology, then the canonical map B → (B*, weak)* (x ↦ evaluation at x) is an isomorphism (every weakly continuous linear functional on B* is evaluation at a unique x ∈ B); for the strong topology this fails in general (e.g. B infinite-dimensional).
items.note: Not used later in the chunk. Mathlib: WeakDual/WeakBilin API (Topology/Algebra/Module/Spaces/WeakBilin.lean, WeakDual.lean) has continuity of evaluations (eval_continuous) but no theorem that the continuous dual of the weak-* dual is B; Analysis/Normed/Module/DoubleDual.lean treats the norm bidual (inclusionInDoubleDual), not this. Tau Ceti: no hits for weak-dual reflexivity. No atlas stage mentions it (L0 text only asks for the two topologies and their completeness/compactness statements). Routed (source) to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0, with the duals of Banach spaces. The review adds: Mathlib has the surjectivity half, LinearMap.dualEmbedding_surjective (Analysis/LocallyConvex/WeakDual.lean:186: every weakly continuous functional on the dual is evaluation at a point), and the bundled equivalence LinearMap.rightDualEquiv (:192) under SeparatingRight; point separation (non-archimedean Hahn–Banach) and the strong-topology failure are not there, so the item stays missing.

items.name: Banach space C(G,L) of continuous functions
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). 𝒞(G,L) is the L-vector space of continuous φ : G → L with valuation v_𝒞(φ)=inf_{x∈G} v_p(φ(x)) (well defined because G is compact, so φ is bounded); v_𝒞 induces the sup norm and makes 𝒞(G,L) an L-Banach space in the sense of Definition 3.2.
items.locator: §3.2, Definition 3.7 and the sentence after it (printed p. 119, PDF 20)
items.note: Mathlib: C(G,L) with compact G carries the sup norm (NormedAddCommGroup instance, Topology/ContinuousMap/Compact.lean:182; ContinuousMap.norm_le :207, norm_coe_le_norm :199), NormedSpace L C(G,L) (ContinuousMap.normedSpace, :301), ultrametric (ContinuousMap.isUltrametricDist, Topology/MetricSpace/Ultra/ContinuousMaps.lean:20) and complete (ContinuousMap.instCompleteSpaceOfCompactlyCoherentSpace, Topology/UniformSpace/CompactConvergence.lean:433; compact spaces are compactly coherent). Same statement, norm language.

items.name: Space of L-valued measures M(G,L) and the integral ∫_G φ·μ
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). M(G,L) := 𝒞(G,L)* = Hom_cts(𝒞(G,L),L), the continuous dual; for φ ∈ 𝒞(G,L), μ ∈ M(G,L) write ∫_G φ(x)·μ(x) (or ∫_G φ·μ) for μ(φ).
items.note: Mathlib: AbstractMeasure X R E := C(X,R) →L[R] E with notation D(X,R) (NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:40,43; 'an R-linear functional on continuous maps X → R', a type synonym so that no topology is chosen), and toCLMEquiv (:80) identifies it with the continuous dual. M(G,L) = D(G,L), integration = application μ f. Same definition, for any topological X and topological ring R.

items.name: 𝒪_L-valued measures M(G,𝒪_L)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). μ ∈ M(G,L) is 𝒪_L-valued, written μ ∈ M(G,𝒪_L), if ∫_G φ·μ ∈ 𝒪_L for every φ ∈ 𝒞(G,𝒪_L). Equivalently (restricting to 𝒞(G,𝒪_L)) M(G,𝒪_L) = Hom_{𝒪_L}(𝒞(G,𝒪_L),𝒪_L) (continuity is automatic), the closed unit ball {v*(μ) ≥ 0} of M(G,L).
items.note: The intrinsic object is Mathlib's AbstractMeasure G 𝒪_L 𝒪_L = D(G,𝒪_L) (Measure/Basic.lean:40); the Mathlib Amice file works on exactly this carrier (D(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p])). The paper's presentation as a subset of M(G,L) needs the comparison D(G,𝒪_L) ≅ unit ball of D(G,L), which is NOT in the library: planned by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0 ('The integral lattice consists of measures taking C(X,O) into O. Prove the integral-lattice description') and realised for G=ℤ_p, L=ℚ_p by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/rational-integral-image ('there is a unique μ∈D(Z_p,Z_p) with extendIntegralCoefficients(μ)=ν iff ‖toCLMEquiv(ν)‖≤1') and for G=ℤ_p^× by L2/rational-unit-integral-image. General G and general 𝒪_L: stage text only.

items.name: M(G,L) = M(G,𝒪_L) ⊗_{𝒪_L} L (boundedness of measures)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Every μ ∈ M(G,L) is bounded, so p^n μ ∈ M(G,𝒪_L) for some n ≥ 0; hence M(G,L) = M(G,𝒪_L) ⊗_{𝒪_L} L = M(G,𝒪_L)[1/p].
items.locator: §3.2, Definition 3.8, second paragraph ('Since measures are continuous (or equivalently, bounded)…') (printed p. 120, PDF 21)
items.note: Boundedness itself is Mathlib's operator norm (le_opNorm). The scaling statement: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/rational-measure-integral-scaling ('For every ν∈D(Z_p,Q_p) there are n≥0 and μ∈D(Z_p,Z_p) such that ν=p^(−n)·extendIntegralCoefficients(μ)') and L2/rational-unit-integral-scaling (domain ℤ_p^×) — special cases G ∈ {ℤ_p, ℤ_p^×}, L=ℚ_p. General profinite G and finite L/ℚ_p: L0 stage text ('boundedness and scaling into that lattice'); packet L0 coverage lists 'general profinite integral-lattice/field-valued comparisons' as remaining.

items.name: Measures on subsets (corrected: compact subsets)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Definitions 3.7 and 3.8 apply verbatim with G replaced by any COMPACT (e.g. closed, or open compact) subset X ⊂ G with the subspace topology (X need not be a group): 𝒞(X,L) with the sup norm is an L-Banach space and M(X,L), M(X,𝒪_L) are defined as before. [Printed: 'any subset X ⊂ G'; false for non-compact X, issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E14.]
items.note: AbstractMeasure is defined for any topological X; the sup norm on C(X,L) needs [CompactSpace X]; closed subsets of the compact G are compact (IsClosed.isCompact, Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean:860; isCompact_iff_compactSpace). The only uses in the paper are X open compact (ℤ_p^×, b+p^nℤ_p). Packet L0 clopen nodes (e.g. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0/clopen-restriction: 'X is a compact topological space, s is a clopen subset … s is compact because it is closed in X') keep compactness. L0 stage: 'Noncompact subsets require a separately stated function space'.

items.name: Dirac measure δ_g
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). For g ∈ G, δ_g ∈ M(G,𝒪_L) is evaluation at g: ∫_G φ·δ_g = φ(g) for φ ∈ 𝒞(G,𝒪_L).
items.note: Mathlib: AbstractMeasure.dirac R x : D(X,R), 'evaluation at x' (Measure/Basic.lean:93), dirac_apply : dirac R x f = f x (:96). Same construction (any R, in particular 𝒪_L).

items.name: Density of locally constant functions
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). The locally constant functions 𝒞^lc(G,𝒪_L) are dense in 𝒞(G,𝒪_L) for the sup norm: every continuous φ is a uniform limit of functions constant on the pieces of finite clopen partitions (for a profinite group, on cosets of open subgroups). [Printed proof uses truncations φ_n = Σ_{a∈ℤ/p^n} φ(a)1_{a+p^nℤ_p}, valid only for G=ℤ_p; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E15.]
items.locator: §3.2, Remark 3.11, first two sentences (printed p. 120, PDF 21)
items.note: Mathlib, Topology/Separation/DisjointCover.lean:140: for f : C(X,V) with X profinite (compact T2 totally disconnected) and S a neighbourhood of the diagonal, ∃ n, g : X → Fin n continuous, h : Fin n → V with (f x, h (g x)) ∈ S for all x — i.e. f is S-close to the locally constant h∘g; :127 gives the disjoint clopen cover and :167 the finite sum of clopen indicators. Taking S = {dist < ε} this is density of locally constant functions in the sup norm, stated in entourage form rather than as a Dense predicate. Same content, general profinite X. The packet cites this baseline for E12. Specialised planned node for ℤ_p^×: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/unit-cylinder-density.
