items.name: Measures = continuous duals of locally constant functions (3-1)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Let M^lc(G,𝒪_L) := Hom_cts(𝒞^lc(G,𝒪_L),𝒪_L). Restriction from 𝒞(G,𝒪_L) to 𝒞^lc(G,𝒪_L) is an isomorphism M(G,𝒪_L) ≅ M^lc(G,𝒪_L) (3-1); the inverse sends μ^lc to μ with ∫φ·μ = lim_n ∫φ_n·μ^lc for any φ_n ∈ 𝒞^lc with φ_n → φ.
items.note: Ingredients in Mathlib: extension of a continuous linear map from a dense subspace (ContinuousLinearMap.extend, Topology/Algebra/Module/ContinuousLinearMap/Extend.lean:29) and uniqueness (ContinuousLinearMap.ext_on, ContinuousLinearMap/Basic.lean:250), locally constant → continuous (LocallyConstant.toContinuousMapLinearMap). The iso itself is not stated. Planned: L0 stage 'Establish extension from dense test-function spaces, uniqueness'; for G=ℤ_p^×, 𝒪=ℤ_p realised by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/unit-coordinate-measure ('The integral measure of finite unit coordinates') and L1/unit-coordinate-measure-locally-constant. General G: stage text only (L0 coverage: 'clopen density and dense extension from the pinned baseline' remaining).

items.name: Measures = finitely additive functions on compact opens
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). M^lc(G,𝒪_L) (hence, by (3-1), M(G,𝒪_L)) is identified with the 𝒪_L-module of finitely additive functions μ : {open compact subsets of G} → 𝒪_L (3-2): μ(U) := ∫_G 1_U·μ; conversely, for φ ∈ 𝒞^lc(G,𝒪_L) factoring through G/H with H ≤ G open, ∫_G φ·μ := Σ_{[a]∈G/H} φ(a)μ(aH).
items.locator: §3.2, Remark 3.12, equation (3-2), and the sentence after it (printed pp. 120–121, PDF 21–22)
items.note: Not in the library. The step 'a locally constant φ on G factors through G/H for an open subgroup H' is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.isOpen_rightTranslationStabilizer (TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/LocallyConstant.lean:59: for compact G and locally constant f, the subgroup {g | ∀x, f(xg)=f x} is open). Planned by L0 stage text: 'Identify integral measures with finitely additive O-valued functions on clopens; identify K-valued measures with bounded such functions.' No packet node (L0 coverage lists 'finitely additive clopen data with the necessary boundedness' as remaining).

items.name: Real Haar measure on ℤ_p is not a p-adic measure
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. There is no μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,L) (bounded) with μ(a+p^nℤ_p) = p^{−n} for all a ∈ ℤ_p, n ≥ 0: the finitely additive function a+p^nℤ_p ↦ p^{−n} exists but is p-adically unbounded (|p^{−n}|_p = p^n).
items.note: Searched packet PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras (and atlas stage texts) for 'Haar', 'unbounded distribution': no node or stage statement. It is an immediate consequence of the L0 identification of L-valued measures with BOUNDED additive functions (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0 text), but that stage does not state this non-example. Not used later in the chunk. Routed (source) to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0, as the non-example to its bounded-measure identification.

items.name: Dirac measure as an additive function
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Under Remark 3.12, δ_g corresponds to δ̃_g(X) = 1 if g ∈ X and 0 if g ∉ X (X open compact).
items.note: The value δ̃_g(X) := δ_g(1_X) = 1_X(g) is dirac_apply applied to the clopen indicator LocallyConstant.charFn (Topology/LocallyConstant/Algebra.lean:91). The ambient identification of Remark 3.12 is planned (item above). Finite-quotient version: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-dirac ('Finite coefficients of Dirac masses').

items.name: Measures on a finite group = group algebra
items.statement: If G is a finite abelian group (discrete topology), 𝒞(G,ℤ) = ℤ^G and M(G,ℤ) its ℤ-dual, then [g] ↦ δ_g (δ_g(φ)=φ(g)) induces an isomorphism ℤ[G] ≅ M(G,ℤ). The proof of Proposition 3.16 uses the same statement with coefficients 𝒪_L: M(G/H,𝒪_L) ≅ 𝒪_L[G/H]. (Abelianness is not needed.)
items.note: Mathlib has the pieces but not the statement: Module.piEquiv ι R M : (ι → M) ≃ₗ[R] ((ι → R) →ₗ[R] M) with piEquiv v w = Σ w i • v i (LinearAlgebra/StdBasis.lean:186–190), Finsupp.linearEquivFunOnFinite (LinearAlgebra/Finsupp/Defs.lean:61), ContinuousMap.equivFnOfDiscrete; continuity of the functionals and matching single g ↦ δ_g still need proof. Realised by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-discrete-coefficient-bijection: 'The native linear map π_id:D(A,R)→(A→₀R) is bijective. Its inverse sends c to Σ_a c(a)δ_a' (A finite discrete, R any topological commutative ring — generalises), and algebra version L1/finite-discrete-algebra-equivalence ('D(A,R)≃MonoidAlgebra R A').

items.name: Locally constant functions as a colimit over finite quotients
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Every locally constant φ : G → 𝒪_L factors through G/H for some open subgroup H ≤ G; hence 𝒞^lc(G,𝒪_L) ≅ lim→_H 𝒞(G/H,𝒪_L), the colimit over open subgroups H.
items.note: The factorisation is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.isOpen_rightTranslationStabilizer (TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/LocallyConstant.lean:59): for a compact group G and locally constant f the stabilizer H={g | ∀x, f(xg)=f x} is an open subgroup, and f factors through G/H (normal as G is abelian). The colimit statement is not in the library. Specialised node: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/unit-locally-constant-factor ('Every locally constant f:U→A … factors as g∘red_n', U=ℤ_p^×). General G: L1 stage text ('For R=O prove the equivalent presentation lim_U O[G/U]'). The review adds the nearest library results: Profinite.exists_locallyConstant (Topology/Category/Profinite/CofilteredLimit.lean:186) and Condensed.isColimitLocallyConstantPresheafDiagram (Condensed/Discrete/Colimit.lean:81) give the colimit over finite discrete quotients; the open-subgroup form is not there.

items.name: Measures as an inverse limit of measures on finite quotients (3-3)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). M(G,𝒪_L) ≅ Hom_cts(lim→_H 𝒞(G/H,𝒪_L),𝒪_L) ≅ lim←_H M(G/H,𝒪_L), the limit over open subgroups H ≤ G along push-forward (fibre-summing) maps.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Proposition 3.16, equation (3-3) (printed p. 122, PDF 23)
items.note: Transition maps are Mathlib's AbstractMeasure.map (Measure/Basic.lean:101). Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection (π_q(μ)(a)=μ(e_(q,a))), L1/finite-projection-refinement ('Refinement sums fiber masses'), L1/finite-projections-separate (injectivity: 'If π_q(μ)=π_q(ν) for every … continuous q:X→Fin n, then μ=ν', X profinite, R normed); surjectivity (existence from compatible families) only for G=ℤ_p^×, 𝒪=ℤ_p: L1/unit-coordinate-existence-uniqueness and L1/unit-coordinates-range. General G, 𝒪_L: L1 stage text.

items.name: Measures = Iwasawa algebra (Proposition 3.16)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). There is a natural isomorphism M(G,𝒪_L) ≅ lim←_H 𝒪_L[G/H], the limit over all open subgroups H of G.
items.note: No completed group algebra in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'Iwasawa', 'completedGroup' in both trees: only Mathlib's unrelated GroupAction/Iwasawa.lean). L1 stage: 'For R=O prove the equivalent presentation lim_U O[G/U] … Prove the topological O-algebra equivalence between integral measures and O[[G]]'; L5 acceptance: 'recover RJW Proposition 3.16'. Packet L1 remaining: 'Compare these exact interfaces with the ProfiniteProPGroups Layer9 completedGroupAlgebra anchor … establish the algebra homeomorphism'. Realised so far only as coordinates for G=ℤ_p^×, 𝒪=ℤ_p (L1/unit-coordinate-existence-uniqueness) without a limit carrier.

items.name: Explicit maps measures ↔ inverse limit
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). For μ ∈ M(G,𝒪_L) viewed as an additive function and H ≤ G open, λ_H := Σ_{[a]∈G/H} μ(aH)[a] ∈ 𝒪_L[G/H]; (λ_H)_H is compatible and gives M(G,𝒪_L) → lim← 𝒪_L[G/H]. Conversely, for λ in the limit with image λ_H = Σ c_a[a], set μ(aH) := c_a; compatibility makes μ an additive function on compact opens, i.e. a measure.
items.locator: §3.3, paragraphs after the proof of Proposition 3.16 (printed p. 122, PDF 23)
items.note: Forward map: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection ('Construct the R-linear map π_q:D(X,R)→(A→₀R) with π_q(μ)(a)=μ(e_(q,a))', any continuous q to a finite discrete A — generalises G/H) and L1/finite-projection-refinement. Inverse: L1/unit-coordinate-measure / L1/unit-coordinate-reconstruction for G=ℤ_p^×, 𝒪=ℤ_p only.

items.name: Iwasawa algebra Λ(G)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). Λ(G) := lim←_H 𝒪_L[G/H] (H over open subgroups), the profinite completion of the group algebra 𝒪_L[G]; as an inverse limit of group algebras it is a (commutative) 𝒪_L-algebra (Remark 3.18). L is suppressed from the notation.
items.note: Mathlib has only the finite-level MonoidAlgebra; no completed group algebra in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'Iwasawa', 'completedGroup', 'CompletedGroupAlgebra'). PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1: 'For a complete adic ring R … define R[[G]] = lim_(n,U) (R/I^n)[G/U] … For R=O prove the equivalent presentation lim_U O[G/U]'. Tau Ceti roadmap ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 prerequisite: 'completedGroupAlgebra p Γ := lim_U ℤ_p[Γ/U] over the open normal subgroups' (coefficients ℤ_p only). NE.0: 'Construct O[[G]] as the inverse limit over open normal subgroups'. No packet node defines the carrier (packet: 'Do not define a second completed carrier').

items.name: Convolution of measures
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). For μ, λ ∈ M(G,𝒪_L), the convolution μ∗λ is the measure ∫_G φ·(μ∗λ) = ∫_G (∫_G φ(x+y)·λ(y))·μ(x); with unit δ_0 it makes M(G,𝒪_L) a commutative 𝒪_L-algebra.
items.note: Mathlib has the product measure (AbstractMeasure.prodMk / prodMk', Measure/Basic.lean:205,225, with Fubini prodMk_eq_prodMk' for profinite spaces :250) and pushforward map, but no convolution at the pin (the upstream Measure/Monoid.lean of Mathlib PR 41961 cited by the packet is absent from Mathlib 082e2d3). Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/convolution-product ('push native prodMk′(μ,ν) forward along multiplication G×G→G'), L1/convolution-evaluation ('(μ∗ν)(f)=μ(convolveFunRight(ν,f))'), L1/convolution-algebra ('make native D(G,R) a ring and an R-algebra'), L1/commutative-convolution (commutativity on profinite abelian monoids). Generalises (locally compact monoids).

items.name: M(G,𝒪_L) ≅ Λ(G) is an 𝒪_L-algebra isomorphism
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. G is a profinite abelian group (the cases G=ℤ_p, G=ℤ_p^× are the ones used later). The isomorphism of Proposition 3.16 carries convolution of measures to multiplication in Λ(G) = lim← 𝒪_L[G/H], so it is an isomorphism of 𝒪_L-algebras (in particular Λ(ℤ_p) ≅ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) as 𝒪_L-algebras).
items.note: Finite-level multiplicativity planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-convolution-multiplicativity ('Π_q(μ∗ν)=Π_q(μ)Π_q(ν) in native MonoidAlgebra R A'), L1/finite-projection-algebra-map, L1/joint-projection-ring-map. The comparison with a completed-algebra carrier is not a node: packet L1 remaining text 'establish the algebra homeomorphism and Dirac/projection compatibility on that existing carrier'; L1 stage text 'Prove the topological O-algebra equivalence between integral measures and O[[G]]'.

items.name: Group elements [a] ∈ Λ(ℤ_p) and Dirac measures
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For a ∈ ℤ_p, under Proposition 3.16 the Dirac measure δ_a corresponds to the compatible system ([a+p^nℤ_p])_{n∈ℕ} ∈ lim←_n 𝒪_L[ℤ_p/p^nℤ_p] (the subgroups p^nℤ_p being cofinal among open subgroups of ℤ_p); this element of Λ(ℤ_p) is denoted [a]. [Printed 'δ̃_a(a)=1 (if a∈X)'; should be δ̃_a(X), issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E16.]
items.note: Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-dirac ('Finite coefficients of Dirac masses'), L1/joint-finite-dirac, L1/dirac-hom ('Bundle g↦δ_g as a monoid homomorphism G→D(G,R)'). The level maps ℤ_p → ℤ/p^n are Mathlib's PadicInt.toZModPow with kernel p^nℤ_p (PadicInt.ker_toZModPow). The element [a] in a completed-algebra carrier: ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 'completedGroupAlgebra.of : Γ →* Λˣ'.

items.name: Binomial (Mahler) functions (x choose n)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For x ∈ ℤ_p and n ≥ 1, (x choose n) := x(x−1)⋯(x−n+1)/n!, and (x choose 0) := 1. Each x ↦ (x choose n) lies in 𝒞(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) and has v_𝒞 = 0 (sup norm 1).
items.locator: §3.4, Definition 3.20 and the sentence after it (printed p. 123, PDF 24)
items.note: Mathlib NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean: mahler k : C(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p]) (:103) with mahler_apply : mahler k x = Ring.choose x k (:107) (Ring.choose in the binomial ring ℤ_[p] is the descending Pochhammer quotient x(x−1)⋯(x−k+1)/k!), mahler_natCast_eq (:110), PadicInt.continuous_choose (:93), PadicInt.norm_mahler_eq : ‖mahler k‖ = 1 (:276), i.e. v_𝒞 = 0. Same statement.

items.name: Mahler's theorem
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Every continuous φ : ℤ_p → L has a unique expansion φ(x) = Σ_{n≥0} a_n(φ)(x choose n) with a_n(φ) ∈ L, a_n(φ) → 0, and v_𝒞(φ) = inf_n v_p(a_n(φ)); equivalently the (x choose n) form an orthonormal basis of 𝒞(ℤ_p,L) (Definition 3.3). Quoted from Colmez [20, Théorème I.2.3].
items.note: Mathlib MahlerBasis.lean: PadicInt.hasSum_mahler (:339) 'for any continuous function f from ℤ_[p] to a p-adic Banach space E, the Mahler series with coefficients n ↦ Δ_[1]^[n] f 0 converges to f'; PadicInt.mahlerEquiv E : C(ℤ_[p],E) ≃ₗᵢ[ℤ_[p]] C₀(ℕ,E) (:357), a linear ISOMETRIC equivalence, which gives uniqueness (injectivity, also fwdDiff_mahlerSeries :313), a_n → 0 (values in C₀(ℕ,E)) and ‖φ‖ = sup‖a_n(φ)‖ ⇔ v_𝒞(φ)=inf v_p(a_n(φ)). Hypotheses on E: NormedAddCommGroup, Module ℤ_[p], IsBoundedSMul ℤ_[p], IsUltrametricDist, CompleteSpace — satisfied by L. Same statement, more general coefficients. L5 acceptance also names 'Theorems 3.21/3.25'. The print (p. 123) cites '[20, Théorème 1.2.3.]'; the item uses Colmez's roman numbering I.2.3, as in Remark 3.4.

items.name: Mahler coefficients via discrete derivatives
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. The a_n(φ) of Theorem 3.21 are the Mahler coefficients of φ. With φ^{[0]}=φ and φ^{[k+1]}(x)=φ^{[k]}(x+1)−φ^{[k]}(x), one has a_n(φ)=φ^{[n]}(0).
items.note: Mathlib: PadicInt.mahlerEquiv_apply : mahlerEquiv E f = fun n ↦ Δ_[1]^[n] f 0 (MahlerBasis.lean:382), with Δ_[1] the forward difference fwdDiff 1 (Algebra/Group/ForwardDiff.lean), so a_n(φ) = (Δ_[1])^n φ (0) = φ^{[n]}(0). Same statement.

items.name: Mahler (Amice) transform A_μ
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L), A_μ(T) := ∫_{ℤ_p}(1+T)^x·μ(x) = Σ_{n≥0}(∫_{ℤ_p}(x choose n)·μ) T^n ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]].
items.note: Mathlib NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean: AbstractMeasure.amiceTransform : D(ℤ_[p],R) →ₗ[R] R⟦X⟧ (:75), 'the power series with n-th coefficient μ(mahler n). More suggestively, this is the series ∫(1+X)^a dμ', coeff_amiceTransform (:80); R any commutative topological ring with continuous ℤ_[p]-algebra structure (so R=𝒪_L). Same definition (the ∫(1+T)^x expression is notation in both).

items.name: Amice transform of a Dirac measure
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For a ∈ ℤ_p, A_{δ_a}(T) = Σ_{n≥0}(a choose n)T^n = (1+T)^a (the binomial series).
items.note: Not stated in Mathlib, but a two-line consequence: PowerSeries.binomialSeries A r := mk (fun n ↦ Ring.choose r n • 1) is '(1+X)^r' (RingTheory/PowerSeries/Binomial.lean:47, coeff lemma :51), and coeff_amiceTransform + dirac_apply give coeff_n A_{δ_a} = mahler n a • 1 = Ring.choose a n • 1. Packet: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/amice-dirac-natural ('For n∈ℕ, the Amice transform of the existing integral Dirac measure δ_n is (1+T)^n') covers only a ∈ ℕ, 𝒪=ℤ_p; general a ∈ ℤ_p is covered by L2 stage text 'Establish multiplication, Dirac transforms'.

items.name: Iwasawa isomorphism Λ(ℤ_p) ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]], [1] ↦ 1+T, and diagram (3-4)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Since 1 topologically generates ℤ_p and 1+T topologically generates 𝒪_L[[T]] ((p,T)-adically), [1] ↦ 1+T extends to an 𝒪_L-algebra isomorphism Λ(ℤ_p) ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]] ([a] ↦ (1+T)^a), and the triangle (3-4) M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) → Λ(ℤ_p) → 𝒪_L[[T]] (Proposition 3.16 then this map) equals the Mahler transform μ ↦ A_μ (checked on Dirac measures δ_a ↦ [a] ↦ (1+T)^a, then by continuity).
items.locator: §3.4, paragraph before and after diagram (3-4) (printed p. 124, PDF 25)
items.note: Only density of ℕ in ℤ_p is in Mathlib (PadicInt.denseRange_natCast, NumberTheory/Padics/RingHoms.lean:501). No completed group algebra exists (see Definition 3.17 item). Planned: ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 'Power-series coordinates. For a chosen topological generator γ of Γ ≅ ℤ_p, the assignment T ↦ γ − 1 extends to an isomorphism of ℤ_p-algebras ℤ_p[[T]] ≅ completedGroupAlgebra p Γ' (ℤ_p coefficients); PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/cyclotomic-weierstrass-polynomials: 'O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) ≅ O[Γ/Γ_n] by T ↦ γ − 1; the resulting O⟦T⟧ ≅ O⟦Γ⟧ is requested from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9'; NE.0 acceptance 'Recover O[[T]] for G=Zp'. The commutativity of (3-4) with the Amice transform is not a node (needs the L1 carrier).

items.name: Amice transform is a bijection M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]] (Theorem 3.25, linear part)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ↦ A_μ is an 𝒪_L-linear bijection M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) → 𝒪_L[[T]]: μ is determined by the values ∫(x choose n)·μ (by Mahler's theorem ∫φ·μ = Σ a_n(φ)∫(x choose n)·μ), and for g = Σ c_nT^n ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] the measure μ_g, ∫φ·μ_g := Σ a_n(φ)c_n (convergent in 𝒪_L), satisfies A_{μ_g} = g.
items.note: Mathlib proves it for 𝒪_L = ℤ_p only: AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ (AmiceTransform.lean:156; its docstring TODO: 'Define this more generally -- this will need a definition for bounded power series over a normed ring'); injectivity holds for general complete ultrametric R (injective_amiceTransform :91, via ext_mahler :55), so injectivity for 𝒪_L IS library. Surjectivity for general 𝒪_L is planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/bounded-inverse ('boundedInvTransform … from BoundedContinuousFunction(N,R) to … D(Z_p,R)', R any complete ultrametric normed ℤ_p-algebra; for R=𝒪_L every sequence is bounded), L2/bounded-inverse-amice ('amiceTransform of boundedInvTransform(c) is PowerSeries.mk(c)'), L2/bounded-inverse-unique; L5 acceptance names Theorem 3.25.

items.name: Amice transform is multiplicative (Theorem 3.25, algebra part)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. The Mahler transform is an 𝒪_L-ALGEBRA isomorphism: A_{μ∗λ} = A_μ·A_λ for the convolution of Remark 3.18 and A_{δ_0} = 1.
items.locator: §3.4, Theorem 3.25 (with the argument around (3-4)) (printed p. 124, PDF 25)
items.note: Not in Mathlib (no convolution at the pin). No packet node: L2 stage text 'Establish multiplication, Dirac transforms, coefficient extraction' and packet L2 remaining text 'convolution and multivariable theory … remain'. Depends on the L1 convolution nodes (L1/convolution-product, L1/convolution-dirac 'δ_x∗δ_y=δ_(xy)'). The paper's proof of this part is only the Dirac/continuity sketch around (3-4).

items.name: 𝒪_L[[T]] as an inverse limit over ω_n = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. 𝒪_L[[T]] ≅ lim←_n 𝒪_L[T]/((1+T)^{p^n}−1); together with (3-3) and the definition of Λ(ℤ_p) each space in (3-4) is an inverse limit, and at level n M(ℤ/p^n,𝒪_L) ≅ 𝒪_L[ℤ/p^n] ≅ 𝒪_L[T]/((1+T)^{p^n}−1) compatibly (the level-n diagram is left to the reader).
items.note: Planned node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/cyclotomic-weierstrass-polynomials: 'ω_n … are distinguished polynomials over O … ⋂_n ω_nO⟦T⟧ = 0, so O⟦T⟧ = lim O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) … O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) ≅ O[Γ/Γ_n] by T ↦ γ − 1'; passing from O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) to the polynomial quotient O[T]/(ω_n) is Weierstrass division (Mathlib PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassDivision, RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean; L4/weierstrass-adapter). IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1: 'The kernel of passage to Γ/Γ^{p^n} is generated by (1+T)^{p^n}−1'. Note the node's 'so' step only gives injectivity of the limit map; surjectivity (completeness) must also be proved.

items.name: Measure μ_g attached to a power series g
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For g ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]], μ_g ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) denotes the unique measure with A_{μ_g} = g.
items.note: Mathlib: AbstractMeasure.invTransform F : D(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p]) with amiceTransform_invTransform (AmiceTransform.lean:128,143) — case 𝒪_L = ℤ_p only. General 𝒪_L: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/bounded-inverse (boundedInvTransform), L2/bounded-inverse-unique.

items.name: L-valued measures ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]][1/p]
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. The Mahler transform induces M(ℤ_p,L) ≅ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L)⊗_{𝒪_L}L ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]]⊗_{𝒪_L}L ≅ 𝒪_L[[T]][1/p] (power series over L with bounded coefficients). [Printed 'O[[T]]' for 𝒪_L[[T]], issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E17.]
items.note: Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/field-amice-range ('For F∈K[[T]], there exists a measure μ with A_μ=F if and only if there is C≥0 such that ‖coeff_n(F)‖≤C for every n', K complete ultrametric nontrivially normed field with ℤ_p-algebra structure — includes L), L2/field-bounded-amice-isometry ('K-linear isometric equivalence (C(Z_p,K)→L[K]K)≃ₗᵢ[K]BoundedContinuousFunction(N,K)'). Bounded coefficients over the discretely valued L is 𝒪_L[[T]][1/p]. The tensor comparison M(ℤ_p,L) = M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L)⊗L is L2/rational-measure-integral-scaling for L=ℚ_p only.

items.name: Moments of μ_g in terms of derivatives of g
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For g ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]]: ∫μ_g = g(0), ∫x·μ_g = g′(0), ∫x²·μ_g = g″(0)+g′(0), ∫x³·μ_g = g‴(0)+3g″(0)+g′(0); in general ∫x^n·μ_g is an integer combination of g^{(r)}(0), 0 ≤ r ≤ n (coefficients the Stirling numbers S(n,r), from x^n = Σ_r S(n,r) r!(x choose r)).
items.note: Checked: x² = 2(x choose 2)+(x choose 1), x³ = 6(x choose 3)+6(x choose 2)+(x choose 1), and g^{(r)}(0) = r!·c_r, giving the printed formulas. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/algebra-ordinary-moment ('For every k≥0, μ(x_R^k)=constantCoeff(∂_R^[k](Aμ))') and L2/ordinary-moment (ℤ_p), which is Corollary 3.30; the Stirling expansion ∂^n = Σ_r S(n,r)(1+T)^r d^r/dT^r is not itself a node (partial).

items.name: Strong topology ↔ p-adic topology on 𝒪_L[[T]]
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Under Theorem 3.25 the strong (operator-norm) topology on M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) corresponds to the p-adic topology on 𝒪_L[[T]] (uniform convergence of coefficients): ‖μ‖ = sup_n |∫(x choose n)·μ|.
items.note: Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/field-bounded-amice-isometry (isometric equivalence of the operator-norm dual with bounded coefficient sequences, sup norm), L2/bounded-inverse-norm ('Exact norm of the bounded inverse'), L2/field-amice-coefficient-bound. These are over a field K ⊇ 𝒪_L, restricting to 𝒪_L-measures via the integral extension (L2/rational-integral-extension-norm for ℚ_p).

items.name: Weak topology ↔ (p,T)-adic topology on 𝒪_L[[T]]
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Under Theorem 3.25 the weak topology on M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) corresponds to the (p,T)-adic topology on 𝒪_L[[T]], i.e. coefficientwise convergence. Example: T^n → 0 (p,T)-adically (so μ_{T^n} → 0 weakly) but not p-adically (not strongly).
items.locator: §3.4, Remark 3.28(3), second part and example (printed pp. 125–126, PDF 26–27)
items.note: Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/integral-amice-weak-homeomorphism ('amiceTransformEquiv is a homeomorphism from D(Z_p,Z_p) with its native weak topology to Z_p[[T]] with the coefficientwise p-adic topology') — case 𝒪_L = ℤ_p only; the coefficientwise topology is Mathlib's PowerSeries.WithPiTopology (tendsto_iff_coeff_tendsto). The T^n example is L5 acceptance text 'demonstrate both topologies on T^n'; the packet realises a different example (L2/dirac-prime-powers-weak-limit, L2/dirac-prime-powers-not-strong-limit with δ_{p^n}).

items.name: Multiplication of a measure by a continuous function (xμ, g(x)μ)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For μ a measure on ℤ_p and g ∈ 𝒞(ℤ_p,L), g(x)μ is the measure ∫f·g(x)μ := ∫f(x)g(x)·μ; in particular xμ: ∫f·xμ = ∫x f(x)·μ.
items.locator: §3.5.1 (printed p. 126, PDF 27) and §3.5.2, first paragraph (printed p. 126, PDF 27)
items.note: Not a Mathlib declaration (Measure/Basic.lean has map, dirac, products, no weighting). Planned node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/weight: 'Define AbstractMeasure.weight g : D(X,R) →ₗ[R] D(X,R) by (weight g μ)(f)=μ(gf)' (X compact, R normed commutative ring — generalises), with weight-evaluation, weight-multiplication, weight-iteration.

items.name: Mahler transform of xμ (Lemma 3.29)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. A_{xμ} = ∂A_μ, where ∂ = (1+T)d/dT. (Proof: x(x choose n) = (n+1)(x choose n+1) + n(x choose n).)
items.note: Checked the recurrence and the coefficient comparison Σ[(n+1)c_{n+1}+nc_n]T^n = (1+T)Σ n c_n T^{n−1}. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/algebra-amice-weight ('A(weight(x_R) μ)=∂_R(Aμ) in R[[T]]', R any normed commutative ℤ_p-algebra — covers 𝒪_L), L2/amice-weight (ℤ_p), L2/mahler-derivation (∂ := (1+T)•PowerSeries.derivative, Mathlib RingTheory/PowerSeries/Derivative.lean:50), L2/mahler-recurrence.

items.name: Moments from the Mahler transform (Corollary 3.30)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. For every k ≥ 0, ∫_{ℤ_p} x^k·μ = (∂^k A_μ)(0).
items.note: Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/algebra-ordinary-moment ('For every k≥0, μ(x_R^k)=constantCoeff(∂_R^[k](Aμ))', general coefficient algebra — exact), L2/ordinary-moment (ℤ_p). Consumed by DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/measure-ordinary-moment.

items.name: Mahler transform of z^x μ
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. For z ∈ 𝒪_L with |z−1| < 1 (so x ↦ z^x = Σ_n (x choose n)(z−1)^n is continuous on ℤ_p): A_{z^xμ}(T) = A_μ((1+T)z − 1), the substitution being defined because (1+T)z−1 has constant term z−1 in the maximal ideal. (Printed proof: 'one has to be slightly careful about convergence issues'.)
items.note: The character x ↦ z^x is Mathlib's PadicInt.addChar_of_value_at_one (z−1) (NumberTheory/Padics/AddChar.lean:60, = mahlerSeries ((z−1)^·), 'the unique continuous additive character of ℤ_[p] mapping 1 to 1+r'); substitution is PowerSeries.subst. The identity is not in the library and has no generic packet node: packet L2 remaining text lists 'multiplication by z^x with convergence hypotheses' as remaining; covered by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 stage text: 'Build all of RJW §3.5: multiplying a measure by a function; the operator ∂=(1+T)d/dT; translations and dilations; roots-of-unity projections to residue classes; phi(T)=(1+T)^p−1; psi; psi phi=1 and phi psi=restriction to pZ_p; restriction to units as 1−phi psi; inversion of multiplication by x on units. Every root-of-unity expression includes scalar-extension/descent and convergence statements.' Special case for the smoothing measure μ_b over O_K: ColemanIntegration:L3/rotated-smoothed-amice ('multiplication by the continuous character x->w^x gives a bounded measure w^x mu_b with Amice transform G_(b,w)') and L3/smoothed-twist-as-sum-of-rotated-measures.

items.name: Restriction Res_X(μ) to a compact open X ⊂ ℤ_p; support
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For X ⊂ ℤ_p compact open with characteristic function 1_X, Res_X(μ) is the measure on ℤ_p with ∫f·Res_X(μ) := ∫f 1_X·μ, also written ∫_X f·μ. μ is supported on X if μ = Res_X(μ).
items.note: Res_X = weight(1_X). Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0/clopen-projector-evaluation ('The ambient clopen projector' j_s∘r_s), L0/clopen-support-characterization ('There exists a unique ν∈D(s,R) with j_sν=μ iff μ(f)=0 for every f vanishing on s'); for X = pℤ_p L2/restriction-pmultiples ('restrictMultiples … weight χ'), for X = a+p^nℤ_p L2/residue-restriction ('P_(n,a) … weight(χ_(n,a))'), for X = ℤ_p^× L2/unit-restriction.

items.name: Restriction as a measure on X (extension by zero)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For X ⊂ ℤ_p compact open and g ∈ 𝒞(X,L), let g̃ be its extension by 0 to ℤ_p; g ↦ ∫_{ℤ_p} g̃·μ is a measure on X, also denoted Res_X(μ) (compatible with the ambient Res_X(μ) under extension by zero).
items.note: Planned nodes (compact X, clopen s — generalises): PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0/clopen-zero-extension ('z_s(f)(x)=f(x) on s and 0 off s'), L0/clopen-restriction ('restrictClopen … r_s(μ)(f)=μ(z_s(f)). Denote by j_s the already existing AbstractMeasure.map along ContinuousMap.subtypeVal s'), L0/clopen-restriction-section, L0/clopen-decomposition-equivalence.

items.name: Characteristic function of a residue disc via roots of unity
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For b ∈ ℤ_p, n ≥ 0 and x ∈ ℤ_p: 1_{b+p^nℤ_p}(x) = p^{−n} Σ_{ξ∈μ_{p^n}} ξ^{x−b} (ξ^y := ξ^{y mod p^n}; values in L(μ_{p^n})).
items.note: Orthogonality ingredients in Mathlib: IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_eq_zero (RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/PrimitiveRoots.lean:444) and AddChar.sum_eq_ite (Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean:329). Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/primitive-root-power-sum: 'ζ∈R primitive of order p … Σ_{i<p} ζ^(in) is p if p divides n, and zero otherwise' — only n=1 (order p); general p^n via PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 stage text: 'Build all of RJW §3.5: multiplying a measure by a function; the operator ∂=(1+T)d/dT; translations and dilations; roots-of-unity projections to residue classes; phi(T)=(1+T)^p−1; psi; psi phi=1 and phi psi=restriction to pZ_p; restriction to units as 1−phi psi; inversion of multiplication by x on units. Every root-of-unity expression includes scalar-extension/descent and convergence statements.'

items.name: Mahler transform of restriction to b+p^nℤ_p (3-5)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. For b ∈ ℤ_p, n ≥ 0: A_{Res_{b+p^nℤ_p}(μ)}(T) = p^{−n} Σ_{ξ∈μ_{p^n}} ξ^{−b} A_μ((1+T)ξ − 1), an identity in 𝒪_{L(μ_{p^n})}[[T]] whose left side lies in 𝒪_L[[T]]. (Obtained from the previous display and §3.5.2 with z = ξ ∉ 𝒪_L in general: requires extension of scalars, see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E18.)
items.note: No node for general n, b: packet L2 remaining text 'The full prime-power Fourier formula (3-5), multiplication by z^x, root-translation convergence and integral descent remain; the preceding order-p root-average theorem alone does not supply them'. Partial nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/residue-restriction and L2/residue-restriction-amice-coefficient ('coeff_k(A(P_(n,a)μ))=μ(χ_(n,a)·M_(R,k))'); L2/root-average ('p·map(j,φ(psiSeries F))=Σ_{i<p}τ_i(F) in O[[T]]', the case n=1, b=0 over ℤ_p with O = 𝒪_{ℂ_p}); L2/rational-root-average-descent. Stage: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 stage text: 'Build all of RJW §3.5: multiplying a measure by a function; the operator ∂=(1+T)d/dT; translations and dilations; roots-of-unity projections to residue classes; phi(T)=(1+T)^p−1; psi; psi phi=1 and phi psi=restriction to pZ_p; restriction to units as 1−phi psi; inversion of multiplication by x on units. Every root-of-unity expression includes scalar-extension/descent and convergence statements.'

items.name: Mahler transform of restriction to ℤ_p^× (3-6)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. A_{Res_{ℤ_p^×}(μ)}(T) = A_μ(T) − p^{−1} Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} A_μ((1+T)ξ − 1).

Planned for 𝒪_L = ℤ_p by combining PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/series-unit-restriction ('A(Eμ)=Aμ−PowerSeries.subst b (psiSeries(Aμ))', b=(1+T)^p−1) with L2/root-average (p·φ(ψ F) = Σ_{i<p} τ_i(F), τ_i(F) = F(ζ^i(1+T)−1)) and L2/root-average-integral-descent. General 𝒪_L: stage text only (packet: 'remaining coefficient-general phi/psi/roots-of-unity comparisons').

items.name: Compact opens of ℤ_p are finite unions of residue discs
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Every compact open X ⊆ ℤ_p (and its complement) is a finite disjoint union of discs b+p^nℤ_p (one may take a single n); hence the Mahler transform of Res_X(μ) is a finite sum of expressions (3-5).
items.note: Not stated in the library. Ingredient: 1_X is locally constant, so its (additive) translation stabilizer is an open subgroup of ℤ_p (TauCeti.isOpen_rightTranslationStabilizer, applied to Multiplicative ℤ_p or read additively — the Tau Ceti lemma is stated for multiplicative groups), hence contains p^nℤ_p = ker PadicInt.toZModPow n. Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/residue-restriction-partition ('the sum of P_(n,a)μ over all a∈ZMod(p^n) equals μ'), L2/residue-fiber-coset, L2/residue-restriction-refinement; the decomposition of an arbitrary clopen is L0 stage text ('restriction to a clopen, extension by zero, support and disjoint decomposition').

items.name: Action σ_a of ℤ_p^× on measures
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For a ∈ ℤ_p^× (the paper's Galois precursor), σ_a(μ) is the measure ∫f(x)·σ_a(μ) = ∫f(ax)·μ, i.e. the pushforward of μ along x ↦ ax; σ_{ab} = σ_a∘σ_b.
items.note: σ_a(μ) = AbstractMeasure.map (x ↦ a·x) μ; map_apply : map f μ g = μ (g.comp f) (Measure/Basic.lean:106) is the defining formula and map_map (:110) gives the action law. The packet uses exactly this (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/amice-dilation: 'd_a is the existing continuous map x↦a x … no new operator or Galois-action carrier is defined').

items.name: Mahler transform of σ_a(μ)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. For a ∈ ℤ_p^×: A_{σ_a(μ)}(T) = A_μ((1+T)^a − 1).
items.note: Planned node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/amice-dilation: 'For every a in Z and integral measure mu in D(Z,Z), A(map(d_a,mu))=S_a(A(mu))', S_a(F)=PowerSeries.subst(binomialSeries a − 1, F) — all a ∈ ℤ_p (generalises the unit hypothesis) but coefficients ℤ_p only (𝒪_L=ℤ_p); with L2/mahler-dilation.

items.name: Frobenius φ on measures and on 𝒪_L[[T]]
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. φ(μ) is the measure ∫f(x)·φ(μ) = ∫f(px)·μ (pushforward along x ↦ px, 'σ_p'); on power series φ(F)(T) := F((1+T)^p − 1).
items.note: On measures φ = AbstractMeasure.map (x ↦ px) (library as a pushforward); named in node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/phi-measure ('Define phiMeasure=AbstractMeasure.map m_p as an R-linear endomorphism of D(Z,R)', R normed commutative ring). On series, φ = PowerSeries.subst((1+T)^p−1) (Mathlib RingTheory/PowerSeries/Substitution.lean:158), used as notation in L2/amice-phi.

A_{φ(μ)} = φ(A_μ) = A_μ((1+T)^p − 1).

items.name: The operator ψ on measures
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. ψ(μ) is the measure on ℤ_p with ∫_{ℤ_p} f(x)·ψ(μ) = ∫_{pℤ_p} f(p^{−1}x)·μ.

items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. φ(ψ(μ)) = Res_{pℤ_p}(μ).

items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. Res_{ℤ_p^×}(μ) = (1 − φ∘ψ)(μ).

items.name: ψ on 𝒪_L[[T]] and the root-of-unity formula (3-9)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. Transporting ψ through the Mahler transform gives an 𝒪_L-linear operator ψ on 𝒪_L[[T]] (ψ(A_μ) := A_{ψ(μ)}); it is the unique operator with φ∘ψ(F)(T) = p^{−1} Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} F((1+T)ξ − 1) for all F ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] (right side computed in 𝒪_{L(μ_p)}[[T]]).

The unique G is psiSeries F'). General 𝒪_L: stage text ('remaining coefficient-general phi/psi/roots-of-unity comparisons').

items.name: φ is injective on 𝒪_L[[T]]
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. F ↦ F((1+T)^p − 1) is injective on 𝒪_L[[T]] (used in the proof of Corollary 3.32 and for uniqueness in (3-9)).
items.note: Follows from ψ∘φ = id on series: planned node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/psi-series-phi ('psiSeries(PowerSeries.subst b F)=F for every F∈B', B=ℤ_p[[T]]) — coefficients ℤ_p. Not a Mathlib lemma (no injectivity theorem for PowerSeries.subst found in RingTheory/PowerSeries/Substitution.lean).

items.name: Support on ℤ_p^× ⇔ ψ(A_μ) = 0 (Corollary 3.32)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. μ ∈ M(ℤ_p,𝒪_L) (identified with Λ(ℤ_p)), A_μ ∈ 𝒪_L[[T]] its Mahler transform. μ is supported on ℤ_p^× (Res_{ℤ_p^×}(μ) = μ) if and only if ψ(A_μ) = 0.
items.note: Planned node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/unit-support-psi: 'Eμ=μ iff ψμ=0' (measure-level ψ, R normed commutative ring — covers 𝒪_L), plus L2/psi-series-intertwining ('psiSeries(Aμ)=A(ψμ)', ℤ_p) for the power-series form.

items.name: Inclusion ι : Λ(ℤ_p^×) ↪ Λ(ℤ_p)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. ι(μ) is the measure on ℤ_p with ∫_{ℤ_p} φ·ι(μ) = ∫_{ℤ_p^×} φ|_{ℤ_p^×}·μ (pushforward along ℤ_p^× ⊂ ℤ_p); Res_{ℤ_p^×}∘ι = id on Λ(ℤ_p^×), so ι is injective.
items.note: ι itself is Mathlib's pushforward AbstractMeasure.map along the continuous inclusion Units.val : ℤ_p^× → ℤ_p (the packet's j_U). The retraction Res_{ℤ_p^×}∘ι = id is planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/intrinsic-unit-restriction ('restrictUnits … D(ℤ_p,R) →ₗ[R] D((ℤ_p)ˣ,R)'), L2/intrinsic-unit-restriction-section ('Intrinsic restriction retracts unit inclusion'), L2/unit-domain-homeomorphism.

items.name: Image of ι is ker ψ
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. A measure μ ∈ Λ(ℤ_p) lies in ι(Λ(ℤ_p^×)) if and only if ψ(μ) = 0; so ι : Λ(ℤ_p^×) ≅ ker ψ.
items.note: Planned nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/unit-measure-kernel-equivalence ('D(U,R) ≃ₗ[R] ker(psiMeasure p R), with forward value j_Uν and inverse r_U'), L2/unit-measure-amice-kernel-equivalence ('D((ℤ_p)ˣ,ℤ_p) ≃ₗ[ℤ_p] ker(psiSeries p)'), with topological versions L2/unit-measure-kernel-weak-homeomorphism, L2/unit-measure-kernel-strong-homeomorphism.

items.name: Λ(ℤ_p^×) is not a subalgebra of Λ(ℤ_p)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. ι(Λ(ℤ_p^×)) is not closed under the (additive) convolution of Λ(ℤ_p) (e.g. δ_1∗δ_{−1} = δ_0 is not supported on ℤ_p^×, and δ_0 ∉ ι(Λ(ℤ_p^×))); ι is 𝒪_L-linear but not multiplicative from the multiplicative convolution on ℤ_p^× to the additive one on ℤ_p.
items.note: Counterexample checked (δ_1, δ_{−1} ∈ ι(Λ(ℤ_p^×)), δ_1∗δ_{−1} = δ_0). Only stage text: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 'The inclusion of measures supported on Z_p^× into measures on additive Z_p is linear, not an algebra homomorphism for the two different convolutions' (the non-homomorphism half; non-closure of the image is not stated). No packet node.

items.name: Multiplicative convolution on Λ(ℤ_p^×) (3-10)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 intro, printed p. 118): L is a finite extension of ℚ_p, v_p is the p-adic valuation on L normalised by v_p(p)=1, 𝒪_L is the ring of integers of L. For λ, μ measures on ℤ_p^×, μ ∗_{ℤ_p^×} λ is the measure with ∫_{ℤ_p^×} f(x)·(μ∗_{ℤ_p^×}λ) = ∫_{ℤ_p^×}(∫_{ℤ_p^×} f(xy)·μ(x))·λ(y) (convolution for the multiplicative group ℤ_p^×; by commutativity and Fubini this equals the order of integration of Remark 3.18).
items.note: Planned nodes (any locally compact monoid, so ℤ_p^× multiplicatively): PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/convolution-product, L1/convolution-evaluation ('(μ∗ν)(f)=μ(convolveFunRight(ν,f))', right-handed orientation), L1/commutative-convolution. Swapping the order of integration is Mathlib's profinite Fubini AbstractMeasure.prodMk_eq_prodMk' (Measure/Basic.lean:250). Used for the unit measure ring M = D(ℤ_p^×,ℤ_p) in L1/unit-measures-weak-topological-ring and L3.

items.name: Total ring of fractions Q(G) of the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let G be a profinite abelian group. Q(G) denotes the ring of fractions of Λ(G), i.e. the total quotient ring: the localisation of the commutative ring Λ(G) at the multiplicative set of its non-zero-divisors, with the injective structure map Λ(G) → Q(G).
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 description: 'For commutative O[[G]], use localization at its non-zero-divisors.' Packet nodes PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-unit-character-evaluation and .../unit-positive-moment-separation fix 'Q=FractionRing M' for M=D(Z_p^×,Z_p) with the (planned, L1) convolution ring structure. The generic carrier exists: mathlib:FractionRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/FractionRing.lean:733, `abbrev FractionRing := Localization (nonZeroDivisors R)`, the total fraction ring, no domain hypothesis) and mathlib:IsFractionRing.injective. What is missing is the ring Λ(G) itself: Mathlib's AbstractMeasure (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:40) is only a module (no convolution product) and Tau Ceti f790474 has no Iwasawa algebra (grep 'Iwasawa', 'AbstractMeasure', 'convolution' over measures: none). Convolution ring is planned at PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/convolution-algebra and .../commutative-convolution.

items.name: Pseudomeasure
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let G be a profinite abelian group and Q(G) the total ring of fractions of Λ(G). A pseudomeasure on G is an element λ ∈ Q(G) such that ([g] − [1])·λ ∈ Λ(G) for every g ∈ G (product in Q(G), extending convolution on Λ(G)).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/pseudomeasures: 'Define Iwasawa.pseudomeasures δ Q : Submodule R Q to be (1 : Submodule R Q) / Submodule.span R (range (g ↦ ι(δ(g)−1)))', with .../pseudomeasure-membership 'z ∈ pseudomeasures δ Q iff ∀ g, ∃ r : R, ι(r)=ι(c_g)z'. This generalises the source (arbitrary δ : G → R into a commutative ring R, any R-algebra Q); specialised to δ = Dirac map into D(Z_p^×,Z_p) in .../actual-unit-character-evaluation ('P is the existing Iwasawa pseudomeasure M-submodule of Q'). Only Z_p coefficients are instantiated in the packet; O_L-coefficients are covered by the generic node. Nothing in Mathlib 082e2d3 or Tau Ceti f790474 (grep 'pseudo' with measure/Iwasawa context: no match).

items.name: Integral of a nontrivial character against a pseudomeasure (3-11)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let G be profinite abelian, χ : G → C_p^× a nontrivial continuous character and λ ∈ Q(G) a pseudomeasure. Choose g ∈ G with χ(g) ≠ 1 and put ∫_G χ·λ := (χ(g) − 1)^{-1} ∫_G χ·([g] − [1])λ, where the right-hand integral is that of the continuous function χ against the measure ([g] − [1])λ ∈ Λ(G) (after extending scalars to C_p).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/admissible-evaluation: 'For g ∈ G with hg : IsUnit (f(c_g)), define Iwasawa.evalAt δ Q A g hg : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] A by z ↦ u⁻¹ f(n_g(z))' and .../admissible-evaluation-spec 'f(c_g) evalAt_g(z)=f(n_g(z))' — a generalisation (any commutative target algebra, unit clearing factor). The concrete case .../actual-unit-character-evaluation ('For κ≠1, define the additive homomorphism Eκ:P→ℚ_p') and .../actual-unit-character-ratio ('Eκ(z)=fκ(n_g(z))/(κ(g)−1)') cover only G = Z_p^× with Z_p coefficients and Z_p-valued characters; the node says 'The source allows C_p-valued characters with additional coefficient-extension data; that broader target is not inferred here'. So C_p-valued characters and O_L coefficients are covered only through the generic node. Not in any library.

items.name: Independence of (3-11) from the clearing element g
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. With G, χ ≠ 1 continuous and λ a pseudomeasure as in (3-11): for all g, h ∈ G with χ(g) ≠ 1 and χ(h) ≠ 1, (χ(g) − 1)^{-1} ∫_G χ·([g] − [1])λ = (χ(h) − 1)^{-1} ∫_G χ·([h] − [1])λ. (Proof: (χ(h) − 1)∫χ·([g] − [1])λ = ∫χ·([g] − [1])([h] − [1])λ = (χ(g) − 1)∫χ·([h] − [1])λ, using that µ ↦ ∫χ·µ is multiplicative on Λ(G) and G is abelian; the printed last integrand 'µ' must be λ, see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E21.)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/independence-of-clearing-factor: 'If f(c_g) and f(c_h) are units, evalAt δ Q A g hg = evalAt δ Q A h hh as R-linear maps' (match field: 'correcting the last occurrence of μ to λ'), resting on .../cross-multiplied-numerators 'c_h n_g(z)=c_g n_h(z) in R'. Generic, so it covers the source statement once G, O_L and the C_p-valued character are instantiated.

items.name: Character integration is a ring homomorphism on Λ(G)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let G be profinite abelian and χ : G → C_p^× a continuous character. Then µ ↦ ∫_G χ·µ is a ring homomorphism Λ(G) → C_p (for the convolution product): ∫χ·(µ∗ν) = (∫χ·µ)(∫χ·ν), ∫χ·[1] = 1, and ∫χ·[g] = χ(g).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/character-integral-algebra-hom: 'For a native ContinuousMonoidHom κ:G→R, define the R-algebra homomorphism D(G,R)→R by μ↦μ(κ.toContinuousMap)', with .../dirac-hom ('Bundle g↦δ_g as a monoid homomorphism G→D(G,R)'). The node takes characters with values in the coefficient ring R itself; a C_p-valued character of an O_L-valued measure needs the coefficient-extension interface of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 (integral-unit-extension-*). The hypothesis 'nontrivial' in the source is not needed for this part. Mathlib has the measure carrier and mathlib:AbstractMeasure.dirac (Measure/Basic.lean:93) but no convolution, so the multiplicativity is not in the library.

items.name: Evaluation of pseudomeasures at a nontrivial character is the unique Λ(G)-compatible extension (corrected Remark 3.35)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let G be profinite abelian and χ : G → C_p^× a nontrivial continuous character; write ε_χ(µ) = ∫_G χ·µ on Λ(G). The map λ ↦ ∫_G χ·λ of (3-11), on the Λ(G)-module of pseudomeasures, is the unique additive map E with E(µ) = ε_χ(µ) for µ ∈ Λ(G) and E(µ·λ) = ε_χ(µ)E(λ) for µ ∈ Λ(G), λ a pseudomeasure. In general ε_χ does NOT extend to a ring homomorphism Q(G) → C_p (a non-zero-divisor s ∈ Λ(G) with ε_χ(s) = 0 obstructs it; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E20), contrary to the printed claim 'This induces a unique homomorphism Q(G) → C_p'.
items.note: Corrected statement. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/uniqueness-of-evaluation ('If L : pseudomeasures δ Q →ₗ[R] A satisfies L(integral r)=f(r) for every r, then L=evalAt_g'; match: 'It does not assert a ring homomorphism on all of Q(G)'), .../actual-unit-character-uniqueness ('Eκ is the unique additive map L:P→ℚ_p satisfying L(μ·z)=fκ(μ)L(z) and L(iμ)=fκ(μ)'), .../evaluation-on-integral-elements, and the obstruction .../obstruction-to-fraction-extension ('If s ∈ nonZeroDivisors R and f(s)=0, there is no F : Q →+* A with F.comp (algebraMap R Q)=f') and .../actual-mass-fraction-obstruction. Stage L3 description: 'Do not construct a character map on the entire total quotient ring'.

items.name: Lemma 3.36(i): positive moments separate measures on Z_p^×
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let µ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) (an O_L-valued measure on Z_p^×) with ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·µ = 0 for all integers k > 0. Then µ = 0.
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/unit-positive-moment-separation: 'If μ∈M satisfies μ(t_k)=0 for every k>0, then μ=0', M=D(Z_p^×,Z_p), t_k(u)=u^k, any prime p including 2; proof via .../positive-mahler-vanishing, .../positive-moments-constant-amice and the kernel of ψ — the source argument. The node is the O_L = Z_p case ('arbitrary finite-extension lattices ... remain separate'). The proof uses ι : Λ(Z_p^×) ↪ Λ(Z_p) (Remark 3.33), (3-8) and ψ(c) = c for constants.

items.name: Lemma 3.36(ii): nonvanishing positive moments give a non-zero-divisor
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let µ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) with ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·µ ≠ 0 for all integers k > 0. Then µ is not a zero divisor in Λ(Z_p^×) (for the multiplicative convolution (3-10) on Z_p^×). (Proof uses ∫x^k·(µ ∗ λ) = (∫x^k·µ)(∫x^k·λ) and part (i).)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/unit-moment-regularity: 'If μ∈M has μ(t_k)≠0 for every k>0, then μ belongs to native nonZeroDivisors M', with .../unit-convolution-moments '(μ∗ν)(t_k)=μ(t_k)ν(t_k)'. O_L = Z_p case only.

items.name: Lemma 3.36(iii): positive moments separate pseudomeasures on Z_p^×
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let λ ∈ Q(Z_p^×) be a pseudomeasure with ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·λ = 0 (integral in the sense of (3-11)) for all integers k > 0. Then λ = 0. (Proof, corrected: choose an integer a prime to p with a ∉ {1, −1}, e.g. a = p + 1; then ([a] − [1])λ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) has all positive moments (a^k − 1)∫x^k·λ = 0, so vanishes by (i), and [a] − [1] is a non-zero-divisor by (ii) since a^k ≠ 1 for k > 0. The printed choice 'a ≠ 1' allows a = −1, for which [a] − [1] is a zero divisor; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E22.)
items.locator: §3.6, Lemma 3.36(iii) (printed p. 130, PDF 31; proof printed p. 131, PDF 32)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-pseudomoment-separation: 'If z∈P has every positivePseudoMoment(k,z)=0 for k>0, then z=0', with .../actual-positive-pseudomoment (moments via admissible evaluation), .../actual-pseudomoment-numerator, .../regular-one-add-prime-difference ('For any a∈U with underlying value p+1, the actual measure δ_a−1 is regular') and .../regular-dirac-difference — the corrected proof with a = p+1. Z_p coefficients only.

items.name: Augmentation ideal at finite level I((Z/p^n)^×)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. For n ≥ 1, the degree (augmentation) map is the ring homomorphism O_L[(Z/p^nZ)^×] → O_L, Σ_a c_a[a] ↦ Σ_a c_a, and I((Z_p/p^n)^×) ⊂ O_L[(Z_p/p^n)^×] is its kernel.
items.note: TauCeti/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/Exactness.lean:55 `noncomputable def augmentation (K : Type v) [Monoid K] : _root_.MonoidAlgebra R K →+* R` ('The coefficient-sum augmentation of a monoid algebra'), for any ring R; the source's I is `RingHom.ker (augmentation O_L (ZMod (p^n))ˣ)` (same statement, specialised). Line 87 `ker_augmentation_eq_span`: the kernel is `Ideal.span (range fun k ↦ single k 1 − 1)` — the generation by [k] − 1 used in Lemma 3.38.

items.name: Degree map on Λ(Z_p^×) and the augmentation ideal I(Z_p^×)
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. The finite-level degree maps O_L[(Z/p^nZ)^×] → O_L are compatible with the projections, so pass to the limit Λ(Z_p^×) = lim_n O_L[(Z/p^nZ)^×] → O_L; equivalently µ ↦ ∫_{Z_p^×} 1·µ (total mass). Its kernel is the augmentation ideal I(Z_p^×) ⊂ Λ(Z_p^×).
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1: 'define R[[G]] = lim_(n,U) (R/I^n)[G/U] ... Prove ... functoriality, augmentation, Dirac elements'; stage L3: 'Prove their module structure, augmentation-ideal description'. Packet nodes PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-mass ('Σ_a π_q(μ)(a)=μ(1), independently of q': compatibility of the finite degrees with total mass) and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/convolution-total-mass ('(μ∗ν)(1)=μ(1)ν(1)', so the degree is a ring map). No node names I(Z_p^×) itself.

items.name: I(Z_p^×) is the inverse limit of the finite augmentation ideals
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Under Λ(Z_p^×) ≅ lim_n O_L[(Z/p^nZ)^×], the augmentation ideal satisfies I(Z_p^×) ≅ lim_n I((Z_p/p^n)^×) (the limit taken along the maps induced by (Z/p^{n+1})^× → (Z/p^n)^×).
items.note: Only the stage description covers it (left exactness of the inverse limit applied to the augmentation of L1: 'Prove ... augmentation, Dirac elements, density of the ordinary group algebra' for R[[G]] = lim (R/I^n)[G/U], and 'For R=O prove the equivalent presentation lim_U O[G/U]'). No packet node states the ideal comparison.

items.name: (Z/p^nZ)^× is cyclic for odd p
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and n ≥ 0. Then the unit group (Z/p^nZ)^× is cyclic.
items.locator: §3.6, proof of Lemma 3.38, first sentence (printed p. 131, PDF 32)
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/ZMod/UnitsCyclic.lean:197 `theorem isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : p ≠ 2) (n : ℕ) : IsCyclic (ZMod (p ^ n))ˣ` — same statement. Quoted (not proved) in the source.

items.name: Augmentation ideal of a finite cyclic group ring is principal
items.statement: Let C be a finite cyclic group with generator c and R a commutative ring (here R = O_L, C = (Z_p/p^n)^× with c = a mod p^n). Then the augmentation ideal I(C) = ker(R[C] → R) equals ([c] − [1])·R[C].
items.note: Corrected by the review from planned to library. Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/FiniteCyclic.lean:113 `Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.leftRegular.range_applyAsHom_sub_eq_ker_linearCombination` (G finite, generated by g): the range of multiplication by [g] − 1 on k[G] equals the kernel of the coefficient-sum (augmentation) map; :55 `Representation.FiniteCyclicGroup.coinvariantsKer_eq_range` is the universe-free form. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.ker_augmentation_eq_span (Exactness.lean:87) identifies that kernel with the span of all single k 1 − 1. The procyclic limit remains at PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 ('For procyclic G prove the principal augmentation-ideal theorem').

items.name: Existence of a topological generator of Z_p^× (integer primitive roots modulo p²)
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime and a an integer that is a primitive root modulo p with a^{p−1} ≢ 1 (mod p²). Then a mod p^n generates (Z/p^nZ)^× for every n ≥ 1, i.e. a is a topological generator of Z_p^×; in particular Z_p^× is procyclic and topological generators a ∈ Z_{>1} exist.
items.note: Quoted standard fact. Searched Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 for primitive-root lifting and topological generation of ℤ_[p]ˣ ('isCyclic_units', 'orderOf_one_add', 'zpowers', 'DenseRange', 'topological generator', 'ℤ_[p]ˣ'): nothing states it. Nearest: mathlib:ZMod.orderOf_one_add_mul_prime (Mathlib/RingTheory/ZMod/UnitsCyclic.lean:181: `orderOf (1 + p * a : ZMod (p ^ (n + 1))) = p ^ n` for p ∤ a, p ≠ 2), which with a^{p−1} = 1 + p·u gives the result in a few lines, and mathlib:ZMod.isCyclic_units_of_prime_pow. Atlas stages: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 and LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3 mention 'change of generator' / 'coordinate change for a different topological generator' but presuppose a generator; tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-7-demushkin-groups-their-invariants-and-the-orientation plans 'ℤ_pˣ ≅ μ_{p-1} × (1 + pℤ_p)' (which implies procyclicity) but not this criterion. The DirichletPadicLFunctions packet avoids generators altogether (it uses the regular, non-generating a = p+1). Routed (source) to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 ('change of generator' for procyclic groups).

items.name: Lemma 3.38: µ/([a] − [1]) is a pseudomeasure
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let p be odd, a a topological generator of Z_p^× and µ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×). Then [a] − [1] is a non-zero-divisor of Λ(Z_p^×) (Lemma 3.36(ii), since a^k ≠ 1 for k > 0), and µ′ := µ/([a] − [1]) ∈ Q(Z_p^×) is a pseudomeasure. Key step: I(Z_p^×) = ([a] − [1])Λ(Z_p^×), so for each g ∈ Z_p^× there is ν ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) with [g] − [1] = ν([a] − [1]) and ([g] − [1])µ′ = νµ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×).
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3: 'For procyclic G prove the principal augmentation-ideal theorem, existence and uniqueness statements used by RJW §§3–4, and change of generator.' No packet node realises the lemma as stated. The Kubota–Leopoldt construction in the DirichletPadicLFunctions packet bypasses it: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-fraction-clearing ('If a∈U has value p+1, then for every g∈U, alg(θ_g)·mk′(λ_a,θ_a)=alg(λ_g) in Q') proves the pseudomeasure property of its specific fraction from the cross-numerator identity .../padic-intrinsic-cross, with the regular but non-generating a = p+1. The source's proof also passes from finite levels to the limit ('In the inverse limit we see') without comment; a compactness/Mittag-Leffler step is implicit (not recorded as an error).

items.name: Every pseudomeasure on Z_p^× has the form µ/([a] − [1])
items.statement: Standing notation (§3 opening, printed p. 118, PDF 19; §3.5 Notation, printed p. 126, PDF 27): L/Q_p is a fixed finite extension, O_L its ring of integers, v_p(p)=1; for a profinite group G, Λ(G)=Λ_{O_L}(G)=O_L[[G]] is the Iwasawa algebra, identified with the O_L-valued measures M(G,O_L), with product the convolution of measures; [g]∈Λ(G) is the Dirac measure at g. Let p be odd, λ ∈ Q(Z_p^×) a pseudomeasure and a ∈ Z_p^× a topological generator. Then µ := ([a] − [1])λ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) and λ = µ/([a] − [1]).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/cleared-numerator ('the unique n_g(z) satisfying ι(n_g(z))=ι(c_g)z') and .../cleared-numerator-spec give µ = n_a(λ); dividing needs c_a regular (.../regular-dirac-difference: 'If a∈U satisfies (a:Z)^k≠1 for every k>0, then δ_a−1 is regular'). The form λ = n_a(λ)/c_a is not stated as a node; DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure-regular-parameter states it for ζ_p only.

items.name: Rigid analytic functions on the open unit disc R⁺ (and bounded ones)
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. B(0,1) = {z ∈ C_p : |z| < 1}. An L-valued function on B(0,1) is rigid analytic if it is given by a power series Σ_{n≥0} a_n T^n ∈ L[[T]] convergent on all of B(0,1), i.e. |a_n| r^n → 0 as n → ∞ for every 0 < r < 1; R⁺ ⊂ L[[T]] denotes the space of such series. Such a function is bounded if sup_n |a_n| < ∞.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform names 'R⁺, the power series converging on the open unit disc v_p(T) > 0 with the valuations v_{B(0,u_h)}'; ColemanIntegration:L0/disc-analytic-functions defines 'The ring O_K(D^-(a, r)) of analytic functions on the open disc ... equivalently f(z) = sum_n c_n (z - a)^n with |c_n| rho^n -> 0 for every rho < r' (general disc; covers R⁺ as a = 0, r = 1). Mathlib has only generic analytic-function API (HasFPowerSeriesOnBall, FormalMultilinearSeries.radius); no subspace R⁺ ⊂ L⟦X⟧ and no rigid-analytic space of [BGR] (the source's 'rigid analytic space in the sense of [10]').

items.name: Bounded rigid functions on B(0,1) are O_L[[T]] ⊗ L ≅ M(Z_p, L)
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. The bounded elements of R⁺ form O_L[[T]] ⊗_{O_L} L, and the Mahler transform µ ↦ A_µ(T) = Σ_n (∫_{Z_p} C(x,n)·µ) T^n (Remark 3.28/Theorem 3.25) is an isomorphism M(Z_p, L) ≅ O_L[[T]] ⊗_{O_L} L; thus bounded L-valued measures on Z_p are bounded rigid analytic functions on B(0,1).
items.note: Library special case only: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:156 `def amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧` (the integral, L = Q_p case); its TODO: 'Define the Amice transform as an equivalence over more general base rings; this requires developing some theory of bounded power series over normed rings.' The O_L and ⊗L versions are planned: stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 ('identify M(Z_p,O) with O[[T]]'); LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform ('on bounded measures A_μ is the bounded Amice (Mahler) transform, so D ⊃ M corresponds to R⁺ ⊃ 𝒪_L⟦T⟧ ⊗ L'). The theorem itself is B1's Theorem 3.25; here it is restated.

items.name: Locally analytic functions C^la(Z_p, L)
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. A function f : Z_p → L is locally analytic at z ∈ Z_p if there are an integer n_z ≥ 0 and a_k(z) ∈ L (k ≥ 0) such that Σ_{k≥0} a_k(z)(x − z)^k converges to f(x) for all x ∈ U_z := z + p^{n_z}Z_p; f is locally analytic if it is locally analytic at every z ∈ Z_p; C^la(Z_p, L) is the L-vector space of locally analytic functions Z_p → L.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-radius ('LA_h(ℤ_p, L) is the space of φ : ℤ_p → L whose restriction to each a + p^hℤ_p is the restriction of some φ_{a,h} ∈ An(B(a, h), L) ... every locally analytic function lies in some LA_h') with .../disc-analytic-functions (Colmez §I.4.1). Mathlib's AnalyticAt/AnalyticOn (for maps between normed spaces over a nontrivially normed field) is the nearest generic notion; no C^la(ℤ_[p], L) in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep 'LocallyAnalytic', 'locally analytic': only an unrelated docstring in TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Padic.lean).

items.name: Banach spaces C^{n-an}(Z_p, L) of functions analytic on discs of radius p^{-n}
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. For n ∈ N, f : Z_p → L is locally analytic of radius p^{−n} if it is locally analytic with n_z = n for all z, i.e. given by a single power series Σ_k a_k(z)(x − z)^k on each z + p^nZ_p. C^{n−an}(Z_p, L) is the space of these; it is an L-Banach space for v_n(f) = inf_{z∈Z_p/p^nZ_p} inf_{k∈N}(nk + v_p(a_k(z))), equivalently ‖f‖_n = sup_{z∈Z_p/p^nZ_p} sup_k |a_k(z)| p^{−nk} (the series being required to converge on the closed discs, so that these are finite).
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-radius: 'For h ∈ ℕ, LA_h(ℤ_p, L) ... with v_{LA_h}(φ) = inf_a v_{B(a,h)}(φ_{a,h}) ... It is an L-Banach space with orthonormal basis ...' — same space and valuation (v_{B(a,h)}(φ) = inf_k(v_p(a_k)+kh) by .../disc-analytic-functions), with more (orthonormal basis, base change). Stage L0: 'Construct the Banach spaces of functions analytic on every residue ball of a fixed radius, with their Gauss norms'.

items.name: C^la(Z_p, L) = lim→ C^{n-an}(Z_p, L), with the inductive-limit topology
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. Every locally analytic f : Z_p → L lies in C^{n−an}(Z_p, L) for some n (by compactness of Z_p), and C^{n−an} ⊂ C^{(n+1)−an} continuously; hence C^la(Z_p, L) = lim→_{n∈N} C^{n−an}(Z_p, L), and C^la(Z_p, L) is given the (locally convex) direct-limit topology.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-radius: 'the inclusions LA_h ⊂ LA_{h+1} are continuous of norm ≤ 1. Since ℤ_p is compact, every locally analytic function lies in some LA_h, and LA(ℤ_p, L) = lim→_h LA_h(ℤ_p, L) carries the locally convex inductive-limit topology.' Same statement.

items.name: Remark 3.41: C^la ⊂ C, finer topology, dense image
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. Locally analytic functions are continuous, so C^la(Z_p, L) ⊂ C(Z_p, L); the direct-limit topology on C^la(Z_p, L) is not the one induced from the Banach space C(Z_p, L); the image of C^la(Z_p, L) in C(Z_p, L) is dense (locally constant functions are locally analytic and dense in C(Z_p, L)).
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-topology: 'The inclusion LA(ℤ_p, L) ⊂ C⁰(ℤ_p, L) is continuous with dense image (locally constant functions are dense in C⁰), but the inductive-limit topology on LA(ℤ_p, L) is strictly finer than the topology induced from C⁰.' Same statement (slightly stronger: continuity of the inclusion). Not in any library.

items.name: Locally analytic distributions D^la(Z_p, L)
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. D^la(Z_p, L) := Hom_cts(C^la(Z_p, L), L), the continuous dual for the direct-limit topology; for µ ∈ D^la(Z_p, L) and φ ∈ C^la(Z_p, L) one writes ∫_{Z_p} φ(x)·µ(x) := µ(φ).
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-distributions: 'D(ℤ_p, L) is the space of continuous linear forms on LA(ℤ_p, L), i.e. of linear forms whose restriction to every LA_h is continuous.' Not in any library (Mathlib's AbstractMeasure is the dual of C(X,R), i.e. measures only).

items.name: Mahler (Amice) transform of a locally analytic distribution
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. The binomial polynomials C(x,n) are locally analytic; for µ ∈ D^la(Z_p, L) define A_µ(T) := ∫_{Z_p}(1 + T)^x·µ(x) := Σ_{n≥0} (∫_{Z_p} C(x,n)·µ) T^n ∈ L[[T]].
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform: 'For μ ∈ D(ℤ_p, L) let A_μ(T) = ∫(1 + T)^x μ(x) = Σ_n T^n ∫C(x, n)μ ∈ L⟦T⟧.' The measure version exists: mathlib:AbstractMeasure.amiceTransform (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:75, `D(ℤ_[p], R) →ₗ[R] R⟦X⟧`, n-th coefficient μ (mahler n)), but only on continuous duals of C(ℤ_[p], R), not on D^la.

items.name: Theorem 3.43 (Amice): the Mahler transform D^la(Z_p, L) → R⁺ is bijective
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. The Mahler transform µ ↦ A_µ induces a bijection D^la(Z_p, L) → R⁺ ⊂ L[[T]] (onto the power series convergent on the open unit disc). [Colmez, Fonctions d'une variable p-adique, Theorem II.2.2.]
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform: 'μ ↦ A_μ is an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces from D(ℤ_p, L) onto R⁺' (Colmez Lemma II.2.1 and Theorem II.2.2), with explicit valuation estimates — generalises. Stage L1: 'Prove RJW Theorem 3.43'. Uses LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/amice-mahler-basis (orthonormal basis [n/p^h]!·C(x,n) of LA_h). Not in any library.

items.name: The Mahler transform is an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. Topologise D^la(Z_p, L) as the inverse limit lim← D^{n−an}(Z_p, L) of the strong (Banach) duals D^{n−an} of C^{n−an}(Z_p, L), and R⁺ as the inverse limit over r < 1 of the Banach spaces O(B(0,r)) of analytic functions on the closed discs B(0,r) = {z ∈ C_p : |z| ≤ r}. (A topology induced from a (countable) inverse limit of Banach spaces is a Fréchet topology.) Then the bijection of Theorem 3.43 is an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform ('isomorphism of Fréchet spaces ... Precisely, v_{B(0,u_h)}(A_μ) ≥ v_{LA_h}(μ) ≥ v_{B(0,u_{h+1})}(A_μ) − 1'); LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-distributions ('it is a Fréchet space, equal as a topological vector space to the projective limit lim← D_h of the Banach duals D_h = LA_h(ℤ_p, L)′ (which is also its strong dual topology)'). Stage L1: 'Prove the Frechet topology comparison'.

items.name: Remark 3.44: measures embed in distributions compatibly with the Mahler transform (3-12)
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. Restricting µ ∈ M(Z_p, L) to C^la(Z_p, L) ⊂ C(Z_p, L) gives µ̃ ∈ D^la(Z_p, L); µ ↦ µ̃ is injective (density of C^la in C), so M(Z_p, L) ⊂ D^la(Z_p, L); and the square (3-12) commutes: A_{µ̃} = A_µ, i.e. under the Mahler transforms this inclusion is the inclusion O_L[[T]] ⊗_{O_L} L ⊂ R⁺.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L0/locally-analytic-distributions: 'Restricting a bounded measure to LA(ℤ_p, L) gives an injective continuous map M(ℤ_p, L) → D(ℤ_p, L), by density of LA in C⁰'; LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/amice-transform: 'on bounded measures A_μ is the bounded Amice (Mahler) transform, so D ⊃ M corresponds to R⁺ ⊃ 𝒪_L⟦T⟧ ⊗ L'. Stage L1: 'the compatibility with R01's bounded transform'.

items.name: Remark 3.45: the measure-theoretic toolbox extends to locally analytic distributions
items.statement: L/Q_p finite (fixed coefficient field), O_L its integers, |·| the p-adic absolute value on C_p with |p| = 1/p. The operations of §3.5 — multiplication by x (A ↦ ∂A, ∂ = (1+T)d/dT), restriction to b + p^nZ_p and to Z_p^× (Res_{Z_p^×} = 1 − φ∘ψ), σ_a for a ∈ Z_p^× (A ↦ A((1+T)^a − 1)), φ (A ↦ A((1+T)^p − 1)), ψ (with ψ∘φ = id, φ∘ψ(A) = p^{−1}Σ_{ξ∈µ_p} A((1+T)ξ − 1)) — are defined on D^la(Z_p, L) and correspond under the Mahler transform to the same operators on R⁺.
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-operations: 'The bounded toolbox extends continuously to D(ℤ_p, L), with the following Amice transforms ... A_{xμ} = ∂A_μ ...
