Restriction to b + p^nℤ_p ... σ_a (a ∈ ℤ_p^×), φ and ψ ... ψφ = id, σ_a commuting with φ and ψ, ψ(μ) = 0 iff μ is supported on ℤ_p^×, and Res_{ℤ_p^×} = 1 − φψ.' Stage L1: 'Extend the toolbox of restriction, twisting, phi, psi and differentiation with continuity'. The source's 'identically' is informal; used in §§6.2, 7 (Lemma 6.4/6.5, (7-5)).

items.name: Weight space W(C_p) = Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×)
items.statement: The weight space (its C_p-points) is W(C_p) := Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×), the group of continuous homomorphisms (characters) χ : Z_p^× → C_p^×.
items.note: As a set/group of C_p-points this is a direct instance of existing constructions: Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/ContinuousMonoidHom.lean:57 `structure ContinuousMonoidHom extends A →* B, C(A, B)` with A = ℤ_[p]ˣ, B = ℂ_[p]ˣ, and Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Complex.lean:137 `abbrev PadicComplex := UniformSpace.Completion (PadicAlgCl p)` (notation ℂ_[p], line 140). No named 'weight space' declaration in either library (Tau Ceti's weightSpace/WeightSpace are Lie-algebra weight spaces, unrelated). The rigid-analytic structure is a separate item below (planned).

items.name: Z_p^× = µ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) for odd p
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime. Multiplication gives an isomorphism of topological groups µ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) ≅ Z_p^×, where µ_{p−1} ⊂ Z_p^× is the group of (p−1)-st roots of unity (Teichmüller representatives) and 1 + pZ_p the principal units; consequently Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×) ≅ Hom_cts(µ_{p−1}, C_p^×) × Hom_cts(1 + pZ_p, C_p^×).
items.note: Quoted standard fact. Stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups#layer-7-...: 'For odd p, ℤ_pˣ ≅ μ_{p-1} × (1 + pℤ_p), and the closed subgroups of 1 + pℤ_p are exactly the 1 + p^fℤ_p.' Partial library: tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100, `def teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ`, a section of reduction with image μ_{q−1} (`range_teichmuller`, line 175), for any nonarchimedean local field K, so for K = ℚ_p) and Tau Ceti's unit filtration (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean, `unitFiltrationGradedZeroEquivResidueFieldUnits`); the product decomposition itself is not stated (searched UnitFiltration/*, Teichmuller.lean, Padic.lean for prod/MulEquiv/×: none). Also used in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a and LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3 ('For Z_p^× and odd p obtain p−1 components').

items.name: Weight space as p − 1 open unit discs
items.statement: Let p be odd and γ a topological generator of 1 + pZ_p. Then χ ↦ χ(γ) − 1 is a bijection Hom_cts(1 + pZ_p, C_p^×) → B(0,1) = {z ∈ C_p : |z| < 1} (inverse z ↦ (γ^x ↦ (1+z)^x)). Hence W(C_p) = ⊔_{ν∈(µ_{p−1})^∨} U_ν, where ν ranges over the p − 1 characters of µ_{p−1}, U_ν = {χ ∈ W(C_p) : χ|_{µ_{p−1}} = ν}, and each U_ν is identified with B(0,1). (The printed text says evaluation at γ itself identifies Hom_cts(1 + pZ_p, C_p^×) with B(0,1); the values χ(γ) fill 1 + B(0,1) — issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E28.)
items.note: Library special case: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/AddChar.lean:125 `noncomputable def continuousAddCharEquiv_of_norm_mul : {κ : AddChar ℤ_[p] R // Continuous κ} ≃ {r : R // ‖r‖ < 1}`, given by κ ↦ κ 1 − 1, for R a complete ultrametric normed ℤ_[p]-algebra with multiplicative norm — the Z_p-version of the disc identification (whether ℂ_[p] carries the needed `Algebra ℤ_[p]`/`IsBoundedSMul` instances was not checked). Transport along 1 + pZ_p ≅ Z_p (x ↦ γ^x) and the component decomposition are not in any library. Planned: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3 ('For G=Z_p^d identify its character space with the d-dimensional open polydisc. For Z_p^× and odd p obtain p−1 components ... Prove the coordinate change for a different topological generator'); PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a ('the finite-character components and polydisc charts').

items.name: Rigid analytic weight space W
items.statement: There is a rigid analytic space W over Q_p whose C_p-points are W(C_p) = Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×) (for odd p, a disjoint union of p − 1 open unit discs).
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a: 'construct the rigid analytic space representing continuous characters G→A× on affinoid coefficient algebras A ... prove representability, evaluation of the universal character'; LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: 'Construct the functor of continuous characters of a compact commutative p-adic analytic group on affinoid K-algebras ... Build the corresponding adic/rigid spaces'. No packet node; no library.

items.name: Amice: measures on Z_p^× are bounded rigid functions on weight space
items.statement: Giving a measure µ on Z_p^× (L-valued, bounded) is equivalent to giving a bounded rigid analytic function F_µ on W, via F_µ(χ) := ∫_{Z_p^×} χ·µ for χ ∈ W(C_p); under this correspondence the multiplicative convolution of measures on Z_p^× corresponds to pointwise multiplication of functions.
items.note: Stage LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: 'Construct the universal character and identify distributions with analytic functions in the cases covered by Amice theory; bounded measures give bounded functions'. Pointwise multiplicativity is the character-integral ring homomorphism (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/character-integral-algebra-hom). No node realises the equivalence; no library.

items.name: Pseudomeasures on Z_p^× are rigid functions on W with at most a simple pole at the trivial character
items.statement: Let p be odd, a a topological generator of Z_p^× and λ = µ/([a] − [1]) ∈ Q(Z_p^×) a pseudomeasure (µ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×)). For χ ∈ W(C_p), ∫_{Z_p^×} χ·([a] − [1]) = χ(a) − 1 vanishes iff χ(a) = 1 iff χ is trivial (a generates topologically); hence χ ↦ ∫χ·λ = F_µ(χ)/(χ(a) − 1) is a rigid analytic function on W away from the trivial character, with at most a simple pole there.
items.note: Stage LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: 'pseudo-measures give meromorphic functions on their stated domains'. Partial node: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/unit-character-evaluation-continuity ('For fixed z∈P, the function s↦E_(κ_s)(z) is continuous on the native subtype {s:S | κ_s≠1}') and .../unit-character-clearing-continuity — continuity in a character family away from the trivial character, not rigid analyticity or the pole order. Informal remark in the source ('might have a simple pole').

items.name: Theorem 4.1: the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic zeta function (existence and uniqueness)
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); Λ(Z_p^×) is the Iwasawa algebra of Z_p^× (multiplicative convolution) and Q(Z_p^×) its total ring of fractions. There is a unique pseudomeasure ζ_p ∈ Q(Z_p^×) on Z_p^× such that ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·ζ_p = (1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1 − k) for all integers k > 0, the integral being that of (3-11) against the nontrivial character x ↦ x^k and ζ the Riemann zeta function (values in Q ⊂ C_p). ζ_p (= ζ_p^an of §1) is the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic L-function.
items.locator: §4, Theorem 4.1 (printed p. 136, PDF 37); proof completed after Proposition 4.11 (printed p. 139, PDF 40)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1: 'The endpoint, in RJW's normalization, is the unique pseudo-measure zeta_p satisfying integral_(Z_p^×) x^k dzeta_p = (1−p^(k−1)) zeta(1−k), k≥1. At k=1 the Euler factor is zero; keep this case in the proof rather than claiming zeta(0)=0.' Nodes: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure (construction), .../arithmetic-positive-bernoulli ('For every k>0, M_k(ζ_p)=−(1−p^(k−1))·alg_Q,Q_p(B_k/k)'), .../arithmetic-euler-zeta-comparison ('the complex image of r_(p,k) equals (1−p^(k−1))riemannZeta(1−k)'), .../arithmetic-positive-interpolation ('a unique r∈Q whose complex image is (1−p^(k−1))ζ(1−k) and whose Q_p-image is M_k(ζ_p)'), .../arithmetic-interpolation-unique. The packet works over Z_p coefficients, for every prime p including 2, and compares with ζ(1−k) through a rational number (no field isomorphism C ≅ C_p). IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 imports it ('import the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudomeasure from DirichletPadicLFunctions L1–L2'). Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (grep 'Kubota', 'padicZeta', 'Iwasawa': none).

items.name: Special values ζ(−k) = (−1)^k B_{k+1}/(k+1) (recalled from Lemma 2.7/§2.3)
items.statement: For integers k ≥ 0, ζ(−k) = (−1)^k B_{k+1}/(k+1), where B_n are the Bernoulli numbers of t/(e^t − 1) = Σ B_n t^n/n! (B_1 = −1/2); equivalently ζ(−k) = (−1)^k f^{(k+1)}(0)/(k+1) for f(t) = t/(e^t − 1), which follows from (s − 1)ζ(s) = L(f, s − 1) and Theorem 2.4. (The printed intermediate expression ζ(−k) = (d^k f/dt^k)(0) is wrong; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E23.)
items.locator: §4.1, opening paragraph (printed p. 136, PDF 37), recalling Lemma 2.7 (printed p. 112, PDF 13)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/HurwitzZetaValues.lean:251 `theorem riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli (k : ℕ) : riemannZeta (-k) = (-1 : ℂ) ^ k * bernoulli (k + 1) / (k + 1)`, with Mathlib's `bernoulli` (B_1 = −1/2, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean:205 `bernoulli_one`) — same statement. The generating function: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Bernoulli.lean:269 `bernoulliPowerSeries_mul_exp_sub_one : bernoulliPowerSeries A * (exp A - 1) = X`. The Mellin route (Lemma 2.7, Theorem 2.4) is planned at DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 ('Prove the Mellin-transform continuation argument of RJW Theorem 2.4 ... State the zeta special-value formula with the correct n=0 convention'); it belongs to chunk A (§2).

items.name: The smoothed function f_a(t) = 1/(e^t − 1) − a/(e^{at} − 1)
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p (corrected: the source says 'an integer coprime to p', which allows a ≤ 0; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E24). Put f_a(t) := 1/(e^t − 1) − a/(e^{at} − 1) for t > 0. It extends to a C^∞ (indeed real-analytic) function on [0, ∞) with f_a(0) = (a − 1)/2, and f_a and all its derivatives decay exponentially (like e^{−min(1,a)t}) as t → ∞, so Theorem 2.4 applies to it.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-mellin-kernel ('For real a, define h_a:ℝ→ℝ as the native extended divided difference at zero of x↦β(x)−β(ax). Equivalently away from t=0 it is (β(t)−β(at))/t'), .../smoothed-kernel-away ('h_a(t)=1/(exp(t)−1)−a/(exp(at)−1)'), .../smoothed-kernel-smooth, .../smoothed-kernel-analytic, .../smoothed-kernel-derivative-decay ('For a>0 and every m≥0, h_a^(m) is O(exp(−min(1,a)t))'). The packet's a>0 hypothesis for decay matches the correction. Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Lemma 4.2(a): L(f_a, s) = (1 − a^{1−s})ζ(s), entire
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p and L(f_a, s) = Γ(s)^{−1}∫_0^∞ f_a(t)t^{s−1}dt (Theorem 2.4, analytically continued). Then L(f_a, s) = (1 − a^{1−s})ζ(s) for all s ∈ C, s ≠ 1, and L(f_a, ·) is entire (the zero of 1 − a^{1−s} at s = 1 cancels the pole of ζ; L(f_a,1) = log a).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-mellin-gamma-zeta ('For a>0 and Re(s)>1, mellin(g_a,s)=Γ(s)(1−a^(1−s))ζ(s)'), .../smoothed-mellin-normalized-halfplane, .../smoothed-mellin-zeta-comparison ('For a>0 and every s∈ℂ with s≠1, L_a(s)=(1−a^(1−s))ζ(s)'), .../smoothed-kernel-mellin-entire, .../smoothed-mellin-value-one ('L_a(1)=log(a)'). Mathlib defines riemannZeta via Hurwitz/theta functions (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean), not as the Mellin transform of 1/(e^t − 1); no such identity in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Lemma 4.2(b): derivatives f_a^{(k)}(0) = (−1)^k(1 − a^{1+k})ζ(−k)
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p. For every integer k ≥ 0, f_a^{(k)}(0) = (−1)^k(1 − a^{1+k})ζ(−k) (= (1 − a^{k+1})B_{k+1}/(k+1)).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-kernel-origin-derivatives ('For every real a and every n≥0, h_a^(n)(0)=(1−a^(n+1))B_(n+1)/(n+1) in ℝ') together with .../smoothed-value-complex ('the complex image of the rational number (1−a^(k+1)) B_(k+1)/(k+1) equals (−1)^k (1−a^(k+1)) ζ(−k)'), and .../smoothed-kernel-mellin-values ('normalizedMellinContinuation(g_a,−n)=(−1)^n(1−a^(n+1))B_(n+1)/(n+1)'). The source's proof ('calculations similar to those in the proof of Lemma 2.7') goes through Theorem 2.4: L(f_a,−k) = (−1)^k f_a^{(k)}(0). Checked: k = 0 gives f_a(0) = (a−1)/2 = (1−a)ζ(0).

items.name: The power series F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1)
items.statement: For an integer a prime to p (in fact any a ∈ Z_p^×), F_a(T) := 1/T − a/((1 + T)^a − 1). A priori a Laurent series/rational function; the poles at T = 0 cancel: with (1+T)^a − 1 = aT(1 + T g(T)), g(T) = Σ_{n≥2} a^{−1}C(a,n)T^{n−2} ∈ Z_p[[T]], one has F_a(T) = g(T)/(1 + T g(T)) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4), with constant term (a − 1)/2.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/smoothed-series ('For a with unit image u in R, define F_a=b_a·q_a⁻¹ in R[[T]] ... This constructs the pole cancellation integrally before any rational comparison'), .../smoothing-denominator (q_a with coefficients C(a,n+1), 'the integral quotient of (1+T)^a−1 by T'), .../series-fraction-comparison ('f(F_a)=1/f(T)−a/((1+f(T))^a−1)'), .../series-constant; for a ∈ Z_p^×: .../padic-smoothing-series ('Define F_u=b_u·PowerSeries.invOfUnit(q_u,u) in Z[[T]] for every u∈U'). Stage L1: 'construct F_a(T)=1/T − a/((1+T)^a−1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] by cancellation in power series, not by pretending that T is invertible'. Generic Mathlib power-series API (PowerSeries.mk, invOfUnit) only.

items.name: Lemma 4.3 and (4-1): f_a^{(k)}(0) = (∂^k F_a)(0), ∂ = (1+T)d/dT
items.statement: Under the substitution e^t = 1 + T, d/dt becomes ∂ = (1 + T)d/dT; precisely f_a(t) = F_a(e^t − 1) and d/dt[G(e^t − 1)] = (∂G)(e^t − 1) for power series G. Hence for a positive integer a prime to p and every k ≥ 0, f_a^{(k)}(0) = (∂^k F_a)(0).  (4-1)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/exp-conjugacy ('D(F(h))=(∂F)(h), where h=exp(T)−1 and F(h)=PowerSeries.subst h F'), .../exp-iterate, .../exp-coefficient ('constantCoeff(∂^[k] F)=k! coeff_k(F(h))'); DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/series-exp-bernoulli ('X F_a(E−1)=B−B_a in R[[X]]'), .../series-exp-coefficients, .../smoothed-series-euler-values ('constantCoeff(∂^[k] F_a)=algebraMap ℚ R ((1−a^(k+1))B_(k+1)/(k+1))'); DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-kernel-formal-derivatives ('h_a^(k)(0)=algebraMap ℚ ℝ c_(a,k)') compares the real-analytic and formal sides. Not in any library.

items.name: Proposition 4.4: F_a ∈ Z_p[[T]]
items.statement: Let a be an integer prime to p. Then F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) lies in Z_p[[T]]. Proof (corrected sign): (1+T)^a − 1 = aT(1 + Tg(T)) with g ∈ Z_p[[T]] because a ∈ Z_p^×, so F_a(T) = (1/T)(1 − (1 + Tg)^{−1}) = −(1/T)Σ_{n≥1}(−T)^n g(T)^n = g(T)/(1 + Tg(T)) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (the printed display omits the minus sign; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E25).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/smoothed-series with .../denominator-unit ('If a is a unit in R, then q_a is a unit in R[[T]]'), .../series-cancellation ('q_a F_a=b_a'), .../series-cleared-equation ('Tq_a F_a=q_a−a'), .../series-uniqueness, .../series-fraction-comparison, .../smoothing-geometric-denominator, .../smoothing-geometric-cancellation; ColemanIntegration:L3/rotated-smoothing-denominator and .../rotated-smoothed-coefficient-bound give the rotated version. The statement holds for every integer a prime to p (negative ones included); only the complex Lemma 4.2 needs a > 0.

items.name: Definition 4.5: the measure µ_a
items.statement: For an integer a prime to p, µ_a is the unique measure on Z_p (µ_a ∈ Λ(Z_p) = Z_p[[T]], Z_p-valued) whose Mahler transform is F_a(T), i.e. A_{µ_a} = F_a (Theorem 3.25 and Proposition 4.4).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/smoothed-measure ('define μ_a in the existing measure carrier D(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) as the inverse Amice transform of F_a over ℤ_p'), .../measure-amice, .../measure-mahler, .../measure-uniqueness; all units: .../padic-smoothed-measure ('μ_u=(AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv)⁻¹(F_u)'). The inverse transform exists in Mathlib: mathlib:AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:156, `D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧`) and mathlib:AbstractMeasure.invTransform (line 128); only F_a is missing, so µ_a = amiceTransformEquiv.symm F_a once F_a is built.

items.name: Proposition 4.6: moments of µ_a on Z_p
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p. For every integer k ≥ 0, ∫_{Z_p} x^k·µ_a = (−1)^k(1 − a^{k+1})ζ(−k) (= (1 − a^{k+1})B_{k+1}/(k+1) ∈ Q). Proof: Corollary 3.30 (∫x^k·µ = (∂^k A_µ)(0)), A_{µ_a} = F_a, (4-1) and Lemma 4.2.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/measure-ordinary-moment ('For p prime, p∤a and every k≥0, the image in ℚ_p of μ_a(x↦x^k) equals algebraMap ℚ ℚ_p ((1−a^(k+1)) B_(k+1)/(k+1))'), .../smoothed-measure-formal-values, .../smoothed-value-integral; the comparison with ζ(−k) is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-value-complex. Corollary 3.30 (chunk B1) is PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/ordinary-moment-exp. The packet proves the rational identity formally (no complex analysis), also for all a ∈ Z_p^× (DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/padic-smoothed-ordinary-moments).

items.name: ψ commutes with σ_a
items.statement: For a ∈ Z_p^×, the operators σ_a (∫f(x)·σ_a(µ) = ∫f(ax)·µ; on Mahler transforms A ↦ A((1+T)^a − 1)) and ψ (∫f(x)·ψ(µ) = ∫_{pZ_p} f(p^{−1}x)·µ) on measures on Z_p commute: ψ∘σ_a = σ_a∘ψ.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.7 (printed p. 137, PDF 38); operators from §3.5.5 (printed p. 128, PDF 29)
items.note: Asserted without proof in the source (immediate: 1_{pZ_p}(ax) = 1_{pZ_p}(x) for a a unit). LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/distribution-operations: '... σ_a commuting with φ and ψ ...' (for distributions, hence measures); stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 ('translations and dilations; ... psi'). Related L2 nodes: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/amice-dilation ('A(map(d_a,mu))=S_a(A(mu))'), .../unit-restriction-dilation, .../unit-dilation-psi-kernel ('If a is a unit of Z and psiSeries(F)=0, then psiSeries(S_a(F))=0') — the kernel statement only, not full commutation.

items.name: Partial-fraction identity p^{−1}Σ_{ξ∈µ_p} 1/((1+T)ξ − 1) = 1/((1+T)^p − 1)
items.statement: In the field of fractions (e.g. Q_p(µ_p)(T)), p^{−1}Σ_{ξ∈µ_p} 1/((1 + T)ξ − 1) = 1/((1 + T)^p − 1) = φ(1/T). Equivalently, for a characteristic-0 field K containing a primitive p-th root of unity ζ and y ∈ K with y^p ≠ 1: Σ_{i<p} 1/(ζ^i y − 1) = p/(y^p − 1).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/root-partial-fractions ('For a characteristic-zero field K, ζ primitive of order p and y^p≠1, Σ_{i<p}1/(ζ^i y−1)=p/(y^p−1)'), .../root-denominator-nonzero; DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/smoothing-root-average (the smoothed combination). Verified independently: Σ_η η/(Y − η) = Y·pY^{p−1}/(Y^p − 1) − p = p/(Y^p − 1) with η = ξ^{−1}. Not in any library (searched Mathlib for sums over roots of unity of 1/(ζ^i y − 1): none).

items.name: Lemma 4.7: ψ(µ_a) = µ_a
items.statement: Let a be an integer prime to p. Then ψ(µ_a) = µ_a, i.e. ψ(F_a) = F_a in Z_p[[T]]. (Proof, repaired: by (3-9) and the partial-fraction identity, applied to F_a itself, φ∘ψ(F_a) = p^{−1}Σ_{ξ∈µ_p}F_a((1+T)ξ − 1) = 1/((1+T)^p − 1) − a/((1+T)^{pa} − 1) = φ(F_a), using that ξ ↦ ξ^a permutes µ_p; then injectivity of φ. The printed proof applies ψ and σ_a to 1/T ∉ Z_p[[T]] separately; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E26.)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/measure-psi-fixed ('ψ(μ_a)=μ_a in D(ℤ_p,ℤ_p)'), .../series-psi-fixed ('ψ_B(F_a)=F_a in ℤ_p[[T]]'), .../series-phi-psi-fixed ('φ(ψ_B(F_a))=φ(F_a) ... ψ_B is the exact bounded integral Amice-transported operator'), .../smoothing-root-average; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/rational-root-average ('For ... integral F satisfying QF=P, one has p·J(φ(psiSeries F))=Σ_{i<p}P(ζ^iY−1)/Q(ζ^iY−1) in Frac(ℂ_p[[T]])') is exactly the domain repair; all units: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/padic-measure-psi-fixed.

items.name: Proposition 4.8: restriction to Z_p^× removes the Euler factor
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p. For every integer k ≥ 0, ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·µ_a = (−1)^k(1 − p^k)(1 − a^{k+1})ζ(−k)  (4-2). Proof: Res_{Z_p^×} = 1 − φ∘ψ (3-8), ψ(µ_a) = µ_a, and ∫x^k·φ(µ) = p^k∫x^k·µ.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/unit-smoothed-moment ('For k≥0, the image of ρ_a(x^k) in ℚ_p is (1−p^k)(1−a^(k+1))B_(k+1)/(k+1)'), .../unit-smoothed-measure (ρ_a = Eμ_a, unit restriction), .../unit-smoothed-difference ('ρ_a=μ_a−φμ_a'), .../unit-smoothed-euler ('ρ_a(x↦x^k)=(1−p^k)μ_a(x↦x^k)'), .../unit-smoothed-integral; ζ(−k)-form via DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0/smoothed-value-complex. Checked: the proof is correct as printed.

items.name: Definition 4.9: θ_a = [a] − [1] ∈ Λ(Z_p^×)
items.statement: For an integer a prime to p, θ_a ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) is the element [a] − [1] (difference of Dirac measures on Z_p^×); for every k ≥ 0 (in particular k > 0), ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·θ_a = a^k − 1.
items.note: Used as θ_g = δ_g − δ_1 in DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-fraction-clearing and .../arithmetic-pseudomeasure; Dirac map PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/dirac-hom; its moments by .../character-integral-algebra-hom. Mathlib has the Dirac measure mathlib:AbstractMeasure.dirac (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:93, `def dirac (x : X) : D(X, R)`), so θ_a = dirac a − dirac 1 in D(ℤ_[p]ˣ, ℤ_[p]) is expressible, but the ring Λ(Z_p^×) (convolution) is not in the library; hence planned.

items.name: Multiplication by x^{−1} on measures on Z_p^× (4-3)
items.statement: For a measure µ on Z_p^× define x^{−1}µ by ∫_{Z_p^×} f(x)·x^{−1}µ := ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{−1}f(x)·µ for continuous f (well defined since x ↦ x^{−1} is continuous on Z_p^× with |x^{−1}| = 1, so x^{−1}µ is again an O_L-valued measure).  (4-3)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/inverse-weight ('Define J=inverseWeight p : D→ₗ[Z]D by J=weight ι, where ι:C(Z,Z) bundles the existing PadicInt.inv ... (Jμ)(f)=μ(ιf)'), .../inverse-weight-evaluation, .../inverse-weight-support, .../inverse-weight-unique ('If μ∈D satisfies ψμ=0, there exists a unique ν∈D with ψν=0 and Wν=μ'), .../inverse-mahler (Amice side); LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1/division-by-x-and-primitives ('For μ supported on ℤ_p^× there is a unique x^{−1}μ supported on ℤ_p^×'). Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2: 'inversion of multiplication by x on units'. The source's remark (Remark 12.7) is outside this chunk. Multiplication of a Mathlib AbstractMeasure by a continuous function is not in Mathlib 082e2d3 (Measure/Basic.lean has dirac, map, products only).

items.name: Moments of x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}µ_a
items.statement: Let a be a positive integer prime to p. For every integer k ≥ 1, ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}(µ_a) = ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{k−1}·µ_a = (−1)^k(a^k − 1)(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1 − k). (The source writes x^{−1}µ_a for x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}µ_a.)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/numerator-moment ('For every integer k≥1, the image of ν_a(x^k) in ℚ_p equals (1−p^(k−1))(1−a^k)B_k/k'), .../numerator-moment-shift ('ν_a(x^(k+1))=ρ_a(x^k)'), .../smoothed-numerator ('ν_a := Jμ_a ... x⁻¹ times the unit-restricted smoothing measure'), .../intrinsic-numerator-moment (on the unit group). Checked from (4-2) with k−1: (−1)^{k−1}(1−p^{k−1})(1−a^k)ζ(1−k) = (−1)^k(a^k−1)(1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k).

items.name: Definition 4.10: the p-adic zeta function ζ_p = x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}µ_a / θ_a
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); let a be a positive integer that is a topological generator of Z_p^× (the source says 'a topological generator of Z_p^×'; µ_a and θ_a were defined for integers a prime to p). Then θ_a is a non-zero-divisor of Λ(Z_p^×) (Lemma 3.36(ii)) and ζ_p := x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}(µ_a)/θ_a ∈ Q(Z_p^×), where x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}(µ_a) ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) (viewed as a measure on Z_p^×).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure ('Choose a∈U with value p+1. Define ζ_p as mk′(λ_a,θ_a), with its all-unit membership proof, in the existing PM'), with λ_a = .../intrinsic-numerator (x^{−1}Res µ_a on the unit group) and .../arithmetic-pseudomeasure-regular-parameter ('For every u∈U with θ_u∈nonZeroDivisors M, ζ_p=mk′(λ_u,θ_u) in Q') — so the source's choice (a topological generator, regular by Lemma 3.36(ii)) gives the same element. Difference: the packet's base parameter p+1 is regular but not a topological generator, and the pseudomeasure property is proved via .../arithmetic-fraction-clearing rather than Lemma 3.38. Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1: 'Define the numerator x^−1 Res(mu_a). Divide by [a]−1 only in the total quotient ring, proving regularity and independence of the smoothing parameter.'

items.name: Proposition 4.11(a): ζ_p is a pseudomeasure
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); for a as in Definition 4.10, ζ_p = x^{−1}Res_{Z_p^×}(µ_a)/θ_a ∈ Q(Z_p^×) is a pseudomeasure, i.e. ([g] − [1])ζ_p ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for all g ∈ Z_p^× (by Lemma 3.38).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-fraction-clearing ('for every g∈U, alg(θ_g)·mk′(λ_a,θ_a)=alg(λ_g) in Q'), .../arithmetic-pseudomeasure-clearing ('For every g∈U, alg(θ_g)ζ_p=alg(λ_g) in Q'), .../arithmetic-pseudomeasure-numerator; derived from the cross-numerator identity .../padic-intrinsic-cross ('(δ_v−δ_1)*λ_u=(δ_u−δ_1)*λ_v') rather than from Lemma 3.38 — a stronger, explicit statement (numerator of ([g]−[1])ζ_p is λ_g).

items.name: Proposition 4.11(b): ζ_p is independent of a
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); if a, b are two positive integers that are topological generators of Z_p^×, then x^{−1}Res(µ_a)/θ_a = x^{−1}Res(µ_b)/θ_b in Q(Z_p^×) (both are pseudomeasures with the same positive moments, so Lemma 3.36(iii) applies).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure-regular-parameter ('For every u∈U with θ_u∈nonZeroDivisors M, ζ_p=mk′(λ_u,θ_u) in Q') — stronger (every regular unit parameter, not only integer generators); proved algebraically from .../padic-intrinsic-cross rather than via moments. Also .../arithmetic-pseudomeasure-unique. The source's argument (moments + Lemma 3.36(iii)) is PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-pseudomoment-separation.

items.name: Trivial zeros and ζ(0): ζ(1−k) = 0 for odd k ≥ 3, ζ(0) = −1/2
items.statement: For every odd integer k ≥ 3, ζ(1 − k) = 0 (trivial zeros ζ(−2m) = 0, m ≥ 1); and ζ(0) = −1/2 ≠ 0. (Used, in corrected form, to remove the sign (−1)^k in Proposition 4.11: the printed 'ζ(1 − k) ≠ 0 if and only if k is even' fails at k = 1; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E27.)
items.locator: §4.3, end of proof of Proposition 4.11 (printed p. 139, PDF 40)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:173 `theorem riemannZeta_neg_two_mul_nat_add_one (n : ℕ) : riemannZeta (-2 * (n + 1)) = 0` (same statement, k = 2n+3); line 151 `theorem riemannZeta_zero : riemannZeta 0 = -1 / 2`. Nonvanishing of ζ(1 − k) for even k (B_k ≠ 0), also asserted by the source, is not needed for the argument and was not searched further. Packet: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-odd-moments ('If k is odd, then M_k(ζ_p)=0, including k=1 and p=2').

items.name: Proposition 4.11(c): interpolation property of ζ_p
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); for every integer k > 0, ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·ζ_p = (1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1 − k). Proof: by (3-11) with g = a (a^k ≠ 1) and the moments of x^{−1}Res µ_a, ∫x^k·ζ_p = (a^k − 1)^{−1}(−1)^k(a^k − 1)(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) = (−1)^k(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1 − k); the sign is harmless because ζ(1−k) = 0 for odd k ≥ 3 and 1 − p^{k−1} = 0 for k = 1.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-positive-bernoulli ('For every k>0, M_k(ζ_p)=−(1−p^(k−1))·alg_Q,Q_p(B_k/k)'), .../arithmetic-euler-zeta-comparison, .../arithmetic-positive-interpolation, .../arithmetic-odd-moments; moments computed through PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-positive-pseudomoment and .../actual-pseudomoment-numerator. Consistency checked: −(1−p^{k−1})B_k/k = (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for k ≥ 2 by ζ(1−k) = −B_k/k, and both sides vanish at k = 1.

items.name: Uniqueness in Theorem 4.1
items.statement: p is an odd prime (the paper constructs ζ_p 'for odd p', §2.2.4, printed p. 110); if λ, λ′ ∈ Q(Z_p^×) are pseudomeasures with ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·λ = ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·λ′ for all k > 0, then λ = λ′ (apply Lemma 3.36(iii) to λ − λ′); in particular ζ_p is the unique pseudomeasure with the interpolation property of Theorem 4.1.
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.1 after Proposition 4.11 (printed p. 139, PDF 40)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-interpolation-unique ('If z∈PM satisfies M_k(z)=−(1−p^(k−1))alg(B_k/k) for all k>0, then z=ζ_p'); PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-pseudomoment-separation (linearity of the moments on the pseudomeasure module is part of the admissible-evaluation construction).

items.name: Dirichlet character of p-power conductor as a locally constant function on Z_p
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ of conductor p^n (n≥0), regard χ as the locally constant function x↦χ(x mod p^n) on Z_p^× (Section 2.4.2), extended to Z_p by zero on pZ_p when n≥1 (for n=0, χ=1 is the constant function 1 on Z_p, cf. the remark after (5-6)). In particular χ is constant on each coset c+p^nZ_p and vanishes on pZ_p when n≥1.
items.locator: §5.1, Theorem 5.1 (“seen as a locally constant character of Z_p^×”), (5-1) and proof of Theorem 5.1 (“χ is 0 on pZ_p”), printed pp. 139–143 (PDF 40–44); n=0 convention in the parenthesis after (5-6), printed p. 146 (PDF 47)
items.note: Packet nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/prime-power-character (“Construct w_n,χ∈C(Z,R) by w_n,χ(z)=χ(red_n z)”; hypotheses: “A character at modulus1 lifts to the constant function1; a principal character at a positive p-power level lifts to the unit indicator”), L2/prime-power-character-support (“For n≥1 and every nonunit z∈Z, w_n,χ(z)=0”) and L2/prime-power-character-level. Mathlib has DirichletCharacter and PadicInt.toZModPow but no bundled continuous lift to C(Z_p,R); Tau Ceti has none (searched TauCeti/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean and all files mentioning DirichletCharacter).

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (interpolation of ζ_p at characters of p-power conductor)
items.statement: Let p be odd, n≥1 and χ a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor p^n, viewed as a locally constant character of Z_p^×. Then for every integer k>0, ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)x^k · ζ_p = L(χ,1−k). (The pseudomeasure integral is defined by (3-11) because the character x↦χ(x)x^k is nontrivial; no Euler factor appears since χ(p)=0.)
items.locator: §5.1, Theorem 5.1 (printed p. 139, PDF 40); proof on printed p. 143 (PDF 44)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2 (“Construct the twist by a p-power conductor character and prove the roots-of-unity restriction formula and Gauss-sum computation … This covers RJW Theorems 5.1 and 5.7”). The packet realises the ingredients (twisted-smoothed-measure, twisted-smoothed-gauss-fractions) but has NO node for the endpoint: its coverage entry for L2 lists as remaining “derive the pure p-power interpolation formula, and compare the complex smoothed Gauss kernel and Mellin normalization”. The complex side L(χ,s) is Mathlib DirichletCharacter.LFunction (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:61); the p-adic statement is in neither library (no p-adic measures/pseudomeasures in Tau Ceti: grep for Mahler/Amice/Iwasawa in TauCeti/ is empty).

items.name: Twist of a measure by a character, μ ↦ μ_χ (5-1)
items.statement: For a measure μ on Z_p and χ of conductor p^n (as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/192), μ_χ is the measure on Z_p with ∫_{Z_p} f(x)·μ_χ = ∫_{Z_p} χ(x)f(x)·μ for all continuous f. If n≥1, μ_χ is supported on Z_p^× (Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_χ)=μ_χ), since χ vanishes on pZ_p. Since χ is constant mod p^n, μ_χ = Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ(c) Res_{c+p^nZ_p}(μ) (n≥1).
items.locator: §5.1, equation (5-1) and the following sentence (printed p. 140, PDF 41); decomposition in the proof of Lemma 5.4 (printed p. 141, PDF 42)
items.note: Generic operation: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/weight (“Define AbstractMeasure.weight g … by (weight g μ)(f)=μ(gf)”), residue restrictions L2/residue-restriction and L2/residue-restriction-partition (“the sum of P_(n,a)μ over all a∈ZMod(p^n) equals μ”). Specialisations: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-smoothed-measure (τ_n,χ,a=weight(w_n,χ)(I_R μ_a)), L2/twisted-smoothed-support (“For n≥1, E_Rτ_n,χ,a=τ_n,χ,a”) and L2/twisted-tame-measure (μ_η twisted) — support is noded only for these two specific measures. Mathlib has the carrier AbstractMeasure (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:40) with dirac/map but no weighting or restriction.

items.name: Gauss sum G(χ) (Definition 5.2; extended to conductors D and Dp^n in §5.2)
items.statement: Let χ be a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N (Definition 5.2: N=p^n, n≥1; §5.2 and Lemma 5.12 use the same definition for N=D and N=Dp^n). With ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity in Q̄_p (Definition 5.2 fixes a compatible system (ε_{p^n}) with ε_{p^{n+1}}^p=ε_{p^n}; after fixing Q̄_p≅C one may take ε_N=e^{2πi/N}), G(χ) := Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} χ(c) ε_N^c.
items.locator: §5.1, Definition 5.2 (printed p. 140, PDF 41); extension “replacing the power of p by D” in the proof of Theorem 5.7 (printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:72 `def gaussSum (χ : MulChar R R') (ψ : AddChar R R') : R' := ∑ a, χ a * ψ a`; with R=ZMod N, χ a DirichletCharacter (=MulChar (ZMod N) R'), and ψ=AddChar.zmodChar N hε (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:139, zmodChar_apply: a ↦ ζ^a.val). The sum over all of ZMod N equals the sum over units because χ vanishes on nonunits — same statement. The compatibility ε_{p^{n+1}}^p=ε_{p^n} is not used anywhere in §5 (each formula is independent of the choice of primitive root, cf. the invariance G(χ,ε^u)=χ(u)^{-1}G(χ,ε)). The packet uses exactly G=gaussSum(χ⁻¹,AddChar.zmodChar …) (e.g. DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-gauss-series).

items.name: Remark 5.3(i): G(χ)G(χ^{-1}) = χ(−1)p^n
items.statement: For χ primitive of conductor p^n (n≥1), G(χ)G(χ^{-1}) = χ(−1)p^n. (Used in the same form G(η)G(η^{-1})=η(−1)D for η primitive of conductor D, proof of Theorem 5.7; in particular G(χ)≠0.) Quoted from Diamond–Shurman [30, §4.3].
items.locator: §5.1, Remark 5.3(i) (printed p. 140, PDF 41); used in the proof of Lemma 5.4 (printed p. 141) and in the proof of Theorem 5.7 (printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: Library covers only the prime-modulus case n=1: Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:205 `gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_pow_orderOf_sub_one` (R a finite field, χ≠1, ψ primitive: g(χ)g(χ^(ord−1)) = χ(−1)·#R) and :188 `gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_eq_card`. Nothing for ZMod(p^n), n≥2, or composite N in Mathlib (DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean only has gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive and vanishing lemmas) or Tau Ceti (only Multiquadratic/Cyclotomic/GaussSum.lean, quadratic case). Planned by stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: “Construct generalized Bernoulli numbers, primitive-character Gauss sums, their nonvanishing and inversion formula”. No packet node realises it: the L2/L3 nodes carry “G≠0” as an explicit hypothesis (“Gauss nonvanishing is an explicit hypothesis, with its general theory retained by ModularForms”, L3/complex-gauss-log-integral). Checked numerically for p=5, n=2, χ of order 20: G(χ)G(χ^{-1}) = −25 = χ(−1)·25.

items.name: Remark 5.3(ii): G(χ) = χ(a) Σ_c χ(c) ε^{ac}
items.statement: For χ primitive of conductor p^n and any a∈Z_p^×, G(χ) = χ(a) Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ(c) ε_{p^n}^{ac}. (The proof of Lemma 5.4 also uses, silently, that Σ_{c}χ(c)ε_{p^n}^{bc}=0 when p∣b, which holds because χ is primitive.)
items.locator: §5.1, Remark 5.3(ii) (printed p. 140, PDF 41); used in the proof of Lemma 5.4 (printed p. 141, PDF 42)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:76 `gaussSum_mulShift (χ : MulChar R R') (ψ : AddChar R R') (a : Rˣ) : χ a * gaussSum χ (mulShift ψ a) = gaussSum χ ψ` — exactly (ii) with R=ZMod(p^n), a the unit a mod p^n. The nonunit case used in the proof of Lemma 5.4 is Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean:57 `gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (a : ZMod N) : gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ e`, valid for all a (0 for nonunits), stated for primitive Dirichlet characters.

items.name: Lemma 5.4 (Mahler transform of a twisted measure)
items.statement: Let χ be primitive of conductor p^n (n≥1) and μ∈Λ(Z_p) (over O_L with L∋ε_{p^n} and the values of χ). Then A_{μ_χ}(T) = G(χ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ(c)^{-1} A_μ((1+T)ε_{p^n}^c − 1).
items.locator: §5.1, Lemma 5.4 (printed p. 140, PDF 41); proof printed p. 141 (PDF 42)
items.note: Realised only for μ=μ_a: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-smoothed-gauss (“τ_n,χ,a=G⁻¹ • Σ_(c∈ZMod(q)) χ⁻¹(c) • μ_(n,e,c,a)”, G=gaussSum(χ⁻¹,e), explicit G≠0) and L2/twisted-smoothed-gauss-amice (the Amice-transform form). The mechanism is generic in μ: L2/prime-power-character-gauss (“w_n,χ(z)=G⁻¹ Σ_c χ⁻¹(c) β_c(z), including when z is a nonunit”, β_c(z)=ε^{c·z}) plus the fact that weighting by β_c substitutes (1+T)ε^c−1 in the Amice transform — noded only for μ=μ_a (DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/smoothed-additive-rational, L2/smoothed-additive-fractions); the generic PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/root-translation nodes treat only p-th roots of unity (ζ^p=1, for ψ), not p^n-th. The packet proves it by Fourier-expanding χ instead of the paper’s route through (3-5) (PMIA L2/residue-restriction-amice-coefficient); both give the same identity. No node states it for an arbitrary μ.

items.name: The twisted smoothed measure μ_{χ,a} and its Mahler transform F_{χ,a}
items.statement: μ_{χ,a} := (μ_a)_χ, with A_{μ_{χ,a}}(T) = F_{χ,a}(T) = G(χ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ(c)^{-1} [ 1/((1+T)ε_{p^n}^c − 1) − a/((1+T)^a ε_{p^n}^{ac} − 1) ] ∈ O_L[[T]] (χ primitive of conductor p^n, n≥1; a as in the standing notation). Each bracketed term lies in L[[T]] because ε^c≠1 and ε^{ac}≠1.
items.locator: §5.1, display after the proof of Lemma 5.4 (printed p. 141, PDF 42)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-smoothed-gauss-fractions: “For e from the primitive root ε and G≠0, A_(τ_n,χ,a)=G⁻¹ • Σ_(c∈ZMod(p^n)) χ⁻¹(c) • [(C(ε^(c.val))(1+T)−1)⁻¹−C(a)((C(ε^(c.val))(1+T))^a−1)⁻¹]” with τ_n,χ,a from L2/twisted-smoothed-measure; supporting L2/smoothed-additive-root-power (“If ε_c≠1, then ε_c^a≠1”) and L2/smoothed-additive-fractions. Same statement (the node sums over all of ZMod(p^n) with zero weight at nonunits). The paper labels the measure μ_{a,χ} in the diagram and μ_{χ,a} in the text.

items.name: The complex kernel f_{χ,a}(t)
items.statement: For t≥0, f_{χ,a}(t) := G(χ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ(c)^{-1} [ 1/(e^t ε_{p^n}^c − 1) − a/(e^{at} ε_{p^n}^{ac} − 1) ] (so that F_{χ,a}(e^t−1)=f_{χ,a}(t)). It is a C^∞ function on R_{≥0} (indeed real-analytic on R, since ε^c≠1) all of whose derivatives decay exponentially, so Theorem 2.4 applies to it; for t>0, 1/(e^tε^c−1) = Σ_{k≥1} e^{−kt}ε^{−kc}.
items.locator: §5.1, display before Lemma 5.5 (printed p. 141, PDF 42); geometric expansion in the proof of Lemma 5.5 (printed p. 142, PDF 43)
items.note: No node for the smoothed p-power kernel. The unsmoothed analogue for any nonprincipal complex character η mod D>0 (no p-coprimality needed on the complex side) is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-complex-kernel with L2/complex-gauss-kernel-comparison (“tameComplexKernel η t=Sε(t)”, S the Gauss expression −G⁻¹Σ η⁻¹(a)/(ε^a e^t−1)), L2/tame-complex-regularity, L2/tame-complex-derivative-decay; one has f_{χ,a}(t) = −S_χ(t) + aχ(a)S_χ(at) with S_χ that kernel at modulus p^n. The L2 coverage entry lists “compare the complex smoothed Gauss kernel and Mellin normalization” as remaining. The Mellin machinery of Theorem 2.4 is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 (normalized-mellin-continuation, normalized-mellin-negative-values).

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (first part): L(f_{χ,a},s) = χ(−1)(1−χ(a)a^{1−s})L(χ,s)
items.statement: With L(f,s)=Γ(s)^{-1}∫_0^∞ f(t)t^{s−1}dt continued to C as in Theorem 2.4, L(f_{χ,a},s) = χ(−1)(1−χ(a)a^{1−s}) L(χ,s) for all s∈C (χ primitive of conductor p^n, n≥1, so L(χ,s) is entire). Key steps: Σ_{c}χ(c)^{-1}ε^{−akc} = χ(−ak)G(χ^{-1}); for Re(s)≫0, L(f_{χ,a},s) = Γ(s)^{-1}∫_0^∞ Σ_{k≥1}χ(−k)(e^{−kt} − aχ(a)e^{−akt})t^{s−1}dt = (1−χ(a)a^{1−s})Σ_{k≥1}χ(−k)k^{−s}.
items.locator: §5.1, Lemma 5.5 (printed p. 141, PDF 42) and its proof (printed p. 142, PDF 43)
items.note: Partially realised: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-complex-mellin-comparison (“For every s∈ℂ, normalizedMellinContinuation(f,s)=−η(−1)η.LFunction(s)” for nonprincipal η mod D>0, primitivity not required, p not involved) applies verbatim at modulus p^n to the unsmoothed kernel; with f_{χ,a}(t) = −S_χ(t)+aχ(a)S_χ(at) and Mathlib `mellin_comp_mul_left` (Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:133: mellin (fun t ↦ f (a*t)) s = a^(−s) • mellin f s) this gives the lemma, but no node states the smoothed identity (L2 coverage: remaining). Stage text: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2 “including the detailed calculations left as exercises”. The printed proof has slips (missing factor a; χ(−1) counted twice) — see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E29; the statement is correct (numerically checked for p=5, χ of order 4, a=2).

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (second part) and (5-2): values f_{χ,a}^{(k)}(0)
items.statement: For k≥0, f_{χ,a}^{(k)}(0) = (−1)^k χ(−1)(1−χ(a)a^{k+1}) L(χ,−k) (5-2); consequently f_{χ,a}^{(k)}(0) = −(1−χ(a)a^{k+1})L(χ,−k) if χ(−1)(−1)^k = −1 and f_{χ,a}^{(k)}(0) = 0 if χ(−1)(−1)^k = 1. The vanishing comes from the parity f_{χ,a}(−t) = −χ(−1)f_{χ,a}(t), proved from 1/(e^{−t}ε^c−1) = −1 − 1/(e^tε^{−c}−1) and c↦−c.
items.locator: §5.1, Lemma 5.5 (printed pp. 141–142, PDF 42–43), (5-2) and the parity argument (printed p. 142, PDF 43)
items.note: Unsmoothed tame analogue: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-complex-mellin-values (“For k≥0, normalizedMellinContinuation(f,−k)=(−1)^k b_(η,k)”) and L2/tame-complex-origin-derivatives (“f^(k)(0)=b_(η,k)”) with L0/normalized-mellin-negative-values (“L_f(−n)=(−1)^n D_n f(0)”). No node for the smoothed p-power kernel or for its parity. Numerically checked (p=5, χ of order 4, a=2, k=0..5): (5-2) holds.

items.name: Remark 5.6: trivial zeros L(χ,−k)=0 when χ(−1)(−1)^k=1
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character χ of modulus N>1 (here: conductor p^n, n≥1) and k≥0 with χ(−1)(−1)^k = 1, L(χ,−k) = 0.
items.note: Covered case by case in Mathlib: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:110 `Even.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat (hχ : Even χ) (n) [NeZero n] : LFunction χ (−(2*n)) = 0` (χ even, k even ≥2); :116 `Odd.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_sub_one (hχ : Odd χ) (n) : LFunction χ (−(2*n) − 1) = 0` (χ odd, k odd); k=0, χ even: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean:271 `LFunction_apply_zero_of_even (hΦ : Φ.Even) : LFunction Φ 0 = −Φ 0 / 2`, and χ(0)=0 for N>1 (0 is a nonunit). No single lemma, but the statement is fully covered.

items.name: Algebraic comparison of complex L-values and p-adic integrals
items.statement: The equalities of §5 between p-adic integrals and complex values L(χ,1−k) (Theorems 5.1, 5.7, 5.17, 5.20, Lemmas 5.9, 5.11) are meant via a fixed isomorphism Q̄_p≅C (Definition 5.2): L(χ,−k) is algebraic, lying in Q(χ) (= −N^k/(k+1)·Σ_{a mod N}χ(a)B_{k+1}(a/N) for χ≠1 of modulus N), and for a rational kernel F with algebraic coefficients and f(t)=F(e^t−1), the complex Taylor derivative f^{(k)}(0) equals (∂^kF)(0), ∂=(1+T)d/dT (“under the standard transform e^t=T+1”).
items.locator: Definition 5.2 (printed p. 140, PDF 41); proof of Theorem 5.1 (printed p. 143, PDF 44); proof of Lemma 5.9 (“equating ∂ with d/dt”, printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0: “Do not use a field isomorphism C ≃ C_p to transport arbitrary complex values. Use the algebraic number containing the normalized L-value, together with explicit complex and p-adic embeddings.” Nodes: L2/tame-complex-special-values (“η.LFunction(−k)=b_(η,k)” with b_(η,k)=−D^k/(k+1)Σ η(a)B_(k+1)(a.val/D), nonprincipal η, D>0), L2/tame-special-value-comparison (separate field homomorphisms ιC, ιK), L2/complex-tame-formal-derivatives (“fη^(k)(0)=constantCoeff(∂^[k](tameSeries η hD))”). Mathlib ingredient: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/HurwitzZetaValues.lean:189 `HurwitzZeta.hurwitzZeta_neg_nat (hk : k ≠ 0)` (Bernoulli-polynomial values for k≥1 only; k=0 is a TODO there), from which the Bernoulli formula for ZMod.LFunction follows but is not a named lemma. The paper states the identification only parenthetically.

items.name: Twisted smoothed moments: ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·μ_a = −(1−χ(a)a^{k+1})L(χ,−k)
items.statement: For χ primitive of conductor p^n (n≥1) and k≥0: ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·μ_a = ∫_{Z_p}x^k·μ_{χ,a} = (∂^kF_{χ,a})(0) = f_{χ,a}^{(k)}(0) = −(1−χ(a)a^{k+1})L(χ,−k); hence ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·x^{-1}μ_a = −(1−χ(a)a^k)L(χ,1−k) for k≥1, and with ∫χ(x)x^k·θ_a = χ(a)a^k−1 = −(1−χ(a)a^k) (nonzero), Theorem 5.1 follows from (3-11).
items.note: Part of the missing endpoint of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2 (coverage: “derive the pure p-power interpolation formula”). In the case χ(−1)(−1)^k=1 the text’s appeal to Lemma 5.5 needs Remark 5.6 (L(χ,−k)=0) to give the displayed formula; (5-2) gives it directly. The untwisted analogues are DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1 nodes (padic-smoothed-ordinary-moments etc.).

items.name: Remark 5.8(1): L(η,s) is entire for η nontrivial
items.statement: For a nontrivial Dirichlet character η, L(η,s) extends to an entire function of s (so no smoothing factor a is needed for ζ_η).
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:98 `lemma differentiable_LFunction {χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N} (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : Differentiable ℂ (LFunction χ)` — same statement (LFunction is the meromorphic continuation, :61).

items.name: Theorem 5.7 (existence and interpolation of ζ_η)
items.statement: Let p be odd, D>1 an integer prime to p, and η a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor D, with values in a finite extension L/Q_p (Remark 5.8(2)). There is a measure ζ_η∈Λ(Z_p^×) (over O_L; a genuine measure, not a pseudomeasure) such that for every primitive Dirichlet character χ of conductor p^n, n≥0, and every k>0: ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)x^k·ζ_η = (1 − χη(p)p^{k−1}) L(χη,1−k), where χη is the primitive character (of conductor Dp^n) attached to the product. Construction: ζ_η := x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_η) (Definition 5.13).
items.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.7 (printed p. 143, PDF 44); proof printed pp. 144–146 (PDF 45–47)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2 states exactly this formula (“integral chi(x)x^k dzeta_eta = (1−(chi eta)(p)p^(k−1)) L(chi eta,1−k)”). Realising nodes: L2/tame-zeta-measure (ζ_η=weight(g)(Eμ_η)), L2/tame-zeta-character-common-value (“For k≥1 put b=(1−θ(p)p^(k−1))·(−N^(k−1)/k)·Σ_aθ(a)B_k(a.val/N) … Then ιC(b)=(1−θC(p)p^(k−1))L(θC,1−k), and ιK(b)=ζ_ηK(wχK x_K^k)”), L2/tame-integral-zeta-measure (O-valued), L2/tame-zeta-norm. The nodes use the product-level (possibly imprimitive) θ at N=Dp^n, whose L-value already contains the Euler factor — equal to the paper’s primitive form; they are more general (any prime p, any nonprincipal η with p∤D, χ any character mod p^n).

items.name: Theorem 5.7 (uniqueness of ζ_η)
items.statement: The measure ζ_η of Theorem 5.7 is unique: a measure on Z_p^× is determined by the values ∫_{Z_p^×}x^k·ζ (k>0) (Lemma 3.36(i)), in particular by the interpolation property.
items.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.7 “There exists a unique measure” (printed p. 143, PDF 44); uniqueness via Lemma 3.36(i) (printed p. 130, PDF 31)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/unit-positive-moment-separation (“If μ∈M satisfies μ(t_k)=0 for every k>0, then μ=0”, M=D(Z_p^×,Z_p)) — for Z_p coefficients; the O_L/K-valued version needed here is not a separate node (partial). DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-integral-zeta-unique is only uniqueness of the integral realisation of the already constructed ζ_η, not uniqueness from interpolation. The paper gives no uniqueness argument in §5.2.

items.name: The complex kernel f_η(t)
items.statement: For η primitive of conductor D>1: f_η(t) := −G(η^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/DZ)^×} η(c)^{-1}/(e^t ε_D^c − 1), a C^∞ rapidly decreasing function on R_{≥0} (indeed real-analytic on R).
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.7, display defining f_η (printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-complex-kernel (defined in finite-numerator form f(t)=−D⁻¹β(Dt)Σ_a η(a)dslope(u↦exp(a.val·u),0,t)), L2/complex-gauss-kernel-comparison (“For every real t, tameComplexKernel η t=Sε(t)”, Sε the displayed Gauss expression; assumes D>1, η primitive and explicitly G≠0), L2/complex-gauss-regularity, L2/tame-complex-derivative-decay. Same object.

items.name: The power series F_η(T) (5-3)
items.statement: F_η(T) := −G(η^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/DZ)^×} η(c)^{-1}/((1+T)ε_D^c − 1) (η primitive of conductor D>1, p∤D), so that F_η(e^t−1) = f_η(t).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-series (F_η=Q_η·q_D^{-1}, a pole-cancelled finite form, for any η and D a unit) and L2/tame-gauss-series (“If D is a unit in K, the previously defined tameSeries(η,hDK) equals S, the source normalized Gauss expression”, S=−C(G⁻¹)Σ C(η⁻¹(a))·(C(ε^(a.val))Y−1)⁻¹; hypotheses: η primitive, D>1, G≠0).

items.name: Coefficients of F_η (corrected expansion)
items.statement: F_η(T) = −G(η^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/DZ)^×} η(c)^{-1} Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^k ε_D^{kc}/(ε_D^c − 1)^{k+1} · T^k. (Printed without the sign (−1)^k; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E30.)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-gauss-coefficients: “For every n≥0, coeff_n(F_η)=−G⁻¹(−1)^nΣ_a η⁻¹(a)(ε^(a.val))^n/(ε^(a.val)−1)^(n+1)” — the corrected statement (the node records DirichletPadicLFunctions/E12, which is this paper's E30). Checked numerically for η the quadratic character mod 3: T^3-coefficient 1/9 (printed formula gives −1/9).

items.name: Integrality: F_η ∈ O_L[[T]]
items.statement: If p∤D (and L contains ε_D and the values of η), F_η ∈ O_L[[T]], because G(η^{-1}) is a p-adic unit (G(η)G(η^{-1}) = η(−1)D with p∤D, both factors algebraic integers) and ε_D^c − 1 ∈ O_L^× for c∈(Z/DZ)^× (its norm divides D: N(1−ζ_D) = Φ_D(1) ∈ {ℓ, 1}).
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.7, sentence after the expansion of F_η (printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-coefficient-bound (“If p∤D, then every coefficient f_n of F_η over an eligible normed field K has norm at most1, for every η including the principal character”) and L2/tame-integral-series — proved by a different route (finite numerator over unit denominator q_D), so the Gauss-unit and cyclotomic-unit facts are not needed there. Mathlib ingredients for the paper’s route: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/PrimitiveRoots.lean:333 `IsPrimitiveRoot.sub_one_norm_eq_eval_cyclotomic` (norm of ζ−1 is eval 1 (cyclotomic n ℤ), n>2) and Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Cyclotomic/Eval.lean:137/:42 (Φ_n(1)=1 if n is not a prime power; =p for p^k). The Gauss-unit claim needs PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/196 at modulus D (planned, DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0).

items.name: The measure μ_η ∈ Λ(Z_p) with Mahler transform F_η
items.statement: μ_η is the unique measure on Z_p (over O_L) with A_{μ_η} = F_η.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-measure (“define μ_η=boundedInvTransform(c_η) in the existing D(Z_p,K). Its Amice transform is F_η”), L2/tame-integral-measure (O-valued), L2/tame-gauss-measure (“its actual Amice transform equals S”), L2/tame-measure-unique. Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:156 `AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧` is only for Z_p coefficients (its TODO: general base rings), so the O_L version is planned (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2).

items.name: Lemma 5.9 (first part): L(f_η,s) = −η(−1)L(η,s)
items.statement: For η primitive of conductor D>1: L(f_η,s) = −η(−1)L(η,s) for all s∈C (f_η(t) = −Σ_{k≥1}η(−k)e^{−kt} for t>0).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-complex-mellin-comparison: “For every s∈ℂ, normalizedMellinContinuation(f,s)=−η(−1)η.LFunction(s)” (η≠1, primitivity not required) together with L2/complex-gauss-kernel-comparison and L2/tame-complex-positive-series (“Σ_(m≥1)−η(−1)η(m)exp(−mt) has sum f(t)”). Same statement, slightly more general.

items.name: Lemma 5.9 (second part): ∫_{Z_p}x^k·μ_η = L(η,−k)
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.9 and its proof (printed p. 144, PDF 45)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-ordinary-moments (“the actual tameMeasure … evaluated on x↦x^k equals b_(η,k)”), L2/tame-complex-special-values (“η.LFunction(−k)=b_(η,k)”), L2/tame-special-value-comparison; moments from the Amice transform: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/ordinary-moment. Checked numerically for η mod 3 (k=0..5).

items.name: Root-of-unity partial-fraction identity (5-4)
items.statement: (1/p) Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} 1/((1+T)ξε_D^c − 1) = 1/((1+T)^p ε_D^{pc} − 1); equivalently Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} 1/(ξy−1) = p/(y^p−1) for y^p≠1 in a field of characteristic 0.
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Lemma 5.10, equation (5-4) (printed pp. 144–145, PDF 45–46)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/root-partial-fractions: “For a characteristic-zero field K, ζ primitive of order p and y^p≠1, Σ_{i<p}1/(ζ^i y−1)=p/(y^p−1)” (sourced there to Lemma 4.7) — same identity, applied with y=(1+T)ε_D^c. The paper’s geometric-series justification is formal (the series do not converge T-adically) but the identity is a correct rational-function identity; not recorded as an error.

items.name: Lemma 5.10: ψ(F_η) = η(p)F_η
items.statement: For η primitive of conductor D>1 with p∤D: ψ(F_η) = η(p)F_η, i.e. ψ(μ_η) = η(p)μ_η; proof: (φ∘ψ)(F_η) = (1/p)Σ_{ξ∈μ_p}F_η((1+T)ξ−1) = η(p)φ(F_η) by (5-4) and c↦pc, then injectivity of φ.
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.10 (printed p. 144, PDF 45) and proof (printed p. 145, PDF 46)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-psi (“The existing PMIA operator on actual K-valued measures satisfies ψμ_η=η(p)μ_η”; any prime p, η≠1, p∤D, char 0; proved by a finite-residue route) and L2/tame-integral-psi. Same statement (more general). The first display of the proof has a misprint pG(η)^{-1} (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E31). Checked numerically (η mod 3, p=5) at a sample point.

items.name: Restriction of μ_η to Z_p^× and Frobenius moments
items.statement: Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_η) = (1−φ∘ψ)(μ_η) = μ_η − η(p)φ(μ_η), and ∫_{Z_p}x^k·φ(μ) = p^k∫_{Z_p}x^k·μ for any measure μ.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-unit-restriction (“For the existing ambient unit projector E, Eμ_η=μ_η−η(p)φμ_η”); PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/unit-restriction, L2/phi-evaluation (“φμ(f)=μ(f∘m_p)”), which gives the Frobenius moment formula.

items.name: Lemma 5.11: ∫_{Z_p^×}x^k·μ_η = (1−η(p)p^k)L(η,−k)
items.statement: For k≥0 (η primitive of conductor D>1, p∤D): ∫_{Z_p^×}x^k·μ_η = (1−η(p)p^k)L(η,−k).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-unit-moments (“(Eμ_η)(x↦x^k)=(1−η(p)p^k)μ_η(x↦x^k)”) and L2/tame-unit-special-value-comparison (“u=(1−η(p)p^k)b_(η,k) … Its complex image is(1−ηC(p)p^k)L(ηC,−k), and its K image is(Eμ_ηK)(x_K^k)”). Same statement.

items.name: The product character θ=χη and its conductor
items.statement: For η primitive of conductor D (p∤D) and χ primitive of conductor p^n (n≥0), θ := χη is a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor Dp^n; θ(p)=0 if n≥1 and θ(p)=η(p) if n=0.
items.locator: §5.2, sentence before (5-5) (printed p. 145, PDF 46); remark after (5-6) (printed p. 146, PDF 47)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:420 `primitive_mul` (the primitive character attached to the product, at level (mul χ₁ χ₂).conductor) and :433 `conductor_mul_dvd_lcm_conductor` (conductor of a product divides the lcm) — only the upper bound; the equality cond(χη)=cond(χ)cond(η) for coprime conductors is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (TauCeti/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean has only factorisation-through-divisor lemmas). Planned: stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2 “Define the evaluation at p using the conductor of the primitive character, not an arbitrary modulus … primitive/imprimitive comparisons”; L0 “conductor change”. The packet works with the product-level θ at N=Dp^n (L2/twisted-tame-measure hypotheses), avoiding the conductor equality.

items.name: The measure μ_θ := (μ_η)_χ (5-5)
items.statement: For θ=χη as above, μ_θ := (μ_η)_χ, i.e. ∫f·μ_θ = ∫χ(x)f(x)·μ_η (for n=0, χ=1 on Z_p and μ_θ=μ_η).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-tame-measure: “Define ν=twistedTameMeasure n χ η hD hpD=weight(wχ)μ on the existing D(Z_p,K). Its value at f is μ(wχ f).” Same construction (n≥0, χ any character mod p^n).

items.name: Lemma 5.12: Mahler transform of μ_θ
items.statement: F_θ(T) := A_{μ_θ}(T) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/Dp^nZ)^×} θ(c)^{-1}/((1+T)ε_{Dp^n}^c − 1). (Follows from Lemma 5.4 and the CRT factorisation G(θ^{-1}) = χ^{-1}(D)η^{-1}(p^n)G(χ^{-1})G(η^{-1}), valid when ε_{Dp^n} is chosen with ε_{Dp^n}^D = ε_{p^n} and ε_{Dp^n}^{p^n} = ε_D; the right side does not depend on the choice of primitive root ε_{Dp^n}.)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-tame-amice (“For hN:IsUnit(N:K), ν.amiceTransform=tameSeries θ hN”, N=Dp^n, θ product-level) combined with L2/tame-gauss-series at level N (which requires θ primitive at N, D>1 and G≠0) — the combination gives Lemma 5.12, but no single node states the Gauss form for θ; the CRT Gauss-sum factorisation is not noded (Mathlib has no multiplicativity of Gauss sums under CRT). Partial.

items.name: Twisted moments of μ_η on Z_p: ∫_{Z_p}χ(x)x^k·μ_η = L(θ,−k)
items.statement: For k≥0: ∫_{Z_p}χ(x)x^k·μ_η = ∫_{Z_p}x^k·μ_θ = L(θ,−k).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-tame-moments (“For every k≥0, ν(x_K^k)=−N^k/(k+1)·Σ_(a:ZMod N) θ(a)·B_(k+1)(a.val/N)”) with L2/tame-complex-special-values applied to θ at level N (“η.LFunction(−k)=b_(η,k)” for nonprincipal characters at any modulus) — for the product-level θ, whose L-function equals the primitive one when n≥1 (θ(p)=0 either way) and when n=0 (θ=η).

items.name: (5-6): Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_θ) = (1−θ(p)φ)μ_θ
items.statement: Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_θ) = (1−θ(p)φ)μ_θ; for n≥1 (χ nontrivial) θ(p)=0 and μ_θ is already supported on Z_p^×.
items.locator: §5.2, equation (5-6) and the following parenthesis (printed pp. 145–146, PDF 46–47)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/twisted-tame-psi: “ψν=θ(p)•ν, hence Eν=ν−θ(p)•φν” (θ product-level). Same statement. (The paper writes “if χ is nontrivial”; for a primitive χ of conductor p^n this means n≥1.)

items.name: Twisted unit moments: ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·μ_η = (1−θ(p)p^k)L(θ,−k)
items.statement: For χ primitive of conductor p^n (n≥0), θ=χη and k≥0: ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·μ_η = (1−θ(p)p^k)L(θ,−k).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-zeta-character-shift (“ζ_η(wχ x_K^(k+1))=(Eν)(x_K^k)”) with L2/twisted-tame-psi and L2/twisted-tame-moments; the combined value is the content of L2/tame-zeta-character-common-value. This display (not Lemma 5.11) is what the proof of Theorem 5.20 needs (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E33).

items.name: Definition 5.13: ζ_η := x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_η)
items.statement: ζ_η := x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_η) ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) (multiplication by x^{-1} on measures supported on Z_p^×, (4-3)); then for χ primitive of conductor p^n (n≥0) and k≥1, ∫_{Z_p^×}χ(x)x^k·ζ_η = (1−θ(p)p^{k−1})L(θ,1−k), completing Theorem 5.7.
items.locator: §5.2, Definition 5.13 and the following display (printed p. 146, PDF 47)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-zeta-measure (“Define ζ_η=weight(g)(Eμ_η) … g(x)=algebraMap Z_p K(PadicInt.inv x)”), L2/tame-zeta-weight (“weight(x_K)ζ_η=Eμ_η”), L2/tame-zeta-moment-shift, L2/tame-zeta-character-common-value; generic division by x: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/inverse-weight. Same construction.

items.name: Lemma 5.14 (p-adic exponential and logarithm on pZ_p / 1+pZ_p)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The p-adic exponential series exp(x)=Σx^n/n! converges on pZ_p (it converges exactly for v_p(x)>1/(p−1)), and log(1+y)=Σ(−1)^{n+1}y^n/n converges on pZ_p; exp and log are mutually inverse isomorphisms (pZ_p,+) ≅ (1+pZ_p,×). Quoted from Cassels [11, §12].
items.note: Stage LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1, “Deep units in mixed characteristic”: “Let K/ℚ_p be finite … Let i satisfy (p − 1) * i > e. Then the logarithm is an isomorphism of topological groups U(K,i) ≃ (𝓂[K]^i, +), with exp as its inverse” — for K=Q_p (e=1) and p odd, i=1 gives exactly this; the stage notes “The pin does not provide a ready-made local-field logarithm with the sharp domain or inverse theorems”. Searched Mathlib (NumberTheory/Padics/*, Analysis/SpecialFunctions/*; NormedSpace.exp exists but its radius over ℚ_p is not established) and Tau Ceti (Analysis/Normed/Algebra/LogOneAdd needs ContinuousSMul ℚ≥0 𝕂, which fails for ℚ_p, and its exp-inverse is real-only; no p-adic exp/log). For p=2 the statement is false on 2Z_2 (exp converges only on 4Z_2), consistent with the paper’s standing p odd.

items.name: The power map x ↦ x^s := exp(s·log x) on 1+pZ_p, s∈Z_p
items.statement: For s∈Z_p and x∈1+pZ_p (p odd), x^s := exp(s·log x) ∈ 1+pZ_p is well defined; x↦x^s is a continuous character of 1+pZ_p, (s,x)↦x^s is continuous, and it agrees with the usual power for s∈Z (this is the Z_p-module structure of 1+pZ_p).
items.locator: §5.3, Lemma 5.14 “Hence …” and the sentence after Definition 5.15 (printed pp. 146–147, PDF 47–48)
items.note: Same stage as PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/227: “U(K,i) ≃ ℤ_p^N as ℤ_p-modules” (deepUnitExpLogEquiv). Consumed by the branches of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (“Use Teichmuller decomposition to define the branches”). The packet’s L3/tame-character-value family takes continuous characters κ as supplied inputs and says the “actual odd/dyadic principal-unit families belong to PMIA L0a”. Nothing in either library.

items.name: Decomposition Z_p^× ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p)
items.statement: For p odd, Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p) as topological groups, via x ↦ (ω(x), ⟨x⟩); every x∈Z_p^× is uniquely x = ω(x)⟨x⟩.
items.locator: §5.3, Definition 5.15 (“Recall … we have a decomposition”) (printed pp. 146–147, PDF 47–48)
items.note: Stage LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1, “Structure of Kˣ”: “Prove … 𝒪[K]ˣ ≃ μ_{q−1} × U(K,1)” (with continuity and inverses). Library ingredients present: TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100 `TauCeti.teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ` (image μ_{q−1}, :175 range_teichmuller), TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean:88 `TauCeti.unitFiltration` (U(K,1) = principal units, :173 unitFiltration_one), both applying to ℚ_[p] (Mathlib instance IsNonarchimedeanLocalField ℚ_[p]); the product decomposition itself is not stated (grep for teichmuller uses outside Teichmuller.lean: none). Also DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 and ColemanPowerSeries:L0 (“U_infty=mu_{p−1}×U_infty,1 for odd p”, a different object).

items.name: Definition 5.15: Teichmüller character ω and ⟨·⟩
items.statement: For p odd: ω: Z_p^× → μ_{p−1}, ω(x) := the Teichmüller lift of (x mod p); ⟨·⟩: Z_p^× → 1+pZ_p, ⟨x⟩ := ω(x)^{-1}x. They are the projections for Z_p^× ≅ μ_{p−1}×(1+pZ_p); ω is a character of conductor p (order p−1).
items.note: The lift exists: TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100 `TauCeti.teichmuller K : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ` (unique (q−1)-torsion section of reduction, :158 eq_teichmuller) and Mathlib/RingTheory/Teichmuller.lean:132 `Perfection.teichmuller₀` (for I-adically complete R). The composite character ω on Z_p^× (and the projection ⟨·⟩) is not a declaration in either library. Planned: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (“Use Teichmuller decomposition to define the branches”) and LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 (Teichmüller + structure of Kˣ). Packet L3 notes “instantiate the corrected Teichmüller twist when those interfaces are supplied”.

items.name: Injection Z_p ↪ Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×), s ↦ ω^i⟨·⟩^s
items.statement: For each i∈{1,…,p−1}, s ↦ [x ↦ ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^s] is an injective map Z_p → Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×) (injective since log⟨1+p⟩ ≠ 0); its image lies in the component U_{ω^i} of weight space, and x^k = ω(x)^k⟨x⟩^k equals ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^k iff k ≡ i (mod p−1).
items.locator: §5.3, display after Definition 5.15 and paragraph after Definition 5.16 (printed p. 147, PDF 48)
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: “For Z_p^× and odd p obtain p−1 components … Construct the universal character”; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a (character spaces, finite-character components and polydisc charts); DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 branches. No packet node; the DirichletPadicLFunctions L3 nodes take a family z↦κ_z as a hypothesis (L3/tame-character-analytic-family).

items.name: Definition 5.16: branches ζ_{p,i} of the p-adic zeta function
items.statement: For i∈{1,…,p−1}: ζ_{p,i}(s) := ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i ⟨x⟩^{1−s} · ζ_p (pseudomeasure integral (3-11)), defined for s∈Z_p when i≢0 mod p−1 and for s∈Z_p∖{1} when i=p−1 (at s=1 the character is trivial; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E36).
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3: “Use Teichmuller decomposition to define the branches and prove Theorems 5.17/5.20.” Integration of pseudomeasures against nontrivial characters: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/actual-unit-character-evaluation (“For κ≠1, define the additive homomorphism Eκ:P→ℚ_p”), L3/unit-character-evaluation-continuity; ζ_p itself: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure. The packet has L3 nodes only for the tame measure ζ_η (L3/tame-character-value), none for the branches of ζ_p (L3 coverage: “Construct … actual odd/dyadic analytic branches through their owners … remain”).

items.name: Analyticity of the branches (Iwasawa/Mellin functions are analytic in s)
items.statement: For each i, s ↦ ζ_{p,i}(s) is a p-adic analytic function on Z_p if i≢0 mod p−1, and meromorphic with (at most) a simple pole at s=1 if i≡0 (more generally s ↦ ∫ω^i⟨x⟩^s·μ is analytic for any measure μ on Z_p^×). Asserted (“hence we can define a meromorphic function”, “analytic functions on Z_p”), not proved in §5.3; it is Remark 3.47/5.22 made concrete.
items.locator: §5.3, opening paragraph, sentence before Definition 5.16, and Remark 5.22 (printed pp. 146–148, PDF 47–49)
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: “identify distributions with analytic functions … bounded measures give bounded functions and pseudo-measures give meromorphic functions on their stated domains. Prove the Mellin transform, evaluation, derivatives in weight”; DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (Theorem 7.1: “exactly the trivial weight-space component can have the indicated pole”). Packet DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/tame-character-analytic-family proves analyticity only conditionally (“If z↦κ_z.toContinuousMap is AnalyticAt K at s as a map into C(U,K), then z↦Vη(κ_z) is AnalyticAt”) and only for ζ_η.

items.name: Theorem 5.17 (interpolation by the branches ζ_{p,i})
items.statement: For all integers k≥1 with k≡i (mod p−1): ζ_{p,i}(1−k) = (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k). (Because ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^k = x^k for such k, this is Proposition 4.11.)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 names Theorem 5.17 explicitly (“prove Theorems 5.17/5.20”). The underlying moment formula is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-positive-interpolation (“For every k>0 there is a unique r∈Q whose complex image is (1−p^(k−1))ζ(1−k) and whose Q_p-image is M_k(ζ_p)”). No node for the branch statement.

items.name: ζ_{p,i} ≡ 0 for i odd
items.statement: If i is odd, ζ_{p,i} is identically zero (all its interpolated values vanish: ζ(1−k)=0 for odd k≥3, and at k=1 (only for i=1) the Euler factor 1−p^0 vanishes; alternatively, ζ_p is even, i.e. [−1]ζ_p=ζ_p, while ω^i⟨·⟩^{1−s} is odd).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure-even (“δ_(−1)•ζ_p=ζ_p in PM for every prime p”) and L1/arithmetic-odd-moments (“If k is odd, then M_k(ζ_p)=0, including k=1”) give the vanishing at odd characters; no node states it for the branch functions (the tame analogue is L3/tame-character-parity). The printed justification is wrong at k=1 (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E34); the conclusion holds.

items.name: Definition 5.18: p-adic L-function L_p(θ,s)
items.statement: Let θ=χη with η of conductor D prime to p and χ of conductor p^n (n≥0). L_p(θ,s) := ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)⟨x⟩^{1−s} · ζ_η for s∈Z_p, where ζ_η is the measure of Theorem 5.7 if D>1 and (implicitly, as Remark 5.21 requires) ζ_η := ζ_p if D=1 (then s≠1 when θ=1).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/tame-character-value (“Define Vη(κ)=ν(κ.toContinuousMap) in K using the actual intrinsic restriction of ζ”) evaluated at κ = χ·⟨·⟩^{1−s} (κ supplied as a ContinuousMonoidHom), and L3/tame-character-ambient — covers D>1 only; the D=1 case (ζ_p) is covered only by the L3 stage text (“Cover pure p-power conductor as well as nontrivial tame conductor”). See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E35 on the D=1 convention.

items.name: Remark 5.19 / (5-7): L_p(θ,s) in terms of μ_η
items.statement: L_p(θ,s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} χω^{-1}(x)⟨x⟩^{−s} · μ_η (s∈Z_p, D>1), since x^{-1} = ω(x)^{-1}⟨x⟩^{-1}; for s∈Z this also equals ∫_{Z_p^×} χω^{s−1}(x)x^{−s} · μ_η.
items.note: Follows from DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-zeta-weight (“weight(x_K)ζ_η=Eμ_η”) and L3/tame-character-ambient; no node states (5-7). The last expression is only meaningful for s∈Z (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E40).

items.name: Remark 5.19: comparison with Washington’s L_p(s,χ)
items.statement: The functions L_p(θ,s) of Definition 5.18 agree with the p-adic L-functions constructed directly (without measures) in Washington [81, Thm 5.11], which satisfy L_p(1−k,θ) = (1−θω^{−k}(p)p^{k−1})L(1−k,θω^{−k}); the naive Mellin transform ∫χ(x)⟨x⟩^{−s}·μ_η of μ_η differs from them by the twist ω (the factor ω^{-1} in (5-7)).
items.locator: §5.3, Remark 5.19, last three sentences (printed p. 147, PDF 48)
items.note: The remark is ambiguous (“the more direct approach differs … by precisely this factor of ω”): by Theorem 5.20 and Washington Thm 5.11 the interpolation formulas coincide, so Definition 5.18 equals Washington’s normalization; the ω-difference is between Washington’s function and the untwisted Mellin transform of μ_η. Only partial planning: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 “prove its comparison with the Bernoulli-distribution/Stickelberger normalization used here, including the Euler factor at p, Teichmüller twists and the trivial-character pole”. No stage mentions Washington’s L_p(s,χ) itself.

items.name: Theorem 5.20 (interpolation of L_p(θ,s))
items.statement: For all k≥1: L_p(θ,1−k) = (1 − θω^{−k}(p) p^{k−1}) L(θω^{−k},1−k), where θω^{−k} is the primitive character attached to the product. Proof (D>1): χω^{-1}(x)⟨x⟩^{k−1} = χω^{−k}(x)x^{k−1}, then apply the twisted unit-moment formula (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/225) to χω^{−k} and k−1.
items.locator: §5.3, Theorem 5.20 (printed p. 147, PDF 48); proof printed p. 148 (PDF 49)
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 names Theorem 5.20. DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/tame-character-arithmetic (“For k≥1 and κ(u)=wχ(u)x_K(u)^k, Vη(κ)=(1−θ(p)p^(k−1))(−N^(k−1)/k)Σ_(a:ZMod N)θ(a)B_k(a.val/N)”, η≠1) realises the values at arithmetic characters; the identification of χ⟨·⟩^{1−s} at s=1−k with such a κ (Teichmüller) is not noded. D=1 is not covered by any node (needs Theorem 5.1 and Proposition 4.11; issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E35). The printed proof has a missing ω^{-1} (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E32) and cites Lemma 5.11 instead of the twisted formula (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E33).

items.name: Remark 5.21: ζ_{p,i}(s) = L_p(ω^i,s) and its values
items.statement: ζ_{p,i}(s) = L_p(ω^i,s) (with ζ_1:=ζ_p, D=1); hence for every k>0, ζ_{p,i}(1−k) = (1−ω^{i−k}(p)p^{k−1}) L(ω^{i−k},1−k), which for k≡i (mod p−1) is Theorem 5.17.
items.note: Stage DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 (“Cover pure p-power conductor as well as nontrivial tame conductor”). Values follow from Theorem 5.1 (ω^{i−k} nontrivial, conductor p, Euler factor 1) and Proposition 4.11 (ω^{i−k}=1). No packet node (the L3 nodes are for η≠1).

items.name: Mellin transform Mel_{μ,i} of a measure on Z_p^×
items.statement: For a measure (or pseudomeasure) μ on Z_p^× and i∈{1,…,p−1}: Mel_{μ,i}(s) := ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i ⟨x⟩^s · μ (s∈Z_p; for a pseudomeasure, (i,s) ≠ (p−1,0)); then ζ_{p,i}(s) = Mel_{ζ_p,i}(1−s).
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3: “Construct the universal character … Prove the Mellin transform, evaluation, derivatives in weight, twisting”. Pairing a measure with a continuous character: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/character-integral-algebra-hom (“For a native ContinuousMonoidHom κ:G→R, define the R-algebra homomorphism D(G,R)→R by μ↦μ(κ.toContinuousMap)”). No node for Mel itself.

items.name: Remark 5.22: branches as restrictions to components of weight space
items.statement: A measure (resp. pseudomeasure) μ on Z_p^× defines a rigid analytic (resp. meromorphic) function F_μ on weight space W, W(C_p)=Hom_cts(Z_p^×,C_p^×)=⊔_{ν∈(μ_{p−1})^∨} U_ν with each U_ν an open unit ball (p odd); ζ_{p,i} is F_{ζ_p} restricted to U_{ω^i} (pulled back along s↦ω^i⟨·⟩^{1−s}), explaining the p−1 branches.
items.locator: §5.3, Remark 5.22 (printed p. 148, PDF 49), referring to Remark 3.47 (printed p. 135, PDF 36)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a (“construct the rigid analytic space representing continuous characters … the finite-character components and polydisc charts”) and LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3 (“For Z_p^× and odd p obtain p−1 components … pseudo-measures give meromorphic functions”). No packet node.

items.name: The value L_p(θ, 1) as a negative moment
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Let μ_η be the measure on Z_p with Amice transform F_η (proof of Theorem 5.7; requires D > 1), μ_θ = (μ_η)_χ (Mahler transform F_θ of Lemma 5.12), ζ_η = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_η) (Definition 5.13) and L_p(θ,s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_η for s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.18). If D > 1 then (6-2): L_p(θ,1) = ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)x^{-1}·μ_η = ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{-1}·μ_θ. If D = 1 (θ = χ ≠ 1 of p-power conductor) no measure μ_θ exists; with ζ_η read as ζ_p (as in Remark 5.21) one has L_p(χ,1) = ∫_{Z_p^×} χ·ζ_p = (χ(a) − 1)^{-1} ∫_{Z_p^×} χ(x)x^{-1}·μ_a for any topological generator a of Z_p^× (by (3-11)).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/padic-value-as-negative-moment: 'For every integer k >= 1, L_p(theta*omega^{1-k}, k) = int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu_theta' with hypothesis 'D > 1'; at k = 1 this is exactly (6-2). The D = 1 case is ColemanIntegration:L3/padic-value-as-smoothed-negative-moment: 'L_p(chi*omega^{1-k}, k) = (chi(b) b^{1-k} - 1)^{-1} int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu_{chi,b}', which at k = 1 is the D = 1 formula above. The printed (6-2) is stated for every nontrivial θ, but μ_η only exists for D > 1 (see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E45). No Mathlib/Tau Ceti declaration: Mathlib has AbstractMeasure and amiceTransform on ℤ_[p] (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure) but no ζ_η, μ_θ or L_p.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(i): classical value L(θ,1) via cyclotomic logarithms
items.statement: Let θ be a nontrivial primitive complex Dirichlet character of conductor N (so N > 1), ε_N ∈ C a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Then L(θ,1) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) log(1 − ε_N^c), with log the principal branch (Re(1 − ε_N^c) > 0). The right side is independent of the choice of ε_N (replacing ε_N by ε_N^b multiplies both G(θ^{-1}) and the sum by θ(b)).
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(i) (printed p. 149, PDF 50); proof in §6.1 (printed pp. 149–150, PDF 50–51), following Washington, Thm 4.9
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/complex-lvalue-one-log: 'η.LFunction 1=−G⁻¹Σ_(c∈(ZMod D)ˣ)η⁻¹(c)Complex.log(1−ε^c)' for 'D>1, η primitive and nonprincipal, ε a primitive D-th complex root and G=gaussSum(η⁻¹,AddChar.zmodChar D ε)≠0' (D there is any conductor > 1, so this is the full statement; G ≠ 0 is carried as a hypothesis, discharged by the Gauss-sum identity of PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/250). Also ColemanIntegration:L3/complex-coleman-formula ('for every integer k >= 1, L(theta, k) = G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) Li_k(e^{2 pi i c/N})') and L3/recovers-leopoldt-formula. Not in Mathlib: Mathlib has DirichletCharacter.LFunction, ZMod.LFunction_dft (NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean:208) and DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.fourierTransform_eq_inv_mul_gaussSum (Analysis/Fourier/ZMod.lean:220), which give L(θ,s) as a Gauss-sum combination of HurwitzZeta.expZeta, but no evaluation of expZeta(x,1) as −log(1 − e^{2πix}); searched 'polylog', 'expZeta.*log', 'log (1 - ' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti.

items.name: Theorem 6.1(ii): Leopoldt's formula for L_p(θ,1)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Let L_p(θ,s) be as in Definition 5.18 (with ζ_η read as ζ_p when D = 1) and log_p the Iwasawa logarithm on C_p^× (log_p(p) = 0; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/263). Then L_p(θ,1) = −(1 − θ(p)p^{-1}) G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) log_p(1 − ε_N^c), where θ(p) = 0 if p | N. The right side does not depend on the choice of ε_N nor on the branch of the p-adic logarithm (when D = 1 all 1 − ε_N^c have the same valuation and Σ_c θ^{-1}(c) = 0).
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.1(ii) (printed p. 149, PDF 50); Remark 6.2 attributes it to Leopoldt; proof in §6.2 (printed pp. 150–153, PDF 51–54)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/recovers-leopoldt-formula: 'At k = 1, ColemanIntegration:L3/coleman-formula is RJW Theorem 6.1(ii): L_p(theta, 1) = -(1 - theta(p) p^{-1}) G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) log_p(1 - eps_N^c) ... The proof ... covers both conductor cases of RJW §6.2: tame part D > 1 (including n = 0) through the geometric measures and the distribution relation, and pure p-power conductor D = 1 through the smoothed measure.' DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage: 'Prove the complex logarithmic formula and Leopoldt's p-adic formula of Theorem 6.1 ... Cover pure p-power conductor as well as nontrivial tame conductor'. The notes' own proof covers only D > 1 (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E45) and never defines log_p on C_p^× (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E44); the statement is nevertheless true (it is Washington, Thm 5.18, whose L_p agrees with Definition 5.18 by Theorem 5.20). Branch independence: ColemanIntegration:L2/values-at-roots-of-unity-of-p-power-order (a) 'for a nontrivial character θ of (Z/p^r)^×, Σ_c θ^{−1}(c)Li^a_1(ζ^c) is independent of a'. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (no p-adic logarithm on C_p, no p-adic L-function).

items.name: Transcendence of L(θ,1) (footnote 10)
items.statement: For every nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character θ, L(θ,1) is transcendental. (Printed justification: Baker's theorem — a nonzero Q̄-linear combination of logarithms of nonzero algebraic numbers is transcendental — applied to Theorem 6.1(i); the argument also needs L(θ,1) ≠ 0.)
items.note: Searched packets and stage descriptions for 'Baker', 'transcendental', 'L(θ,1)'. Baker's theorem itself is planned: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/baker-linear-independence-of-logarithms ('Let λ_1, …, λ_m ∈ 𝓛 be linearly independent over ℚ.
