Then 1, λ_1, …, λ_m are linearly independent over ℚ̄') and DT.3/baker-transcendence-of-linear-form; the nonvanishing is in Mathlib: DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero (NumberTheory/LSeries/Nonvanishing.lean:408, 'theorem LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero (hχ : χ ≠ 1) : LFunction χ 1 ≠ 0'). No stage or node states the transcendence of L(θ,1); it is a short corollary of those two and PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/244. The footnote omits the nonvanishing input (not recorded as an issue: the omission is of a classical theorem and the claim is correct). Routed (source) to DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0, importing Baker's theorem from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3.

items.name: Parity vanishing at s = 1 for odd characters (Remark 6.2 context)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. If θ is odd (θ(−1) = −1) then L_p(θ,s) = 0 for all s ∈ Z_p (Theorem 5.20: every interpolated value (1 − θω^{-k}(p)p^{k−1})L(θω^{-k},1−k), k ≥ 1, vanishes, because θω^{-k}(−1) ≠ (−1)^k gives L(θω^{-k},1−k) = 0 unless θω^{-k} = 1 and k = 1, where the Euler factor 1 − p^0 = 0; and the points 1 − k are dense), and Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) log_p(1 − ε_N^c) = 0 (pair c with −c, using log_p(−ε_N^{-c}) = 0). So both sides of Theorem 6.1(ii) vanish.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/tame-character-parity: 'If η≠1 and κ(−1)≠η(−1), then Vη(κ)=0', with Vη(κ)=ν(κ) the integral of κ against the unit restriction of the tame zeta measure; for κ = χ this is L_p(θ,1) and κ(−1) ≠ η(−1) ⟺ θ odd (covers D > 1 only). Right side: ColemanIntegration:L2/twisted-sums-for-primitive-characters (c) 'Parity: S_k(θ, ε) = −θ(−1)(−1)^k·S_k(θ, ε), so S_k(θ, ε) = 0 unless θ(−1) = (−1)^{k+1}' (k = 1). The D = 1 vanishing of L_p(χ,s) for odd χ is not a separate node.

items.name: Orthogonality of additive characters modulo N
items.statement: For N ≥ 1, ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and a, n ∈ Z: (1/N) Σ_{c∈Z/NZ} ε_N^{(a−n)c} = 1 if n ≡ a (mod N), and 0 otherwise.
items.locator: §6.1, proof of Theorem 6.1(i), first display (printed p. 149, PDF 50)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:258, 'theorem sum_mulShift ... {ψ : AddChar R R'} (b : R) (hψ : IsPrimitive ψ) : ∑ x : R, ψ (x * b) = if b = 0 then Fintype.card R else 0' (R' a domain). Apply with R = ZMod N, ψ(c) = ε_N^c (primitive because ε_N is a primitive root) and b = a − n. Same statement up to dividing by N.

items.name: Twisted Gauss sums of a primitive character
items.statement: Let θ be a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N and ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity, G(θ) = Σ_{a∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ(a)ε_N^a. Then for every c ∈ Z/NZ: Σ_{a∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ(a)ε_N^{ac} = θ^{-1}(c)G(θ); in particular the left side is 0 when gcd(c,N) > 1.
items.locator: §6.1, proof of Theorem 6.1(i), second equality of (6-1) (printed p. 150, PDF 51); Remark 5.3(ii) for N = p^n (printed p. 140)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/GaussSum.lean:57: 'lemma gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive [IsDomain R] {χ : DirichletCharacter R N} (hχ : IsPrimitive χ) (a : ZMod N) : gaussSum χ (e.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ e' for any additive character e. With e(x) = ε_N^x this is the statement (the vanishing for non-units is part of it). The notes justify the non-unit case only by 'θ^{-1}(c) = 0 if (c,N) ≠ 1', which needs this primitivity lemma.

items.name: Product of Gauss sums of a primitive character
items.statement: Let θ be a primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity. Then G(θ)G(θ^{-1}) = θ(−1)N; in particular G(θ^{-1}) ≠ 0.
items.locator: §6.1, proof of Theorem 6.1(i), third equality of (6-1) (printed p. 150, PDF 51), citing Remark 5.3(i) (stated there only for conductor p^n, printed p. 140)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L0 stage: 'Construct generalized Bernoulli numbers, primitive-character Gauss sums, their nonvanishing and inversion formula'. ColemanIntegration:L3/gauss-sum-root-of-unity-independence also asserts 'G_eps(theta^{-1}) != 0'. Mathlib has only gaussSum_mul_gaussSum_eq_card (NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:188), which requires the domain R to be a field (finite field), so it does not apply to ZMod N for composite N; no Dirichlet-character version found (searched 'gaussSum χ⁻¹', 'gaussSum .* gaussSum', 'norm_gaussSum' in Mathlib/NumberTheory and Tau Ceti). The notes use the identity for general N although Remark 5.3 states it for N = p^n.

items.name: Formula (6-1): L(θ,s) as a Gauss-sum combination of polylogarithm series
items.statement: Let θ be a nontrivial primitive complex Dirichlet character of conductor N, ε_N ∈ C a primitive N-th root of unity. For Re(s) > 1 (and, by continuity, at s = 1): L(θ,s) = G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) Σ_{n≥1} ε_N^{nc} n^{-s}. Equivalently L(θ,s) = G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_c θ^{-1}(c) Li_s(ε_N^c).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/complex-coleman-formula: 'For every s in C, L(theta, s) = G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_{c in (Z/NZ)^x} theta^{-1}(c) expZeta(c/N, s)' (theta primitive of conductor N >= 2; G formed with mathlib:ZMod.stdAddChar). This generalises (6-1) to all s. Mathlib ingredients (not the statement): ZMod.LFunction_dft (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/ZMod.lean:208, 'LFunction (𝓕 Φ) s = ∑ j : ZMod N, Φ j * expZeta (toAddCircle (-j)) s' when Φ 0 = 0 ∨ s ≠ 1) and DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.fourierTransform_eq_inv_mul_gaussSum (Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/ZMod.lean:220, '𝓕 χ k = χ⁻¹ (-k) * gaussSum χ stdAddChar').

items.name: Boundary Taylor expansion of −log(1 − z)
items.statement: For z ∈ C with |z| = 1 and z ≠ 1 (in the application z = ε_N^c, c ∈ (Z/NZ)^×, N > 1), the series Σ_{n≥1} z^n/n converges and equals −log(1 − z) (principal branch); combined with continuity in s of Σ_n ε_N^{nc}n^{-s} on Re(s) > 0, this evaluates (6-1) at s = 1.
items.locator: §6.1, end of the proof of Theorem 6.1(i) (printed p. 150, PDF 51)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L2/complex-polylogarithm-at-roots-of-unity (a): 'For k = 1 and ζ ≠ 1 a root of unity, Li_1^ℂ(ζ) = −Log(1 − ζ) with the principal logarithm', built on Polylogarithms:P.1 ('Define Li_n(z) by its convergent power series on the unit disk. Prove ... analytic continuation'). DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 takes an integral route instead (complex-log-kernel-integral: '∫_(0,∞)qα(t)dt=−Complex.log(1−α)' for ‖α‖=1, α≠1). Mathlib has only the open-disc case, Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_neg_log (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Complex/LogBounds.lean:281, '‖z‖ < 1 → HasSum (fun n ↦ z ^ n / n) (-log (1 - z))'), and Abel's limit theorem Complex.tendsto_tsum_powerSeries_nhdsWithin_stolzCone (Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/AbelLimit.lean:241); the boundary identity itself is not stated.

items.name: Remark 6.3: L(θ,1) for even θ
items.statement: Let θ be a nontrivial primitive even (θ(−1) = 1) complex Dirichlet character of conductor N and ε_N ∈ C a primitive N-th root of unity. Then L(θ,1) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) log|1 − ε_N^c| (real logarithm), because log(1 − ε_N^c) + log(1 − ε_N^{-c}) = 2 log|1 − ε_N^c|.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/complex-lvalue-one-even-log: 'η.LFunction1=−G(η⁻¹,ε)⁻¹Σ_units c η⁻¹(c)Real.log‖1−ε^c‖' for 'D>1 ... primitive, nonprincipal and even, ε a primitive D-th root, ... G nonzero'. Exact match (printed 'log|1 − ε^c|' drops the subscript N; harmless).

items.name: Remark 6.3: L(θ,1) for odd θ (corrected: canonical root of unity)
items.statement: Let θ be a nontrivial primitive odd complex Dirichlet character of conductor N, ε_N = e^{2πi/N}, G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_c θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c and B_{1,θ^{-1}} = (1/N)Σ_{a=1}^{N} θ^{-1}(a)a. Then L(θ,1) = −iπ G(θ^{-1})^{-1} B_{1,θ^{-1}}. For another primitive root ε_N = e^{2πib/N} the right side must be multiplied by θ(b).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3/complex-lvalue-one-odd-bernoulli: 'η.LFunction1=−πi·G(η⁻¹,ε)⁻¹·Σ_(a:ZModD)η⁻¹(a)algebraMap(B₁(a.val/D))' with hypothesis 'ε is primitive with the explicit equality ε=exp(2πi/D)' (the B₁-polynomial sum equals B_{1,η⁻¹}). The printed remark omits the normalisation ε_N = e^{2πi/N} (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E43). Generalized Bernoulli numbers are not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'generalized Bernoulli', 'bernoulliGen').

items.name: The logarithmic primitive F̃_θ(T)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1 (so every ε_N^c − 1, c ∈ (Z/NZ)^×, is a p-adic unit). Define F̃_θ(T) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) log((1+T)ε_N^c − 1) ∈ L[[T]], where log((1+T)ε_N^c − 1) := log_p(ε_N^c − 1) + Σ_{n≥1} ((−1)^{n−1}/n)(ε_N^{cn}/(ε_N^c − 1)^n)T^n. It is a candidate for ∂^{-1}F_θ, where ∂ = (1+T)d/dT and F_θ is the Mahler transform of μ_θ (Lemma 5.12).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/comparison-with-rjw-distribution-argument: 'for tame part D > 1, RJW's Ftilde_theta(T) = -G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) log((1+T) eps_N^c - 1) equals G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) Ftilde^{(1)}_{eps^c}(T) (the constant log_p(-1) = 0)', with Ftilde^{(k)}_w the Taylor expansion of Li_k(w(1+T)) (L3/polylog-primitive-on-residue-disc). The printed definition is made for every nontrivial θ; for D = 1 it involves log_p of non-units and has logarithmic singularities inside the disc (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E45).

items.name: Lemma 6.4: F̃_θ lies in R^+ (tame part D > 1)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1. Then F̃_θ(T) ∈ R^+, the space of Σ a_nT^n ∈ L[[T]] with |a_n|r^n → 0 for every 0 ≤ r < 1 (Remark 3.39). More precisely the coefficients have logarithmic growth: for p ∤ N the coefficient of T^n has valuation ≥ −v_p(n); in general F̃_θ = (F̃_η)_χ(T) = G(χ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/p^nZ)^×} χ^{-1}(c) F̃_η((1+T)ε_{p^n}^c − 1) with ε_N = ε_{p^n}ε_D (corrected sign, issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E46). For D = 1 the statement is false.
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L2/polylogarithm-expansion-at-a-root-of-unity (b): 'For a nontrivial Dirichlet character θ modulo N ... and ε of order N not a power of p, F̃_{θ,k}(T) := G(θ^{−1}, ε)^{−1}·Σ_{c∈(Z/N)^×}θ^{−1}(c)P_{k,ε^c}(T) ... lies in R^+, has logarithmic growth'; at k = 1, F̃_{θ,1} = F̃_θ exactly, since P_{1,ε}(T) = Li_1((1+T)ε) = −log_p(1 − (1+T)ε) and log_p(−1) = 0. 'ε of order N not a power of p' is exactly D > 1. LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1: 'Applications involving logarithms of (1+T)xi−1 must justify their analytic domain and cancellation of apparent poles, especially when xi has p-power order.' Restriction to D > 1: issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E45.

items.name: The locally analytic distribution μ̃_θ
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1. By Theorem 3.43 (Amice: the Mahler transform is a bijection D^la(Z_p, L) → R^+) there is a unique locally analytic distribution μ̃_θ ∈ D^la(Z_p, L) with Mahler transform A_{μ̃_θ} = F̃_θ.
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/polylog-primitive-on-residue-disc: 'The locally analytic distribution mutilde^{(k)}_w in D^la(Z_p, K) with Amice transform Ftilde^{(k)}_w (RJW Theorem 3.43) satisfies x . mutilde^{(k)}_w = mutilde^{(k-1)}_w'; μ̃_θ is the Gauss-sum combination of these at k = 1 (comparison-with-rjw-distribution-argument). Theorem 3.43 itself: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1 'Prove RJW Theorem 3.43: the Amice transform identifies distributions on Z_p with power series convergent on every closed disc of radius r<1'. Mathlib has the bounded case only (AbstractMeasure.amiceTransform, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:75).

items.name: Lemma 6.5 (first part): x·μ̃_θ = μ_θ
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1. Then x·μ̃_θ = μ_θ as locally analytic distributions on Z_p; equivalently (Lemma 3.29) ∂F̃_θ(T) = (1+T)(d/dT)F̃_θ(T) = F_θ(T) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)/((1+T)ε_N^c − 1). This follows from ∂log((1+T)ε_N^c − 1) = 1 + 1/((1+T)ε_N^c − 1) and Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) = 0.
items.locator: §6.2, Lemma 6.5 and proof, display (6-4) (printed p. 152, PDF 53)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/polylog-primitive-on-residue-disc (c): '(1+T) d/dT Ftilde^{(k)}_w = Ftilde^{(k-1)}_w' and (b) 'Ftilde^{(0)}_w = A_{mu_w}', with L3/mu-theta-as-sum-of-geometric-measures: 'mu_theta = G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) mu_{eps_N^c}' (D > 1). Together these give x·μ̃_θ = μ_θ (comparison-with-rjw-distribution-argument: 'Lemma 6.5 is x . mutilde^{(1)} = mu'). The printed proof writes ε_D and (Z/DZ)^× for ε_N and (Z/NZ)^× (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E47).

items.name: Lemma 6.5 (second part) and division by x on units
items.statement: Multiplication by x is an invertible operator on measures and on locally analytic distributions on Z_p^×. Consequently, for D > 1, Res_{Z_p^×}(μ̃_θ) = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_θ).
items.locator: §6.2, Lemma 6.5 (second display) and last paragraph of its proof (printed p. 152, PDF 53)
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1: 'Prove division by x on distributions supported on units without using a globally defined function x^−1 on Z_p.' PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 (measures): 'restriction to units as 1−phi psi; inversion of multiplication by x on units'. ColemanIntegration:L3/unit-moment-via-distribution-primitive packages the consequence ('Then x^k lambda = mu, and int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu = lambda(1_{Z_p^x})').

items.name: Equation (6-5): L_p(θ,1) = ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_θ)(0)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1. Then L_p(θ,1) = A_{x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_θ)}(0) = A_{Res_{Z_p^×}(μ̃_θ)}(0) = ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_θ)(0), where (φ∘ψ)(F)(T) = p^{-1} Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} F((1+T)ξ − 1) (3-9) and Res_{Z_p^×} = 1 − φ∘ψ (3-8), extended to distributions (Remark 3.45).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/unit-moment-via-distribution-primitive: 'Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, mu ... a bounded measure, k >= 0, and Ftilde in R^+ ... with ((1+T) d/dT)^k Ftilde = A_mu. ... int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu = lambda(1_{Z_p^x}) = ((1 - phi o psi) Ftilde)(0) = Ftilde(0) - p^{-1} sum_{xi in mu_p} Ftilde(xi - 1)'. At k = 1, μ = μ_θ this is (6-5) (general form).

items.name: The Euler factor at s = 1: ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_θ)(0) = (1 − θ(p)p^{-1})F̃_θ(0)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Assume D > 1. (1) If n ≥ 1 then μ̃_θ = (μ̃_η)_χ is supported on Z_p^×, so φ∘ψ(F̃_θ) = 0 and L_p(θ,1) = F̃_θ(0) (= (1 − θ(p)p^{-1})F̃_θ(0) since θ(p) = 0). (2) If n = 0 (p ∤ N) then (φ∘ψ F̃_θ)(0) = p^{-1}Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} F̃_θ(ξ − 1) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1}p^{-1} Σ_c θ^{-1}(c) log_p(ε_N^{pc} − 1) = θ(p)p^{-1}F̃_θ(0), using Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} log_p(ξz − 1) = log_p(z^p − 1) and that c ↦ pc permutes (Z/NZ)^×. Hence in all cases L_p(θ,1) = (1 − θ(p)p^{-1})F̃_θ(0), and F̃_θ(0) = −G(θ^{-1})^{-1}Σ_c θ^{-1}(c)log_p(1 − ε_N^c) (log_p(−x) = log_p(x)).
items.locator: §6.2, proof of Theorem 6.1(ii), cases (1) and (2) (printed pp. 152–153, PDF 53–54)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/euler-factor-from-p-power-map: 'sum_{c in (Z/NZ)^x} theta^{-1}(c) f(eps_N^{pc}) = theta(p) sum_{c} theta^{-1}(c) f(eps_N^c), with theta(p) = 0 when p | N'; L3/primitive-character-fibre-sum-vanishes (the p | N case, a different route from the notes' support argument); ColemanIntegration:L2/distribution-relation 'Σ_{ζ∈μ_m} Li^a_k(ζz) = m^{1−k}·Li^a_k(z^m)' (m = p, k = 1 gives the log_p product identity). Case (1) is printed with 'n > 1' (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E48).

items.name: Product formula over p-th roots of unity
items.statement: For p odd and X an indeterminate (or any element of an integral domain containing a primitive p-th root of unity): Π_{ξ∈μ_p}(Xξ − 1) = X^p − 1; also Π_{ξ∈μ_p} ξ = 1 and {ξ^a : ξ ∈ μ_p} = μ_p for p ∤ a.
items.locator: §6.2, proof of Theorem 6.1(ii) case (2) (printed p. 153, PDF 54); proof of Lemma 7.5 (printed pp. 157–158, PDF 58–59)
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:119: 'theorem X_pow_sub_one_eq_prod {ζ : R} {n : ℕ} (hpos : 0 < n) (h : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) : X ^ n - 1 = ∏ ζ ∈ nthRootsFinset n (1 : R), (X - C ζ)'. The printed form is equivalent: Π_ξ(Xξ − 1) = (Π_ξ ξ)·Π_ξ(X − ξ^{-1}) and Π_ξ ξ = 1 for odd p (reindexing ξ ↦ ξ^{-1}). Mathlib states the X − ζ form, not literally the Xξ − 1 form.

items.name: The Iwasawa p-adic logarithm log_p on C_p^×
items.statement: log_p : C_p^× → C_p is the unique group homomorphism that agrees with the series log(1+u) = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n−1}u^n/n on 1 + m_{C_p} and satisfies log_p(p) = 0. It kills all roots of unity, so log_p(−x) = log_p(x) and log_p(a) = log_p(⟨a⟩) for a ∈ Z_p^×; it maps K^× into K for every finite K/Q_p.
items.locator: Used without definition in Theorem 6.1(ii) (printed p. 149), the proof of Theorem 6.1(ii) ('log_p(x) = log_p(−x) for x ∈ C_p^×', printed p. 153) and Lemma 7.2 (printed p. 155); only exp/log on pZ_p, 1 + pZ_p are introduced (Lemma 5.14, printed p. 146)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L0/iwasawa-logarithm: 'The Iwasawa branch of the p-adic logarithm is log_p := log_0 (L0/log-branch): the unique group homomorphism C_p^x -> C_p that is the series log(1 + u) on 1 + m_{C_p} and satisfies log_p(p) = 0 ... imported by DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3'. L0/log-branch: 'It vanishes at all roots of unity, satisfies log_a(-x) = log_a(x)'. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'def log' across both trees, 'padicLog', 'iwasawaLog', 'ℂ_[p]'). Issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E44 records that the notes never define it.

items.name: The complex polylogarithm Li_s(z) (Remark 6.6)
items.statement: For s, z ∈ C with |z| < 1, Li_s(z) := Σ_{n≥1} z^n/n^s. For fixed s it has a unique analytic continuation to C ∖ {z ∈ R : z ≥ 1}; Li_s(1) = ζ(s) (Re s > 1) and Li_1(z) = −log(1 − z).
items.note: Polylogarithms:P.1: 'Define Li_n(z) by its convergent power series on the unit disk. Prove differentiation, analytic continuation on a specified cut domain, branch-change formulas and distribution relations.' ColemanIntegration:L2/complex-polylogarithm-at-roots-of-unity: 'Li_k^ℂ(e^{2πix}) = Σ_{n≥1}e^{2πinx}/n^k = expZeta(x, k) (Mathlib's HurwitzZeta.expZeta)'. No polylogarithm in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched 'polylog', 'Polylog'); HurwitzZeta.expZeta covers the values on the unit circle only.

items.name: Coleman's p-adic polylogarithms Li_{k,p}
items.statement: For k ≥ 1 there are unique Coleman functions Li_k on P^1(C_p) ∖ {1, ∞} (for a fixed branch of the p-adic logarithm; the notes' Li_{k,p}) with Li_1(z) = −log_p(1 − z), z·d/dz Li_k = Li_{k−1} (k ≥ 2), and Li_k(z) = Σ_{n≥1} z^n/n^k for |z| < 1; they are locally analytic on C_p ∖ {1}. Local antiderivatives alone do not determine them (Coleman's Frobenius-compatible integration fixes the locally constant ambiguity).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L2/p-adic-polylogarithm: 'The Iwasawa branch a = 0 gives Li_k := Li^0_k, the function written Li_{k,p} in RJW Theorem 6.7 and Li_k in Coleman's formula'; L2/existence-and-uniqueness-of-coleman-polylogarithms: 'For every k ≥ 1 there is a unique sequence of Coleman functions Li^a_1, …, Li^a_k ... (i) Li^a_1 = −log_a(1 − z); (ii) d Li^a_j = Li^a_{j−1}·dz/z'; L2/locally-analytic-antiderivatives-and-a-non-example. The notes only say 'Coleman constructed p-adic analogues Li_{k,p}(z), which are locally analytic functions on C_p ∖ {1}'. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Theorem 6.7(i) (Coleman): classical values L(θ,k)
items.statement: Let θ be a nontrivial primitive complex Dirichlet character of conductor N, k ≥ 1 an integer, ε_N ∈ C a primitive N-th root of unity. Then L(θ,k) = G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) Li_k(ε_N^c) (principal-branch polylogarithm; for k = 1 this is Theorem 6.1(i)).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/complex-coleman-formula: 'Hence for every integer k >= 1, L(theta, k) = G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_c theta^{-1}(c) Li_k(e^{2 pi i c/N}) with the principal-branch complex polylogarithm (RJW Theorem 6.7(i))' (stated for the canonical root; independence of the root: L3/gauss-sum-root-of-unity-independence). Mathlib ingredients as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/251.

items.name: Theorem 6.7(ii) (Coleman's formula), corrected
items.statement: Standing notation (§§5–6): p an odd prime; L/Q_p a finite extension inside C_p containing μ_N and the values of the characters; θ a nontrivial primitive Dirichlet character of conductor N, written θ = χη with χ primitive of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and η primitive of conductor D with p ∤ D, so N = Dp^n; ε_N a primitive N-th root of unity and G(θ^{-1}) = Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c)ε_N^c. Let k ≥ 1 and Li_k = Li_{k,p} Coleman's p-adic polylogarithm (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/265). Then L_p(θω^{1−k}, k) = (1 − θ(p)p^{-k}) G(θ^{-1})^{-1} Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ^{-1}(c) Li_k(ε_N^c), with ω the Teichmüller character and θ(p) = 0 if p | N. The printed statement 'L_p(θ,k) = …' (without the twist ω^{1−k}) holds exactly when (p − 1) | (k − 1); for k = 1 both agree and give Theorem 6.1(ii).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/coleman-formula: 'For every integer k >= 1: L_p(theta omega^{1-k}, k) = (1 - theta(p) p^{-k}) G(theta^{-1})^{-1} sum_{c in (Z/NZ)^x} theta^{-1}(c) Li_k(eps_N^c) ... This is RJW Theorem 6.7(ii) with the Teichmueller twist omega^{1-k} that the printed statement omits'; L3/coleman-formula-rjw-normalisation gives L_p(θ,k) itself via the primitive character attached to θω^{k−1}. Note: the ColemanIntegration:L3 stage description still quotes the printed (uncorrected) formula 'L_p(theta,k) = (1−theta(p)p^(−k)) / G(theta^−1) * sum_c ...'; the node is corrected. Issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E49.

items.name: Perrin-Riou's p-adic Beilinson conjecture (cited, Remark 6.8)
items.statement: Perrin-Riou's conjectures describe noncritical special values of p-adic L-functions of motives by p-adic regulators; for Dirichlet characters they express L_p(θω^{1−k},k) (k ≥ 1) through p-adic (syntomic) regulators of cyclotomic units/elements, of which Theorems 6.1(ii) and 6.7(ii) are instances. (Not stated precisely in the notes.)
items.locator: §6.2, Remarks 6.2 and 6.8 (printed pp. 149 and 154, PDF 50 and 55), citing [67], [18], [38], [50]
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/padic-beilinson-conjecture: 'The proposition PBC(k, E, pi, n, p) is the conjunction of: (1) ... (2) L_p(n, chi_pi (x) omega_p^{1-n}, Q) D(M^E_pi)^{1/2,p} = e_p Eul_p(n, chi_pi (x) id, Q) R_{n,p}(M^E_pi) ... This is a definition of a statement about defined objects; it is not asserted.' L3/padic-beilinson-for-dirichlet-motives and L3/coleman-formula-as-syntomic-regulator-formula give the Dirichlet instance (n ≥ 2). The k = 1 regulator interpretation (cyclotomic units) is not a separate node. A cited conjecture, included because the notes name Theorem 6.1(ii) as an instance of it.

items.name: Residue of the Riemann zeta function at s = 1
items.statement: ζ(s) has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1: lim_{s→1, s≠1} (s − 1)ζ(s) = 1.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:242: 'lemma riemannZeta_residue_one : Tendsto (fun s ↦ (s - 1) * riemannZeta s) (𝓝[≠] 1) (𝓝 1)'. Same statement. Quoted as motivation for Theorem 7.1.

items.name: Theorem 7.1(i): ζ_{p,i} has no pole at s = 1 for i ≠ p − 1
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). If i ∈ {1, …, p−2} then ζ_{p,i} is analytic at s = 1 (indeed the denominator g_{a,i}(s) = ω(a)^i⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1 of (7-1) is a p-adic unit for all s ∈ Z_p, so ζ_{p,i} is analytic on Z_p).
items.locator: §7, Theorem 7.1(i) (printed p. 154, PDF 55); proof via Lemma 7.2(i) (printed p. 155, PDF 56)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage: 'Prove Theorem 7.1: exactly the trivial weight-space component can have the indicated pole, and in the s-coordinate of RJW its residue is 1−p^−1. Separate the numerator evaluation, convergence, nonvanishing of log_p(a), and division by the simple zero.' No packet node yet (the packet's L3 coverage lists 'pole/residue analysis' as remaining). Weight-space form: pseudo-measures are analytic away from the trivial character (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3, LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3). Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Theorem 7.1(ii): the residue of ζ_p at s = 1
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). The function ζ_{p,p−1} has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue 1 − p^{-1}: lim_{s→1} (s − 1)ζ_{p,p−1}(s) = 1 − p^{-1} (s ∈ Z_p ∖ {1}).
items.locator: §7, Theorem 7.1(ii) (printed p. 154, PDF 55); proof completed at the end of §7 (printed p. 158, PDF 59)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage (quoted under PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/270). EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/trivial-character-component uses it as a hypothesis ('ζ_{p,p−1} has a simple pole at s = 1 with residue (1 − p^{−1}) (RJW Theorem 7.1(ii))') and states the measure-level consequence 'the value of ([a] − [1])ζ_p at the trivial character is −(1 − p^{−1})·log_p(a)'. The numerator is planned by ColemanIntegration:L3/negative-moments-of-smoothed-measure (see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/280). No node proves the s-coordinate residue itself.

items.name: Formula (7-1) for ζ_{p,i}(s) and the denominator g_{a,i}
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). For every i ∈ {1, …, p−1} and s ∈ Z_p with g_{a,i}(s) ≠ 0: ζ_{p,i}(s) = (∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^{i−1}⟨x⟩^{−s}·μ_a) / g_{a,i}(s), where g_{a,i}(s) := ω(a)^i⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1 = ∫ ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·θ_a. (The notes write the integrand as ω(x)^{s+i−1}x^{−s}, a formal rewriting of ω(x)^{i−1}⟨x⟩^{−s}.)
items.locator: §7, display (7-1) and definition of g_{a,i} (printed p. 155, PDF 56), using (3-11) and Definition 4.10
items.note: Specialisation of the pseudo-measure evaluation rule (3-11) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3: 'evaluation at nontrivial characters by clearing a factor [g]−1 whose evaluation is nonzero. Prove independence of g') to ζ_p and the characters ω^i⟨·⟩^{1−s}; the DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage asks for 'division by the simple zero'. No dedicated node.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(i): g_{a,i}(1) ≠ 0 for i ≠ p − 1
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). For i ∈ {1, …, p−2}, g_{a,i}(1) = ω(a)^i − 1 ≠ 0 (ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity). Hence (7-1) has no pole at s = 1 and Theorem 7.1(i) holds.
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage: 'exactly the trivial weight-space component can have the indicated pole'. Elementary; no node. Ingredient in Tau Ceti: TauCeti.teichmuller (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100, the Teichmüller lift 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ, injective by TauCeti.teichmuller_injective, line 152), so ω(a) has the multiplicative order of a mod p; the lemma itself is not stated in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(ii): the simple zero of g_{a,p−1} at s = 1
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). g_{a,p−1}(s) = ⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1 satisfies g_{a,p−1}(1) = 0 and lim_{s→1} (s − 1)^{-1} g_{a,p−1}(s) = −log_p(a). Proof: ⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1 = Σ_{n≥1} C(1−s, n)(⟨a⟩ − 1)^n = (1 − s) Σ_{n≥1} (1/n)C(−s, n−1)(⟨a⟩ − 1)^n (using C(1−s,n) = ((1−s)/n)C(−s,n−1)), and at s = 1, using C(−1, n−1) = (−1)^{n−1}, the sum is Σ_{n≥1} (−1)^{n−1}(⟨a⟩ − 1)^n/n = log_p⟨a⟩ = log_p(a). Moreover log_p(a) ≠ 0 (log_p is injective on 1 + pZ_p for odd p and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1).
items.locator: §7, Lemma 7.2(ii) and proof, display (7-2) (printed pp. 155–156, PDF 56–57)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage: 'Separate the numerator evaluation, convergence, nonvanishing of log_p(a), and division by the simple zero.' EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/trivial-character-component lists 'lim_{s→1}(s − 1)^{−1}(⟨a⟩^{1−s} − 1) = −log_p(a) (Lemma 7.2(ii))' as an input hypothesis, not as a node. The printed conclusion writes g_{a,s−1} for g_{a,p−1} (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E50). No p-adic logarithm or binomial-series continuity in s in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Equation (7-3): residue as a negative moment of μ_a
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). lim_{s→1} (s − 1)ζ_{p,p−1}(s) = −(∫_{Z_p^×} x^{-1}·μ_a) / log_p(a).
items.note: Combination of (7-1) at i = p − 1 (numerator ∫_{Z_p^×}⟨x⟩^{−s}ω(x)^{−1}·μ_a, continuous in s, equal to ∫_{Z_p^×}x^{-1}·μ_a at s = 1) with Lemma 7.2(ii). DirichletPadicLFunctions:L3 stage ('division by the simple zero'). No node.

items.name: The logarithmic primitive F̃_a(T)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). F̃_a(T) := log( (T/(1+T)) · ((1+T)^a/((1+T)^a − 1)) ) = log( (T/((1+T)^a − 1))·(1+T)^{a−1} ) (7-5), where, writing (1+T)^a − 1 = aT(1 + Tg(T)) and 1/((1+T)^a − 1) = (aT)^{-1}(1 + Th(T)) with g, h ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, (7-6)), log(T/((1+T)^a − 1)) := −log_p(a) + Σ_{n≥1} ((−1)^{n+1}/n)T^nh(T)^n (7-7) and log((1+T)^{a−1}) := (a − 1)log(1+T).
items.locator: §7, definition of F̃_a before Lemma 7.3 and (7-5)–(7-7) (printed pp. 156–157, PDF 57–58)
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/smoothed-polylog-combination: 'Phi^{(k)}_b(z) := -Li_k(z) + b^{1-k} Li_k(z^b) + (b - 1) log(z)^k/k! ... extends to a rigid analytic function on the whole disc D^-(1,1)'; at k = 1, Φ^{(1)}_a(1+T) = log(T/((1+T)^a − 1)) + (a − 1)log(1+T) = F̃_a(T) (L3/comparison-with-rjw-distribution-argument: 'RJW's Ftilde_a of §7, which is Phi^{(1)}_a(1+T)'). Also L3/rotated-smoothed-transform and rotated-smoothed-evaluation (the pole-cancelled transform G_{b,w}, whose w = 1 case is F_b).

items.name: Lemma 7.3: ∂F̃_a = F_a
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). With ∂ = (1+T)d/dT: ∂F̃_a(T) = F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1), since ∂log(((1+T)^a − 1)/(1+T)^a) = a/((1+T)^a − 1) and ∂log(T/(1+T)) = 1/T.
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/smoothed-polylog-combination (b)–(c): 'z d/dz Phi^{(k)}_b = Phi^{(k-1)}_b for k >= 1' and '(1+T) d/dT applied k times to it gives A_{w^x mu_b}(T) = G_(b,w)(T)'; at k = 1, w = 1 this is ∂F̃_a = F_a (with (a) 'Phi^{(0)}_b(z) is the pole-cancelled value F_b(z-1)').

items.name: Lemma 7.4: F̃_a lies in R^+
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). F̃_a(T) ∈ R^+ (power series over Q_p converging on the open unit disc); its coefficients have logarithmic growth.
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/smoothed-polylog-combination (c): 'for w in D^-(1,1) ..., Ftilde^{(k)}_{b,w}(T) := Phi^{(k)}_b(w(1+T)) lies in R^+'; w = 1, k = 1 is Lemma 7.4.

items.name: Equation (7-4): ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{-1}·μ_a = ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_a)(0)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). Let μ̃_a ∈ D^la(Z_p, Q_p) be the locally analytic distribution with Mahler transform F̃_a (Theorem 3.43, Lemma 7.4). Then x·μ̃_a = μ_a (Lemma 7.3 and Lemma 3.29), Res_{Z_p^×}(μ̃_a) = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a), and ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{-1}·μ_a = ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_a)(0) = F̃_a(0) − p^{-1}Σ_{ξ∈μ_p} F̃_a(ξ − 1).
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/unit-moment-via-distribution-primitive (k = 1, μ = μ_a, F̃ = F̃_a): 'int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu = lambda(1_{Z_p^x}) = ((1 - phi o psi) Ftilde)(0) = Ftilde(0) - p^{-1} sum_{xi in mu_p} Ftilde(xi - 1)'. Distribution theory: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L1 (Theorem 3.43, division by x on units).

items.name: Lemma 7.5: ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_a)(0) = −(1 − p^{-1})log_p(a)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). F̃_a(0) = −log_p(a) (7-8); (φ∘ψ)(F̃_a)(T) = p^{-1}log( ((1+T)^p − 1)/((1+T)^{ap} − 1) · (1+T)^{(a−1)p} ) (by Π_{ξ∈μ_p}(Xξ − 1) = X^p − 1, {ξ^a} = μ_p, Π ξ^{a−1} = 1), whose value at T = 0 is −p^{-1}log_p(a). Hence ((1 − φ∘ψ)F̃_a)(0) = −log_p(a) + p^{-1}log_p(a) = −(1 − p^{-1})log_p(a), and with (7-3), (7-4): lim_{s→1}(s − 1)ζ_{p,p−1}(s) = 1 − p^{-1}.
items.note: ColemanIntegration:L3/negative-moments-of-smoothed-measure: 'In particular, at w = 1, int_{Z_p^x} x^{-k} . mu_b = (1 - p^{-k}) Phi^{(k)}_b(1)' with L3/smoothed-polylog-combination (d) 'Phi^{(1)}_b(1) = -log_p(b)': at k = 1 this is (7-4) + Lemma 7.5 combined, ∫_{Z_p^×}x^{-1}·μ_a = −(1 − p^{-1})log_p(a). The φ∘ψ evaluation is L3/smoothed-polylog-distribution-relation ('sum_{xi in mu_p} Phi^{(k)}_b(xi w) = p^{1-k} Phi^{(k)}_b(w^p) ... including w in mu_p'). EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/trivial-character-component restates the value of ([a] − [1])ζ_p at the trivial character as −(1 − p^{−1})log_p(a). The printed final line has a sign slip (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E51).

items.name: The Eisenstein series G_k
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}. G_k(z) := Σ_{(c,d)∈Z²∖{(0,0)}} (cz + d)^{-k}, an absolutely convergent series on H.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/Defs.lean:186: 'def eisSummand (k : ℤ) (v : Fin 2 → ℤ) (z : ℍ) : ℂ := (v 0 * z + v 1) ^ (-k)'; G_k = ∑' v : Fin 2 → ℤ, eisSummand k v z (the v = 0 term is 0 by Lean's zpow convention), summable for k ≥ 3 (summable_eisSummand, EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:211). Same object. The notes call it the Eisenstein series 'of level k' (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E52).

items.name: G_k is a modular form of weight k for SL_2(Z)
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}. G_k is a modular form of weight k and level 1; indeed G_k = 2ζ(k)·E_k^{norm}, where E_k^{norm} = ½ Σ_{gcd(c,d)=1}(cz+d)^{-k} is the normalised Eisenstein series with constant term 1.
items.locator: §8, sentence after the definition of G_k (printed pp. 158–159, PDF 59–60)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/QExpansion.lean:249: 'lemma tsum_eisSummand_eq_riemannZeta_mul_eisensteinSeries {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) (z : ℍ) : ∑' v : Fin 2 → ℤ, eisSummand k v z = riemannZeta k * eisensteinSeries (N := 1) 0 k z', and EisensteinSeries/Basic.lean:47 'def E {k : ℕ} (hk : 3 ≤ k) : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k := ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • eisensteinSeriesMF (mod_cast hk) 0)...'. So G_k = 2ζ(k)·(E hk) pointwise, a modular form of weight k for SL_2(Z); the combination is not a single named declaration.

items.name: Normalised Fourier expansion of E_k
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}. E_k(z) := G_k(z)(k−1)!/(2(2πi)^k) = ζ(1−k)/2 + Σ_{n≥1} σ_{k−1}(n)q^n; in particular E_k has rational Fourier coefficients (ζ(1−k) = −B_k/k).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/normalized-eisenstein: 'For k≥4 define Eᵃ_k=(−B_k/(2k))·E_k^lib in the existing complex ModularForm(SL₂(ℤ),k), where E_k^lib is the pinned ModularForm.E'; L4/normalized-eisenstein-coeff 'a_n(Eᵃ_k)=σ_(k−1)(n) if n>0'; L4/normalized-eisenstein-zeta-constant 'a₀(Eᵃ_k)=ζ(1−k)/2'. Mathlib has the same expansion in other normalisations: tsum_eisSummand_eq_tsum_sigma_mul_cexp_pow (QExpansion.lean:220: '∑' v, eisSummand k v z = 2 * riemannZeta k + 2 * ((-2 * π * I) ^ k / (k - 1)!) * ∑' (n : ℕ+), σ (k - 1) n * cexp (2 * π * I * z) ^ (n : ℕ)' for even k ≥ 3), EisensteinSeries.q_expansion_bernoulli (298) and EisensteinSeries.E_qExpansion_coeff (323); the ζ(1−k)/2 normalisation needs riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli (HurwitzZetaValues.lean:251) in addition. Hence planned (routine corollary of library statements).

items.name: Dirac measures δ_d on Z_p^× and their moments
items.statement: For d ∈ Z_p^× (e.g. a positive integer prime to p), δ_d is the measure f ↦ f(d) on Z_p^×; for every k ∈ Z, ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·δ_d = d^k.
items.locator: §8, paragraph after the Fourier expansion (printed p. 159, PDF 60)
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:93: 'def dirac (x : X) : D(X, R) := toCLMEquiv.symm (ContinuousMap.evalCLM R x)' and :96 '@[simp] lemma dirac_apply (x : X) (f : C(X, R)) : dirac R x f = f x'. General statement (any compact X, any continuous f); with X = Z_p^× and f = x^k it gives d^k.

items.name: k ↦ p^k is not interpolated by a measure on Z_p^×
items.statement: (p odd.) There is no measure θ_p ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) ⊗ Q_p with ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·θ_p = p^k for all integers k ≥ 0 (or for all k in a set containing an integer k and a sequence k_n → +∞ with k_n ≡ k mod (p−1) and k_n → k p-adically): along such a sequence x^{k_n} → x^k uniformly on Z_p^×, so p^{k_n} → p^k, while p^{k_n} → 0.
items.note: Searched packets and stage descriptions for 'p^k', 'no measure', 'interpolat', 'Dirac ... δ_p', 'obstruction': the nearest is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-unbounded-moments ('For every B∈R there exist a positive natural n ... with B<‖M_n(ζ_p)‖'), a different obstruction. Elementary (continuity of μ and uniform convergence of x^{k_n}), but not planned. The printed argument uses an arbitrary sequence k_n → k p-adically, which does not make x^{k_n} → x^k (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E53); statement above uses the corrected hypothesis. Routed (source) to DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4, as the motivating obstruction for the Eisenstein family.

items.name: Definition 8.1: the p-stabilisation E_k^{(p)}
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}, and p prime: E_k^{(p)}(z) := E_k(z) − p^{k−1}E_k(pz).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/p-stabilized-eisenstein: 'For every prime p and k≥4 construct Eᵃ_{k,p}=res_(Γ₀(p)) Eᵃ_k−p^(k−1)V_p(res_(Γ₀(1)) Eᵃ_k) in the existing ModularForm(Γ₀(p),k). Here V_p is TauCeti.ModularForm.levelRaise, so pointwise Eᵃ_{k,p}(z)=Eᵃ_k(z)−p^(k−1)Eᵃ_k(pz).' Library ingredient: TauCeti.ModularForm.levelRaise (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Degeneracy.lean:278, '(V_d f) τ = f (d τ)' by levelRaise_apply, line 291).

items.name: Fourier expansion of E_k^{(p)}
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}, and p prime: E_k^{(p)} = ½(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) + Σ_{n≥1} σ^p_{k−1}(n)q^n, where σ^p_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d} d^{k−1} = σ_{k−1}(n) − p^{k−1}σ_{k−1}(n/p) (the last term only if p | n).
items.locator: §8, Definition 8.1, 'An easy check shows' (printed p. 159, PDF 60)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/p-stabilized-q-expansion ('qExpansion₁(Eᵃ_{k,p})=Q_k−p^(k−1)·expand_p(Q_k)'), L4/p-stabilized-positive-coeff ('a_n(Eᵃ_{k,p}) is the complex image of S_(p,k,n)=Σ_{d∣n,p∤d}d^(k−1)'), L4/p-stabilized-zeta-constant ('a₀(Eᵃ_{k,p})=(1−p^(k−1))ζ(1−k)/2'), L4/divisor-sum-euler-deletion. Tau Ceti has the q-expansion of level raising (TauCeti.ModularForm.qExpansion_levelRaise, Degeneracy.lean, QExpansion section) as an ingredient.

items.name: E_k^{(p)} is a modular form of weight k for Γ_0(p)
items.statement: For k ≥ 4 an even integer, H = {z ∈ C : Im z > 0}, q = e^{2πiz}, σ_{k−1}(n) = Σ_{0<d|n} d^{k−1}, and p prime, E_k^{(p)} is a modular form of weight k and level Γ_0(p) = {(a b; c d) ∈ SL_2(Z) : p | c}.
items.locator: §8, last sentence of Definition 8.1 (printed p. 159, PDF 60)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/p-stabilized-eisenstein constructs it 'in the existing ModularForm(Γ₀(p),k)' from ModularForm.E, restriction and TauCeti.ModularForm.levelRaise (V_p maps level-1 forms to Γ₀(p)). Mathlib has CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0 and ModularForm; no declaration for this specific form.

items.name: The coefficient measures A_n (n ≥ 1)
items.statement: For p prime and n ≥ 1: A_n := Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d} δ_d ∈ Λ(Z_p^×); for every integer e, ∫_{Z_p^×} x^e·A_n = Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d} d^e, in particular ∫ x^{k−1}·A_n = σ^p_{k−1}(n).
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/positive-eisenstein-measure: 'Define A_n=Σ_{d∣n,p∤d}δ_u(d) in the existing D(U,ℤ_p) ... This is an integral measure for every p and every n>0'; L4/positive-eisenstein-moment: 'For every e≥0, A_n(x^e)=Σ_{d∣n,p∤d}d^e in ℤ_p'. Built on Mathlib AbstractMeasure.dirac (see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/284).

items.name: The constant coefficient A_0 = xζ_p/2
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). Multiplication by the character x (μ ↦ xμ, ∫f·xμ = ∫f(x)x·μ) is a ring automorphism of Λ(Z_p^×) (for the convolution product) and extends to the total quotient ring Q(Z_p^×). Define A_0 := xζ_p/2 = (Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/2)/(a[a] − [1]) ∈ Q(Z_p^×). Then ∫_{Z_p^×} x^{k−1}·A_0 = ½∫_{Z_p^×} x^k·ζ_p = ½(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for k ≥ 1. A_0 is not a pseudo-measure in the sense of Definition 3.34: x^{-1}A_0 = ζ_p/2 is, i.e. (g[g] − [1])A_0 ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for all g ∈ Z_p^×, and its possible pole is at the character x^{-1}.
items.locator: §8, proof of Theorem 8.2, first sentence (printed p. 160, PDF 61)
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4 stage: 'Construct the coefficient measures A_n=sum_(d|n,p∤d) delta_d for n>0 and the pseudo-measure A_0=x zeta_p/2'; the packet's L4 coverage: 'Construct A₀=xζ_p/2 in the actual localized algebra using L1 arithmetic zeta and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 ... No A₀ is supplied by the positive-index constructor.' No node yet. The stage repeats the notes' incorrect word 'pseudo-measure' (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E54).

items.name: Theorem 8.2(a) (corrected): the coefficients of the Eisenstein family
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). There is E(z) = Σ_{n≥0} A_n q^n ∈ Q(Z_p^×)[[q]] with A_n ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for all n ≥ 1 and A_0 ∈ Q(Z_p^×) such that x^{-1}A_0 is a pseudo-measure (namely A_0 = xζ_p/2, A_n = Σ_{0<d|n, p∤d}δ_d). [Printed: 'A_0 is a pseudomeasure'; no pseudo-measure A_0 can satisfy (b), see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E54.]
items.note: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4 stage: 'Construct the coefficient measures ... and ... A_0=x zeta_p/2. Prove coefficientwise specialization at x^(k−1) gives the p-stabilized form, exactly RJW Theorem 8.2.' Positive part: L4/positive-eisenstein-series ('There is a canonical native AbstractMeasure(U,Z,Z[[q]]), denoted E⁺ ... This is the positive part of the source family, and does not define its missing A₀'). A_0: no node (see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/290).

items.name: Theorem 8.2(b): specialisation of the family at even weights
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). For every even k ≥ 4: Σ_{n≥0} (∫_{Z_p^×} x^{k−1}·A_n) q^n = E_k^{(p)}(z) as q-expansions, i.e. ∫x^{k−1}·A_0 = ½(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) (by Proposition 4.11: ∫_{Z_p^×}x^k·ζ_p = (1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k)) and ∫x^{k−1}·A_n = σ^p_{k−1}(n) for n ≥ 1.
items.note: n ≥ 1: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4/positive-eisenstein-modular-comparison ('For every prime p, even k≥4 and n>0, there is a unique integer S such that a_n(Eᵃ_{k,p})=ι_ℂ(S) and A_n(x^(k−1))=ι_ℤp(S) ... This is the positive-index specialization in Theorem8.2') and L4/positive-eisenstein-series-modular-comparison (whole series minus constant term). n = 0: only the L4 stage description (needs A_0, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/290, and the L1 interpolation of ζ_p).

items.name: Serre's constant-term principle (Remark 8.3(1))
items.statement: (Serre, 'Formes modulaires et fonctions zêta p-adiques', Corollaire 2, as paraphrased.) If the nonconstant Fourier coefficients of a family of (classical) modular forms of varying weight k are p-adically interpolated (converge as k varies p-adically), then so is the constant term; applied to Eisenstein series this constructs the p-adic zeta function (of Q, and of totally real fields) from the easy interpolation of σ_{k−1}(n).
items.locator: §8, Remark 8.3(1) (printed p. 160, PDF 61), citing Serre [73, Corollaire 2]
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3: 'For a totally real field F construct the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure ... Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof ... Specialization F=Q agrees with R03.' PadicFamilies:L0: 'Construct p-adic modular forms from the ordinary tower and the corresponding spaces of q-expansions, including the q-expansion principle'. Only paraphrased in the notes (not used later); the colloquial 'if k and k′ are close p-adically' must be read in Z/(p−1) × Z_p (Remark 8.3(2)).

items.name: Remark 8.3(2): the Eisenstein family on weight space (corrected)
items.statement: Standing notation (§§4–5, 7): p an odd prime; a a topological generator of Z_p^× (so ω(a) is a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨a⟩ ≠ 1); μ_a the measure on Z_p with Mahler transform F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a − 1) ∈ Z_p[[T]] (Proposition 4.4, Definition 4.5); θ_a = [a] − [1]; ζ_p = x^{-1}Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a)/θ_a the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure (Definition 4.10); ω the Teichmüller character, ⟨x⟩ = ω^{-1}(x)x; ζ_{p,i}(s) = ∫_{Z_p^×} ω(x)^i⟨x⟩^{1−s}·ζ_p for i ∈ {1, …, p−1}, s ∈ Z_p (Definition 5.16); log_p the Iwasawa logarithm (log_p(a) = log_p⟨a⟩). Let W(C_p) = Hom_cts(Z_p^×, C_p^×) (Remark 3.47), κ_k : x ↦ x^k; κ_k and κ_{k′} lie in the same component U_{ω^i} iff k ≡ k′ (mod p−1). Let O^+(W) be the bounded rigid analytic functions on W (↔ measures on Z_p^×, μ ↦ F_μ(κ) = ∫κ·μ) and Q(W) the rigid meromorphic functions with at most a simple pole at the trivial character (↔ pseudo-measures). Put B_n := F_{x^{-1}A_n}, i.e. B_n(κ) = ∫_{Z_p^×} κ(x)x^{-1}·A_n. Then B_0 = F_{ζ_p/2} ∈ Q(W), B_n ∈ O^+(W) for n ≥ 1, and for every even k ≥ 4: Σ_{n≥0} B_n(κ_k)q^n = E_k^{(p)}. (Equivalently, with B′_n := F_{A_n}: Σ B′_n(κ_{k−1})q^n = E_k^{(p)}, and B′_0 has its pole at κ_{−1}.)
items.note: Weight space and the measure/function dictionary: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0a ('construct the rigid analytic space representing continuous characters G→A× ... the finite-character components and polydisc charts') and LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L3 ('For Z_p^× and odd p obtain p−1 components ... bounded measures give bounded functions and pseudo-measures give meromorphic functions on their stated domains'). The family on weight space: PadicFamilies:L0 ('Construct the ordinary Eisenstein family from R03 and prove the geometric/cohomological identification of its q-expansion'); DirichletPadicLFunctions:L4 stage: 'Its realization on weight-space affinoids and comparison with Hida/Coleman theory belongs to R13.' The notes call E a 'Λ-adic modular form' (Remark 8.3(1)); that notion is PadicFamilies:L0's. The printed remark specialises at κ_k without the shift x^{-1} and omits 'even' (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E55).

items.name: Gauss sum of a Dirichlet character of arbitrary conductor
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character θ modulo N and a primitive N-th root of unity ε_N (in C or in Q̄_p): G(θ) := Σ_{c∈(Z/NZ)^×} θ(c)ε_N^c (= Σ_{c∈Z/NZ} θ(c)ε_N^c, θ vanishing off the units). It depends on ε_N: G_{ε_N^b}(θ) = θ^{-1}(b)G_{ε_N}(θ) for b ∈ (Z/NZ)^×.
items.locator: Used for general conductor N throughout §6 (Theorem 6.1, printed p. 149, PDF 50; Theorem 6.7, printed p. 154); defined for conductor p^n in Definition 5.2 (printed p. 140, PDF 41) and extended to conductor D in the proof of Theorem 5.7 (printed p. 144, PDF 45: 'defined as in Definition 5.2, replacing the power of p by D')
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/GaussSum.lean:72: 'def gaussSum (χ : MulChar R R') (ψ : AddChar R R') : R' := ∑ a, χ a * ψ a'; with R = ZMod N and ψ = AddChar.zmodChar N hε (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:139, c ↦ ε^c for ε^N = 1) this is G(θ). The dependence on the root is gaussSum_mulShift_eq (GaussSum.lean:83: 'gaussSum χ (ψ.mulShift a) = χ⁻¹ a * gaussSum χ ψ' for a a unit). Same definition.

items.name: Global cyclotomic fields F_n and F_n^+ (standing notation of Part II)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of Part II: p is an odd prime and the coefficient field is L = Q_p. For n ≥ 1, F_n := Q(μ_{p^n}) is the p^n-th cyclotomic field and F_n^+ := Q(μ_{p^n})^+ is its maximal totally real subfield, i.e. the fixed field of complex conjugation c.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:654 `CyclotomicField n K := (cyclotomic n K).SplittingField` (instance IsCyclotomicExtension {n} K); NumberField/InfinitePlace/TotallyRealComplex.lean:125 `NumberField.maximalRealSubfield K : Subfield K` (x with star(φ x)=φ x for every φ:K→+*ℂ); NumberField/CMField.lean:565 `IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.isCMField` (a cyclotomic extension of ℚ with some n>2 in S is CM; here p^n≥3), :143 `IsCMField.complexConj : K ≃ₐ[K⁺] K`, :199 `complexConj_eq_self_iff : complexConj K x = x ↔ x ∈ K⁺`. Same statement. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 also plans 'Construct Q(mu_m), its real subfield, roots of unity, ramification ...'.

items.name: Global units V_n and V_n^+
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, V_n := O_{F_n}^× and V_n^+ := O_{F_n^+}^× (the global units of F_n and F_n^+); V_n^+ ⊆ V_n.
items.note: Units of `𝓞 K` (NumberField.RingOfIntegers) for K = CyclotomicField (p^n) ℚ and K⁺; CMField.lean:270 `IsCMField.realUnits : Subgroup (𝓞 K)ˣ := (Units.map (algebraMap (𝓞 K⁺) (𝓞 K))).range` is V_n^+ ⊆ V_n. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 plans the unit groups, their norm maps and the cyclotomic units inside them.

items.name: Local cyclotomic fields K_n, K_n^+ and local units U_n, U_n^+
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, K_n := Q_p(μ_{p^n}) and K_n^+ := Q_p(μ_{p^n})^+, where for K_n '(−)^+' must be read as the fixed field of the automorphism ζ ↦ ζ^{−1} (the image of complex conjugation, i.e. of −1 ∈ Z_p^× ≅ Gal(K_n/Q_p)), equivalently K_n^+ = Q_p(ξ_{p^n} + ξ_{p^n}^{−1}), the completion of F_n^+ at p_n^+; U_n := O_{K_n}^× and U_n^+ := O_{K_n^+}^× are the local units.
items.locator: §9 Notation (printed p. 161, PDF 62); recalled §10.1 (printed p. 163, PDF 64)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/local-cyclotomic-level: 'Define K_n as native IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ_p {ρ_n} inside Ω ... the native IsCyclotomicExtension {p^(n+1)} instance'; L0/cyclotomic-integral-closure (O_n = ℤ_p[π_n]) and L0/continuous-unit-norm (units O_n^×). Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1. K_n^+ and U_n^+ have no packet node; stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4 works with U_{∞,1}^+ ('U_infty,1^+ / C_infty,1^+ ≃ ...'), so the plus part is planned only at stage level. Libraries: the objects are expressible but nothing is proved about them — `CyclotomicField (p^n) ℚ_[p]` (Mathlib Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:654, any base field) and `integralClosure ℤ_[p] K` (RingTheory/IntegralClosure/Algebra/Basic.lean:216) with its units; no file in either tree combines ℚ_[p] with cyclotomic/IsPrimitiveRoot, and the reviewed audit (data/library-coverage.json, ColemanPowerSeries:L0, 'partial') lists the ring of integers ℤ_p[ζ] and local-field structure as missing. The printed gloss 'maximal totally real subfield (i.e. fixed points under complex conjugation)' is literally meaningful only for F_n; the reading above is the intended one (not recorded as a mistake).

items.name: F_n/Q is Galois of degree (p−1)p^{n−1}, totally ramified at p, with unique prime p_n
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, F_n/Q is Galois of degree φ(p^n) = (p−1)p^{n−1} with Gal(F_n/Q) abelian; p is totally ramified in F_n: there is exactly one prime ideal p_n of O_{F_n} above p, namely p_n = (ξ_{p^n} − 1), with ramification index (p−1)p^{n−1} and residue degree 1.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:565 `isGalois [IsCyclotomicExtension S K L] : IsGalois K L`; NumberField/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:45 `Rat.finrank : finrank ℚ K = k.totient`; NumberField/Cyclotomic/Ideal.lean (namespace IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat, K with IsCyclotomicExtension {p^(k+1)} ℚ K): :136 `ncard_primesOver_of_prime_pow : (primesOver (p) (𝓞 K)).ncard = 1`, :149 `eq_span_zeta_sub_one_of_liesOver`, :175 `ramificationIdxIn_eq_of_prime_pow = p^k*(p−1)`, :168 `inertiaDegIn_eq_of_prime_pow = 1`; NumberField/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:302 `IsPrimitiveRoot.zeta_sub_one_prime`. Mathlib's k is n−1. Same statement.

items.name: F_n^+/Q: degree (p−1)p^{n−1}/2, Galois, totally ramified at p with unique prime p_n^+
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 (p odd), [F_n : F_n^+] = 2, so [F_n^+ : Q] = (p−1)p^{n−1}/2; F_n^+/Q is Galois (a subextension of the abelian extension F_n/Q); p is totally ramified in F_n^+ and p_n^+ := p_n ∩ O_{F_n^+} is the unique prime of F_n^+ above p.
items.note: Library part: CMField.lean:83 instance `IsCMField.isQuadraticExtension : IsQuadraticExtension K⁺ K` with :565 `IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.isCMField` gives [F_n:F_n^+]=2. Not found in Mathlib/Tau Ceti: the ramification and unique-prime statement for F_n^+ (it follows from the F_n statement by multiplicativity of ramification indices, which Tau Ceti uses in NumberTheory/NumberField/Cyclotomic/IrreducibleOfUnramified.lean but does not state for K⁺). Planned by the stage description of IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0: 'Construct Q(mu_m), its real subfield, roots of unity, ramification ...' (no packet node).

items.name: K_n/Q_p and K_n^+/Q_p: Galois, totally ramified, of degrees (p−1)p^{n−1} and (p−1)p^{n−1}/2
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, the cyclotomic polynomial Φ_{p^n} is irreducible over Q_p (Φ_{p^n}(X+1) is Eisenstein at p), so K_n/Q_p is Galois of degree (p−1)p^{n−1}, totally ramified, with residue field F_p and maximal ideal (π_n); K_n^+/Q_p is Galois, totally ramified, of degree (p−1)p^{n−1}/2.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/shifted-cyclotomic-eisenstein ('Φ_(p^(n+1))(X+1) over ℤ_p is Eisenstein at (p)'), L0/local-cyclotomic-irreducible ('Φ_(p^(n+1)) is irreducible over ℚ_p'), L0/local-cyclotomic-degree ('[K_n:ℚ_p]=p^n(p−1)'), L0/relative-cyclotomic-degree, L0/cyclotomic-prime-ideal-power ('pO_n = m_n^(d_n)', total ramification), L0/cyclotomic-residue-field (residue field ZMod p). Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1. Library: RingTheory/Polynomial/Eisenstein/IsIntegral.lean:79 (Eisenstein over ℤ only) and the generic Galois statement; the Q_p field itself is not in either library. K_n^+ has no node (stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4 uses plus parts).

items.name: Infinite towers F_∞, F_∞^+, K_∞, K_∞^+ and the primes 𝔭, 𝔭^+
items.note: Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension S K L allows the infinite set S = {p^n : n ≥ 1}, so F_∞ (and K_∞ over ℚ_[p]) is expressible, and Basic.lean:565 isGalois applies; the uniqueness of the prime above p in the infinite extension is in neither library. Planned: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 'Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension ..., its finite layers, Galois actions, norm maps, decomposition and inertia groups' and L1 (inverse limits over the tower); ColemanPowerSeries:L0 builds the local tower K_n inside one algebraically closed Ω.

items.name: Galois groups Γ = Gal(F_∞/Q) and Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/Q) = Γ/⟨c⟩
items.statement: Γ := Gal(F_∞/Q), a profinite group identified by infinite Galois theory with lim_n Gal(F_n/Q); Γ^+ := Gal(F_∞^+/Q) = Γ/⟨c⟩, c complex conjugation.
items.note: Library ingredients (general infinite Galois theory, not this instance): Mathlib FieldTheory/Galois/Profinite.lean:323 `InfiniteGalois.continuousMulEquivToLimit` (Gal(K/k) ≅ limit of Gal(L/k) over all finite Galois subextensions L); FieldTheory/Galois/Infinite.lean:228 `InfiniteGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient (H : ClosedSubgroup Gal(K/k)) [H.Normal] : Gal(K/k) ⧸ H ≃* Gal(fixedField H/k)`, which gives Γ/⟨c⟩ ≅ Gal(F_∞^+/Q) once c is defined (⟨c⟩ is finite, hence closed, and normal as Γ is abelian). Not packaged: complex conjugation on the infinite extension F_∞ (Mathlib's IsCMField.complexConj is for number fields), and the limit over the chain (F_n). Planned with the cyclotomic tower in IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 ('Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension ..., its finite layers, Galois actions').

items.name: Mod-p^n cyclotomic character χ_n : Gal(F_n/Q) ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^×
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 there is an isomorphism χ_n : Gal(F_n/Q) → (Z/p^nZ)^× determined by σ(ξ) = ξ^{χ_n(σ)} for every σ ∈ Gal(F_n/Q) and every primitive p^n-th root of unity ξ.
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Gal.lean:77 `IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow (h : Irreducible (cyclotomic n K)) : Gal(L/K) ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ` (f μ = μ^k), with RingTheory/Polynomial/Cyclotomic/Roots.lean:190 `cyclotomic.irreducible_rat`; NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:212 `modularCyclotomicCharacter`. Same statement.

items.name: Cyclotomic character χ : Γ ≅ Z_p^× (9-1) and Γ^+ ≅ Z_p^×/{±1}
items.statement: χ := lim_n χ_n is an isomorphism of profinite groups Γ = Gal(F_∞/Q) ≅ lim_n (Z/p^nZ)^× ≅ Z_p^×, characterised by σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ(σ)} for all ζ ∈ μ_{p^∞}; since χ(c) = −1 it induces Γ^+ ≅ Z_p^×/{±1}.
items.note: Library part: CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307 `cyclotomicCharacter (p) : (L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ` with :323 spec (g ζ = ζ^(χ(g) mod p^n)) and :336 continuity — a homomorphism, not the isomorphism. Bijectivity is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Planned: Tau Ceti's BelyiMaps roadmap, milestone 13.2 'Cyclotomic surjectivity: `cyclotomicCharacter ℓ` is surjective onto `ℤ_[ℓ]ˣ` ... over ℚ' (injectivity on Gal(F_∞/Q) is immediate since F_∞ is generated by μ_{p^∞}); IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 plans the cyclotomic tower's Galois actions. The quotient statement Γ^+ ≅ Z_p^×/{±1} has no separate plan (a formal consequence).

items.name: Principal units U_{n,1} and U_{n,1}^+ (9-2)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, U_{n,1} := {u ∈ U_n : u ≡ 1 (mod 𝔭_n)} (𝔭_n read as the maximal ideal (π_n) of O_{K_n}, the completion of the global prime 𝔭_n) and U_{n,1}^+ := U_{n,1} ∩ U_n^+.
items.note: Generic library: RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationSubring.lean:635 `principalUnitGroup`; Tau Ceti NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean:88 `unitFiltration K i : Subgroup Kˣ` for a nonarchimedean local field K, with :173 `unitFiltration_one` identifying U(K,1) with principalUnitGroup. They apply once K_n is constructed. Planned: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-integral-reduction (red_n : O_n → F_p, kernel (ϖ_n)) and L0/principal-norm-compatible-units ('the native kernel subgroup of normLimitResidue') — finite-level U_{n,1} = ker(red_n on O_n^×) is implicit there. Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Z_p-module structure on principal units
items.statement: For u ∈ U_{n,1} (or U_{n,1}^+) and a ∈ Z_p the series u^a := Σ_{k≥0} binom(a,k)(u−1)^k converges in O_{K_n}; this extends the Z-module structure and makes U_{n,1}, U_{n,1}^+ Z_p-modules. The full unit groups U_n, U_n^+ are only Z-modules (they contain μ_{p−1}).
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L0: '... principal units form its compact Z_p-module ... Do not put a Z_p-module structure on all local units: their prime-to-p torsion remains.' Coverage note of that stage: 'Verify principal-unit pro-p hypotheses before importing the ℤ_p-module construction; full units are not a ℤ_p-module.' No node yet. Library: Mathlib NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean:78 `PadicInt.instBinomialRing` (binom(a,k) ∈ ℤ_p) only; no ℤ_p-power on principal units or on abelian pro-p groups in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched `Module ℤ_[p]`, padic pow names, TauCeti Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite).

items.name: Notation convention X_n^+, X_{n,1}, X_{n,1}^+
items.statement: For any subgroup X_n ⊆ U_n (in particular any X_n ⊆ V_n, via V_n ⊆ U_n induced by F_n ↪ K_n): X_n^+ := X_n ∩ U_n^+, X_{n,1} := X_n ∩ U_{n,1}, X_{n,1}^+ := X_n^+ ∩ U_{n,1}^+.
items.note: Pure notation; realised where used: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1 ('closures of global principal units, semilocal principal units ... All closures and principal-unit restrictions must agree with R04') and ColemanPowerSeries:L4 ('Use the actual global subgroup D_n ... intersected with units'). The embedding V_n ⊆ U_n (completion of F_n at 𝔭_n) is part of those stages.

items.name: Infinite-level local units U_∞, U_{∞,1}, U_∞^+, U_{∞,1}^+ (9-3)
items.statement: U_∞ := lim_n U_n, U_{∞,1} := lim_n U_{n,1}, U_∞^+ := lim_n U_n^+, U_{∞,1}^+ := lim_n U_{n,1}^+, inverse limits over n ≥ 1 with respect to the norm maps N_{n,n−1} = N_{K_n/K_{n−1}} : U_n → U_{n−1} (which preserve principal and plus parts).
items.locator: §9, display (9-3) (printed pp. 162–163, PDF 63–64); recalled §10.1 (printed p. 163, PDF 64)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/norm-compatible-units ('Define normCompatibleUnits(p) as the native subgroup of V consisting of u with N_n(u_(n+1))=u_n for every n'), L0/principal-norm-compatible-units, L0/integral-relative-norm, L0/continuous-unit-norm (norm transitions O_{n+1}^× → O_n^×). Plus parts: no node (stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4 uses U_{∞,1}^+). Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Compactness, Γ-action and Λ(Γ)-module structure of the infinite-level units (corrected)
items.statement: U_∞, U_{∞,1}, U_∞^+, U_{∞,1}^+ are compact (profinite) abelian groups carrying continuous actions of Γ = Gal(F_∞/Q) ≅ Gal(K_∞/Q_p) (p is totally ramified in F_∞), resp. of Γ^+. The principal parts U_{∞,1} and U_{∞,1}^+ are compact Z_p-modules, hence continuous Λ(Γ)- resp. Λ(Γ^+)-modules. [Correction: U_∞ and U_∞^+ are not Z_p-modules: U_∞ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1} and U_∞^+ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1}^+.]
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/norm-compatible-units-compact ('The actual normCompatibleUnits(p) subtype is a compact space'), L0/principal-norm-compatible-compact; stage L0: 'principal units form its compact Z_p-module. Extend the G-action to a continuous completed-group-ring action via R01. Do not put a Z_p-module structure on all local units ... Prove U_infty=mu_{p−1}×U_infty,1 for odd p'. Λ(Γ) itself: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 (completed group rings); not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched completedGroupAlgebra/IwasawaAlgebra). The printed sentence calls all four modules compact Z_p-modules — see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E62.

items.name: Compatible system of roots of unity (ξ_{p^n}) and π_n = ξ_{p^n} − 1
items.statement: Fix, once and for all, primitive p^n-th roots of unity ξ_{p^n} (n ≥ 1) with ξ_{p^{n+1}}^p = ξ_{p^n} for all n, and put π_n := ξ_{p^n} − 1.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/compatible-cyclotomic-roots ('Choose ρ_0 primitive of order p in Ω. Recursively choose ρ_(n+1) as a pth root of ρ_n'), L0/cyclotomic-root-compatibility (ρ_(n+1)^p=ρ_n), L0/cyclotomic-root-primitivity, L0/primitive-root-lift. Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1. For the global fields the compatible roots are requested from IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 (see EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/p-extended-cyclotomic-number). Mathlib has IsPrimitiveRoot but no packaged compatible system.

items.name: π_n is a uniformiser of K_n
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, π_n = ξ_{p^n} − 1 generates the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring O_{K_n}; π_n^{(p−1)p^{n−1}} = p·(unit).
items.locator: §9, end (printed p. 163, PDF 64); used in Lemma 10.1
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-difference-irreducible ('ϖ_n is irreducible in O_n, hence is a uniformizer of this algebraic DVR'), L0/cyclotomic-integers-dvr, L0/cyclotomic-maximal-ideal, L0/cyclotomic-difference-power-unit (ϖ_n^(d_n)=p·u). Library has only the global analogue: NumberField/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:302 `IsPrimitiveRoot.zeta_sub_one_prime` (ζ−1 prime in 𝓞 F_n). Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Evaluation of Z_p[[T]] at π_n (bounded functions on the open unit disc)
items.statement: Every f ∈ Z_p[[T]] converges on B(0,1) = {z ∈ C_p : |z| < 1} and defines a bounded rigid analytic function there (Remark 3.39); in particular f(π_n) ∈ O_{K_n}, and f ↦ f(π_n) is a ring homomorphism Z_p[[T]] → O_{K_n}, continuous for the (p,T)-adic topology.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-series-evaluation ('Construct seriesEvaluation(n): ℤ_p⟦T⟧→O_n as a ring homomorphism, using native PowerSeries.eval₂Hom at ϖ_n'), L0/cyclotomic-series-evaluation-continuity, L0/cyclotomic-evaluation-polynomial. Library (generic): Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Evaluation.lean:158 `PowerSeries.eval₂Hom (hφ : Continuous φ) (ha : HasEval a)` and :211 `aeval` for topologically nilpotent a in a complete linearly topologised ring. The C_p-disc statement is Remark 3.39 (earlier chunk).

items.name: Lemma 10.1 (finite-level interpolation)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and u ∈ U_n. There exists f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× with f(π_n) = u (constructed digit by digit in the π_n-adic expansion; f is far from unique). In fact f can be taken to be a polynomial of degree < [K_n:Q_p] with f(0) ∈ Z_p^×.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-unit-series-evaluation-lift: 'For every u∈O_nˣ there exists f∈ℤ_p[T] with degree less than d_n such that its native power-series image is a unit and seriesEvaluation(n)(f)=u' (stronger, polynomial form; also L0/cyclotomic-unit-polynomial-lift). The 'exercise' that f is invertible is Mathlib RingTheory/PowerSeries/Inverse.lean:111 `PowerSeries.isUnit_iff_constantCoeff`. Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Theorem 10.2 (Coleman)
items.statement: There exists a unique injective homomorphism of multiplicative groups U_∞ → Z_p[[T]]^×, u ↦ f_u, such that f_u(π_n) = u_n for all u = (u_n)_{n≥1} ∈ U_∞ and all n ≥ 1.
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L1: 'Prove uniqueness of an interpolating unit power series via Weierstrass preparation. Construct it by compactness and norm iteration and prove the group isomorphism U_infty ≃ {f∈Z_p[[T]]^× : N(f)=f}. This is Theorem 10.13'; L4 acceptance 'Theorems 10.2/10.13/10.15'. Packet coverage for L1 says injectivity and surjectivity are not yet supplied by nodes (L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-map constructs the map in the other direction). Theorem 10.13 is the sharper form.

items.name: Local cyclotomic units c_n(a)
items.statement: For a ∈ Z prime to p and n ≥ 1, c_n(a) := (ξ_{p^n}^a − 1)/(ξ_{p^n} − 1) ∈ U_n; it is a unit because ξ_{p^n}^a is again a primitive p^n-th root of unity, so ξ_{p^n}^a − 1 and ξ_{p^n} − 1 are both uniformisers of K_n. (For a > 0, c_n(a) = Σ_{i=0}^{a−1} ξ_{p^n}^i; for a < 0, c_n(a) = −ξ_{p^n}^{a} c_n(−a).)
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'For c_n(a)=(xi_{p^n}^a−1)/(xi_{p^n}−1), compute Delta(f_c)=a−1−F_a'; global form EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/smoothed-unit-comparison: 'c_m(a) = (1 − ζ_m^a)/(1 − ζ_m) = ∑_{i<a} ζ_m^i is a unit of ℤ[ζ_m] ... for m = p^n it is RJW's c_n(a)' (a ∈ ℕ coprime to m). The unit property itself is library for natural a in any domain: Mathlib RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/CyclotomicUnits.lean:100 `IsPrimitiveRoot.geom_sum_isUnit (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hj : j.Coprime n) : IsUnit (∑ i ∈ range j, ζ^i)`; it becomes the local statement once K_n exists (ColemanPowerSeries:L0).

items.name: Relative minimal polynomial of ξ_{p^n} and norms of ξ_{p^n}^b − 1
items.statement: For n ≥ 2 the minimal polynomial of ξ_{p^n} over K_{n−1} is X^p − ξ_{p^{n−1}}; consequently, for every b ∈ Z prime to p, N_{K_n/K_{n−1}}(ξ_{p^n}^b − 1) = Π_{η∈μ_p}(ξ_{p^n}^b η − 1) = ξ_{p^n}^{bp} − 1 = ξ_{p^{n−1}}^b − 1, using X^p − 1 = Π_{η∈μ_p}(Xη − 1) (valid because p is odd).
items.locator: §10.2, proof of Lemma 10.3 (printed p. 165, PDF 66); reused in the proof of Lemma 10.9 (printed p. 167)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/relative-cyclotomic-minpoly ('The minimal polynomial of ζ_(n+1) over K_n is X^p−ζ_n'), L0/relative-cyclotomic-difference-norm ('N_(K_(n+1)/K_n)(ζ_(n+1)−1) equals (−1)^(p+1)(ζ_n−1)': the case b=1). The general b is not a node (ColemanPowerSeries:L2 coverage: 'proving membership, relative norm compatibility and interpolation' remains). Global analogues: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/minpoly-step-of-dvd and L0/distribution-relation-of-dvd ('N_{L/K}(1 − ζ) = 1 − η' for ℓ | m). Checked: Π_{η∈μ_p}η = 1 for odd p, so Π_η(Xη−1) = X^p−1.

items.name: Lemma 10.3 (the cyclotomic units form a norm-compatible system)
items.statement: For a ∈ Z prime to p, N_{K_n/K_{n−1}}(c_n(a)) = c_{n−1}(a) for all n ≥ 2; hence c(a) := (c_n(a))_{n≥1} ∈ U_∞.
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2 (coverage remaining: 'Identify the explicit f_a with the Coleman series of the actual unit tower c(a), proving membership, relative norm compatibility and interpolation'); stage L4 ('Construct the principal Teichmüller-adjusted compatible generator ... Prove its membership, norm compatibility'). No node proves it for general a yet.

items.name: Coleman power series of c(a): f_{c(a)}(T) = ((1+T)^a − 1)/T (corrected polynomial remark)
items.statement: For a ∈ Z prime to p, f_{c(a)}(T) := ((1+T)^a − 1)/T ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× ((1+T)^a the binomial series; division by T is exact and the constant term a is a p-adic unit) satisfies f_{c(a)}(π_n) = c_n(a) for all n ≥ 1, so it is the Coleman power series of c(a). It is a polynomial, Σ_{i=0}^{a−1}(1+T)^i, when a > 0; for a < 0 it is not a polynomial: f_{c(a)} = −(1+T)^{a} f_{c(−a)} (e.g. f_{c(−1)} = −(1+T)^{−1}).
items.locator: §10.2, between Lemma 10.3 and Proposition 10.4 (printed p. 165, PDF 66)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L2/cyclotomic-series ('For every a∈ℕ, f_a(T)=Σ_(0≤i<a)(1+T)ⁱ'), L2/cyclotomic-series-unit, L2/cyclotomic-unit-value, L2/negative-cyclotomic-factorization ('f_(−a)=−B_(−a)q_a satisfies T f_(−a)=B_(−a)−1'), L2/negative-cyclotomic-unit. The interpolation f_{c(a)}(π_n)=c_n(a) and norm-invariance remain stage-level (ColemanPowerSeries:L2 coverage). See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E59 on the 'polynomial' remark (lead ColemanPowerSeries/E3).

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (logarithmic derivative of f_{c(a)})
items.statement: For a ∈ Z prime to p: ∂log f_{c(a)}(T) := ∂f_{c(a)}/f_{c(a)} = a − 1 − F_a(T) in Z_p[[T]].
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L2/cyclotomic-smoothed-comparison ('Let a∈ℕ be a unit in R. If F∈B satisfies T f_a F=f_a−C(a), then Δ(u_a)=C(a−1)−F'), L2/cyclotomic-logarithmic-derivative-cleared, and for negative a L2/negative-smoothed-comparison ('Δ(v)=C(−a−1)−F_(−a)'). Computation re-checked: ∂log((1+T)^a−1) − ∂log T = a + a/((1+T)^a−1) − 1 − 1/T = a−1−F_a.

items.name: Lemma 10.5 (cyclotomic units versus μ_a)
items.statement: For a ∈ Z prime to p: Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_{∂log f_{c(a)}}) = −Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_a); equivalently (1 − φ∘ψ)∂log f_{c(a)} = −(1 − φ∘ψ)F_a, because 1 − φ∘ψ kills the constant a − 1 (ψ fixes constants).
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'For c_n(a)=... compute Delta(f_c)=a−1−F_a and hence Col_0(c(a)) = −([a]−1) zeta_p'. The ingredient 'φψ fixes constants' follows from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/psi-series-phi (ψ∘φ = id) and φ(c)=c; the restriction formula is L2/series-unit-restriction. No dedicated node.

items.name: Weierstrass preparation for Z_p[[T]] and finiteness of zeros (quoted)
