items.statement: Every nonzero h ∈ Z_p[[T]] can be written h = p^m·u(T)·r(T) with m ≥ 0, u ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× and r a (distinguished) polynomial; hence h, which converges on the maximal ideal of O_{Q̄_p} (indeed of O_{C_p}), has only finitely many zeros there (u has none).
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/nonzero-power-series-factorization: 'Every nonzero f ∈ O⟦T⟧ factors uniquely as f = ϖ^μ·F·u ... Consequently f has at most deg F zeros in the open unit disc of any complete valued field extending Frac O (for instance ℂ_p), and power series agreeing at infinitely many points of that disc are equal' (it cites this proof). Library core: Mathlib RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean:813 `PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassFactorization (hg : g.map (IsLocalRing.residue A) ≠ 0) : ∃ f h, g.IsWeierstrassFactorization f h` (A complete local); the p^m extraction and the zero count are not in Mathlib.

items.name: Lemma 10.7 (uniqueness of the interpolating series)
items.statement: Let u = (u_n) ∈ U_∞ and f, g ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× with f(π_n) = g(π_n) = u_n for all n ≥ 1. Then f = g. (More generally, two elements of Z_p[[T]] agreeing at the infinitely many distinct points π_n are equal.)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/nonzero-power-series-factorization (last clause: 'power series agreeing at infinitely many points of that disc are equal'); stage ColemanPowerSeries:L1: 'Prove uniqueness of an interpolating unit power series via Weierstrass preparation' (packet coverage: 'Import pinned Weierstrass through PMIA L4 ... prove interpolation uniqueness').

items.name: Frobenius and evaluation at the tower: φ(f)(π_{n+1}) = f(π_n) (10-1)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/arithmetic-frobenius-evaluation: 'In K_(n+1), the value of ε_(n+1)(φF) equals the inclusion of ε_n(F).' Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Z_p[[T]] is free of rank p over φ(Z_p[[T]])
items.statement: B = Z_p[[T]] is a free module of rank p over A = φ(Z_p[[T]]) = Z_p[[φ(T)]], with basis 1, 1+T, …, (1+T)^{p−1}; B = A[1+T] with (1+T)^p = 1 + φ(T) ∈ A.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/frobenius-power-basis ('Construct the basis (1,Y,…,Y^(p−1)) of B over B with scalar algebra φ ... Its rank is exactly p'), L1/frobenius-coordinate-injectivity, L1/frobenius-coordinate-surjectivity, L1/residue-coordinate-uniqueness. The printed proof asserts the degree without proof (packet locator: 'finite-free algebra implicit in the degree-p assertion').

items.name: Lemma 10.8 (Coleman's norm operator N)
items.statement: There is a unique multiplicative operator N : Z_p[[T]] → Z_p[[T]] such that (φ∘N)(f)(T) = Π_{η∈μ_p} f(η(1+T) − 1) for every f ∈ Z_p[[T]], the product being computed in O_{K_1}[[T]] (T ↦ η(1+T) − 1 is a convergent substitution since η − 1 ∈ 𝔭_1). Concretely N = φ^{−1}∘N_{B/A}, where N_{B/A} is the determinant norm of the free rank-p extension B/A; after base change to O_{K_1} the maps T ↦ (1+T)η − 1 (η ∈ μ_p) are the automorphisms of O_{K_1}[[T]] over O_{K_1}[[φ(T)]], which identifies N_{B/A}(f) with the product (they are not automorphisms of Z_p[[T]] for η ≠ 1).
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-determinant-norm ('Define N:B→*B to be the existing Algebra.norm for B with its explicitly chosen Frobenius scalar algebra'), L1/coleman-norm-matrix, L1/coleman-norm-root-product ('iota(phi(N(F)))=product_(i in Fin p) tau_i(F) in O[[T]]'), L1/coleman-norm-root-product-unique (uniqueness). Stage L1: 'Only after adjoining p-th roots of unity identify the determinant with the product ... These substitutions are not automorphisms over Z_p before adjoining xi.' See the gap issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E58 (lead ColemanPowerSeries/E2).

items.name: ψ = p^{−1}φ^{−1}∘Tr_{B/A}
items.statement: With B/A as above, ψ = p^{−1}·φ^{−1}∘Tr_{B/A} on Z_p[[T]] (in particular Tr_{B/A}(f) ∈ p·A).
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-trace-psi ('For every F∈B, colemanTrace(F)=p·AbstractMeasure.psiSeries(F)'), L1/coleman-integral-trace, L1/coleman-trace-divisibility, L1/frobenius-zeroth-coordinate-psi.

items.name: Norm-fixed units (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id}
items.statement: Since N is multiplicative it preserves Z_p[[T]]^×; (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id} := {f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× : N(f) = f}, a subgroup.
items.locator: §10.3, after Lemma 10.8 and Proposition 10.10 (printed p. 167, PDF 68)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-norm-fixed-units ('Define the subgroup B_Nˣ={u∈Bˣ : N(u)=u}'), L1/coleman-norm-fixed-membership, L1/coleman-fixed-constant-units (C(c) norm-fixed iff c^(p−1)=1).

items.name: Lemma 10.9 (norm operator versus field norms)
items.statement: For f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× and n ≥ 1: f(π_n) ∈ U_n (as f(π_n)^{−1} = f^{−1}(π_n) is integral), and N_{K_{n+1}/K_n}(f(π_{n+1})) = (N f)(π_n); i.e. diagram (10-2) commutes.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/arithmetic-norm-evaluation ('For every F∈ℤ_p[[T]], integralNorm_n(ε_(n+1)(F))=ε_n(colemanNorm(F)) in O_n' — for all F, not only units), L1/arithmetic-unit-norm-evaluation (unit form), L1/arithmetic-multiplication-matrix. Packet indexing: the ColemanPowerSeries packet's level n is Q_p(mu_{p^(n+1)}) (n>=0), i.e. the paper's K_{n+1}; the paper's K_n=Q_p(mu_{p^n}) starts at n=1.

items.name: Proposition 10.10 (the evaluation map R)
items.statement: R : (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id} → U_∞, f ↦ (f(π_n))_{n≥1}, is a well-defined injective group homomorphism.
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-map ('Construct normFixedEvaluation(p):normFixedUnits(p)→normCompatibleUnits(p) as a native continuous monoid homomorphism'), L1/norm-fixed-arithmetic-compatibility, L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-closed-image. Injectivity is Lemma 10.7 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/nonzero-power-series-factorization); packet coverage: 'the constructed map and closed image do not supply either assertion'. The printed proof only checks well-definedness; injectivity is the preceding Lemma 10.7 (not treated as a mistake).

items.name: Lemma 10.11(i) (Frobenius reflects congruences to 1)
items.statement: Let f ∈ Z_p[[T]] and k ≥ 0. If φ(f) ≡ 1 (mod p^k) then f ≡ 1 (mod p^k).
items.locator: §10.3, Lemma 10.11(i) (printed p. 168, PDF 69); proof left as exercise [16, Lemma 2.3.1]
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/frobenius-congruence-reflection: 'For every f∈B and k≥0, p^k divides φ(f)−1 if and only if p^k divides f−1.' (iff, stronger).

items.name: Lemma 10.11(ii) (N(f) ≡ f mod p)
items.statement: For every f ∈ Z_p[[T]] (no unit hypothesis): N(f) ≡ f (mod p).
items.locator: §10.3, Lemma 10.11(ii) (printed p. 168, PDF 69); proof left as exercise [16, Lemma 2.3.1]
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-norm-residue-identity: 'For every f∈B, p divides N(f)−f. No unit hypothesis is imposed.' Checked: φ(Nf) ≡ f^p ≡ f(T^p) ≡ φ(f) (mod p), then the additive form of (i).

items.name: Lemma 10.11(iii) (the norm improves congruences to 1)
items.statement: Let f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× with f ≡ 1 (mod p^k) for some k ≥ 1. Then N(f) ≡ 1 (mod p^{k+1}).
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-norm-improves-one-congruence ('For f∈B and k≥1, if p^k divides f−1 then p^(k+1) divides N(f)−1' — no unit hypothesis needed). The proof's congruences modulo 𝔭_1 p^k Z_p[[T]] are correct, but they are asserted in the ring 𝔭_1ℤ_p⟦T⟧, where 𝒪_{K_1}⟦T⟧ is meant: issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E105 (the lead ColemanPowerSeries/E4).

items.name: Lemma 10.11(iv) (convergence of norm iterates)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-norm-iterate-congruence ('For an actual unit u∈Bˣ and integers k₂≥k₁≥0, p^(k₁+1) divides N^[k₂](u)−N^[k₁](u)'), with L1/coleman-norm-iterated-improvement.

items.name: Compactness of Z_p[[T]]^× and continuity of evaluation (used in Proposition 10.12)
items.statement: Z_p[[T]] with its (p,T)-adic (= coefficientwise) topology is compact, Z_p[[T]]^× (constant term in Z_p^×) is closed in it, hence compact (and metrisable, so every sequence has a convergent subsequence); for each n ≥ 1, f ↦ f(π_n) ∈ O_{K_n} is continuous.
items.note: Compactness: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/integral-measures-weak-compact with L2/integral-amice-weak-homeomorphism (weak topology on measures = coefficientwise topology on ℤ_p⟦T⟧); ColemanPowerSeries:L3/norm-fixed-units-compact (norm-fixed units compact). Continuity: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-series-evaluation-continuity. Neither library states compactness of a power-series ring (searched CompactSpace with PowerSeries/MvPowerSeries). The printed proof uses the continuity of evaluation without stating it.

items.name: Proposition 10.12 (surjectivity of R)
items.statement: R : (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id} → U_∞ is surjective. (Proof: for u ∈ U_∞ pick f_n ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× with f_n(π_n) = u_n; then (N^k f_{n+k})(π_n) = u_n, g_m := N^m f_{2m} satisfies g_m(π_n) ≡ u_n (mod p^{m+1}) for m ≥ n, a limit point f_u of (g_m) satisfies f_u(π_n) = u_n for all n, and N(f_u) = f_u by Lemmas 10.9 and 10.7.)
items.locator: §10.3, Proposition 10.12 and proof (printed pp. 168–169, PDF 69–70), display (10-4)
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L1: 'Construct it by compactness and norm iteration'; packet coverage: 'prove interpolation uniqueness, compact successive approximation and surjectivity onto the entire norm-compatible tower'. Partial nodes take a different route: L1/coleman-norm-limit (L(u) := lim_k N^[k](u) coefficientwise), L1/coleman-norm-limit-fixed (N(L(u))=L(u)), L1/coleman-norm-limit-precision.

items.name: Theorem 10.13 (Coleman's isomorphism)
items.statement: There is a unique group isomorphism U_∞ → (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id}, u ↦ f_u, such that f_u(π_n) = u_n for all u ∈ U_∞ and n ≥ 1 (namely R^{−1}).
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L1: 'prove the group isomorphism U_infty ≃ {f∈Z_p[[T]]^× : N(f)=f}. This is Theorem 10.13, not merely an injective map with interpolation assumed.' L4 acceptance: 'Theorems 10.2/10.13/10.15'.

items.name: Logarithmic derivative ∂log
items.statement: For f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^×, ∂log f := ∂f/f = (1+T)f′(T)/f(T) ∈ Z_p[[T]]; ∂log is a homomorphism from the multiplicative group Z_p[[T]]^× (in particular from (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id}) to the additive group Z_p[[T]].
items.locator: §10.4, Definition 10.14 (second map) (printed p. 170, PDF 71); used in §10.2
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative ('For f∈Bˣ define Δ_R(f)=Y·D(f)·f⁻¹ in B'), L2/logarithmic-derivative-product, L2/logarithmic-derivative-constants; L2/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-map (on norm-fixed units Δ lands in ker(ψ−id), sharper than the printed target Z_p[[T]]).

items.name: ∂^{−1} on Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} is multiplication by x^{−1} (recalled)
items.statement: ∂ restricts to a bijection of Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0}; its inverse ∂^{−1} corresponds under A to multiplication by x^{−1} on measures supported on Z_p^×.
items.locator: §10.4, Definition 10.14 (fourth map) and the sentence before it (printed p. 170, PDF 71)
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/inverse-weight (J = division by x on unit-supported measures), L2/inverse-mahler ('H=A∘J∘A⁻¹ ... ψSeries(HF)=0'), L2/inverse-mahler-unique ('If ψSeries F=0, there exists a unique integral formal series G with ψSeries G=0 and ∂G=F. It is G=HF').

items.name: Definition 10.14 (the Coleman map Col)
items.statement: Col : U_∞ → Λ(Z_p^×) is the composite U_∞ →(u ↦ f_u) (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id} →(∂log) Z_p[[T]] →(1−φ∘ψ) Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} →(∂^{−1}) Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} →(A^{−1}) Λ(Z_p^×); i.e. Col(u) = A^{−1}(∂^{−1}(1 − φ∘ψ)∂log f_u) = x^{−1}·Res_{Z_p^×}(μ_{∂log f_u}). It is a group homomorphism (∂log turns products into sums).
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'Define Delta(f)=∂f/f and the pipeline Col_0 = A^−1 ◦ ∂^−1 ◦ (1−phi psi) ◦ Delta ◦ Coleman. The inverse of ∂ here is defined on psi=0 through multiplication by x^−1 on units'. The atlas names this composite Col_0 and reserves Col = −Col_0 for the sign-corrected Theorem 10.15. No node yet.

items.name: Theorem 10.15 (ζ_p from cyclotomic units via Col; corrected sign)
items.statement: For every integer a that is a topological generator of Z_p^× (so p ∤ a): Col(c(a)) = −θ_a·ζ_p, i.e. ζ_p = −Col(c(a))/θ_a as pseudo-measures in Q(Z_p^×). [Printed: ζ_p = Col(c(a))/θ_a, which holds with Col replaced by −Col.] The same sign affects the seven-step procedure preceding Definition 10.14.
items.note: Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'compute Delta(f_c)=a−1−F_a and hence Col_0(c(a)) = −([a]−1) zeta_p. Define Col=−Col_0 if a positive explicit reciprocity identity is desired, and prove the comparison rather than altering zeta_p. The source's Theorem 10.15 has the opposite sign from its preceding definitions'. L4 acceptance lists 10.15 'with recorded sign comparison'. See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E57 (lead ColemanPowerSeries/E1).

items.name: Absolute Galois group G_F and continuous Galois cohomology H^1(F, A)
items.statement: For a field F (here a number field or a finite extension of Q_p), G_F := Gal(F̄/F) with its Krull topology; for a topological G_F-module A, H^1(F, A) := H^1(G_F, A), the continuous group cohomology (continuous 1-cocycles modulo coboundaries).
items.note: Mathlib FieldTheory/AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean:43 `Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K := AlgebraicClosure K ≃ₐ[K] AlgebraicClosure K`; Tau Ceti FieldTheory/Galois/AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean:230 `TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup := Gal(SeparableClosure K/K)` (compared with Mathlib's there); Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LowDegree.lean:674 `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1 := Z1 G M ⧸ B1` built from continuous cochains of a topological group acting on a topological module; Mathlib RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131 `continuousCohomology n A` (homogeneous continuous cochains, all degrees). Same definition. Lattice/limit coefficients (Z_p(1)) and the lim^1 comparison are ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1 (audit: neither library has lim^1).

items.name: Kummer short exact sequence (10-5) on F̄-points
items.statement: For m ≥ 1 and a field F of characteristic 0 (e.g. a number field): 1 → μ_{p^m} → F̄^× →(x ↦ x^{p^m}) F̄^× → 1 is a short exact sequence of discrete G_F-modules.
items.locator: §10.5, display (10-5) and the sentence after it (printed pp. 170–171, PDF 71–72)
items.note: Tau Ceti FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Coefficients.lean:195 `kummerShortExact (hn : IsUnit (n : K))` (the Kummer sequence of discrete G_K-modules μ_n → (Kˢ)ˣ → (Kˢ)ˣ), :166 `kummerSequence_exact`, :178 `unitsCoeffPow_surjective`. Kˢ is the separable closure, = F̄ in characteristic 0; n = p^m is invertible. Same statement.

items.name: Long exact Kummer sequence (10-6)
items.statement: For a number field F and m ≥ 1 the Kummer sequence induces an exact sequence 0 → μ_{p^m}(F) → F^× →(x ↦ x^{p^m}) F^× →δ H^1(F, μ_{p^m}) → H^1(F, F̄^×).
items.note: Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LongExact.lean: exactness at H⁰(A) (:145, injectivity), H⁰(B) (:155), H⁰(C) (:226, 'the image of the projection on invariants is the kernel of δ⁰') and H¹(A) (:294, 'the node where δ⁰ lands') for any DiscreteShortExact; applied to kummerShortExact with Coefficients.lean:266 `baseUnitsEquivInvariants : Kˣ ≃* ((Kˢ)ˣ)^{G_K}`. GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean:187 `kummerMap` is the resulting δ and :260 `ker_kummerMap : (kummerMap K n hn).ker = powerSubgroup Kˣ n`. Same statement (read through the named identification of F^× with invariants).

items.name: Hilbert 90 for G_F: H^1(F, F̄^×) = 0
items.statement: For a field F (here a number field), H^1(G_F, F̄^×) = 0 (continuous cohomology, F̄^× discrete).
items.note: Library has only finite Galois extensions: Mathlib RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Hilbert90.lean:84 `groupCohomology.isMulCoboundary₁_of_isMulCocycle₁_of_aut_to_units` (L/K finite) and :107 `H1ofAutOnUnitsUnique`. The profinite version is planned by Tau Ceti's ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 ('the Galois interface: Hilbert 90 and Kummer theory', via the finite-quotient colimit of Layer 4); Tau Ceti's Kummer.lean states that 'surjectivity ... is Hilbert 90 for Kˢ/K' and is 'What is not here'. The reduction step exists: Tau Ceti ContCohomology/FiniteQuotient/Colimit.lean:513 `subsingleton_H1_of_forall_openNormalSubgroup` (H¹(G,M) vanishes if every finite layer H¹(G⧸U, M^U) does); the audit (data/library-coverage.json, ProfiniteCohomology layer 9) marks profinite Hilbert 90 itself 'absent'.

items.name: Finite-level Kummer isomorphism F^×/(F^×)^{p^n} ≅ H^1(G_F, μ_{p^n}) with explicit cocycle
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and F a field of characteristic 0: the map F^×/(F^×)^{p^n} → H^1(G_F, μ_{p^n}), [a] ↦ [c_a] with c_a(σ) = σ(b)/b for any b ∈ F̄^× with b^{p^n} = a, is well defined (independent of b), c_a is a coboundary iff a is a p^n-th power in F^×, and the map is an isomorphism (surjectivity by Hilbert 90).
items.note: All but surjectivity is library: Tau Ceti FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean:120 `kummerCocycle_mem_Z1` (g ↦ gα/α is a continuous 1-cocycle), :143 `kummerCocycleClass_congr` (independence of the root), :215 `kummerMap_eq_kummerCocycleClass`, :268 `kummerMap_eq_one_iff : kummerMap a = 1 ↔ ∃ b, b^n = a`, :298 `kummerClassMap_injective`. Surjectivity (the isomorphism) is planned in ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 (Kummer.lean docstring: 'Surjectivity is the only missing input for the Kummer isomorphism').

items.name: The p-adic Kummer map δ (10-7) (corrected: p-adic completion)
items.statement: For a number field F, the inverse limit over m of the isomorphisms F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} ≅ H^1(F, μ_{p^m}) is an isomorphism δ : (F^×)^∧ := lim_m F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} → H^1(F, Z_p(1)), Z_p(1) := lim_m μ_{p^m}, where lim_m H^1(F, μ_{p^m}) = H^1(F, Z_p(1)) because lim^1_m μ_{p^m}(F) = 0 (finite groups). The algebraic tensor product F^× ⊗_Z Z_p injects into (F^×)^∧ but is not equal to it (F^× is not finitely generated). [Printed: δ : F^× ⊗ Z_p ≅ H^1(F, Z_p(1)), obtained by 'taking inverse limits over m ≥ 1, which is exact'.]
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/padic-kummer-identification: 'For a field K with p invertible, H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim_m K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} = (K^×)^ ... an isomorphism because the Milnor term lim^1 H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) vanishes ... the target is the completion, not K^× ⊗ ℤ_p'; L0/kummer-limit-map; L0/kummer-level-compatibility. Stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0: 'do not replace its completion by an algebraic tensor product without a theorem'. See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E61 (lead SelmerIwasawaCohomology/E1).

items.name: Tate twists Z_p(1), Q_p(1) and V^*(1)
items.statement: Z_p(1) := lim_m μ_{p^m} (transition maps ζ ↦ ζ^p), a free Z_p-module of rank 1 on which G_F acts through the p-adic cyclotomic character; Q_p(1) := Z_p(1) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p, L(1) := L ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(1), and for V ∈ Rep_L G, V^*(1) := Hom_L(V, L(1)).
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/padic-kummer-identification ('ℤ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^m} is a compact coefficient module'); stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0 imports 'twists, duals' from ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02. Library: only the character (Mathlib CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307 `cyclotomicCharacter`); the audit (data/library-coverage.json, SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0) records 'What is not there is a Tate twist of a Galois module'.

items.name: Generalised cyclotomic elements c_m (corrected: the printed c_m is a root of unity)
items.statement: Let m = Dp^n with n ≥ 1 and D ≥ 1 prime to p, and let (ξ_m)_m be compatible roots of unity (ξ_{mℓ}^ℓ = ξ_m). The printed c_m := (ξ_m^{−1} − 1)/(ξ_m − 1) equals −ξ_m^{−1}, a root of unity. The intended non-torsion cyclotomic elements are, e.g., c_m(a) := (ξ_m^a − 1)/(ξ_m − 1) ∈ O_{Q(μ_m)}^× for a fixed integer a ∉ {0, ±1} prime to m (D = 1 gives the c_n(a) of §10.2), or Rubin's c̃_m := N_{Q(μ_{mp})/Q(μ_m)}(1 − ξ_{mp}).
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/p-extended-cyclotomic-number ('c̃_m = N_{ℚ(μ_{mp})/ℚ(μ_m)}(1 − ζ_{mp})'), L0/smoothed-unit-comparison ('c_m(a) = (1 − ζ_m^a)/(1 − ζ_m) ... a = ±1 gives the torsion elements 1 and −ζ_m^{−1}; the nondegenerate smoothing uses a ∉ {0, ±1}'), L0/p-extended-nontorsion; stage L0: 'The notes' displayed choice c_m=(xi_m^−1−1)/(xi_m−1)=−xi_m^−1 is torsion'. Unit property for natural a: Mathlib CyclotomicUnits.lean:100. See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E60 (lead EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture/E2).

items.name: Norm relations of the cyclotomic elements (corrected)
items.statement: For the non-torsion elements c_m(a) (a prime to mℓ) and a prime ℓ: N_{Q(μ_{mℓ})/Q(μ_m)}(c_{mℓ}(a)) = c_m(a) if ℓ | m, and = c_m(a)^{1 − σ_ℓ^{−1}} = c_m(a)/σ_ℓ^{−1}(c_m(a)) if ℓ ∤ m, where σ_ℓ ∈ Gal(Q(μ_m)/Q) is the Frobenius at ℓ (ξ_m ↦ ξ_m^ℓ); similarly N(1 − ξ_{mℓ}) = (1 − ξ_m)^{1 − σ_ℓ^{−1}} for ℓ ∤ m. [Printed: '= (1 − ℓ^{−1})c_m if ℓ ∤ m'; read in Q(μ_m)^× ⊗ Z_p this holds only for the printed torsion c_m, on which σ_ℓ acts through the cyclotomic character.]
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/p-extended-auxiliary-relation ('N_{ℚ(μ_{mℓ})/ℚ(μ_m)}(c̃_{mℓ}) = c̃_m^{1 − Fr_ℓ^{−1}} if ℓ ∤ m, and = c̃_m if ℓ ∣ m'), L0/p-extended-tower-relation, L0/distribution-relation-of-dvd, L0/smoothed-unit-comparison (the smoothed family 'satisfies the relations ... for the primes ℓ ∤ a'). Relation re-derived here: for ℓ ∤ m write ξ_{mℓ} = αβ (α ∈ μ_m, β primitive of order ℓ); then α = σ_ℓ^{−1}(ξ_m) and Π_{β′}(1 − αβ′) = (1 − α^ℓ)/(1 − α).

items.name: Frobenius at ℓ ≠ p acts on Z_p(1) by ℓ
items.statement: For a prime ℓ ≠ p, an (arithmetic) Frobenius at ℓ acts on μ_{p^k} (k ≥ 1) by ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ (the library statement); hence, once Z_p(1) = lim_k μ_{p^k} is built (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/348), on Z_p(1) as multiplication by ℓ.
items.note: Tau Ceti NumberTheory/NumberField/Cyclotomic/Frobenius.lean:96 `apply_eq_pow_absNorm_of_pow_eq_one`: for K a number field, ζ ∈ F with ζ^m = 1, 𝔭 ∤ m and σ an arithmetic Frobenius at Q | 𝔭, σ ζ = ζ^{N𝔭} (over ℚ: ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ); :133 `autToPow_eq_absNorm`. This is the finite-level statement (m = p^k); the Z_p(1) form is its inverse limit. Note the printed use of this fact to rewrite (1 − ℓ^{−1}) as (1 − Frob_ℓ^{−1}) on H^1 classes is valid only for the torsion classes of the printed c_m (see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E60).

items.name: Kummer classes z_m and their corestriction relations (corrected)
items.statement: Put z_m := δ(c_m) ∈ H^1(Q(μ_m), Z_p(1)) for the non-torsion cyclotomic elements c_m. Then cores_{Q(μ_{mℓ})/Q(μ_m)}(z_{mℓ}) = z_m if ℓ | m, and = (1 − σ_ℓ^{−1})z_m if ℓ ∤ m, where σ_ℓ acts on H^1(Q(μ_m), Z_p(1)) through Gal(Q(μ_m)/Q) (this is a module action on classes, not the scalar ℓ).
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/cyclotomic-kummer-classes ('κ_N(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(G_{ℚ(μ_m)}, μ_{p^N}) is the Tau Ceti Kummer class ... define κ(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(ℚ(μ_m), ℤ_p(1))'), L0/cyclotomic-euler-system ('Cor κ(c̃_{mq}) = ... = (1 − Fr_q^{−1})κ(c̃_m) if q ∤ m and = κ(c̃_m) if q ∣ m'). Compatibility of δ with norm/corestriction: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/padic-kummer-identification ('compatible with restriction and with corestriction versus the norm'). Library corestriction in degree 1: Tau Ceti ContCohomology/Corestriction.lean:457 `explicitCor1` (finite-index open subgroups), not yet compared with norms.

items.name: p-adic Galois representations Rep_L G_Q and the Euler factor P_ℓ(V^*(1), X)
items.statement: Rep_L G_Q: finite-dimensional L-vector spaces V (L/Q_p finite) with a continuous L-linear G_Q-action; for V unramified at ℓ ≠ p, V^*(1) := Hom_L(V, L(1)) and P_ℓ(V^*(1), X) := det(1 − Frob_ℓ^{−1}X | V^*(1)^{I_ℓ}) ∈ L[X], the Euler factor at ℓ of the L-function of V^*(1).
items.note: Library ingredient: Mathlib RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Basic.lean:54 `ContRepresentation` (each g acts continuously; the audit notes joint continuity is not required). ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1 ('Construct continuous representations on finite projective coefficient modules ... For field coefficients construct invariant lattices using compactness'), R01.2 (decomposition groups, inertia); EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.2 ('Construct the normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention'). No Galois-representation carrier in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched GaloisRep; ContRepresentation is the nearest).

items.name: Definition 10.16 (Euler system for (V, T, Σ))
items.statement: Let Σ be a finite set of primes containing p, V ∈ Rep_L G_Q unramified outside Σ, and T ⊆ V a G_Q-stable O_L-lattice. An Euler system for (V, T, Σ) is a collection of classes z_m ∈ H^1(Q(μ_m), T), for m = p^n m′ with n ≥ 0 and m′ a square-free product of primes not in Σ, such that for every prime ℓ with mℓ again of this form: cores_{Q(μ_{mℓ})/Q(μ_m)}(z_{mℓ}) = z_m if ℓ = p, and = P_ℓ(V^*(1), σ_ℓ^{−1})·z_m if ℓ ≠ p, where σ_ℓ is the image of Frob_ℓ in Gal(Q(μ_m)/Q).
items.note: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.2: 'Define systems over an explicit directed family of finite abelian extensions ... The ES norm relation uses corestriction ... Separate the p-power tower relation from the auxiliary-prime relation. A system allowed by the definition may be zero.' (general Rubin form; RJW's is the specialisation to the fields Q(μ_m)); EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0 specialises to the cyclotomic directed family.

items.name: The cyclotomic units form an Euler system for Z_p(1)
items.statement: The Kummer classes z_m = δ(c̃_m) of Rubin's cyclotomic elements c̃_m := N_{Q(μ_{mp})/Q(μ_m)}(1 − ξ_{mp}) (or their smoothings c̃_m^{σ_a − 1}, with the primes dividing a added to Σ) form an Euler system for (Q_p(1), Z_p(1), {p}) in the sense of Definition 10.16; for V = Q_p(1), V^*(1) = Q_p with trivial action, so P_ℓ(V^*(1), X) = 1 − X and the relation is cores(z_{mℓ}) = (1 − σ_ℓ^{−1})z_m. (They underlie Rubin's proof of the Main Conjecture.) (The smoothed family (ξ_m^a − 1)/(ξ_m − 1) does not satisfy the ℓ = p relation at n = 0: its norm from Q(μ_{pm′}) to Q(μ_{m′}) carries the factor 1 − Fr_p^{−1}.)
items.note: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/cyclotomic-euler-system: 'The classes κ(c̃_m) ∈ H¹(ℚ(μ_m), ℤ_p(1)) ... form an Euler system for (ℤ_p(1), ℚ^ab, p) ... RJW's Definition 10.16 convention, P_ℓ(V^*(1), σ_ℓ^{−1}) with V = ℚ_p(1), gives the same factor 1 − σ_ℓ^{−1}.' As printed (with c_m = −ξ_m^{−1}) the family is torsion and vanishes after ⊗Q_p.

items.name: Local Kummer isomorphisms and (10-8) (corrected: p-adic completions)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1: (K_n^×)^∧ := lim_m K_n^×/(K_n^×)^{p^m} ≅ H^1(K_n, Z_p(1)), where (K_n^×)^∧ ≅ Z_p × U_{n,1} (π_n^{Z_p} times the principal units; the algebraic K_n^× ⊗_Z Z_p surjects onto it with nonzero kernel); these isomorphisms intertwine N_{K_{n+1}/K_n} with cores_{K_{n+1}/K_n}, so lim_n (K_n^×)^∧ ≅ lim_n H^1(K_n, Z_p(1)) (10-8). [Printed with K_n^× ⊗ Z_p.]
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/local-completion ('(K^×)^ ≅ ℤ_p × (𝓞_K^×)^, where (𝓞_K^×)^ = U^1_K if ℓ = p ... The map K^× ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → (K^×)^ is surjective but not injective'), L0/padic-kummer-identification (compatible with corestriction versus norm), L4/local-units-iwasawa-cohomology ('lim_n K̂_n^× ≅ lim_n H^1(K_n, ℤ_p(1)) = H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) (RJW (10.8), corrected)'). See issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E61 (lead SelmerIwasawaCohomology/E1).

items.name: Iwasawa cohomology H^1_Iw(Q_p, Q_p(1))
items.statement: H^1_Iw(Q_p, Q_p(1)) := (lim_{n≥1} H^1(K_n, Z_p(1))) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p, the inverse limit taken along corestriction maps.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/local-units-iwasawa-cohomology ('lim_n H^1(K_n, ℤ_p(1)) = H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1))'); PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.5 ('For rational coefficients specify H¹_Iw(K,T)⊗Q_p rather than silently interchanging rationalization with an arbitrary inverse limit'). Library ingredient only: Tau Ceti ContCohomology/Corestriction.lean:457 `explicitCor1 : H1 U M →+ H1 G M`.

items.name: The map κ : U_∞ → lim_n H^1(K_n, Z_p(1))
items.statement: The inclusions U_n = O_{K_n}^× ⊂ K_n^× induce norm-compatible maps U_n → (K_n^×)^∧ (printed: K_n^× ⊗ Z_p), hence U_∞ → lim_n (K_n^×)^∧; composing with (10-8) gives κ : U_∞ → lim_{n≥1} H^1(K_n, Z_p(1)).
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/local-units-iwasawa-cohomology: 'The inclusion of principal units gives κ : U_∞ → H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1))'.

items.name: Col factors through Iwasawa cohomology: Col = Col′∘κ
items.statement: There is a map Col′ : H^1_Iw(Q_p, Q_p(1)) → M(Z_p^×, Q_p) = Λ(Z_p^×) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p (Q_p-valued measures on Z_p^× ≅ Γ) such that Col′∘κ = Col on U_∞ (κ followed by ⊗Q_p). (Asserted without proof: 'One can then show'.)
items.locator: §10.5, diagram after the definition of κ (printed pp. 172–173, PDF 73–74)
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators:L3: 'Identify the rank-one Tate case with R04's Coleman map, with the chosen sign and Tate twist'; SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 acceptance: 'RJW §10.5's cohomological reinterpretation'; PhiGamma PG.5 supplies H¹_Iw ≅ D(T)^{ψ=1}. No node constructs Col′.

items.name: ζ_p from the localised cyclotomic Euler system via Col′ (corrected sign)
items.statement: Localising the cyclotomic-unit Euler system at p gives the class κ(c(a)) ∈ H^1_Iw(Q_p, Q_p(1)), and Col′(κ(c(a))) = Col(c(a)) = −θ_a ζ_p; so ζ_p = −Col′(κ(c(a)))/θ_a (dividing by θ_a introduces the pole). [Printed without the sign, citing Proposition 10.4.]
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/local-units-iwasawa-cohomology ('their localisations at p along the tower m = Dp^n define a class in H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) (RJW §10.5, the cohomological reinterpretation of the Coleman map)' — note this node still uses the printed torsion c_m); sign from ColemanPowerSeries:L2. Same sign issue as Theorem 10.15. The review adds: that node must be corrected under issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E60, since its class δ(c_m) is torsion and has Col = 0.

items.name: Iwasawa cohomology H^1_Iw(Q_p, V) of a p-adic representation
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep_L G_{Q_p} (a finite-dimensional L-vector space with continuous linear G_{Q_p}-action) and any G_{Q_p}-stable O_L-lattice T ⊆ V: H^1_Iw(Q_p, V) := (lim_{n≥1} H^1(K_n, T)) ⊗_{O_L} L, the limit along corestrictions (independent of the choice of T).
items.note: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.5 (Rlim_n RΓ(K_n,T) under corestriction 'in the stated cyclotomic setting'; H¹_Iw ≅ D(T)^{ψ=1}); SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3 ('construct H^i_Iw(F,T) using corestriction' — stated for Z_p^d-extensions of number fields); PadicHodgeRegulators:L2 ('(phi,Gamma)-modules and Iwasawa cohomology'); lattices by compactness in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1. Independence of T is implicit in the source.

items.name: Crystalline representations (footnote 11)
items.statement: V ∈ Rep_L G_{Q_p} is crystalline if dim_{Q_p} D_cris(V) = dim_{Q_p} V, where D_cris(V) = (B_cris ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_{Q_p}}; it is the p-adic analogue of an ℓ-adic representation (ℓ ≠ p) of G_{Q_p} being unramified. (The source gives only the loose description.)
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2: 'Define D_HT, D_dR, D_cris and D_st and their comparison maps. Prove ... exactness in the admissible categories'. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (Mathlib mentions 'crystalline' only in divided-power docstrings).

items.name: An elliptic curve over Q is crystalline at p iff it has good reduction at p (footnote 11)
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E/Q, the p-adic Galois representation V_p(E) restricted to G_{Q_p} is crystalline if and only if E has good reduction at p.
items.note: PadicHodgeTheory:R06.6/good-reduction-iff-crystalline: 'The p-adic criterion of good reduction: good reduction iff V_p(A) is crystalline' (abelian varieties over finite K/Q_p; E/Q_p is the case dim 1).

items.name: Bloch–Kato exponential and dual exponential maps
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep_L G_{Q_p} de Rham (e.g. crystalline), the Bloch–Kato exponential exp : D_dR(V)/Fil^0 → H^1(Q_p, V) and dual exponential exp^* : H^1(Q_p, V) → Fil^0 D_dR(V) (and their versions over K_n), in terms of which Log_V's interpolation property is expressed.
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators:L1: 'Construct the exponential and dual exponential from the fundamental exact sequences. Prove their domains, kernels, local duality relation, twist compatibilities ... Work first over a finite extension of Q_p'. The source only names them.

items.name: Perrin-Riou's big logarithm Log_V
items.statement: (Perrin-Riou) For crystalline V ∈ Rep_L G_{Q_p}, after some choices there is a map Log_V : H^1_Iw(Q_p, V) → D^la(Z_p^×, L) satisfying interpolation properties at characters expressed through the Bloch–Kato exponential and dual exponential maps; for V = Q_p(1) it recovers Col′.
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators:L3: 'For crystalline V construct L_V : H^1_Iw(Q_p,V) → H(G) ⊗_K D_cris(V) ... prove the interpolation at every finite-order character and integral twist using Bloch–Kato exponential/dual exponential maps ... Identify the rank-one Tate case with R04's Coleman map ... For general V a scalar projection is an additional defined map; it is not canonical from V alone.' The atlas's target is D_cris(V)-valued; the printed scalar version is a choice of projection ('Under some choices').

items.name: Programme: Euler systems → loc_p → Log_V → p-adic L-functions
items.statement: Heuristic programme (stated conditionally, not as a theorem): given an Euler system for a global p-adic representation V, localisation at p of its p-power tower gives a class in H^1_Iw(Q_p, V), and Perrin-Riou's Log_V turns it into a p-adic L-function for V: {Euler systems} →(loc_p) H^1_Iw(Q_p, V) →(Log_V) {p-adic L-functions}. This splits the construction into a global problem (the Euler system) and a local one (the big logarithm).
items.note: Instances in the atlas: the cyclotomic case (this section; ColemanPowerSeries:L2 and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4) and Kato's explicit reciprocity (KatoEulerSystems:L3: 'Localize at p, apply R09's vector regulator, and project using the chosen refinement'), with the local map from PadicHodgeRegulators:L3. The general statement is a programme ('conjectural construction'), not a theorem to formalise.

items.name: Λ(Γ) ≅ Λ(Z_p^×) via the cyclotomic character; ζ_p as a pseudo-measure on Γ
items.statement: Let p be odd, Γ = Gal(F_∞/Q) and χ : Γ → Z_p^× the cyclotomic character (σ(ξ) = ξ^{χ(σ)} for ξ ∈ μ_{p^∞}), a topological group isomorphism. Transport along χ identifies Λ(Γ) = Z_p[[Γ]] (the Z_p-valued measures on Γ) with Λ(Z_p^×) as topological Z_p-algebras, and Q(Γ) with Q(Z_p^×); under this identification ζ_p becomes a pseudo-measure on Γ, i.e. an element of Q(Γ) with ([g] − [1])ζ_p ∈ Λ(Γ) for all g ∈ Γ. Likewise χ induces Γ^+ = Γ/⟨c⟩ ≅ Z_p^×/{±1}.
items.locator: §11 introduction and §11.1, first two paragraphs (printed p. 174, PDF 75)
items.note: No library statement that χ is bijective on Gal(Q(μ_{p^∞})/Q). Mathlib has the pieces: mathlib:cyclotomicCharacter (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307, `cyclotomicCharacter (p) : (L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ`, a homomorphism only; grep for surj/bij/equiv lemmas about it found none), mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Gal.lean:77, `Gal(L/K) ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ` given irreducibility of Φ_n: the finite-level iso), and mathlib:AbstractMeasure.arrowCongrLeft (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:128, `(φ : X ≃ₜ Y) : AbstractMeasure X R E ≃ₗ[R] AbstractMeasure Y R E`, transport of measures along a homeomorphism; linear only, no convolution). Planned: ColemanPowerSeries:L0 stage ‘Extend the G-action to a continuous completed-group-ring action via R01’, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 stage (completed group rings, functoriality, convolution; node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/convolution-pushforward ‘Pushforward preserves convolution’). The atlas stages use Z_p[[G]] with G = Γ throughout (e.g. ColemanPowerSeries:L3 endpoint), so the identification is assumed there; no node constructs the infinite-level isomorphism χ itself (it is §9 notation, eq. (9-1), of the previous chunk).

items.name: Lemma 11.1 (± decomposition under complex conjugation)
items.statement: Let c ∈ Γ be complex conjugation, R a ring in which 2 is invertible, and M an R-module with a continuous R-linear action of Γ. Then M = M^+ ⊕ M^−, where M^± = e^±M with e^± = (1 ± c)/2, and c acts as +1 on M^+ and as −1 on M^−. In particular (p odd) Λ(Γ) = Λ(Γ)^+ ⊕ Λ(Γ)^−, and the functors M ↦ M^± (equivalently M ↦ M^{⟨c⟩} for M^+) are exact.
items.note: The decomposition itself is not stated in either library. General tool: mathlib:LinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.isCompl (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean:653, inside namespace LinearMap: `(hf : IsIdempotentElem f) : IsCompl (range f) (ker f)`), which applied to f = (1+c)/2 gives the statement; Tau Ceti/Mathlib grep for plusPart/minusPart/involution eigenspace decompositions found nothing relevant. Planned (partial, finer): node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition ‘Let Γ = H × Γ′ with H finite abelian of order prime to p … every Λ(Γ)-module decomposes as M = ⊕_ω M^{(ω)} with M^{(ω)} = e_ωM’; with H = μ_{p−1} ∋ c, M^± = ⊕_{ω(c)=±1} M^{(ω)}. That node covers Λ(Γ)-modules (the case used in §§11–13), not arbitrary R-modules with 2 ∈ R^×. The exactness of ⟨c⟩-invariants is used in the proof of Theorem 12.23(ii).

items.name: Lemma 11.2 (Λ(Γ)^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+))
items.statement: Let p be odd. The projection Γ → Γ^+ = Γ/⟨c⟩ induces a surjection Λ(Γ) → Λ(Γ^+) which kills Λ(Γ)^− and restricts to an isomorphism of Λ(Γ)-modules (and Z_p-algebras) Λ(Γ)^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+). At finite level Z_p[Γ_n]^+ ≅ Z_p[Γ_n^+], both free of rank (p−1)p^{n−1}/2 (basis [g] + [cg] ↦ 2[ḡ], 2 ∈ Z_p^×); pass to the inverse limit. Henceforth Λ(Γ^+) is identified with the submodule Λ(Γ)^+ of Λ(Γ).
items.locator: §11.1, Lemma 11.2 and its proof (printed pp. 174–175, PDF 75–76)
items.note: Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti (MonoidAlgebra/completed group ring invariants, ‘quotient group’, ‘invariants’; no Iwasawa algebra in Tau Ceti: grep for Iwasawa/IwasawaAlgebra/completedGroupRing in TauCeti = 0 files) and all packets (regex for Λ(G/H), Λ(Γ^+), invariants of measures, quotient by ±1): no node or library statement. Nearest planned material: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 stage (functoriality of R[[G]], giving the map Λ(Γ) → Λ(Γ^+) but not the isomorphism on the + part) and node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition (Λ(H × Γ′) ≅ ⊕_ω Λ over characters of H of order prime to p), from which the lemma follows by grouping the even characters; neither states it. Routed (source) to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 (functoriality of completed group rings). The review adds the finite-level ingredient tauceti:TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.ker_mapDomainRingHom_eq_span (TauCeti/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/Exactness.lean:166): the kernel of R[G] → R[G/H] is spanned by single k 1 − 1, k ∈ H. Λ(Γ)^+ = e^+Λ(Γ) is a ring with identity e^+.

items.name: Lemma 11.3 (moment criterion for measures on Γ^+)
items.statement: Let p be odd and μ ∈ Λ(Γ). Then μ ∈ Λ(Γ^+) (= Λ(Γ)^+, Lemma 11.2) if and only if ∫_Γ χ(x)^k · μ = 0 for all odd k ≥ 1. (Proof: μ^± = ½(1 ± c)μ; ∫χ^k·μ^+ = 0 for odd k and ∫χ^k·μ^− = 0 for even k, so for odd k ∫χ^k·μ = ∫χ^k·μ^−; conclude by Lemma 3.36(i), a measure on Z_p^× all of whose positive moments vanish is zero.)
items.locator: §11.1, Lemma 11.3 and its proof (printed p. 175, PDF 76)
items.note: Corrected proof sentence (see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E64: the printed ‘∫χ(k)·μ^+’ must read ‘∫χ^k·μ^−’). Not stated anywhere: searched packets for odd moments / parity / plus part and Tau Ceti/Mathlib. Its input Lemma 3.36(i) is planned as PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/unit-positive-moment-separation (‘If μ∈M satisfies μ(t_k)=0 for every k>0, then μ=0’, M = D(Z_p^×, Z_p)); a related parity statement for tame measures is DirichletPadicLFunctions:L2/tame-character-parity-test (vanishing of tests with incompatible reflection parity), which is the ‘only if’ direction in a different setting. The ‘if’ direction (odd moments vanish ⇒ even measure) is nowhere planned. Routed (source) to PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3, next to L3/unit-positive-moment-separation.

items.name: Corollary 11.4 (ζ_p is a pseudo-measure on Γ^+)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure ζ_p is invariant under complex conjugation, [c]ζ_p = ζ_p, and is a pseudo-measure on Γ^+: ([g] − [1])ζ_p ∈ Λ(Γ^+) (= Λ(Γ)^+) for every g ∈ Γ. Reason: ∫_Γ χ^k · ([g]−[1])ζ_p = (χ(g)^k − 1)(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) vanishes for every odd k ≥ 1 — for odd k ≥ 3 because ζ(1−k) = 0, and for k = 1 because the Euler factor 1 − p^0 = 0 (ζ(0) = −1/2 ≠ 0) — so Lemma 11.3 applies to the measures ([g]−[1])ζ_p.
items.locator: §11.1, Corollary 11.4 and its proof (printed p. 175, PDF 76)
items.note: Corrected proof (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E65: the printed reason ‘ζ(1−k) = 0 for odd k ≥ 1’ is false at k = 1). Planned by nodes DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure-even (‘δ_(−1)•ζ_p=ζ_p in PM for every prime p’; this is [c]ζ_p = ζ_p, since c = σ_{−1}) and DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-odd-moments (‘If k is odd, then M_k(ζ_p)=0, including k=1 and p=2’), and by the stage description of DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1: ‘At k=1 the Euler factor is zero; keep this case in the proof rather than claiming zeta(0)=0. Prove parity and descent to the quotient by ±1 for odd p.’ The descent to an element of Q(Γ^+) via Lemma 11.2 is not a node (Lemma 11.2 is missing).

items.name: Augmentation ideals I(Γ), I(Γ^+)
items.statement: I(Γ) = ker(Λ(Γ) → Z_p), the kernel of the augmentation (degree) map induced by [g] ↦ 1 for g ∈ Γ; equivalently the closed (topological) ideal of Λ(Γ) generated by the elements [g] − [1], g ∈ Γ. I(Γ^+) ⊂ Λ(Γ^+) is defined in the same way (new in this chunk; I(Γ) is recalled from Definition 3.37).
items.locator: §11.2, second paragraph (printed p. 175, PDF 76); recalls Definition 3.37
items.note: Mathlib has only the abstract notion mathlib:Ideal.IsAugmentation (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/IsAugmentation.lean: ‘I.IsAugmentation R ↔ IsCompl 1 (I.restrictScalars R)’), not the augmentation ideal of a completed group ring. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 stage (‘Prove … functoriality, augmentation, Dirac elements …’) with node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/character-integral-algebra-hom (integration against a continuous character, the trivial character giving the augmentation) and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/finite-projection-mass (‘Augmentation of finite coefficients’); PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 stage (‘augmentation-ideal description’). The printed definition has a misprint ‘[g] ↦ 1 for any σ ∈ Γ’ (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E66).

items.name: Principal augmentation ideal of a procyclic group
items.statement: Let G be procyclic (here G = Γ ≅ Z_p^× or G = Γ^+, p odd) and σ a topological generator. Then I(G) = Λ(G)·([σ] − [1]); more generally I(G) is the closure of the ideal generated by {[g] − [1] : g ∈ G}. (Used in the proof of Proposition 11.5 — ‘I(Γ) is the topological ideal generated by the elements [g] − [1]’ — and, implicitly, in the proof of Theorem 12.23, where Col of the single generator of C^+_{∞,1} is ([σ_a] − [1])ζ_p up to sign and the image is asserted to be all of I(Γ)ζ_p.)
items.locator: §11.2, proof of Proposition 11.5 (printed p. 176, PDF 77); stated for ℤ_p^× in the proof of Lemma 3.38 (printed p. 131, PDF 32: 'I(ℤ_p^×) = ([a] − [1])Λ(ℤ_p^×)'); used implicitly in the proof of Theorem 12.23 (printed p. 188, PDF 89)
items.note: Planned by the PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3 stage description: ‘For procyclic G prove the principal augmentation-ideal theorem, existence and uniqueness statements used by RJW §§3–4, and change of generator. Treat Z_2^× as {±1}×(1+4Z_2), not as a procyclic group.’ No packet node yet (PMIA L3 nodes cover pseudomeasures and their evaluation). Z_p^× is procyclic for odd p; a ∈ Z is a topological generator of Z_p^× iff a generates (Z/p^2)^× (Mathlib has cyclicity of (ZMod (p^n))ˣ in Mathlib/RingTheory/ZMod/UnitsCyclic.lean, not the profinite statement).

items.name: Proposition 11.5 (I(Γ)ζ_p is an ideal of Λ(Γ))
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Λ(Γ)-submodule I(Γ)ζ_p = {λζ_p : λ ∈ I(Γ)} of Q(Γ) is contained in Λ(Γ), hence is an ideal of Λ(Γ). (Because ([g] − [1])ζ_p ∈ Λ(Γ) for all g and I(Γ) is topologically generated by the [g] − [1].)
items.locator: §11.2, Proposition 11.5 and its proof (printed p. 176, PDF 77)
items.note: Planned: node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/pseudomeasures defines pseudo-measures as the colon submodule ‘(1 : Submodule R Q) / Submodule.span R (range (g ↦ ι(δ(g)−1)))’, i.e. exactly {z : (span of [g]−1)·z ⊆ R}, so I·z ⊆ R for the algebraic augmentation ideal; node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/pseudomeasure-membership (‘z ∈ pseudomeasures δ Q iff ∀ g, ∃ r, ι(r)=ι(c_g)z’); stage description ‘Prove their module structure, augmentation-ideal description’. Passing from the algebraic span to the closed ideal I(Γ) uses the principal augmentation ideal (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/373). ζ_p itself: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure.

items.name: Proposition 11.5 (I(Γ^+)ζ_p is an ideal of Λ(Γ^+))
items.statement: Let p be odd. Regarding ζ_p as a pseudo-measure on Γ^+ (Corollary 11.4), I(Γ^+)ζ_p is contained in Λ(Γ^+) and is an ideal of Λ(Γ^+). Moreover, under Λ(Γ^+) = Λ(Γ)^+ one has I(Γ)ζ_p = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (since e^−ζ_p = 0).
items.locator: §11.2, Proposition 11.5, second sentence, and proof (printed p. 176, PDF 77)
items.note: Same planned evidence as item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/374 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L3/pseudomeasures, pseudomeasure-membership) combined with the evenness DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure-even. The equality I(Γ)ζ_p = I(Γ^+)ζ_p is not printed but follows from Lemmas 11.1–11.2 and is what makes the two parts of Theorem 12.23 compatible; the identification Λ(Γ^+) = Λ(Γ)^+ (Lemma 11.2) is missing. Also used: node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/trivial-character-component states e₁(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = e₁Λ (trivial-character component), which presupposes this ideal.

items.name: Definition 11.6 (global cyclotomic units D_n, D_n^+)
items.statement: For p odd and n ≥ 1, D_n is the intersection of O_{F_n}^× with the subgroup of F_n^× generated by {±ξ_{p^n}} ∪ {ξ_{p^n}^a − 1 : 1 ≤ a ≤ p^n − 1}; D_n^+ = D_n ∩ F_n^+.
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclotomic-unit-group: ‘For an odd prime p and n ≥ 1, D_n is the intersection of 𝓞^×_{ℚ(μ_{p^n})} with the subgroup of ℚ(μ_{p^n})^× generated by ±ζ_{p^n} and ζ_{p^n}^a − 1 (1 ≤ a < p^n), and D_n^+ = D_n ∩ ℚ(μ_{p^n})^+’ (same statement); real subfield: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/real-subfield. No cyclotomic-unit group in Tau Ceti (grep cyclotomicUnit/CyclotomicUnit = 0 files). Mathlib ingredient: mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.associated_sub_one_pow_sub_one_of_coprime (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/CyclotomicUnits.lean:61: ζ − 1 and ζ^j − 1 are associated for j coprime to n), so the quotients (ξ^a − 1)/(ξ − 1), (a,p) = 1, are units.

items.name: Theorem 11.7(a) (index of real cyclotomic units = h_n^+)
items.statement: Let p be odd and n ≥ 1, V_n^+ = O_{F_n^+}^× and h_n^+ = #Cl(F_n^+). Then D_n^+ has finite index in V_n^+ and [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+.
items.locator: §11.3, Theorem 11.7 (printed p. 176, PDF 77); quoted from Washington [81, Theorem 8.2], not proved
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/index-formula: ‘For p odd and n ≥ 1, D_n^+ has finite index in V_n^+ and [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+ = #Cl(ℚ(μ_{p^n})^+); hence also [V_n : D_n] = h_n^+’, and by the IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 stage description (‘Prove the regulator determinant calculation for cyclotomic units using Gauss sums and the complex L(chi,1) formula. Combine it with the proved analytic class-number formula and unit theorem to obtain [O^× : D_n] = [O^{+×} : D_n^+] = h_n^+. This is RJW Theorem 11.7.’). Not in either library.

items.name: Theorem 11.7(b) ([V_n : D_n] = [V_n^+ : D_n^+])
items.statement: Let p be odd, n ≥ 1, V_n = O_{F_n}^×. Then D_n has finite index in V_n and [V_n : D_n] = [V_n^+ : D_n^+] (= h_n^+). (Uses Hasse’s unit index Q(F_n) = [V_n : μ_{F_n}V_n^+] = 1 for p-power cyclotomic fields, and D_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩·D_n^+.)
items.locator: §11.3, Theorem 11.7 (printed p. 176, PDF 77); quoted from Washington [81, Theorem 8.2]
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/unit-index-real-full: ‘For p odd, [V_n : D_n] = [V_n^+ : D_n^+], where V_n = 𝓞^×_{ℚ(μ_{p^n})}; equivalently Hasse's unit index Q(ℚ(μ_{p^n})) = 1, so V_n = μ_{2p^n}·V_n^+’. Mathlib has only the general bound mathlib:NumberField.IsCMField.indexRealUnits_eq_one_or_two (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean:374, the index of realUnits ⊔ torsion is 1 or 2) and the criterion indexRealUnits_eq_two_iff (line 386); the value 1 for Q(μ_{p^n}) is not there.

items.name: Analytic class number formula (used in the proof of Theorem 11.7)
items.statement: For a number field K, lim_{s→1^+} (s − 1)ζ_K(s) = 2^{r_1}(2π)^{r_2} R_K h_K / (w_K √|d_K|). The proof of Theorem 11.7 applies it to K = F_n^+ (and F_n).
items.locator: §11.3, proof of Theorem 11.7 (printed p. 176, PDF 77): ‘… and then using the class number formula’
items.note: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:77: `theorem tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ ↦ (s - 1) * dedekindZeta K s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (dedekindZeta_residue K))` with `dedekindZeta_residue K = (2 ^ nrRealPlaces K * (2 * π) ^ nrComplexPlaces K * regulator K * classNumber K) / (torsionOrder K * Real.sqrt |discr K|)` (line 56). Same statement. The IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 stage consumes it (‘Combine it with the **proved** analytic class-number formula’). The factorisation ζ_{F_n^+}(s) = ∏_{χ even} L(s, χ) needed alongside is not in the library (grep of DedekindZeta.lean shows only the residue theorem).

items.name: Regulator of cyclotomic units in terms of L(1, χ) (used in the proof of Theorem 11.7)
items.statement: (As in Washington [81], proof of Theorem 8.2; the notes give only a one-line sketch.) For p odd and n ≥ 1, the regulator of the independent units γ_{n,a} (1 < a < p^n/2, (a,p) = 1), which with −1 generate D_n^+, is R = ±∏_{χ ≠ 1 even, χ mod p^n} (½ Σ_{1≤a≤p^n, (a,p)=1} χ(a) log|1 − ξ_{p^n}^a|) (group determinant, Washington Lemma 5.26), and for each even χ ≠ 1 of conductor f_χ, L(1, χ) = −(τ(χ)/f_χ) Σ_{a mod f_χ} χ̄(a) log|1 − ξ_{f_χ}^a| (Washington Theorem 4.9); with the class number formula for F_n^+ and ζ_{F_n^+}(s) = ∏_{χ even} L(s, χ) this yields [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+.
items.locator: §11.3, proof sketch of Theorem 11.7 (printed p. 176, PDF 77): ‘the regulator of cyclotomic units is given in terms of special L-values at s = 1 of Dirichlet L-functions’ (Washington [81], Lemma 8.1/Theorem 8.2 and Theorem 4.9)
items.note: The text only names this input; the formula above is Washington’s (Theorem 8.2 proof, with Theorem 4.9 for L(1,χ)). Planned by the IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0 stage description: ‘Prove the regulator determinant calculation for cyclotomic units using Gauss sums and the complex L(chi,1) formula.’ No packet node beyond L0/index-formula. Mathlib has mathlib:NumberField.Units.regulator (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/Regulator.lean) but no cyclotomic-unit regulator formula; Tau Ceti has none.

items.name: Definition 11.8 (local cyclotomic units C_n, C_{n,1}, C_{∞,1} and + parts)
items.statement: For n ≥ 1: C_n = the p-adic closure of D_n in the local units U_n = O_{K_n}^× (via F_n ⊂ K_n); C_n^+ = C_n ∩ U_n^+; C_{n,1} = C_n ∩ U_{n,1}; C^+_{n,1} = C_n^+ ∩ U_{n,1}; C_{∞,1} = lim_n C_{n,1} and C^+_{∞,1} = lim_n C^+_{n,1}, inverse limits for the norm maps (so C_{∞,1} ⊂ U_{∞,1}, C^+_{∞,1} ⊂ U^+_{∞,1}). Here U_{n,1} = {u ∈ U_n : u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n} and U^+_{∞,1} = lim U^+_{n,1} are the principal local units (Part II notation).
items.locator: §11.3, Definition 11.8 (printed p. 176, PDF 77); footnote 12 points to Lemma 12.20
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description (‘Use the actual global subgroup D_n … the passage from a finitely generated integer subgroup of principal units to its Z_p-span as its closure … Compute the image of the closed cyclotomic tower under Col’); ColemanPowerSeries:L4 has no packet nodes yet. The objects are used, with this locator, in node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence (‘U^+_{∞,1}, E^+_{∞,1}, C^+_{∞,1} the limits of the principal local units, the closures of the global units and of the cyclotomic units in them (RJW Definitions 11.8, 13.12)’). The recall sentence before the definition says U^+_{∞,1} consists of units ‘congruent to 1 (mod p)’; it should be mod 𝔭_n (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E67).

items.name: Theorem 11.9 = Theorem 12.23(ii) (Iwasawa’s theorem)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Coleman map Col : U_{∞,1} → Λ(Γ) (restricted to U^+_{∞,1}, with image in Λ(Γ)^+ = Λ(Γ^+)) induces an isomorphism of Λ(Γ^+)-modules U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p. (Independent of the sign convention for Col, since only the ideal I(Γ^+)ζ_p enters.)
items.locator: §11.3, Theorem 11.9 (printed p. 177, PDF 78); restated and proved as §12.5, Theorem 12.23(ii) (printed pp. 188–189, PDF 89–90)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description: ‘Compute the image of the closed cyclotomic tower under Col using continuity and the completed action. Conclude Theorem 12.23, including U_infty,1^+ / C_infty,1^+ ≃ Z_p[[G^+]] / (I(G^+) zeta_p)’, acceptance ‘Theorems … 11.9, 12.9/12.17/12.23’. No node yet (ColemanPowerSeries packet has L0–L3 nodes only). Consumers: node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture (hypothesis: ‘The local-unit theorem U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p through the Coleman map (RJW Theorem 12.23(ii), Iwasawa) is requested from ColemanPowerSeries L4’) and the IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3 stage (‘Combine L1 with R04.L4 …’). A general-coefficient analogue (Q_p-rational, χ-components) is node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L4/greither-stickelberger-image.

items.name: Λ(Γ)-module structure on the principal local units U_{∞,1}
items.statement: Let p be odd. For u = (u_n)_n ∈ U_{∞,1} = lim_{N} U_{n,1} and a ∈ Z_p put u^a = (u_n^a)_n with u_n^a := Σ_{k≥0} binom(a,k)(u_n − 1)^k (convergent since u_n − 1 ∈ 𝔭_n); this extends the Z-module structure and makes U_{∞,1} a compact Z_p-module (no such extension exists on U_∞, which contains μ_{p−1}). Γ ≅ Gal(K_∞/Q_p) acts on U_∞ coordinatewise, fixes μ_{p−1} and hence stabilises U_{∞,1}; the two actions commute and are continuous, so U_{∞,1} (and U^+_{∞,1}, over Λ(Γ^+)) is a Λ(Γ)-module.
items.locator: §12.1 introduction, §12.1.1 first paragraph and the paragraph before Corollary 12.6 (printed pp. 177 and 180, PDF 78 and 81); Z_p-structure recalled from (9-3)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L0 stage description: ‘Define norm-compatible units as the actual inverse limit; principal units form its compact Z_p-module. Extend the G-action to a continuous completed-group-ring action via R01. Do not put a Z_p-module structure on all local units: their prime-to-p torsion remains.’ Nodes so far: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/norm-compatible-units, L0/principal-norm-compatible-units (kernel of the residue map normLimitResidue), L0/principal-norm-compatible-compact; the ColemanPowerSeries gap list says the G-action and ‘principal-unit pro-p hypotheses before importing the ℤ_p-module construction’ are still to be supplied. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 stage: ‘the universal property for continuous actions on complete separated linearly topologized modules’. No Z_p-power on principal units in Tau Ceti or Mathlib (grep principalUnit: only TauCeti.unitFiltration_one and Mathlib’s ValuationSubring.principalUnitGroup, neither with a Z_p-action).

items.name: Γ ≅ Gal(K_∞/Q_p) (total ramification of p in F_∞)
items.statement: Let p be odd. Restriction to the completion at the unique prime above p identifies Γ = Gal(F_∞/Q) with Gal(K_∞/Q_p), K_∞ = Q_p(μ_{p^∞}); equivalently Φ_{p^n} is irreducible over Q_p for every n, so Gal(K_n/Q_p) ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^× compatibly with Γ_n ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^×. Hence Γ acts on the local units U_n and U_∞, and σ_a (χ(σ_a) = a) acts by ξ_{p^n} ↦ ξ_{p^n}^a.
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L0/local-cyclotomic-irreducible (‘The polynomial Φ_(p^(n+1)) is irreducible over ℚ_p’) and L0/local-cyclotomic-degree (‘[K_n:ℚ_p]=p^n(p−1)’), with the ColemanPowerSeries:L0 stage (‘total ramification, residue fields and norm maps’). Given irreducibility, Mathlib’s mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Gal.lean:77, `(h : Irreducible (cyclotomic n K)) : Gal(L/K) ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ`) gives the finite-level isomorphisms; Tau Ceti’s tauceti:IsCyclotomicExtension.card_aut_eq_totient (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Aut.lean) and tauceti:IsCyclotomicExtension.irreducible_cyclotomic_iff_finrank_eq_totient (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Irreducible.lean:93) are general tools, not the Q_p statement.

items.name: Principal units ↔ Coleman series with constant term ≡ 1 (claim (12-1))
items.statement: Let u ∈ U_∞ with Coleman power series f_u = Σ_{k≥0} a_k(u)T^k ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× (f_u(π_n) = u_n, N(f_u) = f_u). Then u ∈ U_{∞,1} if and only if a_0(u) = f_u(0) ≡ 1 mod p; in particular for u ∈ U_{∞,1}, f_u − 1 ∈ (p, T). (Since f_u(π_n) ∈ a_0(u) + 𝔭_n and 𝔭_n ∩ Z_p = pZ_p.)
items.locator: §12.1.1, proof of Proposition 12.1, claim (12-1) (printed p. 178, PDF 79)
items.note: The printed expansion ‘f_u = Σ_{k≥1} a_k(u)T^k’ must start at k = 0 (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E68, lead ColemanPowerSeries/E9). The text proves the ‘only if’ direction; node ColemanPowerSeries:L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-principal states both: ‘The evaluated tower of a norm-fixed unit series F is principal if and only if toZMod(constantCoeff F)=1’ (with L1/norm-fixed-evaluation-residue: the residue of the evaluated tower is toZMod(constantCoeff F)).

items.name: Coleman series of a Z_p-power: f_{u^a} = f_u^a
items.statement: For u ∈ U_{∞,1} and a ∈ Z_p, the series f_u^a := Σ_{j≥0} binom(a,j)(f_u − 1)^j converges in Z_p[[T]] ((p,T)-adically complete), is N-invariant, and equals the Coleman power series of u^a: f_u^a = f_{u^a}. Consequently ∂log(f_u^a) = a·∂log(f_u).
items.note: Uses uniqueness of Coleman series (Lemma 10.7). Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage (‘Prove additivity, continuity, Z_p-linearity on principal units and G-equivariance’); partial node ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-integer-powers (‘For f∈Bˣ and n∈ℤ, Δ(fⁿ)=n·Δ(f)’) covers only integer exponents. Mathlib has mathlib:PowerSeries.binomialSeries (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Binomial.lean:47) for (1+X)^a, not the composite f^a for a general principal unit series.

items.name: Proposition 12.1 (Col is Z_p-linear on U_{∞,1})
items.statement: Let p be odd. The restriction Col : U_{∞,1} → Λ(Z_p^×) of the Coleman map Col = A^{−1} ∘ ∂^{−1} ∘ (1 − φψ) ∘ ∂log ∘ (u ↦ f_u) is Z_p-equivariant: Col(u^a) = a·Col(u) for u ∈ U_{∞,1}, a ∈ Z_p.
items.locator: §12.1.1, Proposition 12.1 and its proof (printed pp. 177–178, PDF 78–79)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage description: ‘Define Delta(f)=∂f/f and the pipeline Col_0 = A^−1 ◦ ∂^−1 ◦ (1−phi psi) ◦ Delta ◦ Coleman … Prove additivity, continuity, Z_p-linearity on principal units and G-equivariance.’ No node for the Z_p-linearity itself (L2 nodes stop at the norm-fixed logarithmic derivative map). The linear pieces 1 − φψ, ∂^{−1} (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/inverse-mahler, a Z-linear map) and A^{−1} are Z_p-linear by construction in the PMIA packet.

items.name: Lemma 12.2, finite level (U_n = μ_{p−1} × U_{n,1})
items.statement: Let p be odd and n ≥ 1. Since p is totally ramified in K_n, O_{K_n} has residue field F_p, and reduction mod 𝔭_n gives a split short exact sequence 1 → U_{n,1} → U_n → μ_{p−1} (≅ F_p^×) → 1; hence U_n = μ_{p−1} × U_{n,1}, with μ_{p−1} ⊂ Z_p^× the Teichmüller representatives.
items.note: Planned for any nonarchimedean local field by the Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 description (‘Structure of Kˣ. Prove … 𝒪[K]ˣ ≃ μ_{q−1} × U(K,1)’); the residue field F_p of K_n is node ColemanPowerSeries:L0/cyclotomic-residue-field (‘ring equivalence from … ResidueField(O_n) to ZMod p’). Library ingredients already in Tau Ceti (not the product statement): tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100, `teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ`), tauceti:TauCeti.residue_teichmuller (line 132, section of reduction), tauceti:TauCeti.range_teichmuller (line 175, image = rootsOfUnity (q−1)), tauceti:TauCeti.unitFiltration_one (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean:173, U(K,1) = principal unit group) and tauceti:TauCeti.unitFiltrationGradedZeroEquivResidueFieldUnits (line 211, U(K,0)/U(K,1) ≃* 𝓀[K]ˣ). These are stated for `IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K`; the comparison of K_n (packet: intermediate field of an algebraic closure of Q_p) with that structure is a separate step (ColemanPowerSeries gap ‘Compare the concrete fields … with the LocalFieldsRamification named structures’).

items.name: Lemma 12.2 (U_∞ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1})
items.statement: Let p be odd. With μ_{p−1} ⊂ U_∞ embedded diagonally (v ↦ (v)_n, norm-compatible since N_{n+1,n}(v) = v^p = v), U_∞ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1}.
items.locator: §12.1.1, Lemma 12.2 and its proof (printed p. 178, PDF 79)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L0 stage description: ‘Prove U_infty=mu_{p−1}×U_infty,1 for odd p and identify the Tate-module subgroup Z_p(1).’ Nodes give the kernel side: ColemanPowerSeries:L0/norm-limit-residue (continuous homomorphism normCompatibleUnits → (ZMod p)ˣ by reduction of coordinate 0), L0/norm-compatible-residue-constant, L0/principal-norm-compatible-units (its kernel). The splitting is listed as outstanding in the packet gaps (‘Supply … norm-compatible Teichmüller splitting’).

items.name: Lemma 12.3 (Col kills μ_{p−1})
items.statement: For v ∈ μ_{p−1} ⊂ U_∞ the Coleman series is the constant f_v = v, and ∂log(v) = 0; hence Col(v) = 0. In particular Col(U_∞) = Col(U_{∞,1}), so no information is lost by restricting Col to U_{∞,1}.
items.locator: §12.1.1, Lemma 12.3 and its proof (printed pp. 178–179, PDF 79–80)
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-constants (‘For c∈Rˣ, Δ(C(c))=0’) together with the Coleman isomorphism (ColemanPowerSeries:L1 stage: ‘U_infty ≃ {f∈Z_p[[T]]^× : N(f)=f}’) and the L2 pipeline; no node states Col(μ_{p−1}) = 0 as such.

items.name: Remark 12.4 (kernel of u ↦ ∂log f_u is μ_{p−1})
items.statement: The kernel of ∂log on Z_p[[T]]^× consists of the constant series; a constant c ∈ Z_p^× satisfies N(c) = c iff c^p = c; hence the kernel of U_∞ → Z_p[[T]], u ↦ ∂log f_u, is exactly μ_{p−1}.
items.note: Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-kernel (‘If the additive group of R is torsion-free, then Δ(f)=0 iff f=C(constantCoeff f), for every f∈Bˣ’) and ColemanPowerSeries:L3/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-kernel (‘For u in normFixedUnits, its image under normFixedLogDeriv is zero if and only if u is the constant unit associated with a c in Z_p units satisfying c^(p-1)=1’). Same statements (the node phrases N(c) = c^p ⇔ c^{p−1} = 1).

items.name: σ_a and the Γ-action on Z_p[[T]] and on measures
items.statement: For a ∈ Z_p^×, σ_a ∈ Γ is the element with χ(σ_a) = a. Γ acts on Z_p[[T]] by σ_a(f)(T) = f((1+T)^a − 1) ((1+T)^a = Σ_k binom(a,k)T^k), and on measures on Z_p (and Z_p^×) by pushforward along x ↦ ax: ∫ f(x)·σ_aμ = ∫ f(ax)·μ; the Amice transform intertwines the two actions, and on Λ(Γ) ≅ Λ(Z_p^×) this is multiplication by [σ_a].
items.locator: §12.1.2, Notation and proof of Proposition 12.5 (printed pp. 179–180, PDF 80–81)
items.note: Planned by node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/amice-dilation (‘For every a in Z and integral measure mu in D(Z,Z), A(map(d_a,mu))=S_a(A(mu))’, with S_a(F)=PowerSeries.subst(b_a,F), b_a = binomialSeries a − 1, d_a = x ↦ a x) and L2/mahler-dilation. Library ingredients: mathlib:PowerSeries.binomialSeries (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Binomial.lean:47), mathlib:AbstractMeasure.map (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:101, pushforward along a continuous map), mathlib:AbstractMeasure.amiceTransform (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:75).

items.name: Γ-equivariance of the Coleman series: f_{σ_a u} = σ_a f_u
items.statement: For u ∈ U_∞ and a ∈ Z_p^×, f_{σ_a(u)}(T) = f_u((1+T)^a − 1), because f_u((1+π_n)^a − 1) = f_u(ξ_{p^n}^a − 1) = σ_a(f_u(π_n)) = σ_a(u_n) (f_u has Z_p-coefficients) and Coleman series are unique.
items.locator: §12.1.2, proof of Proposition 12.5, first bullet (printed p. 179, PDF 80)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage (‘G-equivariance’); the packet gap for L2 says ‘Establish the actual tower action, interpolation compatibility …’, i.e. not yet a node.

items.name: Equation (12-2): ∂log(σ_a f) = a·σ_a(∂log f)
items.statement: For f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× and a ∈ Z_p^× (indeed any a ∈ Z_p), ∂log(f((1+T)^a − 1)) = a·(∂log f)((1+T)^a − 1), where ∂log f = (1+T)f′/f.
items.locator: §12.1.2, proof of Proposition 12.5, second bullet, equation (12-2) (printed p. 179, PDF 80)
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-padic-substitution: ‘For every a∈ℤ_p and f∈ℤ_p[[T]]ˣ, put g_a=B_a−1 … Then Δ(f[g_a])=a·(Δf)[g_a] … In particular the identity holds for p-adic unit exponents, with the twist a of equation (12-2)’ (generalises to all a ∈ Z_p), resting on L2/padic-binomial-weighted-derivative (Y·D(B_a)=a·B_a) and the general chain rule L2/logarithmic-derivative-substitution.

items.name: Restriction to Z_p^× commutes with the Γ-action
items.statement: For a ∈ Z_p^× and a measure μ on Z_p, Res_{Z_p^×}(σ_aμ) = σ_a Res_{Z_p^×}(μ) (multiplication by a preserves Z_p^× and pZ_p); in power-series terms (1 − φψ)∘σ_a = σ_a∘(1 − φψ).
items.locator: §12.1.2, proof of Proposition 12.5, third bullet (printed p. 179, PDF 80)
items.note: Planned by node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/unit-restriction-dilation: ‘For any normed commutative coefficient ring R, unit a in Z and mu in D(Z,R), unitRestriction(map(d_a,mu))=map(d_a,unitRestriction(mu))’ (same statement), with L2/unit-dilation-psi-kernel.

items.name: Equation (12-3): ∂^{−1}∘σ_a = a^{−1}σ_a∘∂^{−1}
items.statement: On Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} (measures supported on Z_p^×), with ∂^{−1} corresponding to multiplication of measures by x^{−1}: ∂^{−1}(σ_aF) = a^{−1}σ_a(∂^{−1}F) for a ∈ Z_p^×. (∫ f(x)·∂^{−1}σ_aμ = ∫ f(ax)/(ax)·μ = a^{−1}∫ f(x)·σ_a∂^{−1}μ.)
items.locator: §12.1.2, proof of Proposition 12.5, fourth bullet, equation (12-3) (printed pp. 179–180, PDF 80–81)
items.note: Planned by nodes PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/inverse-mahler-dilation (‘For a unit a in Z and every F in B, inverseMahler(S_a(F))=a inverse times S_a(inverseMahler(F))’) and L2/inverse-weight-dilation (‘J(AbstractMeasure.map d_a μ)=a⁻¹·AbstractMeasure.map d_a(Jμ)’); same statements (the packet’s inverseMahler is defined on all of Z_p[[T]], extending by zero off Z_p^×).

items.name: Proposition 12.5 (Col is Γ-equivariant)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Coleman map Col : U_∞ → Λ(Γ) satisfies Col(σ_a u) = σ_a·Col(u) = [σ_a]·Col(u) for all u ∈ U_∞ and a ∈ Z_p^×; the factor a from (12-2) cancels the factor a^{−1} from (12-3), and A^{−1} is equivariant by definition of the action.
items.locator: §12.1.2, Proposition 12.5 and its proof (printed pp. 179–180, PDF 80–81)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage description: ‘Prove additivity, continuity, Z_p-linearity on principal units and G-equivariance. The factors a and a^−1 in the logarithmic derivative and the inverse derivative must cancel explicitly.’ Component nodes: items PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/394–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/396 (ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-padic-substitution, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/unit-restriction-dilation, L2/inverse-mahler-dilation, L2/amice-dilation); the tower part (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/393) has no node. Remark 12.7 (conceptual reason for ∂^{−1}) is not a separate item.

items.name: Corollary 12.6 (Col is Λ(Γ)-linear on U_{∞,1})
items.statement: Let p be odd. Col restricts to a homomorphism of Λ(Γ)-modules U_{∞,1} → Λ(Γ) (for the Λ(Γ)-structure of item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/383), and to a Λ(Γ^+)-module map U^+_{∞,1} → Λ(Γ)^+ = Λ(Γ^+).
items.note: Combination of Propositions 12.1 and 12.5 plus continuity (Λ(Γ)-linearity from Z_p[Γ]-linearity needs continuity of Col, which the text does not prove explicitly). Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage (‘additivity, continuity, Z_p-linearity on principal units and G-equivariance’); no node.

items.name: Definition 12.8 (logarithmic derivative Δ)
items.statement: For f(T) ∈ Z_p[[T]]^×, Δ(f) := ∂log f = ∂f/f = (1+T)f′(T)/f(T) ∈ Z_p[[T]]. Δ turns products into sums.
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative (‘For f∈Bˣ define Δ_R(f)=Y·D(f)·f⁻¹ in B’, B = R[[T]], Y = 1+T, D = PowerSeries.derivative; generalises to any commutative R) and L2/logarithmic-derivative-product. Mathlib ingredient: mathlib:PowerSeries.derivative (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Derivative.lean:50, a Derivation R R⟦X⟧ R⟦X⟧). Not in Tau Ceti (its logDeriv hits are complex-analytic, modular forms).

items.name: Δ∘φ = p·φ∘Δ
items.statement: For f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^×, Δ(φ(f)) = p·φ(Δ(f)), where φ(f)(T) = f((1+T)^p − 1).
items.note: Planned as the case m = p of node ColemanPowerSeries:L2/logarithmic-derivative-natural-power-substitution (‘For m∈ℕ and g_m=Yᵐ−1, Δ(f[g_m])=m·(Δ(f))[g_m]’), since φ(f) = f[g_p].

items.name: Lemma 12.10 (Δ maps norm-invariant units to ψ-invariant series)
items.statement: Let W = (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id}. For f ∈ W, ψ(Δf) = Δf; i.e. Δ(W) ⊆ Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id}. (Apply Δ to φ(f) = φ(N f) = ∏_{η∈μ_p} f((1+T)η − 1) and use Δ∘φ = pφ∘Δ and injectivity of φ.)
items.locator: §12.2.1, Lemma 12.10 and its proof (printed p. 181, PDF 82)
items.note: Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L2/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-psi-fixed (‘For every element u of the existing normFixedUnits subgroup, psi(Delta u)=Delta u’) and, more generally, L2/logarithmic-derivative-norm-psi (‘For every unit u of B, Delta(N_units u)=psi(Delta u)’, generalising); the packet proves it via the trace identity L2/coleman-trace-logarithmic-derivative (τ(Δu) = pΔ(N u)) rather than via η-translates.

items.name: Lemma 12.11 (reduction of surjectivity of Δ to mod p)
items.statement: Let A = Δ(W) mod p and B = Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id} mod p, subsets of F_p[[T]]. If A = B then Δ(W) = Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id}. (Successive approximation: f_0 ∈ Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id}, Δ(g_i) − f_{i−1} = pf_i with f_i ψ-fixed; h_n = ∏_{k≤n} g_k^{(−1)^{k−1}p^{k−1}} has Δ(h_n) = f_0 + (−1)^{n−1}p^n f_n; a limit point h ∈ W (compact) has Δ(h) = f_0.)
items.locator: §12.2.1, Lemma 12.11 and its proof (printed pp. 181–182, PDF 82–83)
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L3/logarithmic-derivative-surjective-mod-p (‘Under the residual image hypothesis, the existing group homomorphism normFixedLogDeriv:S→Multiplicative(W) is surjective’), with supporting nodes L3/norm-fixed-units-compact, L3/psi-fixed-p-saturation (division by p in ψ-fixed series), L3/logarithmic-derivative-precision-step/-approximation, L3/logarithmic-derivative-image-closed.

items.name: Lemma 12.12 (W mod p = F_p[[T]]^×)
items.statement: The reduction mod p of W = (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id} is all of F_p[[T]]^×: every f ∈ F_p[[T]]^× lifts to some f̃_0 ∈ Z_p[[T]]^×, and f̃ = lim_k N^k(f̃_0) exists, is N-invariant and reduces to f (by N(g) ≡ g mod p and N^{k_2}(g) ≡ N^{k_1}(g) mod p^{k_1+1}, Lemma 10.11(ii),(iv)).
items.locator: §12.2.1, Lemma 12.12 and its proof (printed p. 182, PDF 83)
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L3/norm-fixed-unit-residue-surjective (‘Every v∈B_0 units is the reduction of some u∈S’, S = norm-fixed units; same statement), using ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-norm-residue-identity (‘p divides N(f)−f’), L1/coleman-norm-iterate-congruence, L1/coleman-norm-limit and L1/coleman-norm-limit-fixed.

items.name: Projection formula for ψ and ψ-invariance of (T+1)/T (used in Lemma 12.13)
items.statement: For g, f ∈ Z_p[[T]] (and for the mod-p reductions), ψ(g·φ(f)) = ψ(g)·f; in F_p[[T]], φ(T^m) = T^{pm}; and ψ((T+1)/T) = (T+1)/T (in F_p((T)), equivalently ψ((1+T)T^{p−1}) = 1+T in F_p[[T]]). Hence ψ((T+1)/T · Σ_m d_m T^{pm}) = (T+1)/T · Σ_m d_m T^m.
items.locator: §12.2.1, proof of Lemma 12.13 and footnote 13 (printed p. 182, PDF 83); refers to the proof of Lemma 4.7
items.note: Planned mod p by nodes PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/residue-psi-semilinear (‘For F,G in B_0, psi_0(F(T^p)G)=F psi_0(G)’), L2/residue-psi-pole-basis (‘In B_0, psi_0(Y T^(p−1))=Y’), L2/residue-psi-pole-cancelled (‘psi_0(Y T^(p−1) H(T^p))=Y H’) and L2/residue-psi-comparison (reduction commutes with ψ); integrally by ColemanPowerSeries:L1/coleman-trace-frobenius-scalars (‘τ(φ(a)F)=aτ(F)’) with L1/coleman-trace-psi (τ = p·ψ). The packet avoids the Laurent series (T+1)/T by writing (1+T)T^{p−1}H(T^p).

items.name: Lemma 12.13 (B = Δ(F_p[[T]]^×))
items.statement: The reduction mod p of Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id} equals Δ(F_p[[T]]^×). (⊇: Lemmas 12.10, 12.12. ⊆: write f = Δ(a) + b with b = (T+1)/T·Σ_{m≥1} d_mT^{pm} (Lemma 12.14); ψ(f) = f and ψ(Δa) = Δa force ψ(b) = b, but ψ(b) = (T+1)/T·Σ d_mT^m, so b = 0.)
items.locator: §12.2.1, Lemma 12.13 and its proof (printed p. 182, PDF 83)
items.note: Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L3/residue-psi-fixed-logarithmic-image (‘Every g∈B_0 satisfying ψ_0(g)=g equals Δ(u) for some actual unit u∈B_0 units’), L3/residue-logarithmic-derivative-psi-fixed (converse: ψ_0(Δu) = Δu), L3/logarithmic-derivative-residue-image-equivalence, and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2/residue-psi-comparison, L2/residue-psi-fixed-error-zero (‘If psi_0(Y T^(p−1) H(T^p))=Y T^(p−1) H(T^p), then H=0’). The packet states B ⊆ {ψ_0 = id} = Δ(F_p[[T]]^×), which with Lemma 12.12 gives the equality.

items.name: Lemma 12.14 (F_p[[T]] = Δ(F_p[[T]]^×) + (T+1)/T·C)
items.statement: F_p[[T]] = Δ(F_p[[T]]^×) + ((T+1)/T)·C, where C = {Σ_{n≥1} a_nT^{pn}} ⊂ F_p[[T]] (so (T+1)/T·C = {(1+T)T^{p−1}H(T^p) : H ∈ F_p[[T]]} ⊂ F_p[[T]]). The Δ-part is Δ(∏_{n≥1}(1 − α_nT^n)) with α_n ∈ F_p chosen inductively (α_m = −d_m/m when p ∤ m).
items.locator: §12.2.1, Lemma 12.14 and its proof (printed pp. 182–183, PDF 83–84)
items.note: Planned by node ColemanPowerSeries:L3/residue-logarithmic-decomposition (‘For every g∈B_0 there are an actual unit u and H∈B_0 with g=Δ(u)+Y T^(p−1)H(T^p)’), the same statement after clearing T; proof nodes L3/frobenius-coefficient-completion, L3/euler-factor-logarithmic-coefficients, L3/euler-factor-frobenius-invariance, L3/euler-correction-step/-sequence, L3/euler-product-unit-limit, L3/frobenius-invariant-logarithmic-primitive. I checked the printed computations Δ(1 − αT^i) = −(T+1)/T Σ_{k≥1} iα^kT^{ik} and d_n = d_{np} (α^p = α in F_p; terms with i | np, i ∤ n carry the factor i ≡ 0): correct.

items.name: Theorem 12.9 (logarithmic derivative exact sequence)
items.statement: Let p be odd and W = (Z_p[[T]]^×)^{N=id}. The logarithmic derivative induces a short exact sequence 0 → μ_{p−1} → W →Δ Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id} → 0.
items.locator: §12.2.1, Theorem 12.9 (printed p. 180, PDF 81); proof completed on printed p. 183 (PDF 84)
items.note: Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L3/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-surjective (‘The actual existing group homomorphism normFixedLogDeriv from norm-fixed units in Z_p[[T]] to the additive ψ-fixed integral series … is surjective’) and L3/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-kernel (kernel = constants c with c^{p−1} = 1), with the map L2/norm-fixed-logarithmic-derivative-map; stage ColemanPowerSeries:L3 (‘Prove the logarithmic derivative exact sequence’). The printed proof says the kernel is ‘μ_p’ (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E69, lead ColemanPowerSeries/E13).

items.name: Lemma 12.15(a) (kernel of 1 − φ on ψ-fixed series)
items.statement: The kernel of 1 − φ : Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id} → Z_p[[T]] is the constants Z_p (constants are ψ-fixed). Reason: if f = a_0 + a_rT^r + … with a_r ≠ 0 the lowest non-constant term, then φ(f) = a_0 + p^r a_rT^r + (higher), and p^r ≠ 1.
items.locator: §12.2.2, Lemma 12.15 and the last paragraph of its proof (printed pp. 183–184, PDF 84–85)
items.note: Printed coefficient ‘p a_r’ should be ‘p^r a_r’ (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E70, lead ColemanPowerSeries/E12). Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L3/frobenius-fixed-constants (‘For F in B, phi(F)=F if and only if F is the native constant series C(F(0))’), L3/frobenius-leading-coefficient (‘coeff_r(phi(F))=p^r coeff_r(F)’), L3/psi-fixed-boundary and L3/psi-fixed-boundary-kernel (‘For F in W, psiFixedBoundary(F)=0 if and only if … F=C(c)’).

items.name: Lemma 12.15(b) (image and cokernel of 1 − φ)
items.statement: (1 − φ)(Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id}) = {f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} : f(0) = 0}, and evaluation at T = 0 maps Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} onto Z_p (ψ(1+T) = 0 and (1+T)(0) = 1). Hence 0 → Z_p → Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=id} →(1−φ) Z_p[[T]]^{ψ=0} →(T=0) Z_p → 0 is exact. (For f ∈ ψ=0 with f(0) = 0, g = Σ_{n≥0} φ^n(f) converges, is ψ-fixed and (1 − φ)g = f.)
items.locator: §12.2.2, Lemma 12.15 and its proof (printed pp. 183–184, PDF 84–85)
items.note: Planned by nodes ColemanPowerSeries:L3/psi-fixed-boundary-range (‘The range of psiFixedBoundary equals the kernel of the native coefficient-zero linear map restricted to U’, U = ker ψ), L3/psi-kernel-evaluation-surjective (‘The native coefficient-zero map U→Z is surjective; a section on values is c↦cY’), L3/frobenius-sum, L3/frobenius-sum-telescoping, L3/frobenius-sum-psi-fixed, L3/frobenius-iterate-decay and L3/psi-fixed-boundary-topology. Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L3: ‘Prove the exact sequence for 1−phi on psi=1, using the convergent sum of phi iterates and evaluation at T=0.’

items.name: Definition 12.16 (Z_p(1))
items.statement: Z_p(1) := lim_n μ_{p^n} (transition maps x ↦ x^p), a free Z_p-module of rank 1 on which σ ∈ Γ acts by σ·x = χ(σ)x; inside U_∞ it is {(ξ_{p^n}^a)_n : a ∈ Z_p} ⊂ U_{∞,1}, whose Coleman series are (1+T)^a.
items.locator: §12.2.2, Definition 12.16 (printed p. 184, PDF 85), and proof of Theorem 12.17 (printed p. 185, PDF 86)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L0 stage description (‘identify the Tate-module subgroup Z_p(1)’; packet gap: ‘Tate-module inclusion with the correct dyadic norm convention’). No Tate module of μ in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (grep TateModule/tateModule: 0 files in Tau Ceti; Mathlib has no such declaration name). Mathlib has mathlib:PowerSeries.binomialSeries for (1+T)^a, a ∈ Z_p.

items.name: Theorem 12.17(i) (fundamental exact sequence for U_∞)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Coleman map gives an exact sequence of Γ-modules 0 → μ_{p−1} × Z_p(1) → U_∞ →Col Λ(Γ) → Z_p(1) → 0, where Z_p(1) ↪ U_∞ is (ξ_{p^n}^a)_n ↔ a and the last map is μ ↦ ∫_Γ χ·μ (Γ-equivariant: ∫χ·σμ = χ(σ)∫χ·μ).
items.locator: §12.2.2, Theorem 12.17 and its proof (printed pp. 184–185, PDF 85–86)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L3 stage description: ‘Identify the full kernel of Col_0 with mu_{p−1}×Z_p(1). Identify its cokernel with Z_p(1), with quotient map the cyclotomic moment. … Recover Theorem 12.17.’ (no single node; the components are items PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/399–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/409). General-coefficient version: node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L4/greither-semilocal-coleman-map (Greither Prop. 2.10: ‘0 → ℤ_p(1)^g → U_∞ →αψ 𝒱(1) → ℤ_p(1)^g → 0’ for principal semilocal units over an unramified 𝒪, in the 1 − X parametrisation) and L4/greither-coleman-sequence-all-p. The sequence is insensitive to the sign convention Col vs −Col (see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E76).

items.name: Theorem 12.17(ii) (fundamental exact sequence for U_{∞,1})
