items.statement: Let p be odd. Restricting to principal units gives an exact sequence of Λ(Γ)-modules 0 → Z_p(1) → U_{∞,1} →Col Λ(Γ) → Z_p(1) → 0 (last map μ ↦ ∫_Γ χ·μ).
items.note: Planned verbatim by the ColemanPowerSeries:L3 stage description: ‘The endpoint on principal units is 0 → Z_p(1) → U_infty,1 → Z_p[[G]] → Z_p(1) → 0. This display uses RJW's Z_p coefficients … Prove exactness as a sequence of topological modules and as ordinary modules … Recover Theorem 12.17.’ Follows from (i) with Lemmas 12.2–12.3 (Col(U_∞) = Col(U_{∞,1})).

items.name: The real cyclotomic units γ_{n,a}
items.statement: For p odd, n ≥ 1 and a ∈ Z prime to p: c_n(a) = (ξ_{p^n}^a − 1)/(ξ_{p^n} − 1) ∈ D_n (recalled from §10.2), and γ_{n,a} := ξ_{p^n}^{(1−a)/2}c_n(a) = (ξ_{p^n}^{a/2} − ξ_{p^n}^{−a/2})/(ξ_{p^n}^{1/2} − ξ_{p^n}^{−1/2}), where the exponent 1/2 is taken in Z/p^n (p odd). γ_{n,a} is fixed by c, so γ_{n,a} ∈ D_n^+; it depends only on a mod p^n, γ_{n,1} = 1 and γ_{n,−a} = −γ_{n,a} (so γ_{n,p^n−1} = −1).
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/smoothed-cyclotomic-unit: ‘For (a, p) = 1: c_n(a) = (ζ^a − 1)/(ζ − 1) = ∑_{i<a} ζ^i ∈ D_n, and γ_{n,a} = ζ^{(1−a)/2} c_n(a) = (ζ^{a/2} − ζ^{−a/2})/(ζ^{1/2} − ζ^{−1/2}) ∈ D_n^+, where ζ^{1/2} is the square root of ζ in μ_{p^n} (p odd)’. Unit property from mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.associated_sub_one_pow_sub_one_of_coprime (Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/CyclotomicUnits.lean:61). The facts γ_{n,−a} = −γ_{n,a}, γ_{n,p^n−1} = −1 are not printed but are needed to see that −1 lies in the Z[Γ_n^+]-span in Corollary 12.19 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclic-generation includes ‘−1 = γ_{n,−1} is included’).

items.name: ξ^a − 1 is associated to ξ − 1 for (a, p) = 1
items.statement: Let ξ be a primitive p^n-th root of unity and a an integer prime to p. Then ξ^a − 1 and ξ − 1 are associated in Z[ξ]; in particular all ξ^a − 1 with (a,p) = 1 have the same p-adic valuation (the text gives its value v_p(ξ^a − 1) = 1/((p−1)p^{n−1})), and c_n(a) = (ξ^a − 1)/(ξ − 1) is a unit.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/CyclotomicUnits.lean:61: `theorem associated_sub_one_pow_sub_one_of_coprime (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ n) (hj : j.Coprime n) : Associated (ζ - 1) (ζ ^ j - 1)` (A a commutative domain). This gives the equality of valuations; the numerical value 1/((p−1)p^{n−1}) is not needed for the argument. The consequence used in the proof (a unit ±ξ^d∏(ξ^a − 1)^{e_a} has Σe_a = 0) is planned as node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/valuation-balance.

items.name: Prime-to-p reduction identity
items.statement: For p odd, (b, p) = 1 and 1 ≤ m < n: ξ_{p^n}^{bp^m} − 1 = ∏_{j=0}^{p^m−1} (ξ_{p^n}^{b + jp^{n−m}} − 1), and each exponent b + jp^{n−m} is prime to p. Hence the generators ξ^a − 1 with p | a are products of those with (a,p) = 1; and ξ^a − 1 = −ξ^a(ξ^{−a} − 1) allows 1 ≤ a < p^n/2.
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/prime-to-p-reduction (‘For p odd, (b, p) = 1 and 1 ≤ m < n: ζ^{bp^m} − 1 = ∏_{j<p^m} (ζ^{b + jp^{n−m}} − 1), with every exponent b + jp^{n−m} prime to p’). I checked the identity: 1 − X^{p^m} = ∏_{η^{p^m}=1}(1 − ηX) with X = ξ^b, η = ξ^{jp^{n−m}}, and the sign (−1)^{p^m+1} = 1 as p is odd.

items.name: Lemma 12.18(i) (generators of D_n^+)
items.statement: Let p be odd and n ≥ 1. The group D_n^+ is generated by −1 and {γ_{n,a} : 1 < a < p^n/2, (a,p) = 1}. (If γ = ±ξ^d ∏ (ξ^a − 1)^{e_a} is a unit then Σ e_a = 0, so γ = ±ξ^e ∏ γ_{n,a}^{e_a} with e = d + ½Σe_a(a−1); γ is real iff ξ^e = 1.)
items.locator: §12.3, Lemma 12.18(i) and its proof (printed pp. 185–186, PDF 86–87); Washington [81, Lemma 8.1]
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclotomic-unit-generators: ‘For p odd and n ≥ 1: D_n^+ is generated by −1 and γ_{n,a} (1 < a < p^n/2, (a, p) = 1), and D_n = ⟨ζ_{p^n}⟩·D_n^+’ (same statement), with L0/prime-to-p-reduction and L0/valuation-balance. The printed ‘γ ∈ D_n^+ if and only if e = 0’ means e ≡ 0 mod p^n (ξ^e real ⇔ ξ^{2e} = 1 ⇔ ξ^e = 1); harmless.

items.name: Lemma 12.18(ii) (D_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩·D_n^+)
items.statement: Let p be odd and n ≥ 1. The group D_n is generated by ξ_{p^n} and D_n^+; in fact D_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × D_n^+ (⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ ∩ D_n^+ = 1 since p^n is odd).
items.locator: §12.3, Lemma 12.18(ii) and its proof (printed pp. 185–186, PDF 86–87)
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclotomic-unit-generators (second clause ‘D_n = ⟨ζ_{p^n}⟩·D_n^+’). The direct-product refinement is not printed; it is what gives C_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × C_n^+ and C_{n,1} = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × C^+_{n,1} (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/424).

items.name: Corollary 12.19 (D_n^+ is cyclic over Z[Γ_n^+])
items.statement: Let p be odd, n ≥ 1, and let a ∈ Z generate (Z/p^nZ)^×. Then γ_{n,a} generates D_n^+ as a Z[Γ_n^+]-module: for b ≡ a^r mod p^n, γ_{n,b} = ∏_{i=0}^{r−1} σ_a^i(γ_{n,a}); in particular −1 = γ_{n,p^n−1} ∈ Z[Γ_n^+]·γ_{n,a}.
items.locator: §12.3, Corollary 12.19 and its proof (printed p. 186, PDF 87)
items.note: Planned by node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclic-generation: ‘If a generates (ℤ/p^n)^×, then D_n^+ = ℤ[Γ_n^+]·γ_{n,a}: every γ_{n,b} is ∏_{i<r} σ_a^i(γ_{n,a}) for b ≡ a^r, and −1 = γ_{n,−1} is included’ (same statement), with L0/tower-galois-compatibility. The printed chain of equalities is wrong termwise (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E71, lead IntegralIwasawaTheory/E81) and the published text has ‘(mod p)^n’ (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E72).

items.name: Lemma 12.20 (p-adic closure of a finitely generated subgroup of principal units)
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, g_1, …, g_r ∈ U_{n,1} and X = ⟨g_1, …, g_r⟩ the Z-submodule (multiplicative subgroup) they generate. Then the p-adic closure of X in U_{n,1} is the Z_p-submodule ∏ g_i^{Z_p} = {g_1^{b_1}⋯g_r^{b_r} : b_i ∈ Z_p} generated by g_1, …, g_r (u^b := Σ_k binom(b,k)(u−1)^k).
items.locator: §12.4, Lemma 12.20 and its proof (printed pp. 186–187, PDF 87–88)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description: ‘Prove … the passage from a finitely generated integer subgroup of principal units to its Z_p-span as its closure.’ No node (ColemanPowerSeries:L4 has none). Not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti: there is no Z_p-module structure on principal units (see item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/383); Mathlib’s closure/span results are for topological modules over the given ring, not for the Z → Z_p completion of exponents.

items.name: Lemma 12.21(i) (the principal generator wγ_{n,a})
items.statement: Let p be odd, a ∈ Z a topological generator of Z_p^×, and w ∈ μ_{p−1} with aw ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n (w = ω(a)^{−1}, independent of n). Then c_n(a) ≡ f_{c(a)}(0) = a mod 𝔭_n (as f_{c(a)} = ((1+T)^a − 1)/T and u_n = f_u(π_n) ≡ f_u(0) mod 𝔭_n), hence γ_{n,a} ≡ a mod 𝔭_n and wγ_{n,a} ∈ U_{n,1}; w is the unique element of μ_{p−1} with this property.
items.locator: §12.4, Lemma 12.21(i) and its proof (printed p. 187, PDF 88)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description: ‘Construct the principal Teichmuller-adjusted compatible generator w gamma_{n,a}. Prove its membership, norm compatibility …’. The Teichmüller lift is in Tau Ceti (tauceti:TauCeti.teichmuller, TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:100) for local fields. The printed proof writes γ_{n,a} = ξ^{a/2}c_n(a) (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E73). Norm-compatibility of (wγ_{n,a})_n (needed in Lemma 12.22(ii), not proved in the text) follows from that of c(a) (Lemma 10.x in §10.2), N_{n+1,n}(ξ_{p^{n+1}}^s) = ξ_{p^n}^s for s ∈ Z_p (p odd) and N(w) = w^p = w.

items.name: Lemma 12.21(ii) ((p−1)D_n^+ is cyclic, generated by (wγ_{n,a})^{p−1})
items.locator: §12.4, Lemma 12.21(ii) and its proof (printed p. 187, PDF 88)
items.note: Immediate from Corollary 12.19 (planned node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/cyclic-generation), since a topological generator of Z_p^× generates every (Z/p^n)^× (p odd). Planned in the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage (‘finite-level spanning’). (p−1)D_n^+ ⊂ U_{n,1} because the residue field is F_p.

items.name: Lemma 12.22(i) (C^+_{n,1} is cyclic over Z_p[Γ_n^+])
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 12.21: C^+_{n,1} is a cyclic Z_p[Γ_n^+]-module generated by wγ_{n,a}. (The closure of (p−1)D_n^+ is Z_p[Γ_n^+]·(wγ_{n,a})^{p−1} by Lemma 12.20, and equals (p−1)C_n^+ = C^+_{n,1}; since p−1 ∈ Z_p^×, C^+_{n,1} = Z_p[Γ_n^+]·wγ_{n,a}.)
items.locator: §12.4, Lemma 12.22(i) and its proof (printed pp. 187–188, PDF 88–89)
items.note: Corrected proof (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E74: the printed equality (p−1)D_n^+ = (p−1)D^+_{n,1} is false in general, though the two closures agree). Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage (‘Prove its membership, norm compatibility, finite-level spanning …’); no node.

items.name: Lemma 12.22(ii) (C^+_{∞,1} is cyclic over Λ(Γ^+))
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 12.21 (a ∈ Z a topological generator of Z_p^×, w = ω(a)^{−1}): the sequence (wγ_{n,a})_{n≥1} is norm-compatible, lies in C^+_{∞,1}, and C^+_{∞,1} = lim_n Z_p[Γ_n^+]·wγ_{n,a} = Λ(Γ^+)·(wγ_{n,a})_n is a cyclic Λ(Γ^+)-module.
items.locator: §12.4, Lemma 12.22(ii) and its proof (printed pp. 187–188, PDF 88–89)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description: ‘Prove its membership, norm compatibility, finite-level spanning and the **inverse-limit** cyclicity theorem. A family of cyclic finite-level modules is not automatically cyclic on inverse limits with an arbitrary chosen generator: establish the compatible generator and surjectivity by compactness/finite-level compatibility.’ The printed proof omits norm-compatibility of the generators and the compactness step (lim of surjections of compact modules is surjective); both are routine and noted in the stage.

items.name: C_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) × C^+_{∞,1}
items.statement: Let p be odd. C_{n,1} = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × C^+_{n,1} for every n (from D_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × D_n^+, Lemma 12.18(ii), passing to closures and to principal parts), hence C_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) × C^+_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) + Λ(Γ)·(wγ_{n,a})_n as Λ(Γ)-modules.
items.locator: Used implicitly in the proof of Theorem 12.23(i) (printed p. 188, PDF 89); not stated in the text
items.note: The printed proof of Theorem 12.23 applies Lemma 12.22 (which concerns only C^+_{∞,1}) to C_{∞,1}; this step is needed for part (i) (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E75). Covered by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage in general terms (‘every equivariance and closure comparison’); no node.

items.name: Image of the local cyclotomic units under Col
items.statement: Let p be odd, a ∈ Z a topological generator of Z_p^×, w = ω(a)^{−1}, b ∈ Z_p. With the Coleman map of Definition 10.14 (as printed), Col((ξ_{p^n}^b w γ_{n,a})_n) = Col(c(a)) = −([σ_a] − [1])ζ_p = −θ_aζ_p (ξ^b, w and the root-of-unity factor ξ^{(1−a)/2} lie in ker Col). Consequently Col(C_{∞,1}) = I(Γ)ζ_p and Col(C^+_{∞,1}) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p. (The text prints Col(c(a)) = +([σ_a] − [1])ζ_p, via Theorem 10.15; the ideal statements are sign-independent.)
items.locator: §12.5, proof of Theorem 12.23 (printed p. 188, PDF 89); uses Theorem 10.15 (§10.4)
items.note: Sign corrected (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E76, lead ColemanPowerSeries/E1). Planned: ColemanPowerSeries:L2 stage (‘For c_n(a)=… compute Delta(f_c)=a−1−F_a and hence Col_0(c(a)) = −([a]−1) zeta_p. Define Col=−Col_0 if a positive explicit reciprocity identity is desired’; nodes L2/cyclotomic-series-unit, L2/cyclotomic-logarithmic-derivative-cleared, L2/cyclotomic-smoothed-comparison) and ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage (‘Compute the image of the closed cyclotomic tower under Col using continuity and the completed action’). The passage from one generator to the whole ideal uses I(Γ) = Λ(Γ)([σ_a] − [1]) (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/373) and C_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) × C^+_{∞,1} (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/424).

items.name: Theorem 12.23(i) (Coleman map modulo cyclotomic units)
items.statement: Let p be odd. The Coleman map induces a short exact sequence of Λ(Γ)-modules 0 → U_{∞,1}/C_{∞,1} → Λ(Γ)/I(Γ)ζ_p → Z_p(1) → 0 (the last map induced by μ ↦ ∫_Γ χ·μ). Taking ⟨c⟩-invariants (exact, 2 ∈ Z_p^×) and using Z_p(1)^{⟨c⟩} = 0 gives part (ii) = Theorem 11.9.
items.locator: §12.5, Theorem 12.23(i) and its proof (printed pp. 188–189, PDF 89–90)
items.note: Planned by the ColemanPowerSeries:L4 stage description (‘Conclude Theorem 12.23 …’; acceptance ‘Theorems … 12.9/12.17/12.23’). Proof: Theorem 12.17(ii) with ker Col = Z_p(1) ⊂ C_{∞,1} and Col(C_{∞,1}) = I(Γ)ζ_p (item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/425). The printed proof has a gap in computing Col(C_{∞,1}) (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E75). Part (ii) is item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/382.

items.name: Pseudo-isomorphism M ∼ M′ of Λ-modules
items.statement: Let L be a finite extension of ℚ_p with ring of integers O_L and Λ := Λ(ℤ_p) = lim← O_L[ℤ_p/p^nℤ_p] ≅ O_L⟦T⟧. For Λ-modules M, M′ write M ∼ M′ (M is pseudo-isomorphic to M′) if there is a Λ-module homomorphism M → M′ with finite kernel and finite cokernel, i.e. an exact sequence 0 → A → M → M′ → B → 0 with A, B finite (of finite cardinality) Λ-modules.
items.note: Packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/pseudo-isomorphism (cites this locator): defines pseudo-isomorphism over a noetherian normal domain A by pseudo-null kernel and cokernel and states 'Over O⟦T⟧ the pseudo-isomorphisms are the maps with finite kernel and cokernel, RJW §13.1's definition' — a generalisation that specialises to RJW's. Proposed library home TauCeti.Iwasawa.IsPseudoIsomorphism does not exist in Tau Ceti f790474: grep -rli 'iwasawa' over the whole TauCeti tree returns 0 files, and 'PseudoIso|pseudoIso|pseudoNull' return 0 in both TauCeti and Mathlib 082e2d3.

items.name: ∼ is an equivalence relation on finitely generated torsion Λ-modules (but not in general)
items.statement: With Λ = O_L⟦T⟧: (a) the relation ∼ is not an equivalence relation on all (finitely generated) Λ-modules (it is not symmetric; e.g. over ℤ_p⟦T⟧ the inclusion of the maximal ideal (p,T) ↪ Λ has finite cokernel but there is no map Λ → (p,T) with finite kernel and cokernel); (b) restricted to finitely generated torsion Λ-modules, ∼ is an equivalence relation.
items.locator: §13.1, paragraph before Theorem 13.1 (printed p. 189, PDF 90), citing Washington [81, Warning, §13.2]
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/pseudo-isomorphism states both halves: 'Between finitely generated torsion modules a pseudo-isomorphism M → N gives one N → M, so ≈ is an equivalence relation there (Remark 1 after 5.1.7). For general finitely generated modules it is not: over Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ the maximal ideal 𝔪 … the inclusion 𝔪 → Λ is a pseudo-isomorphism, and there is no pseudo-isomorphism Λ → 𝔪'. Stage L4 description: 'Record where pseudo-isomorphism is symmetric: do not declare it an equivalence relation for arbitrary non-torsion modules'. The counterexample in (a) is the node's, added here for precision; RJW only cite Washington.

items.name: Distinguished polynomial
items.statement: A polynomial P(T) ∈ O_L[T] is distinguished if P(T) = a_0 + a_1T + ⋯ + a_{n−1}T^{n−1} + T^n (monic) with a_i ∈ 𝔭 (the maximal ideal of O_L) for every 0 ≤ i ≤ n − 1.
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Eisenstein/Distinguished.lean:31: `structure Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt (f : R[X]) (I : Ideal R) : Prop extends f.IsWeaklyEisensteinAt I where monic : f.Monic` — docstring: 'f is of the form xⁿ + a₁xⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + aₙ with aᵢ ∈ I'. Same statement with R = O_L, I = maximal ideal 𝔭. Mathlib also has the Weierstrass division/preparation built on it (RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean: isDistinguishedAt_weierstrassDistinguished etc.), cited by node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/weierstrass-adapter.

items.name: Structure theorem for finitely generated Λ-modules (Theorem 13.1, corrected)
items.statement: Let Λ = O_L⟦T⟧ and ϖ a uniformiser of O_L. Let M be a finitely generated Λ-module. Then M ∼ Λ^r ⊕ (⊕_{i=1}^s Λ/(ϖ^{n_i})) ⊕ (⊕_{j=1}^t Λ/(f_j(T)^{m_j})) for some r, s, t ≥ 0, n_i, m_j ≥ 1 and irreducible distinguished polynomials f_j(T) ∈ O_L[T]. [Printed with Λ/(p^{n_i}); correct only when L/ℚ_p is unramified — see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E77. The data r, (n_i), (f_j, m_j) are moreover unique (needed for Definition 13.3, not stated in the printed theorem — see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E78).]
items.locator: §13.1, Theorem 13.1 (printed p. 189, PDF 90), citing Washington [81, Theorem 13.12]
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-module-structure-theorem (cites Theorem 13.1): 'There are r ≥ 0, integers m_i ≥ 1, irreducible distinguished polynomials F_j … and a homomorphism M → E = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_i Λ/(ϖ^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_j Λ/(F_j^{n_j}) with finite kernel and cokernel. The number r, the multisets … are determined by M' — the corrected statement plus uniqueness. L5 acceptance: 'recover RJW … Theorem 13.1'. Proposed home TauCeti.Iwasawa.exists_pseudoIso_elementary does not exist in Tau Ceti f790474 (no Iwasawa module anywhere). Mathlib has only the Weierstrass preparation input (RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean), no module structure theorem over O⟦T⟧.

items.name: Characteristic ideal Ch_Λ(M) (Definition 13.3, corrected)
items.statement: Let M be a finitely generated torsion Λ-module (Λ = O_L⟦T⟧). Then r = 0 in Theorem 13.1, and the characteristic ideal is Ch_Λ(M) := (ϖ^n)·∏_{j=1}^t (f_j^{m_j}) ⊂ Λ with n = Σ_{i=1}^s n_i. [Printed (p^n); see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E77. Well defined because the elementary data are unique; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E78.]
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal (cites Definition 13.3): defines char_A(M) = ∏_{𝔭 height one} 𝔭^{length(M_𝔭)} intrinsically and states 'For Λ = O⟦T⟧, char_Λ(M) = (ϖ^{μ(M)}·F_{M,γ}), which is RJW Definition 13.3 with p^n read as ϖ^n (E15)' — generalises and compares. Proposed home TauCeti.Iwasawa.charIdeal does not exist in Tau Ceti f790474. Mathlib has Module.length (used by the node) but no characteristic ideal.

items.name: Decomposition Λ(Γ) ≅ O_L[H] ⊗ Λ for Γ = H × Γ′
items.statement: Let Γ = H × Γ′ with H a finite commutative group of order prime to p and Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p (key example Γ = ℤ_p^×, H = μ_{p−1}, Γ′ = 1 + pℤ_p). Then Λ(Γ) ≅ O_L[H] ⊗_{O_L} Λ, where Λ = Λ(Γ′) ≅ O_L⟦T⟧.
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition: 'Let Γ = H × Γ′ with H finite abelian of order prime to p and Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p, so Λ(Γ) ≅ O[H] ⊗ Λ'. L1 ('Completed group rings and convolution') is the owner of Λ(G) itself. No completed group ring of a product decomposing as a tensor product found in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (searched MonoidAlgebra tensor/product equivalences; none are for completed group rings).

items.name: Isotypic projector e_ω
items.statement: With Γ = H × Γ′ as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/432, let H^∧ be the group of characters ω : H → O_L^× (after enlarging L to contain their values). For ω ∈ H^∧ put e_ω := (1/|H|) Σ_{a∈H} ω^{−1}(a)[a] ∈ O_L[H] (1/|H| ∈ O_L since p ∤ |H|).
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition: 'The idempotents e_ω = (1/#H)Σ_{a∈H} ω^{−1}(a)[a] ∈ O[H] are orthogonal with Σ_ω e_ω = 1'; stage L4: 'construct integral character idempotents after adjoining character values'. Nearest library object: tauceti:TauCeti.Representation.primitiveCentralIdempotent (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/CentralIdempotent.lean:303, `(|G|⁻¹ * χ(1)) • Σ_g χ(g⁻¹) g` in k[G]) — only over an algebraically closed FIELD k with |G| invertible, not the integral O_L[H] version; not cited as library.

items.name: Isotypic decomposition of Λ(Γ)-modules (Lemma 13.4)
items.statement: Let Γ = H × ℤ_p with p ∤ |H| and L containing the values of all ω ∈ H^∧, and let M be a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-module. Then H acts on M^{(ω)} := e_ωM through multiplication by ω, M = ⊕_{ω∈H^∧} M^{(ω)} as Λ(Γ)-modules, and each M^{(ω)} is a finitely generated torsion Λ-module.
items.locator: §13.1, Lemma 13.4 (printed p. 190, PDF 91), citing Coates–Sujatha [16, A.1]
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition: 'every Λ(Γ)-module decomposes as M = ⊕_ω M^{(ω)} with M^{(ω)} = e_ωM, on which H acts through ω; M is finitely generated torsion over Λ(Γ) if and only if each M^{(ω)} is over Λ (RJW Lemma 13.4)' — same statement (and the converse).

items.name: Characteristic ideal over Λ(H × ℤ_p) (Definition 13.5)
items.statement: For Γ = H × ℤ_p as above and M a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-module, Ch_{Λ(Γ)}(M) := ⊕_{ω∈H^∧} Ch_Λ(M^{(ω)}) ⊆ ⊕_ω e_ωΛ(Γ) = Λ(Γ) (each e_ωΛ(Γ) identified with Λ).
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition: 'The characteristic ideal is char_{Λ(Γ)}(M) = ⊕_ω char_Λ(M^{(ω)}) (Definition 13.5)'. L5 acceptance: 'recover RJW … Definitions 13.3/13.5'. Inherits the ϖ correction of PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/431 when L/ℚ_p is ramified.

items.name: Multiplicativity of characteristic ideals (Lemma 13.6)
items.statement: For a short exact sequence 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 of finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ)-modules (Γ = H × ℤ_p, p ∤ |H|; in particular for Γ = ℤ_p), Ch_{Λ(Γ)}(M) = Ch_{Λ(Γ)}(M′)·Ch_{Λ(Γ)}(M″).
items.locator: §13.1, Lemma 13.6 (printed p. 190, PDF 91), citing Coates–Sujatha [16, A.1 Proposition 1]
items.note: Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal: 'It is multiplicative in short exact sequences'; character-decomposition: '… multiplicative in exact sequences (Lemma 13.6)'. L5 acceptance lists Lemma 13.6. Mathlib's Module.length_eq_add_of_exact is listed as the node's prerequisite (additivity of length), but there is no characteristic ideal in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: p-ramified extensions 𝓜_n, 𝓜_n^+
items.statement: Standing notation (§9): p odd; F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_n^+ its maximal real subfield, F_∞ = ∪F_n, F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+; 𝔭_n (resp. 𝔭_n^+, 𝔭, 𝔭^+) the unique prime above p in F_n (resp. F_n^+, F_∞, F_∞^+); Γ = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^× via the cyclotomic character χ, Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ) = Γ/⟨c⟩, c complex conjugation. 𝓜_n := the maximal abelian p-extension (pro-p) of F_n unramified outside 𝔭_n; 𝓜_n^+ := the maximal abelian p-extension of F_n^+ unramified outside 𝔭_n^+ (all inside a fixed algebraic closure).
items.note: No packet node (the IntegralIwasawaTheory packet only has L0 nodes). Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Construct each maximal abelian pro-p extension with the stated ramification condition in a common algebraic closure; prove its universal property … Define X for the p-ramified extension'. I.2: 'the appropriate maximal abelian pro-p Galois groups … Distinguish the unramified class-group module from the module classifying extensions unramified outside S'. Searched Mathlib and Tau Ceti for maximal abelian / unramified-outside constructions ('maxAbelian|maximalAbelian|abelianClosure|UnramifiedOutside|unramifiedOutside'): only TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Formation/AbelianLayer.lean (abstract class formations), nothing for number fields.

items.name: Unramified extensions 𝓛_n, 𝓛_n^+ (p-Hilbert class fields)
items.statement: Standing notation (§9): p odd; F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_n^+ its maximal real subfield, F_∞ = ∪F_n, F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+; 𝔭_n (resp. 𝔭_n^+, 𝔭, 𝔭^+) the unique prime above p in F_n (resp. F_n^+, F_∞, F_∞^+); Γ = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^× via the cyclotomic character χ, Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ) = Γ/⟨c⟩, c complex conjugation. 𝓛_n := the maximal unramified abelian p-extension of F_n; 𝓛_n^+ := the maximal unramified abelian p-extension of F_n^+ (the p-parts of the Hilbert class fields; finite extensions).
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1 (as for PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/437: 'Y for the everywhere-unramified extension'). The Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap layer 13 plans `hilbertClassField` as `rayClassField` at modulus one. No Hilbert class field in Mathlib or Tau Ceti f790474 (grep 'HilbertClassField|hilbertClassField' = 0 files in both).

items.name: The towers 𝓜_∞, 𝓜_∞^+, 𝓛_∞, 𝓛_∞^+
items.statement: Standing notation (§9): p odd; F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}), F_n^+ its maximal real subfield, F_∞ = ∪F_n, F_∞^+ = ∪F_n^+; 𝔭_n (resp. 𝔭_n^+, 𝔭, 𝔭^+) the unique prime above p in F_n (resp. F_n^+, F_∞, F_∞^+); Γ = Gal(F_∞/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^× via the cyclotomic character χ, Γ^+ = Gal(F_∞^+/ℚ) = Γ/⟨c⟩, c complex conjugation. 𝓜_∞ := ∪_{n≥1} 𝓜_n, which equals the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞ unramified outside 𝔭; 𝓜_∞^+ := ∪ 𝓜_n^+ = the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞^+ unramified outside 𝔭^+; 𝓛_∞ := ∪ 𝓛_n = the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞; 𝓛_∞^+ := ∪ 𝓛_n^+ = the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞^+. (Each equality of the union with the maximal extension is part of the assertion.)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Relate finite layers and inverse limits, including the composita needed to identify their Galois groups.' The identification of the union with the maximal extension over F_∞ is asserted without proof in RJW (it needs: 𝓜_n ⊆ 𝓜_{n+1}, and every finite abelian p-extension of F_∞ unramified outside p is abelian over some F_n since the Γ-action on a finite group factors through a finite quotient). No library support.

items.name: Iwasawa modules 𝒳_∞, 𝒳_∞^+, 𝒴_∞, 𝒴_∞^+
items.statement: 𝒳_∞ := Gal(𝓜_∞/F_∞), 𝒳_∞^+ := Gal(𝓜_∞^+/F_∞^+), 𝒴_∞ := Gal(𝓛_∞/F_∞), 𝒴_∞^+ := Gal(𝓛_∞^+/F_∞^+) (abelian pro-p groups, i.e. compact ℤ_p-modules).
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Define X for the p-ramified extension and Y for the everywhere-unramified extension, preserving RJW's notation.' Packet nodes that use them as data: EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence ('Let X_∞^+ = Gal(M_∞^+/F_∞^+) and Y_∞^+ = Gal(L_∞^+/F_∞^+)') and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer (hypotheses, 'IntegralIwasawaTheory L1').

items.name: Λ(Γ)-module structure on 𝒳_∞ by conjugation (Remark 13.7)
items.statement: For x ∈ 𝒳_∞ and σ ∈ Γ choose a lift σ̃ ∈ Gal(𝓜_∞/ℚ) and put σ·x := σ̃xσ̃^{−1}. This is independent of the lift (𝒳_∞ is abelian and normal in Gal(𝓜_∞/ℚ)) and defines a continuous action of Γ on 𝒳_∞, which extends by linearity and continuity to a Λ(Γ) = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧-module structure (𝒳_∞ being a compact ℤ_p-module). Likewise Λ(Γ) acts on 𝒴_∞ and Λ(Γ^+) acts on 𝒳_∞^+ and 𝒴_∞^+. [The printed justification cites density of O_L[Γ] in Λ(Γ) and Hausdorffness of Λ(Γ); see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E85.]
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Define the completed Galois action by conjugation and prove it is independent of a lift.' Nearest library infrastructure: tauceti Conjugation file for cohomology (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Conjugation.lean, explicitConj1) is the conjugation action on H¹(N, M), not on an abelian Galois group; not a match.

items.name: Iwasawa Main Conjecture, part (a): 𝒳_∞^+ is finitely generated torsion (Theorem 13.8)
items.statement: For every odd prime p, 𝒳_∞^+ = Gal(𝓜_∞^+/F_∞^+) is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module (Λ(Γ^+) = ℤ_p⟦Γ^+⟧, Γ^+ ≅ ℤ_p^×/{±1} ≅ μ_{p−1}/{±1} × (1 + pℤ_p)).
items.note: Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture (cites Theorem 13.8): 'Then X_∞^+ is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module and char_{Λ(Γ^+)}(X_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (RJW Theorem 13.8) … This holds for every odd p, unconditionally.' Stage L3: 'Deduce finite generation and torsion of X^+'. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 plans Mazur–Wiles' proof. Split from (b) because the Vandiver route (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/446–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/447) gives it too.

items.name: Iwasawa Main Conjecture, part (b): ch(𝒳_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorem 13.8)
items.statement: For every odd prime p, ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p, where ζ_p is the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic zeta pseudo-measure on Γ^+ and I(Γ^+) ⊂ Λ(Γ^+) the augmentation ideal (so I(Γ^+)ζ_p ⊂ Λ(Γ^+)). Proved by Mazur–Wiles, and by Kolyvagin–Rubin–Thaine Euler systems (Remark 13.17).
items.locator: §13.3, Theorem 13.8 (printed p. 192, PDF 93); Remark 13.17 (printed p. 195, PDF 96)
items.note: Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture, same statement ('char_{Λ(Γ^+)}(X_∞^+) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p'), with χ-component form from Rubin III.2.10. Stage L3: 'This is the unconditional Theorem 13.8; Theorem 13.11's stronger cyclic-module isomorphism is not asserted without Vandiver.' IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5: 'Prove the abelian-Q main conjecture of Mazur–Wiles'. No Iwasawa theory in Mathlib/Tau Ceti.

items.name: Even-character (isotypic) form of the Main Conjecture (Remark 13.9)
items.statement: Via the decomposition Λ(Γ^+) = ⊕_{ω} e_ωΛ(Γ^+) over the characters ω of μ_{p−1}/{±1} (i.e. the even Dirichlet characters of Gal(ℚ(μ_p)/ℚ)), Theorem 13.8 is equivalent to the conjunction over all even characters ω of the ω-component statements ch_Λ(e_ω𝒳_∞^+) = e_ω(I(Γ^+)ζ_p); the odd characters require a different formulation (Huber–Kings [42]).
items.note: RJW state this informally ('The above formulation takes into account every such even Dirichlet character'); the equivalence is immediate from Definition 13.5. Stage EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3: 'Prove all equivalent even-character, odd-character/class-group and Tate-twisted Selmer formulations'; node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/odd-character-formulation (cites Remark 13.9) proves the odd-character equivalent via Kummer duality — goes beyond the remark. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Supply the standard isotypic formulations with their Tate twists and involutions as proved comparisons.'

items.name: Class numbers h_n^+ and Vandiver primes (Definition 13.10)
items.statement: h_n^+ := #Cl(F_n^+), the class number of F_n^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^n})^+. The (odd) prime p is a Vandiver prime if p ∤ h_1^+.
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Define Vandiver(p) by p not dividing the class number of Q(mu_p)^+.' Partial library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassNumber.lean:64 `noncomputable def NumberField.classNumber : ℕ := Fintype.card (ClassGroup (𝓞 K))` gives h_n^+ once F_n^+ is set up (Mathlib's `maximalRealSubfield`, used in NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean, gives F_n^+). No Vandiver predicate in Mathlib/Tau Ceti (grep 'Vandiver' = 0 in both).

items.name: Iwasawa's theorem for Vandiver primes: 𝒳_∞^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p (Theorem 13.11)
items.statement: If p is a Vandiver prime, there is an isomorphism of Λ(Γ^+)-modules 𝒳_∞^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p. (Proof: 𝒳_∞^+ ≅ 𝒰_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+ by Corollaries 13.14 and 13.16(i),(iii), and 𝒰_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p by Theorem 11.9.)
items.locator: §13.4, Theorem 13.11 (printed p. 192, PDF 93); proof printed p. 195, PDF 96
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Combine L1 with R04.L4 to prove the actual isomorphism X_infty^+ ≃ Z_p[[G^+]] / (I(G^+) zeta_p).' L4 acceptance: 'Theorem 13.11 and its proof'. Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture only separates it from the unconditional statement ('The stronger statement X_∞^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p (RJW Theorem 13.11) is not asserted; it needs p to be a Vandiver prime'); it does not realise it.

items.name: Main Conjecture for Vandiver primes (Theorem 13.11, 'in particular')
items.statement: If p is a Vandiver prime, then 𝒳_∞^+ is finitely generated torsion and ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+) = ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(Λ(Γ^+)/I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p. (Uses: I(Γ^+)ζ_p is componentwise principal and nonzero in each e_ωΛ(Γ^+) ≅ Λ, and ch_Λ(Λ/(f)) = (f) for f ≠ 0.)
items.locator: §13.4, Theorem 13.11 and the end of its proof (printed pp. 192 and 195, PDF 93 and 96)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Derive Theorem 13.8's ideal equality under Vandiver.' Node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal supplies 'equal to (f) on A/(f) for f ≠ 0'. The componentwise principality of I(Γ^+)ζ_p (e_ω[h]−1 is a unit multiple of e_ω for ω ≠ 1, and e_1 I = (γ−1)e_1Λ) is used silently by RJW.

items.name: Closures of global units ℰ_n, ℰ_n^+, ℰ_{n,1}, ℰ_{n,1}^+, ℰ_{∞,1}, ℰ_{∞,1}^+ (Definition 13.12)
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. For n ≥ 1: ℰ_n := the p-adic closure of 𝒱_n in 𝒰_n; ℰ_n^+ := ℰ_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+; ℰ_{n,1} := ℰ_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; ℰ_{n,1}^+ := ℰ_n^+ ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; ℰ_{∞,1} := lim←_n ℰ_{n,1}; ℰ_{∞,1}^+ := lim←_n ℰ_{n,1}^+ (norm maps).
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'the finite-level exact sequence relating closures of global principal units, semilocal principal units … All closures and principal-unit restrictions must agree with R04'; I.2: 'Define inverse limits of … units … with the transition maps specified individually'. Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence takes 'E^+_{∞,1} … the closures of the global units … (RJW Definitions 11.8, 13.12)' as data. Nearest library-adjacent node: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0/units-completion (p-adic completion ℤ_p ⊗ E_F, not the closure inside local units). Nothing in Mathlib/Tau Ceti. Remark: ℰ_{n,1}^+ equals the closure of 𝒱_{n,1}^+ in 𝒰_{n,1}^+ (used as 'by definition' in the proof of Corollary 13.16(iii)); this needs the short argument x² = lim N_{F_n/F_n^+}(v_k) and 2 ∈ ℤ_p^×.

items.name: Leopoldt's conjecture for F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}) (Brumer), corrected rank
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. For every n ≥ 1 the natural map 𝒱_n ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → 𝒰_n has image of ℤ_p-rank equal to the ℤ-rank of 𝒱_n, i.e. ℰ_{n,1} (a finite-index subgroup of ℰ_n, and a finitely generated ℤ_p-module) has ℤ_p-rank r_1 + r_2 − 1 = p^{n−1}(p−1)/2 − 1 (r_1 = 0, r_2 = p^{n−1}(p−1)/2). Equivalently (by Lemma 12.20): elements of 𝒱_{n,1} that are multiplicatively independent over ℤ are independent over ℤ_p. [Printed 'ℰ_n is a finite ℤ_p-module of rank r_1 + r_2 − 1 = p^{n−1}(p−1)/2'; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E80.]
items.note: Quoted from the literature (Brumer's p-adic Baker theorem; Leopoldt for abelian fields); not used in the Vandiver proof as printed. Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4: 'Where abelian Leopoldt is used, include its proof input: the p-adic logarithmic linear-independence theorem of Baker–Brumer … and its application to abelian units.' Also mentioned in EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L2 ('Use the abelian Leopoldt theorem from R06'). grep 'Leopoldt|Brumer' in Mathlib and Tau Ceti: 0 files. Mathlib has the ℤ-rank side only: NumberField.Units.finrank_modTorsion (NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean:457, `finrank ℤ (Additive ((𝓞 K)ˣ ⧸ (torsion K))) = rank K`, with `rank K := Fintype.card (InfinitePlace K) - 1` at :359), not the p-adic independence.

items.name: Finite-level class field theory sequence (13-1)
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. For n ≥ 1 there is a short exact sequence of ℤ_p[Gal(F_n^+/ℚ)]-modules 0 → ℰ_{n,1}^+ → 𝒰_{n,1}^+ → Gal(𝓜_n^+/𝓛_n^+) → 0, the second map being the (local) Artin map of global class field theory (Gal(𝓜_n^+/𝓛_n^+) is the inertia subgroup at 𝔭_n^+ of Gal(𝓜_n^+/F_n^+)).
items.locator: §13.4, proof of Proposition 13.13, equation (13-1) (printed p. 193, PDF 94), citing Washington [81, Corollary 13.6]
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Derive from ray-class reciprocity the finite-level exact sequence relating closures of global principal units, semilocal principal units and the inertia part of the Galois group.' Global reciprocity/existence and ray-class reciprocity are Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layers 11–12 (layer 12: 'admissible moduli and ray-class reciprocity … rayClassArtinMap'). Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence: 'The finite-level sequence … is global class field theory (Washington, Corollary 13.6), requested with the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer.' Tau Ceti f790474 has ray class groups (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/*.lean) and abstract class formations (ClassFieldTheory/Formation/*.lean) but no number-field Artin reciprocity.

items.name: Exactness of inverse limits of compact modules
items.statement: Let (0 → A_n → B_n → C_n → 0)_{n≥1} be an inverse system of short exact sequences of compact Hausdorff (e.g. finitely generated) ℤ_p-modules with continuous transition maps. Then 0 → lim← A_n → lim← B_n → lim← C_n → 0 is exact. [RJW justify the limit step by 'finitely generated ℤ_p-modules (so satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition)', which is false as a general implication; compactness is the correct reason — see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E82.]
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5: 'Prove exactness for the compact inverse systems actually used in arithmetic; prove the relevant Mittag–Leffler or compactness argument, not the false assertion that finite generation of each Z_p-module alone implies Mittag–Leffler.' IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Take inverse limits using a proved compactness/exactness result.' Library input only: Mathlib's topological Kőnig lemma TopCat.nonempty_limitCone_of_compact_t2_cofiltered_system (Topology/Category/TopCat/Limits/Konig.lean; nonemptiness of cofiltered limits of nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces, which gives surjectivity on limits) and CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean (IsMittagLeffler, nonempty_sections_of_finite_cofiltered_system); the exactness statement itself is not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Units and the p-ramified Galois group at infinite level (Proposition 13.13)
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. There is an exact sequence of Λ(Γ^+)-modules 0 → ℰ_{∞,1}^+ → 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ → Gal(𝓜_∞^+/𝓛_∞^+) → 0 (inverse limit of (13-1)).
items.note: Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence (cites Proposition 13.13 and its proof): 'Then there is an exact sequence of Λ-modules 0 → E^+_{∞,1} → U^+_{∞,1} → Gal(M_∞^+/L_∞^+) → 0 (Proposition 13.13)', with the compactness repair of the limit step. Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1 plans the same sequence. Also uses Gal(𝓜_∞^+/𝓛_∞^+) = lim← Gal(𝓜_n^+/𝓛_n^+) (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/439).

items.name: Galois-theoretic exact sequence 0 → Gal(M/L) → Gal(M/F) → Gal(L/F) → 0
items.statement: For Galois extensions F ⊆ L ⊆ M (possibly infinite) with L/F normal, restriction Gal(M/F) → Gal(L/F) is surjective with kernel Gal(M/L); applied to F_∞^+ ⊆ 𝓛_∞^+ ⊆ 𝓜_∞^+ it gives 0 → Gal(𝓜_∞^+/𝓛_∞^+) → 𝒳_∞^+ → 𝒴_∞^+ → 0 (exact sequence of Λ(Γ^+)-modules).
items.note: General case in Mathlib: FieldTheory/Normal/Basic.lean:233 `theorem AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom_surjective [Normal F K₁] [Normal F E] : Function.Surjective (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom K₁ : Gal(E/F) → K₁ ≃ₐ[F] K₁)` (no finiteness) and FieldTheory/Galois/Basic.lean:411 `lemma IntermediateField.restrictNormalHom_ker (E : IntermediateField K L) [Normal K E] : (restrictNormalHom E).ker = E.fixingSubgroup`; also InfiniteGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient (FieldTheory/Galois/Infinite.lean:228). The instance needs 𝓛_∞^+ ⊆ 𝓜_∞^+ and the fields themselves (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/437–PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/439, planned IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1); Λ(Γ^+)-equivariance is immediate from PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/441.

items.name: Four-term exact sequence (Corollary 13.14)
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. There is an exact sequence of Λ(Γ^+)-modules 0 → ℰ_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+ → 𝒰_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+ → 𝒳_∞^+ → 𝒴_∞^+ → 0, obtained from PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/452 and PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/453 via Gal(𝓜_∞^+/𝓛_∞^+) ≅ 𝒰_{∞,1}^+/ℰ_{∞,1}^+ ≅ (𝒰_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+)/(ℰ_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+) (using 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ ⊆ ℰ_{∞,1}^+). [Printed 'of Λ(G)-modules' and with the quotients reversed in the proof; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E81, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E79.]
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1 ends: 'Prove the exact sequence 0 → E_infty^+/C_infty^+ → U_infty^+/C_infty^+ → X_infty^+ → Y_infty^+ → 0. … the quotient is U/E, not E/U.' Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/galois-unit-four-term-sequence (cites Corollary 13.14): same statement, 'the quotient orientation is corrected (E5)'.

items.name: 𝒴_n^+ ≅ Cl(F_n^+) ⊗ ℤ_p (equation (13-2))
items.statement: 𝒴_n^+ := Gal(𝓛_n^+/F_n^+) ≅ Cl(F_n^+) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p (the p-Sylow subgroup of the class group), via the Artin map; in particular p ∤ h_n^+ ⇔ 𝒴_n^+ = 0.
items.locator: §13.4, equation (13-2) (printed p. 193, PDF 94) and first line of the proof of Corollary 13.16 (printed p. 194, PDF 95)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.2: 'Establish the comparison of class-group and Galois descriptions by class field theory.' Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layer 13 defines hilbertClassField as the class field of the ray subgroup of modulus one (Artin isomorphism Cl ≅ Gal(H/K) then follows from layer 12's globalAbelianGaloisEquiv). Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti f790474.

items.name: Coinvariants of 𝒴_∞^+ recover 𝒴_n^+ (Proposition 13.15)
items.statement: For all n ≥ 1 (the printed range is n ≥ 0; n = 0, where F_0^+ = ℚ, needs the same inertia argument applied to F_∞^+/ℚ and is not trivial, see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E83), (𝒴_∞^+)_{Γ_n^+} = 𝒴_n^+, where here Γ_n^+ := Gal(F_∞^+/F_n^+) and (−)_{Γ_n^+} denotes coinvariants; equivalently 𝒴_n^+ = 𝒴_∞^+/((γ^{p^{n−1}} − 1)𝒴_∞^+) for a topological generator γ of Gal(F_∞^+/F_1^+). (Uses: 𝔭^+ is the only prime above p and is totally ramified in F_∞^+/F_1^+.)
items.locator: §13.4, Proposition 13.15 (printed p. 194, PDF 95), citing Washington [81, Proposition 13.22]; proof = Proposition A.6 (printed pp. 201–202, PDF 102–103)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'For the one-prime, totally ramified tower treated in RJW, prove the decomposition of the Galois group using inertia, compute its closed commutator subgroup, and prove Y_n ≃ Y_infty / ((gamma^(p^n)−1)Y_infty).' (L2 uses the appendix indexing, F_0 = base.) Indexing: RJW print 'For all n ≥ 0' with §13's F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}); Proposition A.6 (appendix indexing F_0 = ℚ(μ_p)^+) proves the §13 range n ≥ 1; n = 0 (F_0^+ = ℚ) is true but needs a separate argument ((𝒴_1^+)_{Δ} = 0). See PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E83.

items.name: Topological Nakayama lemma for compact Λ-modules
items.statement: Let Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ and 𝒴 a compact Λ-module. Then 𝒴 is finitely generated over Λ iff 𝒴/(p,T)𝒴 is finite, and elements generating 𝒴/(p,T)𝒴 generate 𝒴; in particular 𝒴/(p,T)𝒴 = 0 ⇒ 𝒴 = 0. Used as: if Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p acts continuously on the compact pro-p module 𝒴 and 𝒴_{Γ′} = 0, then 𝒴 = 0.
items.locator: §13.4, proof of Corollary 13.16(i) (printed p. 194, PDF 95); stated as Lemma A.7 (printed p. 202, PDF 103), citing Washington [81, Lemma 13.16]
items.note: Stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5: 'Include topological Nakayama, finite generation from finite residual quotient'; IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Prove compact Nakayama applies'; L3: 'Use L2 control plus topological Nakayama to prove Y_infty^+=0'. Nearest library: mathlib Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot (RingTheory/Nakayama.lean:118) — requires N.FG, which is exactly what the compact version must supply; not a match. The appendix Lemma A.7 is outside chunk G but is the statement invoked here. The review notes that this is the same statement as item PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/500 (Lemma A.7); this item records its use in Corollary 13.16(i).

items.name: Vandiver ⇒ 𝒴_∞^+ = 0 (Corollary 13.16(i))
items.statement: If p is a Vandiver prime then 𝒴_∞^+ = 0. (Proof: 0 = 𝒴_1^+ = (𝒴_∞^+)_{Gal(F_∞^+/F_1^+)} by (13-2) and Proposition 13.15, then Nakayama PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/457.)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Use L2 control plus topological Nakayama to prove Y_infty^+=0 under this hypothesis.' The printed proof writes (𝒴_∞^+)_{Γ_0}; with §11's Γ_n = Gal(F_n/ℚ) this is the trivial group, and Nakayama needs the pro-p group Gal(F_∞^+/F_1^+) — see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E83.

items.name: Vandiver ⇒ p ∤ h_n^+ for all n (Corollary 13.16(ii))
items.statement: If p is a Vandiver prime then p ∤ h_n^+ for every n ≥ 1 (𝒴_n^+ = (𝒴_∞^+)_{Γ_n^+} = 0).
items.note: Not named separately in the stage texts; it is the combination of IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 control (Y_n ≃ Y_∞/…) with L3's Y_∞^+ = 0 and (13-2). L3's index step ('Use the finite-level cyclotomic index formula …') needs exactly this for every n.

items.name: [𝒱_{n,1}^+ : 𝒟_{n,1}^+] is prime to p under Vandiver (13-3)
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. If p is a Vandiver prime then for every n ≥ 1 the index [𝒱_{n,1}^+ : 𝒟_{n,1}^+] is finite and prime to p. (Proof: 𝒟_{n,1}^+ = 𝒱_{n,1}^+ ∩ 𝒟_n^+, so 𝒱_{n,1}^+/𝒟_{n,1}^+ ↪ 𝒱_n^+/𝒟_n^+, of order h_n^+ by Theorem 11.7, prime to p by PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/459.)
items.locator: §13.4, proof of Corollary 13.16(iii), claim (13-3) (printed p. 194, PDF 95)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: 'Use the finite-level cyclotomic index formula, principal-unit intersections and flat scalar extension to prove E_infty^+=C_infty^+.' The index formula [𝒱_n^+ : 𝒟_n^+] = h_n^+ is node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/index-formula (Theorem 11.7, earlier chunk). The group-theoretic step S/(S∩N) ≅ SN/N is Mathlib's QuotientGroup.quotientInfEquivProdNormalQuotient (second isomorphism theorem) — elementary.

items.name: Vandiver ⇒ ℰ_{∞,1}^+ = 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ (Corollary 13.16(iii))
items.statement: Notation (§9): 𝒰_n = O_{K_n}^× with K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) (local units at the unique prime 𝔭_n), 𝒰_{n,1} = {u ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_n}, 𝒰_n^+ = O_{K_n^+}^×, 𝒰_{n,1}^+ = 𝒰_{n,1} ∩ 𝒰_n^+; 𝒱_n = O_{F_n}^×; for a subgroup X_n ⊆ 𝒰_n, X_n^+ = X_n ∩ 𝒰_n^+, X_{n,1} = X_n ∩ 𝒰_{n,1}; limits are along norm maps; 𝒰_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒰_{n,1}^+; 𝒟_n^+ the cyclotomic units and 𝒞_{n,1}^+ the closure of 𝒟_{n,1}^+ (Definition 11.8), 𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = lim← 𝒞_{n,1}^+. If p is a Vandiver prime then 𝒞_{n,1}^+ = ℰ_{n,1}^+ for all n ≥ 1, hence ℰ_{∞,1}^+/𝒞_{∞,1}^+ = 0. (Proof: 0 → 𝒟_{n,1}^+ → 𝒱_{n,1}^+ → W_n → 0 with #W_n prime to p; ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p (flat, kills W_n) gives 𝒟_{n,1}^+ ⊗ ℤ_p ≅ 𝒱_{n,1}^+ ⊗ ℤ_p; Lemma 12.20 gives surjections onto 𝒞_{n,1}^+ and ℰ_{n,1}^+ compatible with the inclusion 𝒞_{n,1}^+ ⊆ ℰ_{n,1}^+, which is therefore onto.)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3, sentence quoted under PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/460 ('… to prove E_infty^+=C_infty^+'). Library inputs for the algebra only: Mathlib IsDedekindDomain.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot (RingTheory/Flat/TorsionFree.lean:138) and the instance at :143 (torsion-free over a Dedekind domain ⇒ flat, so ℤ_[p] is ℤ-flat). The closure lemma 12.20 is from an earlier chunk. The proof's 'ℰ_{n,1}^+ is by definition the closure of 𝒱_{n,1}^+' needs the remark in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/448.

items.name: Vandiver's conjecture (Remark 13.17)
items.statement: Conjecture (Kummer–Vandiver): every odd prime p is a Vandiver prime, i.e. p ∤ #Cl(ℚ(μ_p)^+). Under it, Theorem 13.11 proves Theorem 13.8 for all p.
items.note: Corrected by the review from missing to planned. Packet node ArithmeticKTheory:N.7/vandiver-separation states the conjecture ('Vandiver's conjecture asserts that for an irregular prime l the Picard group of the ring of integers of the maximal real subfield of the l-th cyclotomic field has no l-torsion'; proof step 'State the conjecture in both forms'). For regular p the conclusion holds because h^+ divides h, so this is the item's statement. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3 defines Vandiver(p) and uses the conjecture only as a named hypothesis ('does not assume or prove that every prime is Vandiver').

items.name: Unramified cohomology H¹_ur(𝓕_v, M) (footnote 15)
items.statement: Setting (§13.5): 𝓕 := F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, p odd, coefficients in a finite extension L/ℚ_p; for a place v of 𝓕, 𝓕_v is the completion (an algebraic extension of ℚ_ℓ), I_{𝓕_v} its inertia group; H¹ is continuous Galois cohomology. For a topological O_L-module M with continuous O_L-linear G_𝓕-action (unramified outside finitely many places) and a finite place v of 𝓕: H¹_ur(𝓕_v, M) := ker(H¹(𝓕_v, M) → H¹(I_{𝓕_v}, M)), the map being restriction.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/unramified-condition: 'H^1_ur(K_v, B) = ker(H^1(G_v, B) → H^1(I_v, B))' — same definition (plus the inflation description). Library infrastructure only: continuous cohomology exists (Mathlib `continuousCohomology`, RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean:131; Tau Ceti explicit model TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1 with restriction explicitRes1), but no local Galois groups/inertia-based Selmer conditions.

items.name: Selmer structure (Definition 13.18(1)–(2))
items.statement: Setting (§13.5): 𝓕 := F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, p odd, coefficients in a finite extension L/ℚ_p; for a place v of 𝓕, 𝓕_v is the completion (an algebraic extension of ℚ_ℓ), I_{𝓕_v} its inertia group; H¹ is continuous Galois cohomology. Let M be a topological O_L-module with a continuous O_L-linear action of G_𝓕 unramified outside a finite set of places. A Selmer structure 𝓛 = (𝓛_v)_v for M over 𝓕 is a choice, for every finite place v of 𝓕, of a subgroup (O_L-submodule) 𝓛_v ⊆ H¹(𝓕_v, M) such that 𝓛_v = H¹_ur(𝓕_v, M) for all but finitely many v.
items.note: Nodes SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/selmer-data (abstract Selmer data: global module, local modules, localisation maps, local conditions) and SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/galois-selmer-group ('Σ ⊇ {v | p∞} ∪ {ramified primes}; the conditions at v ∉ Σ are unramified') realise this; the packet works over number fields K with finite Σ, while RJW's 𝓕 = F_∞^+ is an infinite extension (the stage passes to it by limits, L3).

items.name: Selmer group H¹_𝓛(𝓕, M) (Definition 13.18(3))
items.statement: Setting (§13.5): 𝓕 := F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, p odd, coefficients in a finite extension L/ℚ_p; for a place v of 𝓕, 𝓕_v is the completion (an algebraic extension of ℚ_ℓ), I_{𝓕_v} its inertia group; H¹ is continuous Galois cohomology. For a Selmer structure 𝓛 on M, H¹_𝓛(𝓕, M) := ker(H¹(𝓕, M) → ⊕_v H¹(𝓕_v, M)/𝓛_v), v over all finite places of 𝓕.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/selmer-kernel: 'Sel(D) = {c ∈ H : res_v(c) ∈ L_v for all v} = ker(H → ∏_v H_v/L_v)', and galois-selmer-group. Proposed home TauCeti/NumberTheory/Selmer/Basic does not exist in Tau Ceti f790474 (the 23 'Selmer' hits there and Mathlib's RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SelmerGroup.lean are the K(S,n) Selmer group of a Dedekind domain, not Galois-cohomological).

items.name: p-ordinary representation (Greenberg filtration), corrected
items.statement: Let T be a finite free ℤ_p-module with continuous G_ℚ-action, V := T ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p, W := V/T (≅ (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)^d as a group). V is p-ordinary if there is a finite, saturated, decreasing filtration (Fil^iV)_i by G_{ℚ_p}-stable subspaces [printed: G_ℚ-invariant; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E84] such that the inertia group I_{ℚ_p} acts on Fil^iV/Fil^{i+1}V through χ^i, χ the cyclotomic character. Fil^1W := image of Fil^1V in W.
items.locator: §13.5.1, Definition 13.19(1) and the paragraph before it (printed p. 196, PDF 97)
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition: 'For a decomposition group G_v at p … and a G_v-stable submodule F^+M ⊆ M … F^+M need only be stable under G_v, not under the global Galois group'; stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2: 'Greenberg's filtration is stable under a decomposition group at p, not generally the global Galois group. Saturation and the passage from V to T and A are separate lemmas.' ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0: 'Define the ordinary Greenberg Selmer group using the selected saturated local submodule'. Library: Mathlib has cyclotomicCharacter (NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307, `(L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ`) but no ordinary filtrations.

items.name: Greenberg local condition 𝓛^Gr_{v_p} (Definition 13.19(1))
items.statement: With V p-ordinary as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/466, 𝓕 = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+ and v_p the unique place of 𝓕 above p: 𝓛^Gr_{v_p} := ker(H¹(𝓕_{v_p}, W) → H¹(I_{v_p}, W) → H¹(I_{v_p}, W/Fil^1W)). The Greenberg Selmer group H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W) uses 𝓛^Gr_{v_p} at v_p and the unramified condition at all v ∤ p.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition (cites Definition 13.19(1)): 'L^Gr_v = ker(H^1(G_v, M) → H^1(I_v, M/F^+M))' — same condition (the composite through H¹(I_v, W) is the same kernel).

items.name: Bloch–Kato condition H¹_f and 𝓛^BK_{v_p} (Definition 13.19(2))
items.statement: H¹_f(𝓕_{v_p}, V) := ker(H¹(𝓕_{v_p}, V) → H¹(𝓕_{v_p}, V ⊗_{ℚ_p} B_cris)), B_cris Fontaine's crystalline period ring; 𝓛^BK_{v_p} := Im(H¹_f(𝓕_{v_p}, V) → H¹(𝓕_{v_p}, W)) induced by V → W. (Mentioned 'for completeness'; for the infinite extension 𝓕_{v_p} = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})^+ the standard definition is the direct limit of the finite-level conditions.)
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/bloch-kato-condition (cites 13.19(2) and Remark 13.20): 'For a finite place v above p and V a de Rham representation of G_{F_v}, H^1_f(F_v, V) = ker(H^1(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, V ⊗ B_cris)) (supplied by PadicHodgeRegulators L1), and … L^BK_v = im(H^1_f(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, W))' — at finite level only; the passage to 𝓕_{v_p} is not addressed. No B_cris in either library: grep 'Bcris|B_cris|BCris|crystallinePeriod|CrystallinePeriod|periodRing|PeriodRing|Fontaine' finds only Mathlib's RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean and RingTheory/Perfectoid/BDeRham.lean (BDeRhamPlus, BDeRham), 0 files in Tau Ceti.

items.name: Tate twists T_n = ℤ_p(n), V_n = ℚ_p(n), W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n)
items.statement: For n ∈ ℤ, T_n := ℤ_p(n) is ℤ_p with G_ℚ acting through χ^n (χ the cyclotomic character, viewed on G_ℚ via G_ℚ ↠ Gal(F_∞/ℚ), hence trivial on G_{F_∞}); V_n := ℚ_p(n); W_n := V_n/T_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n). Complex conjugation c acts on W_n by (−1)^n.
items.note: Used as data in node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer (hypotheses: 'χ is the cyclotomic character, T_n = ℤ_p(n), V_n = ℚ_p(n), W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n)'). Library input: Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter (NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307). No twisted Galois module ℤ_p(n) in Mathlib or Tau Ceti (the Tau Ceti 'Tate twist' file TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Tate/Twist.lean is for Hodge structures).

items.name: H¹ with trivial action is continuous homomorphisms
items.statement: Since G_{F_∞} acts trivially on W_n, H¹(F_∞, W_n) = Hom_cts(G_{F_∞}, W_n). (General fact: for a topological group G acting trivially on a topological abelian group M, H¹_cts(G, M) ≅ Hom_cts(G, M).)
items.note: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LowDegree.lean:840: `noncomputable def H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf : H1 G M ≃+ Additive (ContinuousMonoidHom G (Multiplicative M))` under `(htriv : ∀ (g : G) (m : M), g • m = m)` with G a topological monoid, M a topological additive group, continuous action (namespace TauCeti.ContCohomology). General case; the instance G = G_{F_∞}, M = W_n needs the Tate twist (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/469).

items.name: Inflation–restriction over 𝓕 = F_∞^+
items.statement: For p odd and Gal(F_∞/F_∞^+) = {1, c} ≅ {±1}: H¹(𝓕, W_n) ≅ H¹(G_{F_∞}, W_n)^{{±1}} = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(G_{F_∞}, W_n), the homomorphisms equivariant for the action of Gal(F_∞/F_∞^+) (conjugation on G_{F_∞}, as in Remark 13.7, and the Galois action on W_n). (Inflation–restriction; the outer terms H^i({±1}, W_n^{G_{F_∞}}), i = 1, 2, vanish because 2 is invertible on the p-primary module W_n.)
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer: 'Inflation–restriction gives H^1(F, W_n) = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(G_{F_∞}, W_n)'. Partial library: tauceti:TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfRes_exact (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Inflation.lean:336, `(explicitInfl1 G M N).range = (explicitRes1 G M N).ker`) and explicitInfl1_injective (:237) give exactness of 0 → H¹(G/N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M); the identification of the image of restriction with the invariants and the vanishing of the order-2 group's cohomology are not there. Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 5 plans the inflation–restriction sequence.

items.name: H¹(𝓕, W_n) via the maximal abelian pro-p extension (§13.5.2(1))
items.statement: As W_n is abelian and p-power torsion, every σ ∈ Hom_{cts,{±1}}(G_{F_∞}, W_n) factors through Gal(F_∞^{ab,pro-p}/F_∞), F_∞^{ab,pro-p} the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞; so H¹(𝓕, W_n) = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(Gal(F_∞^{ab,pro-p}/F_∞), W_n).
items.note: Implicit step of node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer; stage L4: 'Recover R06's class-group and p-ramified modules from the Selmer groups of Tate twists'. No library match.

items.name: Greenberg condition for ℚ_p(n) (§13.5.2(3))
items.statement: For V_n = ℚ_p(n) with the filtration Fil^iℚ_p(n) = ℚ_p(n) for i ≤ n and 0 for i > n (so V_n is p-ordinary), and 𝓕_{v_p} = K_∞^+ = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})^+: 𝓛^Gr_{v_p} = H¹(K_∞^+, W_n) if n ≥ 1, and 𝓛^Gr_{v_p} = H¹_ur(K_∞^+, W_n) if n ≤ 0. [Text then says 'for n ≥ 0' where n ≤ 0 is meant; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E86.]
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer (cites §13.5.2): 'Give V_n = ℚ_p(n) the filtration Fil^iℚ_p(n) = ℚ_p(n) for i ≤ n and 0 for i > n. Then L^Gr_{v_p} = H^1(K_∞^+, W_n) for n ≥ 1 and L^Gr_{v_p} = H^1_ur(K_∞^+, W_n) for n ≤ 0.' Same statement.

items.name: Greenberg Selmer group of W_n in terms of 𝒳_∞ and 𝒴_∞ (§13.5.2(2)–(3))
items.statement: For p odd and n ∈ ℤ: H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(𝒳_∞, W_n) if n ≥ 1, and = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(𝒴_∞, W_n) if n ≤ 0 (the unramified conditions away from p make σ factor through 𝒳_∞ = Gal(𝓜_∞/F_∞); for n ≤ 0 the condition at p makes it factor through 𝒴_∞ = Gal(𝓛_∞/F_∞)). [Printed as H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(F_∞, W_n); the group meant is over 𝓕 = F_∞^+; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E87.]
items.note: Covered inside node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer (which goes directly to the c-eigenspace form, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/475). Stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 (quoted under PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/472).

items.name: c-eigenspace decomposition and H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) = Hom(𝒳_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) (§13.5.2(4))
items.statement: For p odd, 𝒳_∞ = 𝒳_∞^{c=1} ⊕ 𝒳_∞^{c=−1} and 𝒴_∞ = 𝒴_∞^{c=1} ⊕ 𝒴_∞^{c=−1}; c acts on W_n by (−1)^n. Hence H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) = Hom_cts(𝒳_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≥ 1 and Hom_cts(𝒴_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≤ 0.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer: '… and hence H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W_n) = Hom_cts(X_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≥ 1 and Hom_cts(Y_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≤ 0.' Same statement.

items.name: (𝒳_∞)^{c=1} ≅ 𝒳_∞^+ and (𝒴_∞)^{c=1} ≅ 𝒴_∞^+
items.statement: For p odd, the natural surjection 𝒳_∞ → 𝒳_∞^+ = Gal(𝓜_∞^+/F_∞^+) (restriction to 𝓜_∞^+ ⊆ 𝓜_∞) induces an isomorphism (𝒳_∞)^{c=1} ≅ 𝒳_∞^+; similarly (𝒴_∞)^{c=1} ≅ 𝒴_∞^+.
items.locator: §13.5.2, paragraph after item (4) (printed p. 198, PDF 99), citing Coates–Sujatha [16, p. 6]
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer: 'Since (X_∞)^{c=1} ≅ X_∞^+, …'; stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Prove the plus/minus, Tate-dual and involution comparisons instead of suppressing them in the notation.' IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3: '… with their Tate twists and involutions as proved comparisons'.

items.name: For even n > 0, H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) = Hom_cts(𝒳_∞^+, W_n), with Pontryagin dual 𝒳_∞^+(−n)
items.statement: For p odd and n > 0 even: H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) = Hom_cts(𝒳_∞^+, W_n), whose Pontryagin dual is 𝒳_∞^+(−n), i.e. 𝒳_∞^+ with Λ(Γ^+)-action twisted by χ^{−n}.
items.locator: §13.5.2, final display (printed p. 198, PDF 99); Example 13.22 (printed p. 198, PDF 99)
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/tate-twist-greenberg-selmer: 'for even n > 0, H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W_n) = Hom_cts(X_∞^+, W_n), whose Pontryagin dual is X_∞^+(−n), the module X_∞^+ with its Λ(Γ^+)-action twisted by χ^{−n} (RJW §13.5.2, Example 13.22)'. Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/tate-twisted-selmer-formulation (b): 'For even n ≥ 2 … S_n^∨ ≅ X_∞^+(−n)'.

items.name: Pontryagin dual
items.statement: For a locally compact (here discrete p-primary or compact pro-p) abelian group A, its Pontryagin dual is A^∨ := Hom_cts(A, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) = Hom_cts(A, ℝ/ℤ) for p-primary/pro-p A, with the contragredient Galois (and Λ-) action; used for the dual of H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W) in Conjecture 13.21(ii) and Example 13.22.
items.locator: §13.5.2 final display, Conjecture 13.21(ii) and Example 13.22 (printed p. 198, PDF 99) — used, not defined
items.note: Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/PontryaginDual.lean:37: `def PontryaginDual := A →ₜ* Circle` — general case (continuous homomorphisms into the circle; for p-primary/pro-p groups these land in the p-power roots of unity ≅ ℚ_p/ℤ_p). The Λ-module structure with contragredient action is node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/pontryagin-dual ('Mathlib's PontryaginDual for the circle, restricted to p-primary M, with the contragredient action').

items.name: Tate dual V^∨
items.statement: For V as in §13.5.1, V^∨ := Hom_cts(V, ℚ_p(1)) with the induced G_ℚ-action (the Tate dual). E.g. ℚ_p(n)^∨ = ℚ_p(1 − n).
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/criticality: 'V^∨ = Hom_cts(V, ℚ_p(1)) is the Tate dual … V^∨ = ℚ_p(1 − n)'. No library.

items.name: L(V, s), the gamma factor L_∞(V, s) and r_V
items.statement: Attached to V (a Galois representation of an arithmetic object) are an L-function L(V, s) and an archimedean Euler factor L_∞(V, s), a product of shifted Gamma functions (no zeros); r_V := the order of the pole of L_∞(V, s) at s = 1. Example: V = ℚ_p(n): L(V, s) = ζ(s − n), L_∞(V, s) = π^{−(s−n)/2}Γ((s − n)/2), with poles at s = n, n − 2, n − 4, …; so r_{ℚ_p(n)} = 1 if n is odd and ≥ 1, and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/criticality (cites §13.5.3): same definition and the same ℚ_p(n) example ('r_{ℚ_p(n)} = 1 if n is odd and positive and 0 otherwise'); hypotheses: 'V is given together with its Gamma factor; the general recipe from Hodge data is listed as remaining.' Library for the analytic pieces only: Mathlib riemannZeta (NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean:121) and Complex.Gamma (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gamma/Basic.lean:287); L(V, s) and L_∞(V, s) for a Galois representation are not formalised.

items.name: Criticality for ℚ_p(n); n = 0 is excluded (Remark 13.23)
items.statement: ℚ_p^∨ = ℚ_p(1), L_∞(ℚ_p(1), s) = L_∞(ℚ_p, s − 1) [printed L_∞(ℚ_p, 1 − s); see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E88], so r_{ℚ_p^∨} = 1 and the hypothesis r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0 of Conjecture 13.21(ii) fails for V = ℚ_p. More generally L(ℚ_p(n), 1) = ζ(1 − n) and L(ℚ_p(n)^∨, 1) = ζ(n) are both critical exactly when n is even and ≥ 2, or n is odd and ≤ −1 (equivalently r_{ℚ_p(n)} = r_{ℚ_p(1−n)} = 0).
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/criticality: '… ℚ_p(n) is critical exactly when n is even and positive or odd and negative (RJW Remark 13.23)'. Checked: with L_∞(ℚ_p(n), s) = Γ_ℝ(s − n), r_{ℚ_p(n)} = 1 iff n odd ≥ 1 and r_{ℚ_p(1−n)} = 1 iff n even ≤ 0, so both vanish iff n even ≥ 2 or n odd ≤ −1, as printed.

items.name: Coates–Perrin-Riou conjecture: existence of p-adic L-functions
items.statement: Conjecture (Coates–Perrin-Riou): for V as in §13.5.1 there is a p-adic L-function L_p(V) in the field of fractions of Λ(Γ^+) interpolating (suitably modified) critical values of L(V ⊗ ψ, s) for finite-order characters ψ of Γ^+.
items.locator: §13.5.3, paragraph before Conjecture 13.21 (printed p. 198, PDF 99), citing [15]; further in §B.3
items.note: RJW state it only in words; the precise interpolation is in §B.3 (another chunk). ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5: 'Define the Greenberg and Coates–Perrin-Riou conjectural generalizations from RJW as mathematical propositions with all their inputs.' AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5: 'State the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence problem using a specified realization, critical set, periods, refinement/Panchishkin subspace and interpolation formula.' SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4 deliberately takes L_p(V) as data ('No theorem asserting existence of a p-adic L-function for every motive is introduced').

items.name: Greenberg's conjecture (i): corank (Conjecture 13.21(i))
items.statement: Conjecture: for V p-ordinary (PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/466) with W = V/T, the Greenberg Selmer group H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W) over 𝓕 = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+ has Λ(Γ^+)-corank (Λ(Γ^+)-rank of its Pontryagin dual) equal to r_V.
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/greenberg-main-conjecture (cites Conjecture 13.21): '(i) the Λ(Γ^+)-corank of H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W) equals r_V … These are propositions; no node assumes them'. For V = ℚ_p(n) node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/tate-twisted-selmer-formulation (a) proves (i) for every n. Stage SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'State RJW Conjecture 13.21 and its hypotheses'. The Λ-corank itself is only partly planned: node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/corank defines the ℤ_p-corank (dim_{ℚ_p} M^∨ ⊗ ℚ_p); the Λ(Γ^+)-corank (Λ(Γ^+)-rank of the dual, componentwise over the characters of μ_{p−1}/{±1}) is left implicit.

items.name: Greenberg's conjecture (ii): characteristic ideal = p-adic L-function (Conjecture 13.21(ii))
items.statement: Conjecture: if moreover r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0, the characteristic ideal (as a Λ(Γ^+)-module, Definition 13.5) of the Pontryagin dual of H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W) coincides with the ideal generated by the p-adic L-function L_p(V) of V. [As printed this cannot hold when L_p(V) ∉ Λ(Γ^+), e.g. V = ℚ_p(n), n even ≥ 2, where H⁰(𝓕, W_n) ≠ 0 — a correction factor is needed; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E89.]
items.note: Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/greenberg-main-conjecture: '(ii) if r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0, the characteristic ideal of the Pontryagin dual of H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W) is (L_p(V))' with L_p(V) supplied data. ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5 (quoted under PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/482).

items.name: Greenberg's conjecture for even positive Tate twists is (a twist of) the Main Conjecture (Example 13.22, corrected)
items.statement: For p odd and n > 0 even: the Pontryagin dual of H¹_{𝓛^Gr}(𝓕, W_n) is 𝒳_∞^+(−n), and Theorem 13.8 is equivalent to ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+(−n)) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p, where Tw_n is the ring automorphism [g] ↦ χ(g)^n[g] of Λ(Γ^+) (on measures: multiplication by x^n, written ∂^n) and ∂^nζ_p is the n-th twist of the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure. [RJW: 'the p-adic L-function in Greenberg's conjecture is ∂^nζ_p, so … Greenberg's conjecture is essentially a (twist of) Theorem 13.8'; ∂^nζ_p ∉ Λ(Γ^+), so the ideal is Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p, not (∂^nζ_p); see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E89.]
items.note: Node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/tate-twisted-selmer-formulation (b): 'For even n ≥ 2 …: S_n^∨ ≅ X_∞^+(−n) and char(S_n^∨) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p' — the corrected form, and its hypotheses explain ∂^nζ_p ∉ Λ(Γ^+). Node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/greenberg-conjecture-tate-twists states that 'Conjecture 13.21(ii) for V is equivalent to the Iwasawa main conjecture … hence holds', which repeats RJW's imprecision (the literal (ii) with L_p = ∂^nζ_p is false; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E89).

items.name: ℤ_p-extension and its layers F_n
items.statement: Let F be a number field and p a prime. A ℤ_p-extension of F is a Galois extension F∞/F with Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p (as profinite groups). For n ≥ 0, F_n denotes the unique intermediate field with Gal(F_n/F) ≅ ℤ/p^nℤ (the fixed field of the closed subgroup p^nℤ_p, the unique open subgroup of index p^n).
items.locator: Appendix A, Definition A.1 (printed p. 199, PDF 100)
items.note: No packet node realises it (the only IntegralIwasawaTheory packet nodes are L0 ones in IntegralIwasawaTheory--I.8.json). Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1: 'Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of a number field, its finite layers ... Identify the procyclic quotient with Z_p after choosing a generator'; IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Extend to an arbitrary Z_p-extension'. Searched Tau Ceti f790474 (grep -rni 'iwasawa|ZpExtension|IsZpExtension' → 0 hits) and Mathlib 082e2d3 (no ℤ_p-extension notion).

items.name: Existence of the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension
items.statement: Let F be a number field and p an odd prime. Restriction identifies H := Gal(F(μ_{p^∞})/F) with the open subgroup Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/F ∩ ℚ(μ_{p^∞})) of Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^×. Its torsion subgroup H_tors = H ∩ μ_{p−1} is finite and H/H_tors ≅ ℤ_p; the fixed field F(μ_{p^∞})^{H_tors} is a ℤ_p-extension of F, the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension (equal to F·ℚ∞). In particular every number field has at least one ℤ_p-extension. (Corrected: the text says the quotient is by 'the finite torsion subgroup μ_{p−1}', which is right only when H ⊇ μ_{p−1}; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E101.)
items.locator: Appendix A, paragraph after Definition A.1 (printed p. 199, PDF 100)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1: 'Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of a number field, its finite layers, Galois actions, norm maps, decomposition and inertia groups, and ramification outside p.' Mathlib has only the finite-level input: IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Gal.lean:77, Gal(L/K) ≃* (ZMod n)ˣ when cyclotomic n K is irreducible); no infinite cyclotomic tower or ℤ_p-extension in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Example A.2: the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of ℚ(μ_p) and of ℚ
items.statement: p odd. For F = ℚ(μ_p), F∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) is the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of F (Gal(F∞/F) ≅ 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p) and F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}}) (the field called F_{n+1} in §9). The cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of ℚ is the fixed field (F∞)^{μ_{p−1}} of the torsion subgroup μ_{p−1} ⊂ ℤ_p^× ≅ Gal(F∞/ℚ).
items.locator: Appendix A, Example A.2 (printed p. 199, PDF 100)
items.note: Packet node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/compatible-cyclotomic-tower (IntegralIwasawaTheory--I.8.json) constructs 'the subfields ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ ℂ, with ℚ(μ_m) ⊆ ℚ(μ_n) for m ∣ n' and L0/tower-galois-compatibility identifies restriction with reduction (ℤ/n)^× → (ℤ/m)^× via autEquivPow; the infinite tower and its identification with ℤ_p^× are I.1 ('Construct the cyclotomic Z_p-extension'). The re-indexing F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^{n+1}}) versus §9's F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}) matters for Proposition 13.15 = Proposition A.6.

items.name: Leopoldt's conjecture (ℤ_p-extension form)
items.statement: Conjecture. Let F be a number field with r₂ complex places (the text says 'r₂ is the number of complex embeddings of F'; corrected, issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E109) and F̃ the compositum of all ℤ_p-extensions of F. Then Gal(F̃/F) ≅ ℤ_p^{r₂+1} ('the number of independent ℤ_p-extensions of F is exactly r₂+1'). In particular a totally real F has a unique ℤ_p-extension, the cyclotomic one.
items.locator: Appendix A, paragraph after Example A.2 (printed p. 199, PDF 100)
items.note: Partial. Packet node Polylogarithms:P.6/leopoldt-statement plans the unit form ('the canonical map E_K ⊗ Z_p → ∏_{𝔭|p} Û_𝔭 is injective', NSW 10.3.6) and P.6/leopoldt-equivalence its equivalent unit/regulator forms; no node or stage plans the class-field-theoretic translation rank_{ℤ_p} Gal(F̃/F) = r₂ + 1 + δ(F) (δ the Leopoldt defect), which is what the ℤ_p-extension form needs (searched atlas stages for 'r_2 + 1', 'independent Z_p-extensions', 'compositum of all Z_p'). The unconditional inequality rank ≥ r₂+1 is not stated in the text.

items.name: Leopoldt's conjecture for abelian fields (Brumer; NSW Theorem 10.3.16)
items.statement: Leopoldt's conjecture holds for every number field F that is an abelian extension of ℚ or an abelian extension of an imaginary quadratic field.
items.locator: Appendix A, paragraph after Example A.2, citing [65, Theorem 10.3.16] (printed p. 199, PDF 100)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4: 'Where abelian Leopoldt is used, include its proof input: the p-adic logarithmic linear-independence theorem of Baker–Brumer with its auxiliary-polynomial/transcendence argument, and its application to abelian units.' The stage names abelian units without singling out the imaginary-quadratic base, so that half is only implicitly covered. Brumer's p-adic Baker theorem is not among the DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3 nodes, which are complex Baker only.

items.name: Λ(Γ) ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧ via a topological generator γ₀ ↦ 1+T
items.statement: Let Γ ≅ ℤ_p with topological generator γ₀. There is a unique isomorphism of topological ℤ_p-algebras Λ(Γ) = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = lim_n ℤ_p[Γ/Γ^{p^n}] → Λ := ℤ_p⟦T⟧ sending γ₀ to 1+T; it maps the kernel of Λ(Γ) → ℤ_p[Γ/Γ^{p^n}] onto (ω_n) = ((1+T)^{p^n} − 1). When γ₀ corresponds to 1 ∈ ℤ_p this is the Mahler (Amice) transform, but the identification exists for every generator.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, first paragraph (printed pp. 199–200, PDF 100–101)
items.note: Mathlib has only the linear Amice transform for Γ = ℤ_p with generator 1: AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:156). It is a linear equivalence, not a ring isomorphism, and it is not attached to an abstract Γ with an arbitrary generator. Plans: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 ('Identify the procyclic quotient with Z_p after choosing a generator, and prove generator-change formulas ... The kernel of passage to Γ/Γ^{p^n} is generated by (1+T)^{p^n}−1'), NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.0 ('Recover O[[T]] for G=Zp'), and packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/cyclotomic-weierstrass-polynomials ('O⟦T⟧/(ω_n) ≅ O[Γ/Γ_n] by T ↦ γ − 1; the resulting O⟦T⟧ ≅ O⟦Γ⟧ is requested from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9').

items.name: Unramified Iwasawa modules L_n, L∞, Y_n, Y∞ and e_n
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). L_n is the maximal unramified abelian p-extension of F_n, and L∞ the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F∞. Y_n = Y_{F,n} := Gal(L_n/F_n) (≅ Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p, the p-Sylow subgroup of the class group, see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/493), Y∞ = Y_{F,∞} := lim_n Y_{F,n} (transition maps induced by restriction), and e_n := v_p(#Y_n), the exponent of p in the class number of F_n. In the proofs Y∞ is used as Gal(L∞/F∞), with Λ(Γ) acting by conjugation through lifts of Γ (so 1+T acts as γ₀); for this identification see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E103.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, first paragraph (printed p. 200, PDF 101)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Construct each maximal abelian pro-p extension with the stated ramification condition in a common algebraic closure ... Define X for the p-ramified extension and Y for the everywhere-unramified extension, preserving RJW's notation. Define the completed Galois action by conjugation and prove it is independent of a lift.' No packet node. Nothing in Tau Ceti or Mathlib (no Hilbert class field; see PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/493).

items.name: Class field theory: Gal(L_n/F_n) ≅ Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p
items.statement: For a number field K, the Artin map of the Hilbert class field H(K)/K is an isomorphism Cl(K) ≅ Gal(H(K)/K). Hence the maximal unramified abelian p-extension L of K has Gal(L/K) ≅ Cl(K) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p, the p-Sylow subgroup of the finite group Cl(K). Applied with K = F_n: Y_n ≅ Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p and #Y_n = p^{e_n}.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, first paragraph, display defining Y_{F,n} (printed p. 200, PDF 101); also (13-2), printed p. 193
items.note: Only finiteness of the class group is in the library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassNumber.lean:58 'noncomputable instance instFintypeClassGroup : Fintype (ClassGroup (𝓞 K))' and NumberField.classNumber (line 64; namespace NumberField.RingOfIntegers for the instance, read in the file). The Hilbert class field and its Galois group are planned: ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 lists `hilbertClassField` and `gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup` and 'Prove also the maximal unramified properties'. grep for 'hilbertClassField|HilbertClassField' in Tau Ceti and Mathlib: 0 hits.

items.name: Iwasawa's class-number growth theorem (Theorem A.3)
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Let e_n = v_p(#(Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p)). There exist integers μ ≥ 0, λ ≥ 0 and ν ∈ ℤ, and n₀ ≥ 0, such that e_n = μp^n + λn + ν for all n ≥ n₀. Stated for an arbitrary ℤ_p-extension of an arbitrary number field; the notes prove it only under hypothesis (H) (Remark A.4(2)), referring to [81, §13] for the reduction. (Corrected: the text asserts ν ≥ 0, which the proof does not give and which is stronger than the standard statement; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E90.) In the proof μ = Σm_i and λ = Σ k_j deg f_j are the invariants of the elementary module attached to Y∞.
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Theorem A.3 (printed p. 200, PDF 101); proof on printed p. 206 (PDF 107)
items.note: Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Obtain v_p(#Cl(F_n)) = mu p^n + lambda n + nu (n sufficiently large), where mu,lambda≥0 and **nu is an integer** ... Extend to an arbitrary Z_p-extension ... Establish every Appendix A reduction that the notes quote from Washington.' The module-theoretic core is packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-growth-formula: 'Let M be a finitely generated torsion Λ-module and n₀ ≥ d(M). Then #(M/(ω_n/ω_{n₀})M) = p^{μp^n + λn + ν} for all sufficiently large n' (NSW 5.3.17). The arithmetic identification Y_n = Y∞/ω_n needs PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/499.
