items.name: Hypothesis (H) holds for ℚ(μ_{p^m}) and ℚ(μ_{p^m})⁺ (Remark A.4(2))
items.statement: p odd, m ≥ 0. For F = ℚ(μ_{p^m}) or F = ℚ(μ_{p^m})⁺ and F∞/F the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension (F∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) resp. ℚ(μ_{p^∞})⁺ for m ≥ 1; ℚ∞ for m = 0), F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p, and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F (hypothesis (H)). The general case of Theorem A.3 reduces to (H) as in [81, §13].
items.locator: Appendix A.1, Remark A.4(2) (printed p. 200, PDF 101)
items.note: Finite-level input is in Mathlib (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Cyclotomic/Ideal.lean): ncard_primesOver_of_prime_pow (l.136, exactly one prime of ℚ(ζ_{p^{k+1}}) over p) and ramificationIdxIn_eq_of_prime_pow (l.175, ramification index p^k(p−1) = degree). Together they give total ramification at every finite layer for F = ℚ(μ_{p^m}); the ⁺ case and the passage to the tower are not in the library. Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 opens 'For the one-prime, totally ramified tower treated in RJW' and requires the general reduction. Load-bearing: Proposition 13.15 is proved by 'See Proposition A.6' for the ⁺ tower.

items.name: Layer compatibility under (H): Y_{n+1} ↠ Y_n
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Hypothesis (H) of Remark A.4(2): F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F. Then F_{n+1} ∩ L_n = F_n, so Y_n = Gal(L_n/F_n) ≅ Gal(L_nF_{n+1}/F_{n+1}) = Y_{n+1}/Gal(L_{n+1}/L_nF_{n+1}); in particular restriction Y_{n+1} → Y_n is surjective. Y∞ carries the Λ(Γ)-action by conjugation (via lifts of Γ to Gal(L∞/F)), and under Λ(Γ) ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧ the element 1+T acts as γ₀.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, second paragraph (printed p. 200, PDF 101)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1: 'Relate finite layers and inverse limits, including the composita needed to identify their Galois groups ... Define the completed Galois action by conjugation and prove it is independent of a lift.' No packet node.

items.name: Inertia splitting G = I·Y∞ and the lift σ of γ₀
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Hypothesis (H) of Remark A.4(2): F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F. Let G := Gal(L∞/F), 𝔭̃ a prime of L∞ above 𝔭 and I ⊆ G its inertia group. Since L∞/F∞ is unramified, I ∩ Y∞ = 1; since F∞/F is totally ramified at 𝔭, restriction I → G/Y∞ ≅ Γ is bijective. Hence G = I·Y∞ = Γ·Y∞, a semidirect product Y∞ ⋊ I. Let σ ∈ I be the element mapping to γ₀; it acts on Y∞ by conjugation as γ₀.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, before Proposition A.5 (printed p. 201, PDF 102)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'prove the decomposition of the Galois group using inertia'. No packet node.

items.name: Proposition A.5: closed commutator subgroup G' = T·Y∞
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Hypothesis (H) of Remark A.4(2): F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F. With G = Gal(L∞/F) = I·Y∞ as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/497, the closure G' of the commutator subgroup of G equals (γ₀ − 1)·Y∞ = T·Y∞. Proof: for a = αx, b = βy (α, β ∈ Γ ≅ I, x, y ∈ Y∞) one has aba⁻¹b⁻¹ = (x^α)^{1−β}(y^β)^{α−1}, and 1 − β, α − 1 ∈ TΛ.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, Proposition A.5 (printed p. 201, PDF 102)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'compute its closed commutator subgroup'. I re-derived the commutator identity: expanding the four conjugates gives αxβyx⁻¹β⁻¹α⁻¹βy⁻¹β⁻¹, which equals aba⁻¹b⁻¹ because Γ (the lift I) is abelian; in additive notation this is (1−β)x^α + (α−1)y^β. No packet node.

items.name: Proposition A.6: Y_n ≅ Y∞/ω_nY∞ (control)
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Hypothesis (H) of Remark A.4(2): F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F. For every n ≥ 0, restriction induces an isomorphism of Λ-modules Y_n ≅ Y∞/ω_n(T)Y∞ = Y∞/((γ₀^{p^n} − 1)Y∞), i.e. Y_n is the module of Γ^{p^n}-coinvariants of Y∞. For n = 0 this is Y₀ = G/⟨G', I⟩ = Y∞/TY∞, because L₀ is the maximal abelian subextension of L∞/F unramified at 𝔭. For n ≥ 1 apply the n = 0 case to F_n, which again satisfies (H), with γ₀^{p^n} and σ^{p^n}.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, Proposition A.6 and proof (printed pp. 201–202, PDF 102–103); = Proposition 13.15 ([81, Proposition 13.22]), printed p. 194
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'prove Y_n ≃ Y_infty / ((gamma^(p^n)−1)Y_infty)'. The hypothesis (H) is necessary. In the cyclotomic ℤ₅-extension of ℚ(i), where both primes above 5 ramify, Y₀ = 0 but Y₁ ≠ 0 (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E92), so the formula fails there (it would force Y∞ = 0 by Lemma A.7). No packet node.

items.name: Lemma A.7: topological Nakayama lemma for compact Λ-modules
items.statement: Let Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ and Y a compact (Hausdorff) Λ-module. Then Y is finitely generated over Λ if and only if Y/(p,T)Y is finite. Moreover, if the images of x₁, …, x_m generate Y/(p,T)Y (over ℤ, equivalently over 𝔽_p), then x₁, …, x_m generate Y as a Λ-module (printed 'x₁, …, x_n', issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E93). In particular, Y/(p,T)Y = 0 implies Y = 0.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, Lemma A.7, citing [81, Lemma 13.16] (printed p. 202, PDF 103)
items.note: Packet node NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.0/compact-nakayama: 'Let J be a pro-p group, 𝔪_J the maximal ideal of Λ(J), and M a compact ... Λ(J)-module ... Then M is finitely generated over Λ(J) iff M/𝔪_J M is finite ... and M = 0 iff M/𝔪_J M = 0'. For J = Γ ≅ ℤ_p, 𝔪_J = (p, T). That node omits the generator-lifting clause, which is in stage PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L5 ('Include topological Nakayama, finite generation from finite residual quotient') and in IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 ('Prove compact Nakayama applies'). Mathlib's Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot (Mathlib/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean:118) needs N.FG, so it is not the compact version.

items.name: Proposition A.8: Y∞ is a finitely generated Λ-module
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Hypothesis (H) of Remark A.4(2): F has exactly one prime 𝔭 above p and 𝔭 is totally ramified in F∞/F. Then Y∞ is a finitely generated Λ-module. Proof: φ(T) = (1+T)^p − 1 ∈ (p, T), so Y∞/(p,T)Y∞ is a quotient of Y∞/φ(T)Y∞ ≅ Y₁ = Cl(F₁) ⊗ ℤ_p (Proposition A.6), which is finite; apply Lemma A.7.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.1, Proposition A.8 (printed p. 202, PDF 103)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Prove compact Nakayama applies and deduce finite generation and torsion.' No packet node.

items.name: Structure theorem applied to Y∞ (Theorem 13.1 over ℤ_p⟦T⟧)
items.statement: Let M be a finitely generated Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧-module. There is an exact sequence 0 → Q → M → 𝒜 → R → 0 with Q, R finite and 𝒜 = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^s Λ/(p^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^t Λ/(f_j(T)^{k_j}) for integers r, s, t ≥ 0, m_i, k_j ≥ 1 and distinguished (irreducible) polynomials f_j ∈ ℤ_p[T]. Applied to M = Y∞.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, first display (printed p. 202, PDF 103), invoking Theorem 13.1 (printed p. 189)
items.note: Packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-module-structure-theorem: 'Let M be a finitely generated module over Λ = O⟦T⟧. There are r ≥ 0, integers m_i ≥ 1, irreducible distinguished polynomials F_j ... and a homomorphism M → E = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_i Λ/(ϖ^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_j Λ/(F_j^{n_j}) with finite kernel and cokernel.' Here O = ℤ_p, so ϖ = p and lead PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E15 (the μ-part should use ϖ) does not affect Appendix A. The theorem itself belongs to the §13 chunk; it is listed here only because A.1.2 uses it. Planned Tau Ceti name TauCeti.Iwasawa.exists_pseudoIso_elementary does not exist at f790474 (no Iwasawa directory).

items.name: Lemma A.9: finite error between Y∞/ω_n and 𝒜/ω_n
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Let M be a finitely generated Λ-module and M → 𝒜 a homomorphism with finite kernel and cokernel onto an elementary module as in PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/502, such that M/ω_nM is finite for all n. Then there are c ∈ ℤ and n₀ with |M/ω_nM| = p^c·|𝒜/ω_n𝒜| for all n ≥ n₀. Applied to M = Y∞. The notes give only a sketch: compare 0 → ω_nM → M → M/ω_nM → 0 with the same sequence for 𝒜; the kernel and cokernel of the right vertical map stabilise for n large ([80, Lemma 13.21]).
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, Lemma A.9 (printed p. 203, PDF 104)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Establish finite-error stabilization under pseudo-isomorphisms'. The same step is inside the proof of packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-growth-formula: 'ν_n is injective on M/M₀ ... the second factor is eventually constant ... For N = M/M₀ ⊆ E (elementary, finite cokernel C), #N/ν_n = #E/ν_n by the snake lemma.' c may be negative; this is one reason ν is only an integer (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E90).

items.name: Weierstrass division in ℤ_p⟦T⟧ (quoted from [10, §5.2.1])
items.statement: Let g ∈ ℤ_p[T] be a distinguished polynomial of degree d (monic, all non-leading coefficients in pℤ_p). Every f ∈ ℤ_p⟦T⟧ can be written uniquely as f = q·g + r with q ∈ ℤ_p⟦T⟧ and r ∈ ℤ_p[T] of degree < d. Equivalently ℤ_p[T]/(g) → ℤ_p⟦T⟧/(g) is an isomorphism, and ℤ_p⟦T⟧/(g) is ℤ_p-free with basis 1, T, …, T^{d−1}. (Weierstrass preparation: every f whose reduction mod p is nonzero is a distinguished polynomial times a unit.)
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, proof of Proposition A.10, Step 1 (printed p. 203, PDF 104); used again in Step 3 (printed p. 205)
items.note: Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean: exists_isWeierstrassDivision (l.504) '[IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A] (hg : g.map (IsLocalRing.residue A) ≠ 0) : ∃ q r, f.IsWeierstrassDivision g q r' (r of degree < the order of g mod 𝔪); IsWeierstrassDivision.unique (l.594); Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt.algEquivQuotient (l.458) '(A[X] ⧸ Ideal.span {g}) ≃ₐ[A] A⟦X⟧ ⧸ Ideal.span {(g : A⟦X⟧)}' for g.IsDistinguishedAt I with [IsAdicComplete I A]; exists_isWeierstrassFactorization (l.813). Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Eisenstein/Distinguished.lean:31) is 'monic and IsWeaklyEisensteinAt I'. AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdjoinRoot.lean:667) gives the basis for monic g. This is the same statement, over any complete local A. Packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/weierstrass-adapter records the match.

items.name: (A-1): Λ/(ω_n) and Λ/(p^k, ω_n); Λ/(g) for distinguished g
items.statement: Let ω_n = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 = T^{p^n} + Σ_{k=1}^{p^n−1} C(p^n,k)T^k. (i) ω_n is a distinguished polynomial of degree p^n. (ii) Λ/(ω_n) ≅ {r ∈ ℤ_p[T] : deg r ≤ p^n − 1} ≅ ℤ_p^{p^n} as ℤ_p-modules; in particular it is infinite. (iii) For k ≥ 0, Λ/(p^k, ω_n) ≅ (ℤ/p^k)^{p^n}, so |Λ/(p^k, ω_n)| = p^{kp^n}. (iv) If g is distinguished of degree d, then V = Λ/(g) ≅ ℤ_p^d, p is injective on V, and |V/pV| = |Λ/(p, T^d)| = p^d.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, proof of Proposition A.10, Steps 1–3, display (A-1) (printed pp. 203–205, PDF 104–106)
items.note: (ii)–(iv) are the general Mathlib statements of PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/504 specialised to g = ω_n resp. g. (i) (ω_n distinguished) is not in the library. It is packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/cyclotomic-weierstrass-polynomials ('ω_n and ξ_n are distinguished polynomials over O (ω_n ≡ T^{p^n} ... mod p)', planned declaration TauCeti.Iwasawa.omega_isDistinguishedAt, absent at f790474). Status is planned because (i) is missing from the library. (ii)–(iv) follow directly from the cited Mathlib statements once (i) is known.

items.name: Proposition A.10: orders of 𝒜/ω_n𝒜 for an elementary module
items.statement: Let 𝒜 = Λ^r ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^s Λ/(p^{m_i}) ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^t Λ/(f_j(T)^{k_j}) with r, s, t ≥ 0, m_i, k_j ≥ 1 and f_j ∈ ℤ_p[T] distinguished; put m = Σ_i m_i and ℓ = Σ_j k_j deg f_j. Suppose 𝒜/ω_n𝒜 is finite for all n ≥ 0. Then r = 0 and there are n₀ and c ∈ ℤ with |𝒜/ω_n𝒜| = p^{mp^n + ℓn + c} for all n ≥ n₀. Sub-steps: |(⊕Λ/(p^{m_i}))/ω_n| = p^{mp^n} for all n; for g distinguished of degree d with V/ω_nV finite for all n and V = Λ/(g), |V/ω_nV| = p^{nd + c_g} for n > n₀(g), where p^{n₀(g)} ≥ d.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, Proposition A.10 and proof (printed pp. 203–206, PDF 104–107)
items.note: Packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-growth-formula proves the torsion-module version (NSW 5.3.17: '#(M/(ω_n/ω_{n₀})M) = p^{μp^n + λn + ν}', with the step '#(Λ/p^m)/ν_n = p^{m(p^n − p^{n₀})}; for E_j = Λ/F_j^{n_j}, Lemma 5.3.18 gives #E_j/ν_{n+1} = p^{n_j deg F_j}·#E_j/ν_n for n ≫ 0'). The deduction r = 0 from finiteness is not in that node. It is covered by IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'compute the coinvariant orders for the elementary modules'. Misprints in the Step 3 computation: issues PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E95, PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E97.

items.name: Lemma A.11: ω_{n+1}V = pω_nV on V = Λ/(g)
items.statement: Let g ∈ ℤ_p[T] be distinguished of degree d, V = Λ/(g), and n₀ with p^{n₀} ≥ d. Then for every n > n₀, ω_{n+1}(T)·V = p·ω_n(T)·V. More precisely, for n > n₀, ω_{n+1} ≡ p·ω_n·u (mod g) with u ≡ 1 (mod p) a unit of Λ (for p odd this already holds for n = n₀; the lemma holds for p = 2 as well, see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E96).
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, Lemma A.11 and proof (printed pp. 204–205, PDF 105–106), display (A-2)
items.note: No node states this lemma. The nearest is NSW Lemma 5.3.18 inside packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-growth-formula: 'if M is free of rank λ over ℤ_p, then (ω_{n+1}/ω_n)M = pM for n > λ(λ − 1)/2'. Applied to M = V (free of rank d) it gives the same conclusion with a different threshold. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 ('compute the coinvariant orders for the elementary modules') covers it by stage description. I checked the proof: the intermediate claim 'φ^{k+1}(T) ≡ pφ^k(T) (mod g)' is false as written (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E96), and (A-2) has misprints (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E95). The lemma itself is true; for p odd the first-stage expansion already gives the unit form, because Σ_{i<p} i ≡ 0 (mod p).

items.name: Corollary A.12: finite ω_n-coinvariants imply torsion
items.statement: Let Y be a finitely generated Λ-module such that Y/ω_n(T)Y is finite for all n (one n suffices). Then Y is a torsion Λ-module. Proof: by the structure theorem Y → 𝒜 has finite kernel and cokernel, 𝒜/ω_n𝒜 is then finite, so r = 0 by Proposition A.10 Step 1 and 𝒜 is killed by its characteristic ideal.
items.locator: Appendix A.1.2, Corollary A.12 (printed p. 206, PDF 107)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'deduce finite generation and torsion'. Packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/finite-coinvariants-euler-characteristic assumes torsion rather than deducing it; the deduction needs the structure-theorem node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/iwasawa-module-structure-theorem plus (A-1)(ii).

items.name: p-torsion A[p] and p-rank rk_p(A) of a finite abelian group
items.statement: For a finite abelian group A: A[p] := {x ∈ A : px = 0}, and rk_p(A) := dim_{𝔽_p}(A/pA) = dim_{𝔽_p}(A[p]). Equivalently, it is the number of cyclic summands of p-power order in the decomposition of A into cyclic groups of prime-power order.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, before Corollary A.13 (printed p. 206, PDF 107)
items.note: The decomposition input is in Mathlib: AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite (Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Basic.lean:135): '∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Fintype ι) (p : ι → ℕ) (_ : ∀ i, Nat.Prime <| p i) (e : ι → ℕ), Nonempty <| G ≃+ ⨁ i : ι, ZMod (p i ^ e i)'. No named p-rank and no proof of dim A/pA = dim A[p] were found (grep 'pRank|p_rank|prank' in Mathlib hits only unrelated files; nothing in Tau Ceti). Stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 plans 'the bounded-p-rank characterization of mu=0', which uses this notion.

items.name: Corollary A.13: μ = 0 ⇔ bounded p-rank of Cl(F_n)
items.statement: Standing notation of Appendix A.1: F a number field, p a prime (Part II fixes p odd, §9), F∞/F a ℤ_p-extension, Γ = Γ_F = Gal(F∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p, γ₀ a topological generator of Γ, Λ = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Λ(Γ) via γ₀ ↦ 1+T, ω_n := φ^n(T) = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 (φ⁰(T) = T). Then μ = 0 if and only if rk_p(Cl(F_n)) is bounded independently of n. (Proved in the notes under (H), using Y_n = Y∞/ω_nY∞, an exact sequence 0 → C_n → Y_n → 𝒜_n → B_n → 0 with |B_n|, |C_n| bounded, and dim_{𝔽_p} 𝒜/(p, ω_n)𝒜 = s·p^n + g for n large, where g = Σ_j deg g_j; μ = 0 ⇔ s = 0.)
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Corollary A.13 and proof (printed pp. 206–207, PDF 107–108)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2: 'Prove the bounded-p-rank characterization of mu=0.' No packet node. Misprints in the proof (exponent s·p^n + t·g, 'O_L[T]', the reference to the proof of Proposition A.10): issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E98. The reduction from bounded group orders to bounded p-ranks uses subadditivity of rk_p in short exact sequences of finite p-groups, which the text leaves implicit.

items.name: Theorem A.14 (Ferrero–Washington)
items.statement: Let F be an abelian number field (finite abelian over ℚ), p any prime, and F∞/F the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension. Then the Iwasawa invariant μ(F∞/F) = 0.
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Theorem A.14, citing [81, §7.5] (printed p. 207, PDF 108)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4: 'Prove the Ferrero–Washington theorem for cyclotomic Z_p-extensions of abelian number fields, including p=2, following the primary proof or Washington §7.5 ... Separate the analytic vanishing of the relevant p-adic L-function mu-invariant from the arithmetic class-group mu-invariant ... **Acceptance:** ... Theorem A.14'. EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L4 consumes it ('Use the independent Ferrero–Washington input'). No packet node.

items.name: Conjecture A.15 (Greenberg)
items.statement: Conjecture (Greenberg [35]). For every totally real number field F and every ℤ_p-extension F∞/F, μ(F∞/F) = λ(F∞/F) = 0; equivalently (by Theorem A.3), the p-parts #(Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p) = p^{e_n} are bounded as n → ∞. (Corrected: the text's 'in other words, the values #Cl(F_n) are bounded' replaces the p-part by the full class number; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E91. Greenberg's paper states the conjecture for the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension, which under Leopoldt's conjecture is the only one.)
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Conjecture A.15 (printed p. 207, PDF 108)
items.note: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L4: 'State Greenberg's Conjecture A.15 on the defined invariants. The equivalence with bounded **p-primary** class-group orders is the formal statement; do not replace it by bounded full class numbers ... a correctly typed statement, not a proof, of A.15.' ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5: 'This package does not claim to prove Greenberg's totally-real mu=lambda=0 conjecture'. Planned as a statement only.

items.name: The three GL(1) p-adic zeta functions ζ_p^an, ζ_p^arith, ζ_p^alg
items.statement: p odd, Γ⁺ := Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})⁺/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^×/{±1}, Λ(Γ⁺) its Iwasawa algebra with total ring of fractions Q(Γ⁺). (1) ζ_p^an ∈ Q(Γ⁺) is the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure of Part I, interpolating special values of the Riemann zeta function. (2) ζ_p^arith is the image under the Coleman map Col of the norm-compatible family of cyclotomic units (§10). (3) ζ_p^alg := Char_{Λ(Γ⁺)}(𝒳∞⁺) ⊂ Λ(Γ⁺), the characteristic ideal of the torsion Λ(Γ⁺)-module 𝒳∞⁺ of §13.
items.note: Recap of Parts I–II (earlier chunks). ζ_p^an: DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1 ('The smoothed measure and Kubota–Leopoldt'). ζ_p^arith: ColemanPowerSeries:L2 ('The Coleman map and its sign') and L4 (acceptance 'Theorems 10.2/10.13/10.15 (with recorded sign comparison)'). ζ_p^alg: characteristic ideal from packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal applied to 𝒳∞⁺, as in EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3. The name 'ζ_p^alg' is new in B.1.

items.name: Theorem 10.15 recalled: ζ_p^an = ζ_p^arith
items.statement: The Coleman-map image of the cyclotomic units equals the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure: ζ_p^an = ζ_p^arith (Theorem 10.15), up to the sign convention for Col (see note).
items.locator: Appendix B.1, after item (3) (printed p. 208, PDF 109), recalling Theorem 10.15 (printed p. 170)
items.note: ColemanPowerSeries:L2: 'Define Col=−Col_0 if a positive explicit reciprocity identity is desired ... The source's Theorem 10.15 has the opposite sign from its preceding definitions'. Lead ColemanPowerSeries/E1 (Theorem 10.15 sign) belongs to the §10 chunk, and B.1 inherits it: with the §10 definitions as printed, Col(c(a)) = −θ_a ζ_p.

items.name: Iwasawa Main Conjecture recalled: ζ_p^alg = I(Γ⁺)ζ_p^an
items.statement: p odd. 𝒳∞⁺ is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ⁺)-module and Char_{Λ(Γ⁺)}(𝒳∞⁺) = I(Γ⁺)·ζ_p^an, where I(Γ⁺) is the augmentation ideal (Theorem 13.8; Mazur–Wiles; proved in the notes for Vandiver primes).
items.locator: Appendix B.1, last sentence (printed p. 208, PDF 109), recalling Theorem 13.8 (printed p. 192)
items.note: Packet node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/cyclotomic-main-conjecture ('The Iwasawa main conjecture over ℚ for odd p (RJW Theorem 13.8; Rubin Theorem III.2.10)'); stage EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3: 'char_(Z_p[[G^+]])(X_infty^+) = I(G^+) zeta_p for every **odd** prime p. This is the unconditional Theorem 13.8'. Vandiver case: IntegralIwasawaTheory:L3.

items.name: Deligne's critical integers (footnote 16)
items.statement: For a motive M with L-function L(M,s) and archimedean Euler factor L∞(M,s), an integer j is critical for L(M,s) if neither L∞(M,s) nor L∞(M^∨,1−s) has a pole at s = j, where M^∨ is the dual motive. (Corrected: the footnote prints L∞(M,1−s); see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E99.)
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, footnote 16, citing Deligne [29, Definition 1.3] (printed p. 208, PDF 109)
items.note: PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1: 'Define completed motivic L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data in admitted cases and derive critical integers from archimedean factors ... Check that criticality is a simultaneous regularity condition for the relevant infinity factors.' SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4: 'Define the Hodge/gamma-factor notion of criticality on explicit realization data'. No packet node.

items.name: Critical integers of ζ(s) and of Dirichlet L-functions
items.statement: L∞(ℚ(0),s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) has poles exactly at s = 0, −2, −4, …; hence the critical integers of ζ(s) are the negative odd integers and the positive even integers. More generally, the Kubota–Leopoldt values L(χ,−k) with k ≥ 0 and χ(−1)(−1)^k = −1 are critical values.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, first paragraph and footnote 16 (printed p. 208, PDF 109)
items.note: PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1: 'Prove the Dirichlet/Tate and separately sourced modular-form cases'. The footnote's 'poles at negative even integers' should read non-positive even integers (issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E100). Mathlib has Γ and ζ, but no notion of criticality.

items.name: Critical values of L(f,s)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). The critical values of L(f,s) in Deligne's sense are L(f,χ,j+1) for χ any Dirichlet character and 0 ≤ j ≤ k (for trivial nebentypus, L∞(f,s) = Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s) and the functional equation relates s to k+2−s, so the critical strip is 1 ≤ s ≤ k+1).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, first paragraph (printed p. 208, PDF 109)
items.note: Partial. Packet node ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L1/critical-value-algebraicity cites this sentence ('Appendix B.2.1, p. 79', arXiv v2) only for 'The range 0 ≤ j ≤ k of critical values'. Its statement is the algebraicity of τ(χ)·j!/(−2πi)^j·L(f,χ̄,j+1)/Ω_f^ε for 0 ≤ j ≤ k, not the Deligne-criticality computation. That computation is PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.1 ('Prove the ... modular-form cases').

items.name: Theorem B.1 (Amice–Vélu, Višik; Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer): analytic p-adic L-function of f
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). If v_p(α_p) < k+1, there is a unique L_p^an(f) ∈ D^la(ℤ_p^×) such that (a) L_p^an(f) has growth of order v_p(α_p) (is v_p(α_p)-admissible), and (b) for every Dirichlet character χ of conductor p^n (n ≥ 0) and every 0 ≤ j ≤ k, L_p^an(f, χ̄, j+1) := ∫_{ℤ_p^×} χ(x)x^j · L_p^an(f) = −α_p^{−n}·(1 − χ(p)p^j/α_p)·G(χ)·j!·p^{nj}/(2πi)^{j+1} · L(f, χ̄, j+1)/Ω_f^±. (The Euler factor 1 − χ(p)p^j/α_p is 1 unless n = 0.)
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, Theorem B.1 (printed p. 208, PDF 109); formula read on the rendered page (the text layer drops the bars on χ̄)
items.note: Packet nodes: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/p-adic-l-function (the construction for slope h < k+1) and L2/interpolation-and-uniqueness ('This is RJW Theorem B.1 with Ω_{B.1}^± = −Ω^±/(2πi), a j-independent conversion. Moreover, L_p(f, α; φ^±) is the unique h-admissible distribution on ℤ_p^× with these values, because h < k + 1'). L1/rjw-b1-comparison checks B.1 against the period dictionary and confirms the printed formula with χ̄ on both sides ('B.1 as printed therefore agrees with the dictionary and needs no source correction'). Uniqueness is LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/amice-velu-vishik ('two distributions of order r that agree on locally polynomial functions of degree ≤ N coincide when ... r < N + 1'). Those nodes work with refinements (f, α) of a newform and Γ₁(N)-level; RJW's f of level Γ₀(N), p | N, is already the refined form (L1/p-stabilised-euler-factors). The TeX (v2) is identical.

items.name: Ordinary case: L_p^an(f) is a measure
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). If f is p-ordinary (v_p(α_p) = 0), a distribution of growth order 0 is a bounded measure, so L_p^an(f) lies in the space of p-adic measures on ℤ_p^× (Λ(ℤ_p^×) ⊗ ℚ_p; integral for a suitably normalised period).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, paragraph after Theorem B.1 (printed p. 208, PDF 109); used again in B.2.3 (printed p. 210)
items.note: LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L2/order-zero-measures: 'D₀(ℤ_p, L) = C⁰(ℤ_p, L)′ is the space of bounded measures'. ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/ordinary-integral-measure: 'Let (f, α) have slope 0 ... Then L_p(f, α; φ^±) is a measure with values in 𝒪 ... Boundedness alone ... gives only an element of 𝒪⟦ℤ_p^×⟧[1/p]'.

items.name: Slope bound: α_p ≠ 0 ⇒ v_p(α_p) ≤ k+1
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). If α_p ≠ 0 then 0 ≤ v_p(α_p) ≤ k+1. Theorem B.1 excludes the critical-slope case v_p(α_p) = k+1.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, paragraph after Theorem B.1 (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: Packet node ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L2/refinement: 'α is an algebraic integer, so h ≥ 0. When p ∤ N, αβ = ε(p)p^{k+1} with β integral gives v_p(α) + v_p(β) = k + 1, so 0 ≤ h ≤ k + 1'; for p | N with a_p ≠ 0 it records slope k/2 when p ‖ N. Together these cover RJW's f (p-stabilised, or p-new).

items.name: Critical-slope p-adic L-functions (Pollack–Stevens [68], Bellaïche [4])
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). If v_p(α_p) = k+1 (critical slope), there is still a p-adic L-function L_p(f) ∈ D^la(ℤ_p^×) of growth order k+1. When the refinement is not θ-critical it is the Pollack–Stevens function (from the unique overconvergent eigen-lift) and satisfies the interpolation formula of Theorem B.1, but interpolation no longer characterises it. When the refinement is θ-critical, Bellaïche's function (through the eigencurve) vanishes at all classical characters and the classical interpolation is carried by a secondary L-function. The text says only that 'the statement is slightly different'.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.1, paragraph after Theorem B.1 (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L3/non-theta-critical-lift ('Let (f, α) be a refinement of critical slope h = k + 1 ... not θ-critical ... L_p(f, α; φ^±) ... is (k + 1)-admissible'), L3/critical-slope-interpolation, L3/critical-slope-non-uniqueness ('Interpolation does not determine critical-slope L-functions'), L3/theta-critical-comparison. Stage PadicFamilies:L3: 'Prove the Pollack–Stevens non-theta-critical and Bellaïche critical-point results'. The text states no precise theorem.

items.name: The Galois representation V_f and a lattice T_f (Deligne)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). Attached to f is a 2-dimensional p-adic Galois representation V_f of G_ℚ over a finite extension of ℚ_p, constructed by Deligne in the étale cohomology of the modular curve (with coefficients in Sym^k of the universal Tate module, equivalently in a Kuga–Sato variety). It is unramified outside Np, with the Eichler–Shimura characteristic polynomial of Frobenius at ℓ ∤ Np. T_f ⊂ V_f is a chosen G_ℚ-stable lattice.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, first paragraph (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.1: 'Construct the weight-two representation from Jacobian cohomology and the higher-weight representation from symmetric-power cohomology or Kuga–Sato varieties. Prove the existence of the required projector and the two-dimensional eigenspace, including coefficient fields and integral lattices. Prove the unramified characteristic polynomial by the geometric Eichler–Shimura relation.' Nothing in Tau Ceti or Mathlib.

items.name: Theorem B.2 (Kato): Kato's Euler system z_Kato(f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). There exists an Euler system z_Kato(f) attached to T_f (up to Tate twist / dual normalisation): a family of classes z_m ∈ H¹(ℤ[ζ_m, 1/p], T) indexed by m in a set S of moduli, compatible under corestriction by the Euler factors P_ℓ(ℓ^{−1}σ_ℓ^{−1}) at the added primes ℓ.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, Theorem B.2, citing Kato [47] (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: Packet node KatoEulerSystems:L2/euler-system-datum-for-the-modular-lattice: 'Then (z_m)_{m in S} is an Euler system for (T,F_lambda,Sigma) in the sense of 13.1: for m | m' in S the corestriction ... sends z_{m'} to the product over primes ell dividing m' but not m of P_ell(ell^{-1} sigma_ell^{-1}) applied to z_m', with T = V_{O_λ}(f)(k−r). Also L2/p-adic-zeta-elements-and-their-norm-relations. Stage KatoEulerSystems:L2: 'The notation z_Kato(f) denotes this constructed object, not an unspecified Euler system whose existence was assumed.' Kato's lattice is a Tate twist of V_{O_λ}(f); RJW's 'attached to T_f' suppresses the twist.

items.name: Localisation z_Kato(f) ∈ H¹_Iw(ℚ_p, V_f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). Restricting the p-power part (z_{p^n})_n of Kato's Euler system to the decomposition group at p and taking the inverse limit over ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}) under corestriction gives a class z_Kato(f) ∈ H¹_Iw(ℚ_p, V_f) := (lim_n H¹(ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}), T_f)) ⊗ ℚ_p (in the appropriate twist/dual of V_f).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, display after Theorem B.2 (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: KatoEulerSystems:L3: 'Localize at p, apply R09's vector regulator, and project ... The primary normalization may use V_f^*(1) rather than V_f. Prove that dictionary'. Local Iwasawa cohomology: PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology:PG.5 ('Deduce H¹_Iw ≅ D(T)^(ψ=1) ... For rational coefficients specify H¹_Iw(K,T)⊗Q_p').

items.name: Perrin-Riou's big logarithm Log_{V_f}
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). For a crystalline representation V of G_{ℚ_p} there is Perrin-Riou's big logarithm L_V : H¹_Iw(ℚ_p, V) → ℋ(G) ⊗ D_cris(V), with G = Gal(ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ_p) ≅ ℤ_p^× and ℋ(G) the algebra of locally analytic distributions; it interpolates Bloch–Kato (dual) exponentials at finite-order characters and integral twists. The text uses the scalar version Log_{V_f} : H¹_Iw(ℚ_p, V_f) → D^la(ℤ_p^×), obtained by pairing with a φ-eigenvector of D_cris(V_f) attached to α_p (the §10.5 'yoga').
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, display after Theorem B.2 (printed p. 209, PDF 110); cf. §10.5
items.note: PadicHodgeRegulators:L3: 'For crystalline V construct L_V : H^1_Iw(Q_p,V) → H(G) tensor_K D_cris(V) ... prove the interpolation at every finite-order character and integral twist ... For general V a scalar projection is an additional defined map; it is not canonical from V alone.' The packet nodes under PadicHodgeRegulators:L3 are only Euler-operator lemmas (quadratic-euler-inverse, …). V_f is crystalline at p only when f is p-old; for p-new f the text's Log_{V_f} needs a semistable variant, which is not planned.

items.name: Arithmetic p-adic L-function L_p^arith(f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). L_p^arith(f) := Log_{V_f}(z_Kato(f)) ∈ D^la(ℤ_p^×), the image of the localised Kato class under Perrin-Riou's big logarithm (scalar, α_p-projected version).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, display after Theorem B.2 (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: KatoEulerSystems:L3: 'The endpoint is the properly normalized version of L_p^an(f,alpha) = projection_alpha(L_(V_f)(loc_p z_Kato(f)))' — the right-hand side is L_p^arith(f).

items.name: Theorem B.3 (Kato's explicit reciprocity law): L_p^an(f) = L_p^arith(f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). Suppose v_p(α_p) < k+1, so that L_p^an(f) of Theorem B.1 is defined. Then L_p^an(f) = L_p^arith(f) in D^la(ℤ_p^×), with compatible normalisations of periods, of the lattice/twist and of the eigenvector used to project Log_{V_f}.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.2, Theorem B.3 (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: Stage KatoEulerSystems:L3 plans exactly this endpoint ('For noncritical finite slope, prove equality with R10's analytic distribution by the exact interpolation and growth uniqueness theorem ... The endpoint is ... L_p^an(f,alpha) = projection_alpha(L_(V_f)(loc_p z_Kato(f)))'). Packet nodes supply the finite-level inputs: KatoEulerSystems:L3/generalised-explicit-reciprocity-law-for-zeta-elements (Kato Thm. 9.5) and L3/zeta-class-interpolation-of-complex-L-values (Kato Thm. 12.5: the L-value in Kato's formula is L_{{p}}(f^*, χ, r), 'of the DUAL form f^*, not of f'). No node yet states the distribution-level equality.

items.name: p-ordinary f ⇒ V_f is p-ordinary (Definition 13.19)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). If f is p-ordinary (v_p(α_p) = 0), then V_f|_{G_{ℚ_p}} has a G_{ℚ_p}-stable filtration 0 ⊂ V' ⊂ V_f with V_f/V' unramified (Frobenius acting through the unit root α_p) and inertia acting on V' by χ_cyc^{k+1} (up to finite order); in particular V_f is p-ordinary in the sense of Definition 13.19 (Greenberg).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.3, first paragraph (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: Packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility takes as hypothesis Kato Prop. 17.1: 'p does not divide N and a_p is a unit ... equivalently V_{F_lambda}(f) is crystalline at p and contains a unique one-dimensional Gal(Qbar_p/Q_p)-stable subspace V'_{F_lambda}(f) which is unramified' (that is Kato's normalisation, the dual of RJW's). Only p ∤ N is covered there. The p | N level of B.2 (p-stabilised or p-new) is covered by stage PadicFamilies:L4 ('Prove the local ordinary filtration, saturation and arithmetic specialization') and ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0 ('the selected saturated local submodule'). SelmerIwasawaCohomology lead E2 (Definition 13.19(1)) concerns the §13 chunk.

items.name: Greenberg Selmer group of f over ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) and its dual X_{p^∞}(V_f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). Assume f p-ordinary; let Γ := Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^× and Λ = Λ(Γ) = Λ(ℤ_p^×). With W_f := V_f/T_f and Greenberg's local condition at p (Definition 13.19(1)) and unramified conditions away from p, the Selmer group is H¹_{L_Gr}(ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), W_f), a discrete Λ-module. X_{p^∞}(V_f) := Hom_cts(H¹_{L_Gr}(ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), W_f), ℚ_p/ℤ_p) is its Pontryagin dual, a compact finitely generated Λ-module. (Corrected: the text writes 'a Selmer group H¹(ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), V_f)' and uses X_{p^∞}(V_f) without defining it; see issue PAPER-RODRIGUES-JACINTO-WILLIAMS-23/E102.)
items.locator: Appendix B.2.3, first paragraph (printed pp. 209–210, PDF 110–111)
items.note: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0: 'Define the ordinary Greenberg Selmer group using the selected saturated local submodule and unramified conditions away from p. Its dual X is compact, with the contragredient Iwasawa action. Prove finite generation and torsion under the hypotheses of the relevant theorem; neither is part of the definition of X.' Local condition: packet node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2/greenberg-condition. KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility defines Kato's X(T) = Hom(Sel_∞(T), F_λ/O_λ) the same way.

items.name: Kato: X_{p^∞}(V_f) is Λ-torsion
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). For p-ordinary f, the dual Selmer group X_{p^∞}(V_f) over ℚ(μ_{p^∞}) is a finitely generated torsion Λ(ℤ_p^×)-module (Kato [47]; the text gives no hypotheses — Kato's Theorem 17.4(1) is stated for good ordinary reduction, p ∤ N).
items.locator: Appendix B.2.3, first paragraph (printed p. 209, PDF 110)
items.note: Packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility: 'Then (Thm. 17.4): (1) X(T) is a torsion Lambda-module', under 'good ordinary reduction at lambda in the precise sense of Prop. 17.1: p does not divide N AND a_p is a lambda-adic unit'. RJW's p | N setting is covered only after passing to the level-prime-to-p newform (p-stabilised case); the p-new ordinary case (e.g. multiplicative reduction) is not in that node.

items.name: Algebraic p-adic L-function L_p^alg(f)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). For p-ordinary f, L_p^alg(f) := ch_{Λ(ℤ_p^×)}(X_{p^∞}(V_f)) ⊂ Λ(ℤ_p^×), the characteristic ideal of the torsion module X_{p^∞}(V_f), computed componentwise over the characters of μ_{p−1} since Λ(ℤ_p^×) ≅ ⊕_{μ_{p−1}^∨} ℤ_p⟦T⟧.
items.note: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L0: 'State the ordinary integral equality char_Lambda X = (L_p(f,alpha))'. Characteristic ideals: packet node PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/characteristic-ideal, plus the isotypic decomposition L4/character-decomposition for Λ(H × ℤ_p) with #H prime to p.

items.name: Theorem B.4: Iwasawa Main Conjecture for f (Kato; Skinner–Urban)
items.statement: Standing data of B.2: p an odd prime; f a cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k+2 (k ≥ 0) and level Γ₀(N) with p | N; α_p its U_p-eigenvalue; L(f,s) and its twists L(f,χ,s) by Dirichlet characters χ; Ω_f^± complex periods (sign ± = χ(−1)(−1)^j); G(χ) the Gauss sum; D^la(ℤ_p^×) the locally analytic distributions (§3.7). Let f be p-ordinary, so that L_p^an(f) ∈ Λ(ℤ_p^×) ⊗ ℚ_p is a measure. Under 'some mild additional technical hypotheses' (not specified in the text; stage ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1 records them, after Fouquet–Wan Theorem 1.6, as: trivial nebentypus, p ∤ N for the newform, absolutely irreducible residual representation, a prime ℓ ‖ N with dim(V̄_f)^{I_ℓ} = 1 and dim(V̄_f)^{G_{ℚ_ℓ}} = 0, an ordinary filtration at p with distinct residual characters, and the standing odd-prime/coefficient conditions), L_p^alg(f) = (L_p^an(f)) as ideals of Λ(ℤ_p^×). Kato proves that L_p^alg(f) divides (L_p^an(f)), i.e. (L_p^an(f)) ⊆ L_p^alg(f) (integrally only under extra hypotheses); Skinner–Urban prove the reverse divisibility.
items.locator: Appendix B.2.3, Theorem B.4, citing [47; 77] (printed p. 210, PDF 111)
items.note: ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L1 ('Ordinary theorem with explicit ramification hypotheses (T1)'): 'Let f be a normalized cuspidal eigenform of weight w≥2 on Gamma0(N), with trivial nebentypus and p not dividing N ... absolute irreducibility of the residual representation, and a prime ell exactly dividing N such that dim(bar V_f)^(I_ell) = 1 ... R12 gives one divisibility and R15.L1–L2 ... gives the opposite divisibility'. Kato's divisibility: packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility (length inequality at height-one primes not containing p; all primes under (12.5.2), p ≠ 2 and good ω, γ). Skinner–Urban: stage AutomorphicCongruences:L1 ('The Skinner–Urban automorphic argument'). The later weakenings the text mentions ([32] Fouquet–Wan) are ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L2.

items.name: Coates–Perrin-Riou / Panchishkin conjecture (existence of L_p^an(V))
items.statement: Conjecture. Let V be a p-adic Galois representation arising from a motive M over ℚ, corresponding (conjecturally) to an automorphic representation π. Under suitable hypotheses at p (Panchishkin/ordinary condition) there should exist a locally analytic p-adic distribution L_p^an(V) on ℤ_p^× interpolating the critical values L(V⊗χ, j) (χ of p-power conductor, j critical), each multiplied by explicit p-adic multipliers and divided by Deligne periods. The text gives no precise formulation, referring to [14; 15; 66].
items.locator: Appendix B.3, item (1) (printed p. 210, PDF 111); also §13.5.3 (printed p. 198)
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5: 'State the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence problem using a specified realization, critical set, periods, refinement/Panchishkin subspace and interpolation formula. Do not add a constructor asserting the conjecture.' ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5: 'Define the Greenberg and Coates–Perrin-Riou conjectural generalizations from RJW as mathematical propositions with all their inputs.' Planned as a statement only.

items.name: Known analytic p-adic L-functions for unitary groups (EHLS [31])
items.statement: For ordinary cuspidal automorphic representations of unitary groups, p-adic L-functions are constructed by Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner [31] via the doubling method (as a survey claim; the text states no theorem).
items.locator: Appendix B.3, item (1), paragraph after the bullets (printed p. 211, PDF 112)
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4: 'Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method ... Prove EHLS Main Theorem 9.2.2 with its stated anti-holomorphic cuspidal ordinary representation, tame type, coefficient modules and chosen bases. Keep Hypothesis 7.3.2 ..., 7.3.3 ... and Proposition–Hypothesis 7.3.5 ... visible.'

items.name: Euler systems (in the sense of Rubin [70])
items.statement: For a p-adic representation T of G_ℚ (finitely generated over the ring of integers 𝒪 of a finite extension of ℚ_p) and a finite set Σ of primes containing p and the ramified primes, an Euler system is a family of classes c_m ∈ H¹(ℚ(μ_m), T) (m running over a set of moduli) such that for m | m', cor_{ℚ(μ_{m'})/ℚ(μ_m)}(c_{m'}) = ∏_{ℓ | m', ℓ ∤ m} P_ℓ(Fr_ℓ^{−1})·c_m, where P_ℓ is the Euler polynomial at ℓ (a characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on the Tate dual of T, in Rubin's normalisation; Kato's modular datum uses P_ℓ(ℓ^{−1}σ_ℓ^{−1})).
items.locator: Appendix B.3, item (2) (printed p. 211, PDF 112); cf. §10.5
items.note: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.2 ('Euler-system modules and norm relations'). EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0: 'Import ES.2's actual Euler-system carrier ... prove its dictionary with Rubin's Tate-dual Euler-polynomial and arithmetic-Frobenius convention.' The text does not define the notion. The statement above is the standard shape of Rubin's definition, recorded for the integrator; I did not check the exact Frobenius/twist convention against Rubin's book.

items.name: Known Euler systems (planned cases): cyclotomic units, Kato, Heegner points, Beilinson–Flach / Rankin–Eisenstein
items.statement: Euler systems exist for: the cyclotomic units (T = ℤ_p(1) twisted by Dirichlet characters); Kato's zeta elements for modular forms (Theorem B.2); the Heegner point system, related to but not literally an Euler system in Rubin's sense (anticyclotomic); and Rankin–Eisenstein/Beilinson–Flach classes for products of two modular forms (Lei–Loeffler–Zerbes [53]).
items.note: Cyclotomic: packet node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L0/cyclotomic-euler-system. Kato: KatoEulerSystems:L2/euler-system-datum-for-the-modular-lattice. Heegner: stage HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.2 ('Geometric norm and reduction-congruence relations'). Beilinson–Flach: AutomorphicCongruences:L2 ('Construct the Rankin–Eisenstein/Beilinson–Flach classes used in FW §4.4 from products of modular curves ... prove the tame and p-power norm relations'). The last covers only the case FW use.

items.name: Explicit reciprocity laws beyond Kato: Rankin–Selberg (KLZ [49])
items.statement: For the Rankin–Eisenstein (Beilinson–Flach) Euler system of a pair of modular forms, the image under the Perrin-Riou logarithm equals the analytic Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function (Kings–Loeffler–Zerbes [49]); summarised with the triple-product case in [55, §B].
items.locator: Appendix B.3, item (2), second paragraph (printed p. 211, PDF 112)
items.note: Partial: AutomorphicCongruences:L2 requires 'explicit reciprocity with Rankin–Selberg L-values' for the Beilinson–Flach classes used by Fouquet–Wan; PadicHodgeRegulators:L4 (mentions Loeffler–Zerbes) plans the vector-regulator coordinates. There is no general KLZ node.

items.name: Euler system + explicit reciprocity ⇒ Selmer torsion and one divisibility
items.statement: Schema. Let V have an Euler system (satisfying the usual hypotheses: nonvanishing, big image) whose arithmetic p-adic L-function L_p^arith = Log(z) equals the analytic one, L_p^an = L_p^arith. Then the corresponding Iwasawa Selmer group (dual) is Λ-torsion and L_p^alg divides (L_p^an) (L_p^alg ⊇ (L_p^an) as ideals, possibly up to powers of p when integral hypotheses fail).
items.note: EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8: 'The application adapters have one-way dependencies: cyclotomic units plus ES.4/8 produce the cyclotomic divisibility ...; Kato classes plus explicit reciprocity produce a modular divisibility'. The Kato instance is packet node KatoEulerSystems:L4/imported-euler-system-bound-over-the-cyclotomic-iwasawa-algebra (Kato Thm. 13.4, hypotheses (i)–(v)) with L4/ordinary-selmer-divisibility. The text's schema omits all hypotheses.

items.name: Norm compatibility of the cyclotomic unit groups
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 the norm N_{n+1,n} : F_{n+1}^× → F_n^× maps 𝒟_{n+1} into 𝒟_n: N(ξ_{p^{n+1}}) = ξ_{p^n}, N(−1) = −1 (p odd), and N(ξ^a_{p^{n+1}} − 1) = ξ^a_{p^n} − 1 for p ∤ a (Lemma 10.3's computation). Hence the local norms map 𝒞_{n+1} into 𝒞_n, 𝒞_{n+1,1} into 𝒞_{n,1} and 𝒞^+_{n+1,1} into 𝒞^+_{n,1} (norms preserve units, reality and principal units and are continuous), so that 𝒞_{∞,1} = lim 𝒞_{n,1} and 𝒞^+_{∞,1} of Definition 11.8 are defined.
items.locator: §11.3, Definition 11.8 (printed p. 176, PDF 77), used implicitly; the norm computation is in §10.2 (printed p. 165, PDF 66)
items.note: Added by the review: Definition 11.8 takes inverse limits of the 𝒞_{n,1} without stating that the norms preserve them. Stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4: 'Construct the principal Teichmuller-adjusted compatible generator w gamma_{n,a}. Prove its membership, norm compatibility, finite-level spanning'; node IntegralIwasawaTheory:L0/tower-galois-compatibility for the tower. No packet node for the global groups 𝒟_n.

routes.reason: These notes are the source this roadmap was designed from (its layer texts cite 'RJW §§3–4'), and its packet already decomposes most of §3 into nodes. This route adds the paper as the blueprint source for what the packet has not yet reached. Five missing items belong inside existing layers. Two concern L0's duals and bounded measures: B*-reflexivity for the weak topology (Remark 3.6) and the unbounded real Haar distribution (Remark 3.13), the non-example to L0's 'bounded finitely additive functions'. The existence of an integer topological generator of ℤ_p^× (Lemma 3.38's example) is L3's 'change of generator' for procyclic groups. Lemma 11.2, Λ(Γ)^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+), is L1's functoriality of completed group rings for the quotient by ⟨c⟩. Lemma 11.3, a measure lies in Λ(Γ^+) iff its odd moments vanish, is L3's positive-moment separation (node L3/unit-positive-moment-separation) with a parity decomposition. The planned items named here are those the layer texts cover without a node, and the paper states each of them: orthonormal bases, the measure/Iwasawa-algebra equivalence and multiplicativity of the Amice transform, Λ(ℤ_p^×) ⊄ Λ(ℤ_p) as algebras, principal augmentation ideals and Lemma 3.38, weight space as p−1 discs, and exactness of limits and topological Nakayama for compact Λ-modules. No new layer is needed: every item is a lemma in a layer's stated direction.

This roadmap's layer texts are written against the notes. L0 cites RJW Theorem 2.2, 2.4 and Propositions 2.9/2.11, and L4's acceptance is 'all named results in RJW §§2–8 except Theorem 6.7'. Two missing items fall inside its layers. The transcendence of L(θ,1) (§6, footnote 10) is a corollary in L0 ('complex special values and algebraicity'): it uses Leopoldt's formula (Theorem 6.1(i)), Mathlib's nonvanishing DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero and Baker's theorem, imported from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3. The observation of §8 that k ↦ p^k is interpolated by no measure on ℤ_p^× is L4's motivating obstruction for the Eisenstein family; it is stated with the corrected hypothesis k_n ≡ k mod (p − 1). The planned items named here are the §§2, 5, 7–8 results that the layer texts list but the packet has not yet decomposed into nodes. They include the class number formula of Theorem 2.2, the idelic dictionary of Propositions 2.9 and 2.11, Theorems 2.15–2.16, 5.1, 5.7 and 5.20's branches, Gauss-sum identities, the residue computation of §7, and Theorem 8.2(a) with A_0 = xζ_p/2. The paper becomes the source for those nodes, with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues.

Part II §§10–12 of the notes is this roadmap's source: Coleman's norm operator, the Coleman power series, the Coleman map, the image of the cyclotomic units, and Iwasawa's theorem on local units modulo cyclotomic units. Its packet has nodes for L0–L3, but L4 ('the end of the proof') has none. The route names as source items the statements the layers plan without nodes. From §10: Coleman's theorem (Theorem 10.2), the surjectivity of R (Proposition 10.12), Coleman's isomorphism (Theorem 10.13), the Coleman map (Definition 10.14) and Theorem 10.15 with its corrected sign Col(c(a)) = −θ_a·ζ_p. From §§11–12: Λ(Γ)-linearity (Proposition 12.1, Corollary 12.6), the fundamental exact sequence for U_{∞,1} (Theorem 12.17(ii)), and the generators of the local cyclotomic units (Lemmas 12.20–12.22) with the unproved splitting C_{∞,1} = ℤ_p(1) × C_{∞,1}^+. The route ends with Theorems 12.23(i) and 11.9. The recorded gaps in the proof of Theorem 12.23 tell the blueprint worker which steps need a proof the paper does not give. Nothing here is missing.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 2.18, printed p. 117 (PDF 18), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical (main2.tex lines 630–636)
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that the theorems give (1−η(p)p^{k−1})L(η,1−k) ≡ (1−η(p)p^{ℓ−1})L(η,1−ℓ) (mod p^m) for every Dirichlet character η with conductor prime to p. It identifies the Riemann zeta case with the generalised Kummer congruences.
sourceIssues.correction: For η nontrivial (conductor D > 1 prime to p) the congruence holds in 𝒪_L, because ζ_η is an integral measure. For η trivial (the Riemann zeta function) ζ_p is only a pseudomeasure: the congruence holds (p odd) only when (p−1) ∤ k, or in general after smoothing: (1−a^k)(1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) ≡ (1−a^ℓ)(1−p^{ℓ−1})ζ(1−ℓ) (mod p^m) for a prime to p.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: p = 3, m = 1, η trivial, k = 2, ℓ = 4 (k ≡ ℓ mod 2). (1−3)ζ(−1) = (−2)(−1/12) = 1/6 and (1−27)ζ(−3) = (−26)(1/120) = −13/60; the difference 1/6 + 13/60 = 23/60 has 3-adic valuation −1, so the two values are not even congruent mod 3 (both have denominators divisible by 3, as von Staudt–Clausen predicts when (p−1) | k). Integrating the congruence x^k ≡ x^ℓ (mod p^m) against ζ_p is not allowed since ζ_p ∉ Λ(ℤ_p^×). Smoothing by a = 2: (1−2²)/6 = −1/2 and (1−2⁴)(−13/60) = 13/4 differ by 15/4, of 3-adic valuation 1, as the integral measure x⁻¹Res μ_a predicts. For (p−1) ∤ k take a a primitive root mod p, so 1−a^k and 1−a^ℓ are units with a^k ≡ a^ℓ (mod p^m), and divide. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.json PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E13; DirichletPadicLFunctions.json DirichletPadicLFunctions/E10.)

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 2.1, definition of L_p(V,s), printed p. 107 (PDF 8), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical (main2.tex line 306)
sourceIssues.printed: L_p(V,s) := det(Id − φ^{−1}p^{−s} | D_cris(V))^{−1}
sourceIssues.correction: L_p(V,s) := det(Id − φ·p^{−s} | D_cris(V))^{−1}, with D_cris(V) = (B_cris ⊗_{ℚ_p} V)^{𝒢_{ℚ_p}} (covariant, as in the cited Berger [7] and Benois [6]); this matches the factor det(Id − Frob_ℓ^{−1}ℓ^{−s} | V^{I_ℓ})^{−1} used at ℓ ≠ p.
sourceIssues.reason: Test on V = ℚ_p(1), the cyclotomic character, whose L-function should be ζ(s+1): at ℓ ≠ p, Frob_ℓ^{−1} acts by ℓ^{−1}, giving (1 − ℓ^{−1−s})^{−1} as the text's convention requires. D_cris(ℚ_p(1)) = ℚ_p·(t^{−1} ⊗ e) and φ(t) = pt, so φ acts by p^{−1}; then det(1 − φp^{−s}) = 1 − p^{−1−s} (correct Euler factor of ζ(s+1)) whereas the printed det(1 − φ^{−1}p^{−s}) = 1 − p^{1−s} (Euler factor of ζ(s−1)). Equivalently, for unramified V, D_cris(V) = (V ⊗ ℚ̂_p^{ur})^{𝒢} and φ = 1 ⊗ σ corresponds to the geometric Frobenius Frob_p^{−1} on V, so φ (not φ^{−1}) plays the role of Frob_ℓ^{−1}. The printed formula would be right only for a contravariant D_cris, which neither cited reference uses.

sourceIssues.correction: …such that (a_i) ↦ Σ a_i e_i is an isometric isomorphism (a surjective isometry) ℓ⁰_∞(I,L) ≅ B.
sourceIssues.reason: An isometry need not be onto: in B = 𝒞(ℤ_p,L) the family e_n = (x choose 2n) gives an isometry ℓ⁰_∞(ℕ,L) → B (by Mahler's theorem the norm of Σa_n(x choose 2n) is sup|a_n|), but its image misses (x choose 1), so it is not a basis. The standard notion (Serre's orthonormal bases of p-adic Banach spaces, which is what the existence statement quoted in Remark 3.4 produces) requires the map to be an isometric isomorphism onto B; the Colmez source text itself was not re-read here. The paper's later assertion that the (x choose n) 'form an orthonormal basis' (after Definition 3.20) is true in the corrected sense, which Mahler's theorem (uniqueness+existence of the expansion) gives.

sourceIssues.locator: Definition 3.5, strong-topology bullet, second sentence, printed p. 119 (PDF 20), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source describes this as the least fine topology in which convergence of (µ_j)_j ⊂ B* is equivalent to uniform convergence, understood for continuous functions on B.
sourceIssues.correction: The strong (operator-norm) topology is the topology of uniform convergence on the unit ball of B (equivalently on bounded subsets of B), not on all of B.
sourceIssues.reason: Take B = L = ℚ_p and µ_n(x) = p^n x. Then v*(µ_n) = n → ∞, i.e. µ_n → 0 strongly, but sup_{x∈B}|µ_n(x)| = ∞ for every n (take x = p^{−n−k}), so µ_n does not converge to 0 uniformly on B. Indeed a sequence of linear functionals converges uniformly on all of B only if it is eventually constant. sourceIssues.locator: Remark 3.6, first sentence, printed p. 119 (PDF 20), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical (rem:strong topology)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts completeness of B* for each of the two topologies.
sourceIssues.correction: B* is complete for the strong topology. For the weak topology it is in general NOT complete when B is infinite-dimensional (its completion is the algebraic dual); only bounded weakly Cauchy nets/sequences converge (Banach–Steinhaus), and the closed unit ball (e.g. M(G,𝒪_L)) is weakly compact since L is locally compact.
sourceIssues.reason: For B = c₀(ℕ,ℚ_p) choose an algebraic linear functional ℓ with ℓ(e_n) = p^{−n} (extend from the span of the e_n by a Hamel basis); it is discontinuous. For every finite F ⊂ B there is a continuous ℓ_F (factor through finitely many coordinates injective on span F) agreeing with ℓ on F; the net (ℓ_F)_F is weakly Cauchy (eventually constant at each vector) but its only possible weak limit is ℓ ∉ B*. The packet lead gives the same construction; I re-derived it. (If 'complete' is read as 'sequentially complete' the weak statement is true by Banach–Steinhaus, but the paper does not say so.) (Also recorded by an earlier worker: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.json PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E10.)

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 3.35, printed p. 130 (PDF 31), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 (main2.tex, remark after (eq:integrate pseudo-measure)) identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that this produces exactly one homomorphism Q(G) → C_p, whose value on a pseudomeasure is the expression (3-11).
sourceIssues.correction: The ring homomorphism ε_χ : Λ(G) → C_p, µ ↦ ∫_G χ·µ, extends to a localisation of Λ(G) only if every inverted element has nonzero image; in general it does NOT extend to the total quotient ring Q(G). What is true: on the Λ(G)-module of pseudomeasures, (3-11) is the unique additive map E with E(µ) = ε_χ(µ) for µ ∈ Λ(G) and E(µλ) = ε_χ(µ)E(λ).
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample meeting the remark's hypotheses: p = 3, G = Z_3, Λ(G) = Z_3[[T]] with [1] ↦ 1 + T (a domain), χ(x) = 4^x, a nontrivial continuous character, so ε_χ(F) = F(3). The element s = T − 3 is nonzero, hence a non-zero-divisor, but ε_χ(s) = 0; a ring homomorphism F : Q(G) → C_p extending ε_χ would give 1 = F(s)F(s^{−1}) = 0. (Checked by hand; the same obstruction exists for G = Z_p^× and many characters.) Reach: the claim in Remark 3.35); nothing downstream, since (3-11) is used directly and its independence of g is proved separately. (Also recorded by an earlier worker: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.json, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras/E1.)

sourceIssues.printed: The proof chooses an integer a ≠ 1 coprime to p and claims that [a] −[1] meets the hypothesis in part (ii), making it a non-zero-divisor.

sourceIssues.reason: μ_η and ζ_η exist only for D > 1 (Theorem 5.7). The proof's reduction F̃_θ = (F̃_η)_χ fails since F̃_1 = −log T. So Lemma 6.4 as stated (for every nontrivial θ) is false when D = 1, and the notes' proof of Theorem 6.1(ii) covers only D > 1. (The lead classed this as a gap affecting the proof; since Lemma 6.4 itself is false for D = 1 it is classed here as an error in a stated result, while Theorem 6.1(ii) remains true.) sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 8.2(a) and the first sentence of its proof, printed p. 160 (PDF 61), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: Part (a) asserts that A_0 is a pseudomeasure, whereas A_n ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for every n ≥ 1. The source identifies A_0 with xζ_p/2.
sourceIssues.correction: (a) x^{−1}A_0 is a pseudomeasure (A_0 = xζ_p/2 ∈ Q(Z_p^×), the twist by the character x of the pseudomeasure ζ_p/2; equivalently (g[g] − [1])A_0 ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for all g ∈ Z_p^×), and A_n ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for n ≥ 1.
sourceIssues.reason: By Definition 3.34 a pseudomeasure λ satisfies ([g] − [1])λ ∈ Λ(Z_p^×) for all g, i.e. as a function on weight space it can have a pole only at the trivial character. Twisting by x is a ring automorphism of Λ(Z_p^×) with x·([g] − [1]) = g[g] − [1], so xζ_p has its pole at κ = x^{−1} (where ∫κ·(xζ_p) = ∫1·ζ_p), not at 1; since ζ_p really has a pole at the trivial character (Theorem 7.1(ii), Lemma 7.5: ∫1·([a]−[1])ζ_p = −(1 − p^{−1})log_p(a) ≠ 0), ([g] − [1])·xζ_p ∉ Λ for g ≠ 1. Moreover no pseudomeasure A_0 can satisfy (b): for k = (p−1)p^m (even, ≥ 4) the character x^{k−1} lies on the component ω^{−1} ≠ 1, where a pseudomeasure µ/([a]−[1]) has |∫x^{k−1}·λ| ≤ ‖µ‖ because |a^{k−1} − 1| = |ω(a)^{−1} − 1| = 1; but |½(1 − p^{k−1})ζ(1−k)| = |B_k/(2k)| = p^{m+1} → ∞ by von Staudt–Clausen. So (a) and (b) as printed are incompatible; the construction A_0 = xζ_p/2 is right and only the word 'pseudomeasure' is wrong.

sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts compactness over Zp for all infinite-level modules, reasoning that they are limits of compact Zp-modules. It equips them naturally with continuous Γ = Gal(F∞/Q) or Γ+ = Gal(F+∞/Q) actions and, consequently, continuous Λ(Γ) or Λ(Γ+) actions.

sourceIssues.reason: The previous paragraph itself says U_n and U_n^+ 'are only Z-modules', so the justification 'inverse limits of compact Z_p-modules' does not apply to U_∞, U_∞^+. Directly: U_n = μ_{p−1} × U_{n,1} (Teichmüller; residue field F_p), and the norm N_{K_n/K_{n−1}} acts on μ_{p−1} ⊂ Q_p by ζ ↦ ζ^p, a bijection, so U_∞ ≅ μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1} (same for the plus parts). sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 12.22(i), printed p. 188 (PDF 89), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: Citing Lemma 12.21(ii), the source gives (p − 1)D_n^+ = (p − 1)D^+_{n,1} ⊂ U^+_{n,1} with Z[Γ_n^+]-generator (wγ_{n,a})^{p−1}. It then cites Lemma 12.20 to claim that its p-adic closure, (p − 1)C^+_{n,1}, has the same generator over Z_p[Γ_n^+].
sourceIssues.correction: By Lemma 12.21(ii), (p − 1)D_n^+ ⊂ U^+_{n,1} is generated as a Z[Γ_n^+]-module by (wγ_{n,a})^{p−1}. By Lemma 12.20 (applied to its finitely many Γ_n^+-conjugates) the p-adic closure of (p − 1)D_n^+ is Z_p[Γ_n^+]·(wγ_{n,a})^{p−1}. This closure is (p − 1)C_n^+ (the image of the compact C_n^+ = closure of D_n^+ under x ↦ x^{p−1}), and (p − 1)C_n^+ = C^+_{n,1}, because U_n^+ = μ_{p−1} × U^+_{n,1}, x ↦ x^{p−1} kills μ_{p−1}, and p − 1 is invertible on the Z_p-module C^+_{n,1}.
sourceIssues.reason: With the Part II convention X^+_{n,1} = X_n^+ ∩ U^+_{n,1} (the text itself uses D^+_{n,1} = V^+_{n,1} ∩ D_n^+ in §13), (p − 1)D^+_{n,1} is in general a proper subgroup of (p − 1)D_n^+. Example p = 5, n = 1: D_1^+ = ⟨−1, γ⟩ with γ = γ_{1,2} = ξ^2 + ξ^3 = (−1 − √5)/2 ≡ 2 mod 𝔭_1; ±γ^k ≡ 1 mod 𝔭_1 iff (+, 4 | k) or (−, k ≡ 2 mod 4), so D^+_{1,1} = ⟨−γ^2⟩ and 4D^+_{1,1} = ⟨γ^8⟩ ≠ ⟨γ^4⟩ = 4D_1^+ (γ is not a root of unity). The index [ (p−1)D_n^+ : (p−1)D^+_{n,1} ] divides p − 1, so the p-adic closures in the pro-p group U_{n,1} coincide (in the example Z_5γ^8 = Z_5γ^4) and the lemma is true.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 12.23, printed p. 188 (PDF 89), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source invokes Lemma 12.22 to reduce the task to computing Col on (ξ^b_{p^n}γ_{n,a})_{n≥1} ∈ U_{∞,1}, with a, b ∈ Z_p^×. Since a ∈ Z_p^× is arbitrary, it claims Col sends C_{∞,1} to I(Γ)ζ_p and C^+_{∞,1} to I(Γ^+)ζ_p.
sourceIssues.correction: Fix a ∈ Z a topological generator of Z_p^× and w = ω(a)^{−1} ∈ μ_{p−1}. Then C^+_{∞,1} = Λ(Γ^+)·(wγ_{n,a})_n (Lemma 12.22) and C_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) × C^+_{∞,1} (from D_n = ⟨ξ_{p^n}⟩ × D_n^+, Lemma 12.18(ii)). Col kills Z_p(1) = {(ξ^b_{p^n})_n : b ∈ Z_p} and μ_{p−1}, so Col((ξ^b_{p^n}wγ_{n,a})_n) = Col(c(a)) = ±([σ_a] − [1])ζ_p. As σ_a topologically generates Γ (and its image generates Γ^+), I(Γ) = Λ(Γ)([σ_a] − [1]) and I(Γ^+) = Λ(Γ^+)([σ_a] − [1]); hence Col(C_{∞,1}) = I(Γ)ζ_p and Col(C^+_{∞,1}) = I(Γ^+)ζ_p.
sourceIssues.reason: (1) γ_{n,a} ≡ a mod 𝔭_n (Lemma 12.21), so (ξ^b γ_{n,a})_n ∉ U_{∞,1} unless a ≡ 1 mod p; the factor w is missing (harmless since Col(w) = 0 by Lemma 12.3). (2) b must range over Z_p (Z_p(1) is not {(ξ^b) : b ∈ Z_p^×}), and a cannot be arbitrary: Lemma 12.22 and Theorem 10.15 are stated for a fixed topological generator. The step from the single generator to the whole ideal needs the principal-augmentation-ideal property of the procyclic groups Γ, Γ^+, which the text does not invoke. (3) Lemma 12.22 describes only C^+_{∞,1}; the decomposition C_{∞,1} = Z_p(1) × C^+_{∞,1} needed for part (i) is not stated or proved. The theorem itself is correct.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 13.7, printed p. 192 (PDF 93), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses density of O_L[Γ] in Λ(Γ) and the Hausdorff property of Λ(Γ) to claim that linearity and continuity extend the action to Λ(Γ) on X_∞.
sourceIssues.correction: Because 𝒳_∞ is a compact (profinite) ℤ_p-module on which Γ acts continuously — 𝒳_∞ = lim← 𝒳_∞/U over open Γ-stable subgroups U, and Γ acts on each finite p-group 𝒳_∞/U through a finite quotient — the ℤ_p[Γ]-action extends uniquely by continuity to ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ = Λ(Γ). The coefficients are ℤ_p (or tensor 𝒳_∞ with O_L), not O_L.
sourceIssues.reason: Extending an action from the dense subring by continuity needs the target 𝒳_∞ to be complete Hausdorff and the action to be (uniformly) continuous for the Λ(Γ)-topology; Hausdorffness of Λ(Γ) itself plays no role. Moreover 𝒳_∞ is a pro-p group, i.e. a ℤ_p-module, not an O_L-module, so O_L[Γ] (L a general finite extension as in §13.1) does not act on it. The asserted conclusion (a Λ(Γ)-module structure with ℤ_p-coefficients) is correct.

sourceIssues.locator: Example 13.22 with Conjecture 13.21(ii), printed p. 198 (PDF 99), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source identifies Greenberg’s p-adic L-function here with ∂^nζ_p, the n-th Kubota–Leopoldt twist, and consequently describes the conjecture as essentially Theorem 13.8 with a twist.
sourceIssues.correction: For n > 0 even, Theorem 13.8 is equivalent to ch_{Λ(Γ^+)}(𝒳_∞^+(−n)) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+)ζ_p) = Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p (Tw_n: [g] ↦ χ(g)^n[g]). Conjecture 13.21(ii) with L_p(ℚ_p(n)) = ∂^nζ_p, read literally, would assert ch = (∂^nζ_p), which is false; Greenberg's formulation needs the correction factor Tw_n(I(Γ^+)) (coming from H⁰(𝓕, W_n) = W_n ≠ 0 for n even), or the conjecture must exclude/adjust this case.
sourceIssues.reason: ζ_p is a pseudo-measure with a pole at the trivial character, not an element of Λ(Γ^+) (node DirichletPadicLFunctions:L1/arithmetic-not-integral: 'There is no μ ∈ M with Iwasawa.integral δ Q μ = ζ_p', on ℤ_p^×; ζ_p is even, and Λ(Γ)^+ ≅ Λ(Γ^+)); Tw_n is a ring automorphism of Λ(Γ^+) (n even, so χ^n factors through Γ^+), hence ∂^nζ_p = Tw_n(ζ_p) ∉ Λ(Γ^+) and (∂^nζ_p) is a fractional ideal not contained in Λ(Γ^+), whereas a characteristic ideal is an integral ideal. Twisting Theorem 13.8 (char(M(−n)) = Tw_n(char M)) gives Tw_n(I(Γ^+))·∂^nζ_p, which differs from (∂^nζ_p) exactly in the component of the character x^{−n}. The word 'essentially' hides this; the packet node EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3/tate-twisted-selmer-formulation records it in its hypotheses, but node SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L4/greenberg-conjecture-tate-twists repeats the literal claim. sourceIssues.locator: Appendix A.1, Theorem A.3, printed p. 200 (PDF 101), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; proof on printed p. 206; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts that integers λ≥0, µ≥0, ν ≥0 and n0 exist with en = µpn + λn + ν for every n ≥n0.
sourceIssues.correction: There exist integers λ ≥ 0, µ ≥ 0 and ν (an arbitrary integer, possibly negative), and n₀, such that e_n = µp^n + λn + ν for all n ≥ n₀.
sourceIssues.reason: The proof gives ν = c + c', where c comes from Lemma A.9 (|Y∞/ω_n| = p^c|𝒜/ω_n|, c ∈ ℤ, and c < 0 happens whenever 𝒜/ω_n is larger than Y∞/ω_n) and c' is the constant of Proposition A.10. Nothing in the argument makes the sum non-negative, and Washington's Theorem 13.13 (the source the text follows, [81, §13]) puts no sign on ν. Proposition A.10's constant can itself be negative. Take p = 3 and 𝒜 = Λ/(g), g = T⁴ − 3 (distinguished, prime to every ω_n). Then #𝒜/ω_n𝒜 = ∏_{ζ^{3^n}=1} |(ζ−1)⁴ − 3|_3^{−1}. ζ = 1 gives valuation 1. So log₃ #𝒜/ω_n𝒜 = 4n − 1 for n ≥ 1: λ = 4, µ = 0, 'ν' = −1. I did not check whether this module occurs as some Y∞ satisfying (H), so this is recorded as an unsupported claim (gap), not a disproved one. The integer ν of the standard statement is the target that stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 already specifies ('**nu is an integer**'). sourceIssues.printed: The source presents Corollary 13.16 as an earlier application of Iwasawa’s theorem in the main conjecture discussion, asserting that in a Zp-extension, coprimality of any one class number to p implies coprimality of every other one.
sourceIssues.correction: Corollary 13.16 is about the tower F_n⁺ = ℚ(μ_{p^n})⁺: if p ∤ h₁⁺ then p ∤ h_n⁺ for all n. The general principle 'if one layer has class number prime to p, so do all layers' holds for ℤ_p-extensions satisfying hypothesis (H) (one prime above p, totally ramified). It follows from Proposition A.6 and Lemma A.7, not from Theorem A.3, and it is false for general ℤ_p-extensions.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: F = ℚ(i), p = 5, F∞ = F·ℚ∞ the cyclotomic ℤ₅-extension. Here h(F) = 1. Both primes above 5 = (2+i)(2−i) are totally ramified in F_n/F, since 5 is totally ramified in ℚ_n/ℚ and [F_n : F] = 5^n. Chevalley's ambiguous class number formula for the cyclic extension F_n/F gives #Cl(F_n)^{Gal(F_n/F)} = h_F·∏_v e_v / ([F_n : F]·[E_F : E_F ∩ N F_n^×]) = 1·5^n·5^n/(5^n·1) = 5^n. The unit index is 1 because E_F = μ₄ has order prime to 5 while E_F/(E_F ∩ N F_n^×) is killed by 5^n. Hence 5 | h(F₁) although 5 ∤ h(F₀). Corollary 13.16's proof (printed p. 194) uses only Proposition 13.15 (= Proposition A.6) and Nakayama's lemma.

sourceIssues.locator: Appendix B.2.1, footnote 16, printed p. 208 (PDF 109), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record; arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source describes Deligne’s criterion for a motivic L(M, s): with L∞(M, s) its infinity Euler factor, s = j is critical exactly when both L∞(M, s) and L∞(M, 1−s) are free of poles at j.
sourceIssues.correction: … s = j is critical for L(M, s) if neither L∞(M, s) nor L∞(M^∨, 1−s) has a pole at s = j, where M^∨ is the dual motive.
sourceIssues.reason: Taken literally, the printed criterion contradicts the next sentence of the text. For M = M(f), f of weight k+2 with trivial character, L∞(M,s) = Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s), and L∞(M,1−s) = Γ_ℂ(1−s) has poles at s = 1, 2, 3, …, so no j + 1 with 0 ≤ j ≤ k would be critical, whereas the text says the critical values are L(f,χ,j+1), 0 ≤ j ≤ k. With M^∨ ≅ M(k+1), L∞(M^∨, 1−s) = Γ_ℂ(k+2−s) has poles at s ≥ k+2, and the criterion gives exactly 1 ≤ s ≤ k+1. For M = ℚ(0) (the ζ example in the footnote) M^∨ = M, so that example is unaffected.

sourceIssues.printed: The proof uses the pseudomeasure property of ζ_p to assert ([g] − [1])ζ_p ∈ Λ(Γ) for every g ∈ Γ. It concludes by identifying I(Γ) as the topological ideal generated by those [g] − [1].

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Corollary 13.16(iii), printed p. 194 (PDF 95), Essential Number Theory 4 (2025) version of record (page image checked); arXiv v2 identical
sourceIssues.printed: The source says the definitions identify ℰ^+_{n,1} and 𝒞^+_{n,1} with the respective p-adic closures of 𝒱^+_{n,1} and 𝒟^+_{n,1} in 𝒰^+_{n,1}.
sourceIssues.correction: By Definitions 11.8 and 13.12, ℰ^+_{n,1} = cl(𝒱_n) ∩ 𝒰_n^+ ∩ 𝒰_{n,1} (and similarly for 𝒞). This equals the closure of 𝒱^+_{n,1} = 𝒱_n^+ ∩ U_{n,1}. U_{n,1} is open, so intersecting a closure with it gives the closure of the intersection. For the real part, if x = lim v_i is real then x² = lim v_iv̄_i is a limit of real units, and x is the unique square root of x² in the pro-p group U_{n,1} (2 is a unit in ℤ_p).
sourceIssues.reason: The definitions in the notes take the closure first and then the plus and principal parts. The proof uses the other order. The two agree, but this needs the short argument above; it is not 'by definition'.
